However, during the later stages of water injection, small pores exhibit an “oil-locking” phenomenon, while large pores show characteristics of “residual gas.” A comparison of different water injection methods indicates that asynchronous injection and production can help maintain reservoir pressure stability and reduce differences in the utilization of different pore types. This study provides an important theoretical foundation for the efficient development of weakly volatile fracture-pore type carbonate reservoirs.

papers.title: Modeling rock permeability considering the coupled damage effect of effective stress and temperature
papers.abstract: Understanding how rock permeability changes with effective stress and temperature is essential for the exploitation of natural resources. Rock permeability exhibits complex behavior due to the combined influence of effective stress and temperature, which cause significant non-linearity and non-monotonicity. To address this, this study proposes a novel permeability model that incorporates the coupled damage effects of effective stress and temperature. This model is based on the tortuous capillary tube framework, considering both the reduction in capillary tube volume and permeability due to compaction from effective stress and thermal expansion. Additionally, the model incorporates damage evolution driven by effective shear stress and temperature, represented using the Weibull distribution. It is validated using three sets of permeability data from existing literature: the individual effect of temperature, effective stress, and their coupled effect. The proposed model effectively captures the permeability behavior of various rocks under different temperature and effective stress conditions, thereby confirming its accuracy and applicability. Notably, it provides a more precise representation of permeability variation across multiple orders of magnitude compared to existing models.

papers.title: Near-field characteristics of drift under crossflow conditions
papers.abstract: A drift from a cooling tower is an important research topic in both academic and practical perspectives due to a similarity to the jet in crossflow and possible relationship to Legionella transmission. The dynamic and thermal characteristics of a drift under crossflow are investigated numerically using an Eulerian–Lagrangian approach and droplet phase change model, focusing on the near-field development under varying Grashof numbers and velocity ratios. Large eddy simulations are performed for the base, low atmospheric temperature, and low velocity ratio (LVR) cases. The development of counter-rotating vortex pair (CVP) in a LVR range shows the opposite trend to that in a high velocity ratio range. Unlike the jet centerline, the droplet trajectory shows higher sensitivity to the Grashof number and distinctive double inflection points in the LVR case. A modified semi-empirical formula for the drift radius is presented with improved prediction accuracy. Time evolution of a two-dimensional probability density function (PDF) on the Lagrangian droplet phase presents two distinctive temperature regimes based on the droplet ejection location and explains the mechanisms driving a branch shape in the PDF. The histograms of the droplet mass show higher sensitivity of smaller droplets to the phase change and increased Grashof number. The LVR case shows distinct droplet evolution mechanism due to the compact and strong CVP collecting hot and small droplets inside. The higher intensity CVP increases the mass of smaller droplets via increased condensation, while stronger crossflow momentum decreases the mass of larger droplets via mixing.

papers.title: Analyzing chaos and bifurcations about fractional order long–short wave interaction system in fluid mechanics models
papers.abstract: The stochastic space-fractional long–short-wave interaction system is a powerful tool for modeling wave phenomena in fluid mechanics and elucidating physical processes in nonlinear optics and plasma physics. In this study, we have made several notable contributions to the understanding of the stochastic space-fractional long–short-wave interaction system by employing the enhanced modified extended tanh-function method. Initially, we have identified a diverse range of exact solutions, including novel Weierstrass elliptic function solutions that have not been explored in previous research. Our analysis has also visually demonstrated how noise intensity affects the accuracy of solutions, highlighting the stabilizing role of multiplicative noise. Furthermore, we have developed innovative visualizations to illustrate the relationship between the obliquity angle and solitary wave solutions, which have not been addressed in prior studies. We have also examined the distinct impacts of various fractional derivative forms on the stochastic space-fractional long–short-wave interaction system. Additionally, we appear to be the first to apply the classic Runge–Kutta method to numerically solve the space-fractional long–short-wave interaction system. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high solution accuracy, exhibits excellent numerical stability, and is straightforward to implement with flexible step size adjustment. Finally, our investigation into sensitivity analysis and chaotic behavior has enhanced our comprehension of the system's evolution and dynamics. Collectively, our work provides novel insight into the stochastic space-fractional long–short-wave interaction system, advancing the research frontier and addressing several unexplored aspects in previous studies.

papers.title: A logic gate based on photonic structure of liquid crystal and the theoretical design of dual polarization multi-physical quantity detection
papers.abstract: In this paper, a multifunctional layered photonic structure capable of implementing various logic gates and detecting multiple physical quantities is proposed. This structure is achieved through the arrangement of various dielectrics with the incorporation of anisotropic plasmas and liquid crystal materials, imparting tunability and multiscale characteristics. Meanwhile, sharp transmission peaks (TPs) can be obtained, which follows the rule of NOR (“NOT OR” gate) logic and AND (“AND” gate) logic gates for transverse magnetic and transverse electric polarization by judging the values of TPs. By locking the frequency point at the TP, simultaneous sensing of the refractive index, the angle between the incident wave and electric field, magnetic field strength, and temperature can be achieved. Various parameters for evaluating sensing performance have also been introduced, and their respective sensitivities within normalized frequency (2πc/dare obtained as follows: 8.75 × 10−4 (2πc/d)/RIU or 2.5 × 10−4 (2πc/d)/RIU, 1.7 × 10−3 (2πc/d)/T or 2 × 10−3 (2πc/d)/T, 0.0882 (2πc/d)/° or 0.0957 (2πc/d)/°, 4.87 × 10−4 (2πc/d)/K or 7.22 × 10−4 (2πc/d)/K. Unlike conventional sensors, this device has the capability of tunable logic gates and multi-physics quantity detection, which has a wide range of application scenarios in light computing and biosensing fields.

papers.title: Fluid-structure-acoustic responses of a nonlinearly supported rigid circular cylinder in viscous flow
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the synchronization mode modulation and fluid-structure-acoustic responses of a rigid circular cylinder supported by a nonlinear spring subjected to viscous flow. A strongly coupled fluid–structure interaction (FSI) model of the cylinder based on the arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian (ALE) framework is developed. Direct numerical simulation is employed to model the compressible viscous flow. Four distinct branches of the sound waves generated by the vibrational cylinder are identified, i.e., the initial branch, upper branch, lower branch, and desynchronized branch. Nonlinear vibration of the cylinder governs the synchronized sound waves, directing their propagation toward the fore-field via balanced lift and drag dipole sound mode interactions. In contrast, desynchronized sound waves, dominated by the transversal lift dipole sound mode at high flow velocities, propagate exclusively toward the backfield. The nonlinear stiffness of the spring is shown to modulate frequency and phase relationships of the fluid-structure-acoustic interaction system, regulating the lock-in range and facilitating transitions between synchronization and desynchronization states of the cylinder. It also influences higher-order harmonic contributions, altering the phase relationship between the response and flow excitation of the cylinder and enabling transitions between the in-phase and the out-phase modes of the cylinder.

papers.title: Effects of gravity and rotation modulation on convection driven by thermal and compositional buoyancy in a porous layer
papers.abstract: This study investigates the linear and weakly nonlinear convection driven by both thermal and compositional buoyancy in a rotating horizontal porous layer, under the influence of: (a) gravity modulation and (b) rotation modulation. It is assumed that the amplitude of gravity and rotation modulation is minimal. In linear stability analysis, the normal mode technique is employed to calculate the thermal Rayleigh number at the onset of stationary convection. A perturbation analysis is applied to study the weakly nonlinear regime, focusing on the small supercritical Rayleigh number. The Nusselt and Sherwood numbers, representing heat and mass transfer, are governed by a nonautonomous Ginzburg–Landau equation. The study explores the effects of variations in the Prandtl number, the Lewis number, the separation parameter, the Taylor number, and the frequency and amplitude of modulation, on heat and mass transfer. The results highlight the dynamics of gravity and rotation modulation, demonstrating that the governing parameters significantly influence the stability of the system. The analysis indicates that gravity modulation improves heat transfer by up to 39% and mass transfer by up to 83%, compared to rotation modulation, and promoting greater efficiency than the unmodulated system. These findings have implications for enhancing efficiency in geothermal energy systems, chemical processes, and space-based fluid dynamics.

papers.title: Residence time distribution in thermal insulation materials
papers.abstract: This paper presents residence time distribution (RTD)-based characterization of thermal insulation materials, constructed upon a boiling water heat source-based testing system. Different types of metals, glasses, and polymeric materials are tested and analyzed. Every test plate material is subjected to a boiling water-based heating at one of its sides (waterside), while the other side (airside) is open to the ambience. The temperature data at these two sides of the test plate are then used to construct the relevant RTD curves. The properties of the RTD curves and the associated RTD parameters are found to be dependent on the thermal insulation capability of the test material. Specifically, the RTD curves unveil maximum heating frequency that the test plate is subjected to, and the stabilization time required by the test plate to achieve equilibrium under heating conditions. Accordingly, new metrics are defined for characterizing thermal insulations: (i) thermal shielding efficiency based on the maximum heating frequency, and (ii) thermal stabilization efficiency based on the stabilization time. Subsequently, the tested materials are characterized using the proposed metrics, along with the conventional thermal resistance-based metric. The proposed metrics are found to bring out the proper thermal shielding abilities of different types of materials that are hitherto remaining obscured by the limited capability of the conventional thermal resistance-based characterization.

papers.title: Effects of short-crestedness and currents on the dynamic response of a floating wave-energy harvesting platform
papers.abstract: The focus of this paper is to investigate the effects of short-crestedness and currents on the dynamic behavior of a wave-energy harvesting platform. After establishing its motion equation, the performance under both operational and severe conditions is simulated in the time domain, which includes some factors such as the current velocity, current direction, and wave distribution. The wave–current interactions are considered to predict the responses of this harvesting system. Additionally, the current study analyzes the responses of the platform motion and mooring line tension within the low-frequency and wave-frequency ranges. Meanwhile, the frequency-domain response spectra are also used to explore the characteristics of the motion and tension responses. Moreover, the motion phase plots evaluate the platform stability performance under severe conditions. The results indicate that the presence of currents alters the magnitude of wave excitation forces, which significantly affects the dynamic behavior of this harvesting system. In summary, the analytical framework and methods introduced in this paper could offer some insights into the design of ocean energy systems under a realistic sea environment.

papers.title: Hydrodynamics and bed morphology in a double-layered partially vegetated mobile bed channel
papers.abstract: This study investigates the hydrodynamics and sediment transport in a double-layered partially vegetated mobile bed channel, focusing on the impact of submerged vegetation with the submergence ratio of 61.53% and 30.77% on flow dynamics and bed morphology. Experiments were conducted in a straight, tilting rectangular flume with staggered double layered submerged vegetation covering half of the channel width. The three dimensional time-averaged velocity components, turbulent intensities, secondary current, turbulent kinetic energy, and Reynolds shear stress are measured and analyzed using contour plots along the channel width. The outcomes reveal that the submerged vegetation induces significant momentum exchange between vegetated and non-vegetated sections. In the vegetated section, the vegetation dampens the streamwise velocity and turbulent intensity near the bed, promoting sediment deposition and enhancing channel stability. Momentum transfer at the interface strengthens shear, increasing flow velocity and turbulence in the non-vegetated section, leading to greater bed erosion. Negative streamwise-vertical Reynolds stress indicates helical flow, while transverse-vertical Reynolds stress peaks near the non-vegetated bed. Flow diversion intensifies erosion in the high-energy non-vegetated section, while vegetation-induced drag decelerates flow, causing a transition to deposition deeper in the vegetated section. Double-layered submerged vegetation in rivers or canals is more effective in stabilizing bed materials. These findings provide critical insight for river restoration and channel management, emphasizing the necessity for integrated vegetation management strategies to balance sediment deposition and erosion across the heterogeneous channel environments.

papers.title: Rotational stall and pressure fluctuations in centrifugal pump impellers with transient flow rates
papers.abstract: To investigate the characteristics of rotational stall and pressure fluctuations, this study presents two large eddy simulations for the five-blade and seven-blade centrifugal pump impellers under transient condition. The transient condition represents that the flow rate and rotational speed are sinusoidal and constant, respectively. Research shows that the processes of stall germination, stall transition and stall stabilization are clearly discerned in the evolution of rotational stall during both the dropping and rising stages. The increase in the number of blades enhances the uniformity of the time-averaged normal vorticity distributions among different passages and has negligible influence on the total time-averaged normal vorticity. The low-frequency pressure fluctuations range for the five-blade impeller is greater compared to that for the seven-blade impeller. The high-frequency components of the pressure fluctuations are intense primarily at the leading and trailing edges of the blade, especially when the instantaneous flow rate is below half load. The first-order dominant frequency is identical to the flow rate frequency in the impeller inlet and the impeller passages, and the increase in the number of blades results in a reduction in the dominant frequency amplitude.

papers.title: Flow and heat transfer behavior of asymmetric synthetic jet
papers.abstract: This research explores the flow dynamics and heat transfer characteristics of asymmetric (elliptical orifice) and symmetric (circular orifice) synthetic jets (SJ). The present investigation clearly distinguishes axis-switching phenomena responsible for variation in heat transfer rate between a non-zero mass flow jet device (SJ) and a steady jet with the same aspect ratio and equivalent opening areas. The axis-switching phenomenon emerging from asymmetric office SJ is correlated with heat transfer for the first time. All SJ cases used orifices with a constant hydraulic diameter of 14 mm, an excitation frequency of 125 Hz, an amplitude of 4 V, and a 5800 Reynolds number. The axis-switching phenomenon is investigated by analyzing the heat transfer distribution and wall pressure measurements for synthetic and steady jets. For a given Reynolds number and aspect ratio, the axis-switching phenomenon is not observed for the steady jet; however, SJ exhibited various switchovers where its locations and strength are strong functions of the aspect ratio. It is found that the axis-switching is influenced by counter-rotating vortex pairs on the major axis and the reorientation of azimuthal vortices causing the primary and secondary switching of vortices. At lower spacings (Z/D < 4) and higher aspect ratios, the heat transfer rate is maximized along the minor axis but shifts to the major axis as surface spacing increases. The effect of axis-switching is less dominant at larger spacings (Z/D > 6), yielding similar average Nusselt numbers for both axes. Further, the findings reveal that a higher aspect ratio (AR = 3.5), asymmetric SJ provides up to 46.6% higher heat transfer rate than a symmetric SJ at a lower Z/D's. This axis-switching behavior in SJs contributes to an increase in the average Nusselt number (Nuavg) at lower surface spacing. The flow visualization using smoke wire is also carried out to capture the instantaneous flow field of the SJ. This helps us understand the flow behavior of both symmetric and asymmetric SJ structures, including the axis-switching behavior, which supports the heat transfer results. In the case of a steady jet, the heat transfer rate is also highest for an asymmetric orifice, but the difference is less pronounced. Compared to the steady jets, the SJ exhibits lower heat transfer rates at small spacings (Z/D ≤ 2) because of the recirculation of the heated air. However, SJs exhibit higher heat transfer rates than steady jets for larger spacings (Z/D > 6) due to higher spread and mixing. This study provides important information on how aspect ratios and jet-to-surface spacings influence heat transfer and fluid dynamics in both steady and SJs.

papers.title: Hybrid computational fluid dynamics-machine learning optimization of Darrieus wind turbines: Aerodynamic improvement and noise reduction through wake and vortex interactions
papers.abstract: This research uniquely explores the effects of wake interactions between adjacent Darrieus wind turbines on their aerodynamic performance and noise emissions, a critical consideration for optimizing wind farm design and operation in proximity to populated areas. Additionally, it examines the vortex interactions between rotor blades and analyzes the dynamic stall phenomenon, offering valuable insights into the unsteady aerodynamic behavior. By utilizing Large-Eddy Simulation, the study analyzes complex turbulence patterns and rotor interactions, thereby deepening the understanding of their aerodynamic and aeroacoustic effects. A multiobjective evolutionary algorithm integrates machine learning with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to improve rotor designs for maximum power efficiency and reduced noise, considering wake interactions. The study assesses the impact of physical and geometric parameters on rotor performance, creating a database via Design of Experiments to replace time-intensive CFD model with an Artificial Neural Network for performance predictions. The nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II refines aerodynamic and aeroacoustic attributes, with optimal design parameters identified using the linear programing technique for multidimensional analysis of preference (LINMAP). The LINMAP-optimized rotor outperforms the Point O rotor in aerodynamic and aeroacoustic performance. Its wider blade spacing enhances airflow and torque coefficient (CT), while the Point O rotor suffers from increased vortex interactions. In the downwind region, the LINMAP rotor maintains positive CT values, whereas the Point O experiences negative torque. Furthermore, the LINMAP design produces stronger low-frequency noise, while the Point O rotor exhibits higher sound pressure levels above 100 Hz.

papers.title: Separation mechanism and performance of hydrocyclone with media size redistribution
papers.abstract: Hydrocyclones have the advantages of fast separation speed, simple structure, small footprint, and convenient operation/maintenance, resulting in satisfactory separation performance and wide applications. However, conventional hydrocyclones are incapable of separating fine particles or droplets. A hydrocyclone with media-size redistribution (HMSR) was designed and studied to alleviate this shortcoming. The overall separation efficiency of the hydrocyclone could be improved by this design. Based on theory analysis and numerical simulation, the redistribution mechanism of redistributed inlet (RI) was studied, the flow characteristics in RI and the redistribution effect were obtained and verified by using the population balance model during simulations, and RI with 90° bent pipe was found to have the optimal redistribution efficiency. By comparing the other two kinds of hydrocyclones, the separation efficiency of HMSR (RI with 90° bent pipe) can be increased by 11.57%. Additionally, the smaller the feed oil droplet size set, the better the improvement effect of separation efficiency. The design of HMSR is expected to provide a new idea for separating fine particles or droplets.

papers.title: Integrating river channel flood diversion strategies into dynamic urban flood risk assessment and multi-objective optimization of emergency shelters
papers.abstract: With the continuous advancement of urbanization, the risk of urban flooding is increasing, making establishment of emergency shelters crucial for mitigating flood disasters. This study uses the Jinshui River flood diversion pipeline project in Zhengzhou as a case to systematically investigate the effect of flood diversion measures on reducing urban flood risks and to optimize the site selection for emergency shelters based on flood risk assessments. First, the InfoWorks integrated catchment management model is used to simulate flooding under different rainfall scenarios. Second, integrating multi-source data, the technique for order preference by similarity to an ideal solution model with four weighting methods is applied to identify high-risk flood areas. Finally, the results of the flood risk assessment are used as weights in a multi-objective site selection model, which is solved by a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm to determine the optimal shelter locations. The results show that: (1) In the 10, 50, and 200-years rainfall scenarios, flood diversion measures significantly reduce flood depth and inundated areas; however, the diversion effect is limited under the extreme “7·20” rainfall event. (2) High-risk flood areas are primarily concentrated in the highly urbanized northeast, and although flood diversion alleviates risk, the overall risk remains high under extreme rainfall events. (3) Under the “7·20” rainfall scenario after flood diversion, 13 optimal shelter locations are identified, with an average evacuation distance of 471.9 meters, covering 97.3% of the population in the study area. These findings provide scientific evidence for urban flood management.

papers.title: Time-periodic electroosmotic flow of non-Newtonian fluid through a polyelectrolyte-grafted circular microchannel
papers.abstract: The present research investigates the characteristics of flow dynamics and heat transfer of couple stress fluid through a circular microtube grafted with a polyelectrolyte layer. An alternating current electric field is applied to influence the fluid flow and heat transfer. A mathematical framework is established to describe the phenomenon of time-periodic alternating current electroosmotic flow by incorporating the Poisson–Boltzmann equations, couple stress fluid momentum equations, and energy equations for both polyelectrolyte and electrolyte layers. In the beginning, the Poisson–Boltzmann equation is solved analytically under the Debye–Hückel approximation to obtain the electric potential distribution. Subsequently, momentum equations of the couple stress fluid are then established for both the polyelectrolyte and electrolyte layers, and analytical solutions for these equations are obtained. Finally, the energy equation is discretized numerically using the finite difference scheme with Thomas algorithm. The primary results of this study indicate that velocity oscillation increases, but it is confined to the region near the interface of polyelectrolyte-electrolyte layers, while the amplitude of velocity oscillation decreases with higher oscillating Reynolds numbers. Temperature magnitude increases with the Debye–Hückel parameter, thickness of polyelectrolyte layer, couple stress parameters, and Brinkman number, while the drag parameter decreases it. Further, as the oscillating Reynolds number increases, the core region of the microtube experiences more frequent temperature oscillations, while the amplitude of the time-periodic temperature decreases. These findings provide deeper insights into electrokinetic transport phenomena, which hold potential for particle manipulation, enhancement techniques, biochip drug delivery, and biomedical engineering advancements.

papers.title: From aperitif to candy: Calcium-induced crust formation in vegan gummies through in situ rheology
papers.abstract: This study investigates the long-term mechanical stability of vegan polysaccharide-based candies using egg-box structures, analyzing how cross-links form and diffuse within such gels. We develop and validate a novel procedure to enhance the mechanical properties of vegan gummy candies, demonstrated using the commercial product Le Crodine®. The process involves immersing the candies in a calcium bath, triggering the egg-box mechanism, which forms a protective crust at the candy-bath interface. This crust shields the candy from mechanical stresses during packaging and transport while reducing stickiness for easier handling. We find that the crust, and thus the diffusion of the ions within the pectin matrix, undergoes two distinct transformations: (1) in the short term, calcium ions diffuse into the bulk, reinforcing the structure, and (2) in the long term, the cross-links redistribute, forming a homogeneous jelly with slightly enhanced moduli compared to the original product. The changes are quantified using linear viscoelastic shear measurements, and reaction dynamics are captured through in situ shear tests. Furthermore, we identify a novel diffusion-time superposition principle, relating the ion solution concentration in the pectin gel and its mechanical properties. To investigate the psycho-rheology, a two-bite texture profile analysis evaluates consumer experience, confirming improved texture and reduced stickiness. This work is significant for applications in polysaccharide-based candies using egg-box structures, such as alginates, and for understanding the diffusion and relaxation dynamics of egg-box cross-links.

papers.title: Influence of Nozzle Wettability and Surface Roughness on Liquid Jet Breakup Length
papers.abstract: The breakup of liquid jets is ubiquitous in a wide range of industrial processes, with the breakup length widely concerned as it dictates the performance of applications such as inkjet printing, fiber manufacture, and drug delivery. However, how the nozzle properties influence the breakup length of liquid jets remains elusive. Here, we study the impact of nozzle wettability and surface roughness on the breakup length of liquid jets, using an experimental platform with reduced background noise to minimize the effect of external disturbances. Results show that the wettability of the nozzle alone has minimal influence on the jet breakup length, despite notable distinctions existing in the menisci formed at the nozzle outlet with different contact angles. An increase in surface roughness of hydrophilic nozzles is found to increase the breakup length, while for hydrophobic nozzles, the increased surface roughness decreases the breakup length. This may be because the surface roughness decreases the initial disturbance by enhancing pinning effect on the meniscus on hydrophilic nozzles, while it increases the initial disturbance when meniscus vanishes on hydrophobic nozzles. Our findings reveal the roles of nozzle wettability and roughness on liquid jet breakup, and thus, provide guidance for the practical control of jet breakup length by nozzle design.

papers.title: A predictive model for overland flow velocity on vegetated slopes considering various environmental factors
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting the arithmetic mean velocity of overland flows on vegetated slopes is essential for developing hydraulic erosion models. However, there exists a significant challenge in predicting this velocity in various vegetation conditions. This study proposed a new predictive model based on the principle of resistance superposition, which accounted for a wide range of environmental factors—e.g., vegetation coverage, slope angle, and flow discharge. The model was validated against a comprehensive database with 4168 datasets established from published sources, showing 83.3% of the calculated R squared values in excess of 0.750. The model was also compared with the existing models, demonstrating superior applicability and reliability at various test conditions. After validation and comparison, parametric analysis was conducted to assess the effects of the environmental factors on the velocity. The results highlighted that the velocity decreased with increasing vegetation coverage until reaching a limit and the strong interactive effects of these environmental factors on the velocity. These findings provide valuable insights into how environmental factors influence flow velocity, offering a theoretical foundation for erosion control on vegetated slopes.

papers.title: Numerical simulation of the infiltration behavior of molten metal in a ceramic porous preform
papers.abstract: Investigating the infiltration mechanism of molten metal in ceramic particle porous preforms provides critical theoretical guidance for optimizing the casting infiltration process and improving the quality of castings. In this study, the microstructural model of the zirconia-toughened alumina ceramic porous preform was precisely reconstructed using high-resolution X-ray computed tomography. Based on the lattice Boltzmann method, the infiltration process of the high-chromium cast iron molten metal in the porous preform of ceramic particles was simulated at the pore scale. The effects of molten metal viscosity (0.00175–17.5 Pa·s), injection velocity (0.005–0.1 m/s), surface tension (0.072–5 N/m), contact angle (20–80°), and preform placement positions on the infiltration behavior of the molten metal in the preform were investigated. The results indicate that increased molten metal viscosity enhances flow front stability by mitigating pore heterogeneity effects, thereby achieving higher steady-state saturation. However, it also increases flow resistance, which reduces steady-state saturation when the driving pressure is insufficient. Increasing the injection velocity or reducing the surface tension significantly improves steady-state saturation. The steady-state saturation distribution diagram of capillary number (Ca) and viscosity ratio (M) yields the empirical relation defining the boundary between high and low saturation regions: LogCac − 0.93LogM = −6.79. Moreover, reducing the contact angle of the preform wall significantly enhances steady-state saturation. Furthermore, positioning the preform in the top or middle regions of the cavity improves steady-state saturation under low injection velocities.

papers.title: Pressure drop characteristics and model construction of the actual rough wellbore wall in gas drilling horizontal well
papers.abstract: Gas drilling is a clean and efficient technology that benefits the environment. While gas drilling in vertical wells has become well-established, the challenge lies in its application in horizontal wells. Special attention must be given to the pressure drop in the annulus during drilling, particularly the management of pressure drops under unbalanced conditions, which is vital for construction safety. However, current research has overlooked the influence of actual wellbore roughness on annular flow. This paper uses experimental and numerical simulation methods to study the frictional pressure drop in the annular space under actual rough wellbore conditions. The experimental results indicate that roughness is the main controlling factor for the pressure drop of annular friction, and there is also a significant interaction with other parameters. Numerical simulations show a significant difference in wall shear stress between the inner and outer walls of the annulus, and roughness causes the wall shear stress relationship between the inner and outer tubes to reverse. This article further establishes a relationship between the friction resistance coefficient through dimensional analysis and theoretical derivation and obtains a predictive model for the friction pressure drop under experimental parameters, which is of great significance for the management of annular pressure drop.

papers.title: Steam condensing flow in cascade turbine blades and nozzles using simple low dissipation upwind scheme
papers.abstract: In various engineering applications, the phase change from steam to water droplet during rapid expansion under supersonic flow conditions is inevitable. The occurrence of condensation waves due to the latent heat released during phase change and aerodynamic shocks reduces equipment performance. Given the complexities of two-phase flow, researchers have always been interested in developing an accurate numerical method that can be used in different flow regimes while reducing computation costs. This research has developed a two-dimensional code using the simple low-dissipation advection upstream splitting method (SLAU) and high-resolution simple low-dissipation advection upstream splitting method (HR-SLAU) in the complex geometry of the steam turbine blades and the convergent–divergent nozzles. The performance of these two schemes was examined using the Eulerian–Lagrangian model under different boundary conditions. The governing equations are investigated using the Eulerian model, which incorporates the SLAU and HR-SLAU schemes, and the equations for determining the wet flow parameters are solved by the Lagrangian approach to predict the liquid mass in the grid cell. Comparative to the experimental data, regarding the simplicity of these two schemes, and in the absence of any tuning flow-dependent variable, the determination of the position and intensity of shocks has been improved considerably, while the droplet radius prediction has been significantly enhanced. Notably, the HR-SLAU scheme, in which the dissipation component of the pressure flux according to a cell-interface orientation angle and flow characteristics is locally controlled by the dissipation coefficient for modeling two-phase flows, leads to fewer numerical errors.

papers.title: Comparative rheology and microstructure analysis of natural rubber latex with conventional and eco-friendly preservatives
papers.abstract: This study explores how three distinct preservation techniques affect the microstructure and rheological properties of natural rubber latex. Traditional ammoniated systems were compared against two emerging eco-friendly preservatives developed by AFLatex Technologies, which demonstrated enhanced latex properties reported in Ammonia-Free Latex Compositions, US Patent Application 63/267,167.2022. 2023. Rheological data were modeled using the Cross model to capture the non-linearity of viscosity and the Krieger–Dougherty (K&D) model to describe viscosity as a function of volume fraction. We also proposed an extended K&D model to better fit experimental observations. Additionally, Taylor–Couette flow simulation were performed to investigate shear-induced particle migration, providing insights into the dynamic behavior of particles under varied shear conditions. Our findings showed differences in critical volume fraction; the ammoniated system exhibited a critical volume fraction range of 0.6–0.7, while the ammonia-free systems had a lower range of 0.4–0.55. These values align closely with the predication from the Cross model, which suggests critical volume fraction of 0.4–0.5 for ammonia-free systems and above 0.6 for ammoniated systems. The extended and original K&D models corroborated these findings, with the ammonia-free systems typically reaching a critical volume fraction of 0.55 and the ammoniated systems approaching 0.7. Simulations under simplified assumptions revealed that shear-induced migration can maintain approximately 20% of the particles at a critical volume fraction of around 0.48, underscoring the complex interplay of particle dynamics and preservation technique in determining natural rubber latex material properties.

papers.title: Gap flow dynamics and air pollutant dispersion mechanism behind building clusters
papers.abstract: Multi-scale gaps within the urban building configuration intricate the wind flow dynamics surrounding the building clusters and hinder the understanding of pollutant removal mechanisms. Consequently, the impact of fluid dynamics caused by gap flow on air pollutant dispersion has not been fully revealed. This work examines such gap flow dynamics and the fundamental air pollutant dispersion mechanisms in three representative building cluster layouts via the large-eddy simulation and bi-directional extended proper orthogonal decomposition (EPOD) analysis framework. Results show that the accelerated jets generated by building gaps exhibit alternating low/high frequency sweeping motions, which interact with the recirculation vortices in the wake, leading to pronounced differences in air pollutant dispersion patterns. Bi-directional EPOD modes capture the turbulent transport effect of pollutant under the combined influence of jet and recirculation flows, as well as the relevant turbulent coherent structures across various scales. The fluctuation of jet flow dominates the turbulent structure and flow dynamics. A small gap size triggers a high-frequency jet fluctuation that undergoes harmonic swing in the crosswind direction, driving the dynamic pollutant transport behind the buildings. Additionally, the continuous harmonic oscillations in dispersion are found along the spanwise direction, favoring the removal of air pollutants.

papers.title: Explicit formulations of widely used wall models for large-eddy simulation
papers.abstract: Algebraic wall models for large-eddy simulations may suffer from robustness issues when applied in complex flow configurations. On the other hand, models based on ordinary differential equations (ODE-based models) are robust, but are slower to converge, computationally more expensive, and are harder to implement. The latter is exacerbated by the plethora of hardware back-ends a modern code is expected to support. Here, approximate explicit formulations for, arguably, the three most widely used wall models are provided: the equilibrium ODE model, Spalding's model, and Reichardt's model. Using these explicit versions of the models makes them trivial to implement and the computation of the stress unconditionally stable. The resulting expressions are compact, yet introduce at most a 1% relative error in the models' velocity profile for all physically realizable values of the von Karman constant and intercept of the logarithmic law. Furthermore, tuned approximations with at most 0.05% relative error are provided for two sets of logarithmic law parameters: modern values based on high-Reynolds-number data and classical ones used in the original formulation of the wall models. In addition to using explicit models directly, they can be utilized to provide an initial guess for the iterative methods used to solve the respective original counterparts. We demonstrate that this leads to increased robustness and, for the ODE model, to faster convergence. While our work covers three wall models, the provided approximation approach is expected to be applicable to any model based on a one-dimensional coupling of the linear and logarithmic laws of the wall.

papers.title: Generalization of the three-dimensional energy loss principle with application to surface wave interaction with a submerged poroelastic plate
papers.abstract: The wave energy dissipation due to the presence of a poroelastic plate in three dimensions engaging both scattering and radiation is obtained by employing Green's second identity, which involves the Kochin function. From this, a general energy balance relation is established. This derivation methodology of energy dissipation is not limited to circular structures and may be used on any plate with a smooth boundary. The hypersingular integral equation technique is adopted to solve the associated boundary value problem along with the modal analysis for structural vibrations. The energy dissipation due to the porosity of the submerged structure is depicted graphically for various physical parameters. Apart from this, other hydrodynamic quantities, such as vertical exciting force, damping coefficient, and added mass, are also computed for different physical factors. The behavior of these physical quantities in relation to the parameters under consideration is also visualized through a graphical representation of the quantities. In order to validate the current study, two distinct methods are used: one by establishing energy conservation relations and the other by recovering existing results from the published articles.

papers.title: A numerical study on suppressing the logarithmic layer energy structures by a near-wall control approach to obtain drag reduction at relatively high Reynolds numbers
papers.abstract: The energy consumption of an aircraft in flight is mainly due to the aerodynamic drag force. The viscous drag, which is directly related to the friction drag, is responsible for almost half of the total drag. At high Reynolds numbers, the energy-containing structures in the logarithmic region (log-layer) are highly effective in enhancing near-wall turbulence. In the present study, a near-wall control approach is applied and explored to a turbulent channel flow. The control approach suppresses the positive wall-normal fluctuations near the wall to manipulate the interplay between the log-layer and near-wall turbulent structures. Amplitude modulation analysis is employed to relate the drag reduction with the absence of energy structures in the logarithmic layer for the control applied case. A channel flow at a frictional Reynolds number of Reτ=800 is used and the results are compared for the controlled and uncontrolled cases. The results show a significant drag reduction related to the absence of large-scale (LS) motions in the log-layer region.

papers.title: Backward injection of liquid jets in crossflow
papers.abstract: The effect of the liquid jet injection opposite the airflow direction and its injection angle was studied experimentally and theoretically. Various flow parameters, including trajectory, breakup point and its length, penetration depth, distribution of droplet size, their orientation and aspect ratio, mean diameter of drops, stability of liquid jet column, and oscillation wavelength in different conditions, were measured. Different breakup regimes, column, arc, bag, and multimode, were identified. The gas Weber number, momentum ratio, and backward injection angle were recognized as influencing parameters. Backward injection and reducing its angle by strengthening the effective aerodynamics force and the shear forces created by the interaction of the liquid with the airflow causes more bending of the jet path, faster breakup, smaller droplets, and the resulting improvement of the atomization process. For stability perusal, linear analysis and the theory of the viscous potential flow were utilized. Based on that, a theoretical model was developed for the influence of the backward injection and its angle on the axial and azimuthal wave growth rate of a viscous liquid jet issued into a viscous gaseous crossflow. The interaction of aerodynamic forces, surface tension, viscosity, and momentum makes Rayleigh–Plateau (capillary), Rayleigh–Taylor, Kelvin–Helmholtz, and azimuthal instabilities in the liquid column. Reducing the backward injection angle increases the growth rate and decreases the wavelength of both axial and azimuthal waves. It strengthens K–H waves. The effect of different parameters such as gas and liquid Weber numbers, Ohnesorge number, density ratio, and viscosity ratio was investigated at different injection angles.

papers.title: Helical and chaotic heat exchangers: Flow regimes and efficiency
papers.abstract: Helical coiled tubes are renowned for enhancing mixing and promoting heat transfer efficiency, making them highly valuable in various heat transfer applications. Nevertheless, the stabilizing effects of secondary flows in helical coils extends the laminar regime to higher Reynolds numbers than in straight pipes. This persistence of laminar flow state reduces longitudinal mixing and consequently limits the rates of convective heat transfer. This research introduces a novel chaotic heat exchanger designed to induce chaotic advection through an alternating Dean flow. To take advantage of a coiled system while improving its performance within the laminar regime of applications. The primary goal is to demonstrate the enhanced capabilities of our chaotic heat exchanger by comparing its performance against traditional helical coils. Utilizing Direct Numerical Simulation, our study explores the flow and heat transfer characteristics within both designs. Results reveal that the new configuration significantly improves hydro-thermal performance and demonstrates great potential across a Reynolds number range of 800–8600. Additionally, the study provides an in-depth analysis of the flow structures and examines the development of the thermal boundary layer, while highlighting the role of chaotic advection in enhancing mixing efficiency.

papers.title: Numerical investigation on the impact of barrel gap and length on the internal flow field of electromagnetic launch
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic launch utilizes electromagnetic force to accelerate projectiles in the barrel. The high-speed projectile induces complex flows dominated by choking in the barrel, which causes a sharp increase in the air pressure and temperature, deteriorates the working environment, and affects the barrel's service life. The three-dimensional numerical model adopted by the dynamic mesh method is established, and the flow field in the barrel is calculated. Moreover, the influence of the gap and length of the barrel is discussed and analyzed. The research results indicate that the flow is choking during the projectile's acceleration, and precursor and tail shock waves are generated in the front of and behind the projectile, respectively, leading to impacts with pressure exceeding 8 MPa and temperature exceeding 3500 K to the inner walls of the barrel. The pressure at the projectile head, aerodynamic drag, and the shock stand-off distance of the precursor shock consistently rise, whereas the tail pressure initially decreases before increasing. As the gap in the barrel expands, the precursor shock diminishes in strength while the tail shock intensifies. When the speed is the same, an increase in barrel length leads to a greater shock stand-off distance of the precursor shock wave and a longer propagation distance of the tail shock wave, while the pressures at both the head and tail, along with aerodynamic drag, stay the same. These results provide important information for designing barrels, protecting components, and assessing launch efficiency.

papers.title: Particle size effects in multiphase Rayleigh–Taylor instability
papers.abstract: The Rayleigh–Taylor instability (RTI) is a fundamental fluid dynamic phenomenon that occurs when a denser fluid pushes against a lighter one under the influence of gravity, leading to complex interfacial instabilities. A similar phenomenon occurs when describing multiphase regions, where one fluid may be laden with a heavy particle phase that is accelerated into a lighter fluid. The rate of coupling between particles and carrier fluid, equilibration time, is finite and the particles can slip through the carrier fluid, altering the growth and evolution of the RTI. A multiphase RTI is studied for various particle equilibration times, using the Euler–Lagrange simulations. The dynamics of the particle and carrier phases are studied, and the growth rate of the multiphase interface is tracked and compared to models for the RTI for both the linear and nonlinear phases. Larger particles, with a long equilibration time, show strong decoupling effects, leading to a reduced vorticity deposition and amplitude growth length. In contrast, smaller particles equilibrate rapidly with the gas, allowing amplitude growth similar to an RTI. At intermediate particle sizes, we find a higher growth rate, in excess of the RTI, due to a concentration of the particle phase, leading to higher localized mixture densities. These findings emphasize the critical role of particle size in multiphase RTI.

papers.title: Revealing the evolution of flow structure and pressure fluctuations in a multiphase pump under varying gas phase conditions
papers.abstract: Multiphase pumps are vital for extracting oil and gas from deep-sea environments and transporting blended media in chemical processes. The gas phase significantly alters these pumps' flow structure and pressure fluctuations. Our study reveals that gas injection boosts axial and circumferential velocities, disrupts velocity matching between the impeller and diffuser, and leads to the backflow structure and pump surge. Further, the flow in the vaneless region is divided into six regions according to the influence of the mainstream, wake jet, clearance, and end wall, and summarizes four-speed triangle transition modes (VSFTM) in the vaneless region. The VSFTMs in the mainstream and end wall areas worsen flow. Moreover, the turbulent kinetic energy and pressure pulsation in these regions are also significantly enhanced. The VSFTM in the wake and gap zones helps with speed matching but reduces water head. Analysis of pressure fluctuation in the vaneless region shows that the standard deviation and the relative amplitude coefficient of pressure pulsation rise with inlet gas volume fraction (IGVF). A 10% IGVF increase results in a surge of 1.4–1.6 times in the peak relative amplitude coefficient. These findings advance our understanding of the gas phase effect and flow structure in multiphase pumps.

papers.title: Lattice Boltzmann simulation reveals supercritical bifurcation in flow mode transitions of power-law fluids in the four-roll mill
papers.abstract: The four-roll mill has been traditionally viewed as a device generating simple extensional flow with a central stagnation point. However, our systematic investigation using a two-relaxation-time regularized lattice Boltzmann (TRT-RLB) model reveals two previously unreported supercritical bifurcation modes: a quadrifoliate vortex mode featuring four symmetrical counter-rotating vortices, and a dumbbell-shaped quad-vortex mode where vortices detach from but remain symmetric about the stagnation point. The numerical framework, representing the first successful extension of TRT-RLB method to power-law fluid dynamics, enables comprehensive mapping of flow characteristics across Reynolds numbers (1≤Re≤50), power-law indices (0.7≤n≤1.3), and geometric configurations. We found that the transition from quadrifoliate vortex mode exhibits distinct pathways depending on the power-law index: at relatively small n, the flow undergoes a direct supercritical bifurcation to simple extensional flow, as the higher viscosity in the central region suppresses curvature formation at the edge of vortices; while at relatively large n, it evolves through an intermediate dumbbell-shaped state, because the lower viscosity in the central region allows smaller vortices to be flattened and separated by incoming flows. Further analysis reveals that the seemingly anomalous phenomenon of vortex generation at high Re, where vortices diminish in size or disappear as Re increases, is fundamentally attributed to the symmetrical geometric structure of the viscous-force-dominated region. Among geometric configurations, the roller radius r emerges as the dominant factor controlling bifurcation points and vortex dimensions, whereas the roller-container gap δ exerts minimal influence on flow regimes.

papers.title: Long wave energy reflection induced between a submerged plate and a viscoelastic mud: Determination of wave damping
papers.abstract: In this work, the long wave–submerged plate–viscoelastic fluid interaction is analyzed. The decay of the elevation of the free surface is determined through the damping, reflection, and transmission coefficients. The system is further divided into two layers: the first is a domain composed of water, further divided into four regions for the submerged plate presence, and the second includes a viscoelastic fluid that obeys a Maxwell rheological model. The hydrodynamics of the water is modeled by adopting the assumption of a potential flow. The viscoelastic mud motion is determined using Cauchy's equations. The damping coefficient is obtained by applying the kinematic boundary condition at the water–mud interface. The horizontal patching boundary conditions for the equality of pressure and mass flux between the different regions are fundamental in determining the reflection and transmission coefficients. The viscoelastic effects are identified to induce an increase in the magnitude of the free surface elevation and, consequently, the reflection coefficient. The maximum damping coefficient is identified to occur when the thickness of the mud is 20% of the total depth of the water. The reflection coefficient increases with increments of the damping coefficient, and when the plate's submergence depth is 25% of the water depth, large values of the reflection coefficient are obtained. The present solution is validated with a classical analytical solution reported in the specialized literature. The present solution can serve, as a first approximation, to identify the effects of the wave–plate–mud interaction on the reflection coefficient.

papers.title: Experimental study on the migration of finite-size spherical particles in rectangular channels in Newtonian and viscoelastic fluids
papers.abstract: We experimentally investigate the finite-size spherical particle migration in micro-rectangular channels in a Newtonian fluid (22 wt. % glycerol aqueous solution) and a viscoelastic fluid (8 wt. % polyvinylpyrrolidone aqueous solution) at various particle size to hydraulic diameter ratios a/Dh and channel aspect ratios H/W. Experiments are performed in rectangular channels at low Reynolds numbers (Re) and Weissenberg numbers (Wi) ranging from 0.09 to 1.53. Particles are almost mono-disperse neutrally buoyant polystyrene spheres with diameters of 20 μm, 30 μm, and 50 μm. The channel aspect ratios are 1, ½, and 1/3. The results show that the migration distributions differ significantly between the two fluids at the same mass flow rate. In square duct flow, we find that Re and a/Dh are key parameters governing particle migration in dilute suspensions. With increasing Re, both in Newtonian and in viscoelastic fluids, we observe a transition from a disordered to an ordered distribution in square duct flow. Particles in Newtonian fluid accumulate at the off-center long midline, while in the viscoelastic fluid, small and large particles accumulate at five points (four corners and the center) and at the center point of the duct, respectively. As the H/W decreases in rectangular channel flow, the focusing position of the particles shifts from four planes near the walls to two planes parallel to the longer walls and eventually to one center-plane in the Newtonian fluid. In the viscoelastic fluid, the focusing position transitions from five points to the center and then to the mid-plane-parallel to longer walls.

papers.title: The fractal analysis of the forced imbibition process in roughened porous media with slip length
papers.abstract: Following the large-scale reconstruction of shale reservoirs, the microscale mechanisms and fluid distribution characteristics of multiscale media imbibition under pressure remain unclear. This ambiguity hinders the development of key technologies necessary for optimizing the design and implementation of volumetric fracturing in continental shale oil reservoirs. This study develops a fractal-based analytical model to quantify forced imbibition (FI) dynamics in shale reservoirs, integrating nanoscale slip effects and wall roughness. By coupling the porous medium layer method with fractal theory, we derive the flow resistance of rough capillaries and upscale it to heterogeneous porous media. The model explicitly links slip length to wettability and roughness parameters, revealing that: (1) Slip effects enhance FI capacity by up to 40% in hydrophobic organic nanopores, but only 10% in hydrophilic inorganic pores. (2) Wall roughness reduces FI rates by 15–50%, depending on pore size and roughness geometry, with roughness radius exhibiting triple stronger impact than height. (3) Fractal dimension dominates FI sensitivity, contributing 45% to rate variability, followed by wettability. These findings provide a predictive framework for optimizing fracturing fluid recovery in mixed-wettability shale reservoirs, emphasizing the interplay between nanoscale slip, roughness, and fractal heterogeneity.

papers.title: Thermodynamic performance analysis and simulation of a new type of compression CO2 energy storage system in salt caverns
papers.abstract: In recent years, renewable energy sources like wind and photovoltaic power have grown rapidly due to their sustainability. However, their random, intermittent nature often leads to energy wastage. Hence, a new energy storage system for storing compressed CO2 through salt caverns was constructed in this study. The system is based on phase transitions and thermodynamic processes in fluid physics, utilizing gas–liquid phase conversion and two-state synergistic energy storage technology. In order to test the performance of the new system, thermodynamic theoretical models and simulation models of the new energy storage system were established. The thermodynamic theoretical model investigates the thermodynamic performance and economic index of the new system. The thermodynamic parameters of the new system at each cyclic state point were calculated by embedding the partial results obtained from the theoretical model in MATLAB. The results show that the theoretical model calculates a system with an energy storage efficiency of 66.8% and an average energy cost of only 9.03 US cents/kW h. Combined with the results of MATLAB calculations, a thermodynamic simulation model of the new system was developed using Ebsilon to analyze the changes in enthalpy, entropy, temperature, and pressure throughout the energy storage process. The results show that the operating efficiency of the simulation model is 68.7%, and the deviation from the MATLAB calculation is less than 2%, which realizes the organic combination of the theoretical model and the simulation model, and not only shows the superiority of the performance of the new system, but also confirms the rationality of the new system. This work highlights the role of fluid physics in the design and optimization of energy storage systems, providing valuable insights for integrated energy system development and new energy storage applications.

papers.title: The Gibbsian permeability model of porous media
papers.abstract: A first-principles equation quantifying the permeability of fluid flow through a porous medium is developed. Existing treatments, like the popular Kozeny–Carman permeability equation, are phenomenological models, which are based on scaling arguments of one-dimensional flow. This paper shows that basic multi-dimensional flow effects make the Kozeny–Carman permeability inaccurate. The current model is based on second law considerations following Gibbs' thermodynamic equation and is generally valid for multi-dimensional porous media geometries and flows. Examples are used to illustrate the accuracy and relative simplicity of the new Gibbs permeability model against the Kozeny–Carman approach. In practice, the new model allows the permeability to be calculated with a single experimental trial compared to the multiple trials needed with D'Arcy's original method and that are required to calibrate the Kozeny–Carman model.

papers.title: Experimental study on uniform momentum zones variations induced by spanwise vortex migration in the turbulent boundary layer
papers.abstract: The migration trajectories of spanwise vortex structures were investigated to reveal their variation patterns and distribution characteristics, explicitly focusing on their correlation with the characteristic quantities of uniform momentum zones (UMZs). This approach is crucial for deepening the understanding of wall turbulence. Using a three-camera array particle image velocimetry experiment, a dataset of the stream-normal flow field was acquired over a region extending 8δ. The space-time cross correlation algorithm was then employed to extract the migration trajectories of spanwise vortex structures. The slope probability density function was applied to classify these migration trajectories, revealing the spatiotemporal topologies of vortices with different migration tendencies. The analysis also explored the relationship between instantaneous changes in the number of UMZs and vortex migration patterns. The results demonstrate that vortex structure migration can be categorized into downward, upward, and straight-line. As the initial height increases, the trajectory distribution becomes more divergent, while higher Reynolds numbers cause the trajectories to converge and exhibit a preference for upward migration. Different migration modes exhibit significant distinctions: downward migration, influenced by the sweep of the upstream vortex head, resulted in reduced vortex size; upward migration, driven by the ejection between the downstream vortex legs, promoted growth and full development of the vortex; straight-line migration reflects stable and steady evolution. The migration of vortex structures directly affects the number of UMZs by altering the heights of the turbulent/non-turbulent interface and UMZ interfaces. Downward migration increases the number of UMZs, while upward migration decreases it. Structural changes in vortex packets caused by migration are the fundamental drivers of variations in the number of UMZs.

papers.title: Hydromagnetic effects on couple stress fluid flow through a porous sphere embedded in another porous medium
papers.abstract: This work concerns the axisymmetric steady flow of an incompressible couple stress fluid through a porous sphere implanted in another unbounded porous medium. The governing equations of motion for couple stress fluid flow through porous media describe the flow. A uniform magnetic field is applied in the direction perpendicular to the flow. The stream function solution for the flow is obtained analytically. Appropriate boundary conditions are used on the surface of the porous sphere, and uniform velocity conditions at infinity are used. Expressions for flow velocities (normal and tangential), vorticities, couple stresses, tangential stresses, and normal stresses of the fluid are obtained. The variations of couple stress parameter, permeability parameter, and Hartman number on flow velocities, streamlines, and drag coefficient are plotted and discussed.

papers.title: Understanding the primary breakup characteristics of impingement of a liquid jet on an opposing gas jet
papers.abstract: We present the results of a computational investigation of the primary breakup characteristics of the impingement of a liquid jet on an opposing gas jet. The numerical simulation of the three-dimensional configuration was performed by employing the volume-of-fluid method with adaptive mesh refinement to visualize the rupture of the liquid sheet, flow patterns, and ligament formation from the liquid sheet. The results presented are in agreement with our numerical results and existing experiments. We observed the primary breakup and atomization characteristics of a liquid jet impinging on the gas jet for dimensionless numbers such as the momentum ratio between the gas and liquid jets (X), the Reynolds number (Re), and the Weber number (We). In addition, this study classified the Weber number into low, intermediate, and high to highlight the distinct breakup regimes. We identified the breakup length and number of ligaments for a range of X, We, and Re. We also discuss the effect of the Rayleigh–Taylor (RT), Kelvin–Helmholtz (KH), and Plateau–Rayleigh (PR) or capillary instability mechanisms. A regime in the We−Re plane is shown to highlight the transition from the turbulent parachute to the turbulent sheet regime for different values of X. These results lay the foundation for optimizing spray systems in several industrial applications that rely on atomization.

papers.title: Droplet impact dynamics on the anisotropic microtextured surface under different wettability
papers.abstract: The degree of surface anisotropy, as a significant factor characterizing the complexity of surface morphology, has a notable impact on the morphological evolution and kinetic parameters of droplets in different directions. The present results show that the microtextured surface with stronger surface anisotropy, which is quantified by Str (texture aspect ratio of the surface), has a more drastic effect on droplet deformation and flow path alteration, and the droplet is more likely to fall into the microgroove to form a prompt splash along the transverse direction. In the longitudinal direction, the formation of coronal liquid film can be observed due to the vertical momentum across the microstructure. In addition, the wettability difference caused by anisotropy on the hydrophilic surface has a limited effect on droplet splashing, while the anisotropy of the surface texture distribution has a more significant effect on the droplet splashing behavior. Meanwhile, the synergistic effect of hydrophobicity and anisotropy changes the mass and momentum distribution of the droplet, resulting in decreased contact time of the droplet hitting the solid surfaces. The results of this work are expected to provide valuable insights into controlling droplet spatter in industrial applications.

papers.title: Lattice Boltzmann modeling of droplet impact on moving superhydrophobic wall
papers.abstract: In this paper, the non-orthogonal multiple-relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann method incorporating contact angle hysteresis is used to study droplets impacting moving superhydrophobic walls. It is found that the contact time depends on wall velocity and is independent of the Weber number, while the horizontal displacement and maximum spreading length are controlled by both the Weber number and wall velocity. Moreover, based on the evolution of kinetic energy, the contact time is divided into the spreading time, retraction time, and separation time. The spreading time and retraction time are independent of wall velocity, while the separation time depends upon wall velocity. In addition, the tangential force depends on both wall velocity and Weber number, while the normal force is independent of wall velocity but depends on the Weber number. These findings offer a deep insight into the dynamic characteristics of droplet impact on superhydrophobic walls.

papers.title: Can flocking aid the path planning of microswimmers in turbulent flows?
papers.abstract: We show that the flocking of microswimmers in a turbulent flow can enhance the efficacy of reinforcement-learning-based path planning of microswimmers in turbulent flows. In particular, we develop a machine-learning strategy that incorporates Vicsek-model-type flocking in microswimmer assemblies in a statistically homogeneous and isotropic turbulent flow in two dimensions. We build on the adversarial-reinforcement-learning of Alageshan et al. [“Machine learning strategies for path-planning microswimmers in turbulent flows,” Phys. Rev. E 101, 043110 (2020)] for non-interacting microswimmers in turbulent flows. Such microswimmers aim to move optimally from an initial position to a target. We demonstrate that our flocking-aided version of the adversarial-reinforcement-learning strategy of Ref. 1 can be superior to earlier microswimmer path-planning strategies.

papers.title: Characteristics of overburden fracture conductivity in the shallow buried close coal seam group and its effect on low-oxygen phenomena
papers.abstract: The distribution and conduction properties of overburden fractures following coal extraction beneath a shallowly buried, proximate coal seam group are extremely complex. These fractures are a primary source of air leakage within the mining zone and contribute to oxygen-deficient conditions at the working face. Therefore, in this study, physical similarity simulation experiments are used to quantitatively analyze the distribution and conductivity characteristics of the overburden fractures during the mining of shallow buried close coal seam group. The results show that with the increase in mining distance, the high level area mainly forms breakage fracture, and its fracture aperture increases significantly, and the penetration is enhanced. The low level area gradually generates delamination fracture and connects with the high level area fracture, constituting a three-dimensional gas leakage channel between the working face, the upper mining area, and the ground surface. Moreover, the changes in the frequency, angle, and aperture of the fractures have a significant effect on the transportation and circulation of low-oxygen gas; the frequency of fractures gradually increases, the density gradually increases, the angle range gradually becomes bigger, and the aperture gradually becomes bigger, which provides a “hotbed” for the enriched storage and transportation and circulation of low-oxygen gas. This study provides a scientific basis for the prevention and control of low-oxygen and safe production in coal mines and helps to protect the life safety of coal miners.

papers.title: Extending the logarithmic velocity profile in turbulent channel flow
papers.abstract: The logarithmic velocity profile is a key feature of wall-bounded turbulence, typically observed in a narrow near-wall region. In this study, we revisit the mixing length (lm) foundation of the logarithmic law in turbulent channel flow and propose a method to extend the logarithmic velocity profile. The derivation follows a bottom-up approach without relying on the uniform shear stress assumption or Prandtl's linear mixing length model. We demonstrate that the logarithmic velocity profile emerges where Prandtl's parabolic model for lm aligns with its true value. Extending this overlap region for lm correspondingly broadens the logarithmic profile. Based on this principle, we propose an enhanced mixing length model with a wider overlap region compared to the existing models. When applied to conventional velocity transformations—such as the IC-type for incompressible flow, and the Van Driest (VD-type) and Trettel and Larsson (TL-type) transformations for compressible flow—enhanced versions of these transformations are obtained accordingly. The enhanced model and corresponding transformations are evaluated using a series of direct numerical simulation data, covering a wide range of Mach and Reynolds numbers. In both incompressible and compressible turbulent channel flows, the predicted mixing length closely follows the theoretical distribution throughout the outer layer. The extended logarithmic profile reaches the channel center, with the corresponding diagnostic function deviating by no more than ±7% from the reference value. Compared to conventional logarithmic and defect laws, the extended logarithmic profile provides a more consistent description of velocity distribution across the outer layer.

papers.title: Suppression of flow separation in a scramjet inlet using Görtler vortices
papers.abstract: This study addresses the issue of boundary layer separation in the inlet of a scramjet engine by employing a strategy centered on Görtler vortices. Numerical simulations are conducted to explore the separation suppression through the use of these vortices at Mach 8. The inlets comprise two-stage compression ramps and a cowl. The turning angle between two ramps is closely related to the occurrence of Görtler vortices and is set at 10° and 15°, with variations in the cowl position. Our findings indicate that the occurrence of Görtler vortices follows a natural transition, and their intensity is influenced by the position of the cowl. The Görtler number, which characterizes Görtler instability, is determined by evaluating the curvature and momentum thickness, both of which are tied to an unsteady separation bubble. The Görtler vortices are intensified by the downstream cowl. A comparison of the results to the two-dimensional cases without vortices reveals that the separation near the throat entrance is effectively suppressed owing to momentum transport by the Görtler vortices. Consequently, the mass flow rate ratio of the duct to the inflow increases significantly, exceeding 0.9. Therefore, the use of Görtler vortices proves to be a valuable method for suppressing critical separation and ensuring the mass flow rate in the inlet duct.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of a high rotating isotopic flow using laminar and turbulent models
papers.abstract: The effective separation of the desired isotope of the elements that are necessary for nuclear applications is a major challenge. Gas centrifuge technology is the most efficient method for isotopic separation, which takes advantage of highly compressible flow. This paper uses ANSYS Fluent software to simulate the behavior of gas in a centrifugal machine with an axially symmetric model in steady state of a high rotating experimental facility. Integrated Computer Engineering and Manufacturing software is used to grid the rotor's geometry in two-dimensional coordinates. The k–ε Re-normalization group model has been used to examine the effects of turbulence on the gas flow inside the rotor because of its acceptable accuracy in a variety of turbulent flows. Following the grid independence study, the simulation's first section examined the changes in mass flux, temperature, and velocity along the radial layers in laminar and turbulent flows. The impact of operating parameters, such as feed flow rate, waste scoop swirl velocity, and temperature differential between the caps, has been assessed in the following to determine the optimal separation power and overall separation factor in both laminar and turbulent flow regimes. The results show that the assumption of laminar flow produces a relative error of 22.7% and turbulent flow produces a relative error of 6.3% in comparison with the measured separation power of the high rotating experimental facility.

papers.title: Influences of floating ice on the water entry process of slender body on the cavity evolution and hydrodynamic characteristics
papers.abstract: The Arctic region is rich in energy resources and plays a critical role in global shipping. Consequently, countries worldwide prioritize the formulation of strategies for this region. Research on water entry has predominantly focused on water-only scenarios, with relatively little attention given to the more complex conditions involving floating ice. This study combines numerical simulations and experiments to investigate the ice-breaking water entry of slender bodies. The findings suggest that, during the water entry of a slender body, floating ice affects the diffusion and contraction of the liquid at the gas–liquid interface, which in turn influences air inflow and cavitation development. This alters the formation and evolution of the cavity. By inducing variations in cavity shape and altering cavity collapse time, the hydrodynamic and ballistic properties of the projectile are ultimately affected.

papers.title: Progress in the research on non-equilibrium condensation of the compressor in the supercritical CO2 closed Brayton cycle system
papers.abstract: The supercritical carbon dioxide (S-CO2) closed Brayton cycle holds significant promise for revolutionizing the future of efficient and comprehensive new energy utilization. However, the compressor operation in this cycle is characterized by rapid pressurization, which induces substantial fluctuations in temperature and pressure, potentially triggering non-equilibrium condensation of S-CO2. This phenomenon disrupts the flow field within the compressor, thereby decreasing the overall performance of the cycle system. Therefore, exploring this mechanism is of great significance for improving the performance of the cycle system. This work summarizes various improvement types of S-CO2 closed Brayton systems and engineering applications across various fields. Subsequently, it reviews the development of non-equilibrium condensation theories within S-CO2 compressors, focusing on the nucleation and growth models. In addition, the current research status of condensation characteristics of S-CO2 under high-speed and high-pressure conditions is summarized, based on convergent-divergent nozzle experiments and simulations.
