papers.title: Electrokinetic instabilities in Boger fluid flows with conductivity gradients
papers.abstract: Electrokinetic instabilities (EKIs) occur when a sufficiently large direct current electric field interacts with a fluid flow with conductivity gradients. While EKIs in Newtonian fluids have been extensively studied for microfluidic applications such as micromixing and sample stacking, the impact of fluid rheology has not been thoroughly explored. This work reports an experimental study on how fluid elasticity affects EKI in hyaluronic acid (HA) solutions that are essentially Boger fluids under experimental conditions. It is found that increasing HA concentration (i.e., more viscoelastic) raises the threshold electric field for the onset of EKI, leading to a higher critical electric Rayleigh number. This observation indicates the suppression effect of fluid elasticity on EKI, which validates a recent numerical prediction based on the Oldroyd-B model [Sasmal, “Fluid viscoelasticity suppresses chaotic convection and mixing due to electrokinetic instability,” Phys. Fluids 34, 082011 (2022)]. Increasing the fluid elasticity also weakens the magnitude of EKI waves but has an insignificant influence on the wave speed and frequency, in contrast to the increasing electroosmotic velocity in higher-concentration HA solutions.

papers.title: Research on fracture propagation patterns and stress field evolution during integrated fracturing of platform wells
papers.abstract: To address the complexities of stress field dynamics and fracture propagation mechanisms during multi-well platform fracturing in unconventional reservoirs, this study establishes a three-dimensional (3D) geomechanical and multi-physical field coupling model under an integrated geoengineering framework. The model elucidates stress interference mechanisms and fracture network formation patterns under multi-well coordinated fracturing. A high-resolution 3D geological model, constructed using the Petrel platform, was employed to simulate the zipper fracturing process of 19 horizontal wells across three platforms (Nos. 61, 62, and 63) in the Jimusar shale oil reservoir. By integrating the boundary element method with fracture mechanics theory, the research quantifies the effects of legacy well-fracturing and ongoing production on in situ stress reorientation (maximum deflection angle: 75°) and fracture propagation in new wells. Results demonstrate that pore pressure depletion and stress direction deflection significantly alter fracture trajectories in new wells, reducing fracture network connectivity and leading to a 19.92% decline in cumulative oil production for new wells adjacent to legacy wells. Orthogonal optimization experiments identified displacement rate (17 m3/min) and cluster density per stage (7 clusters) as critical parameters for productivity enhancement. The optimized solution (A3B3C1D2E4) achieved a 9.7% increase in 6-year cumulative oil production compared to the baseline. Leveraging four-dimensional (4D) geomechanical inversion and intelligent parameter optimization, this work provides a theoretical foundation and operational strategies for multi-platform collaborative fracturing, advancing the efficient development of complex unconventional reservoirs.

papers.title: Vibration and wettability effects on droplet impaction and penetration in a mesh
papers.abstract: A numerical study is conducted to investigate droplet impaction on vibrating mesh surfaces using a multiphase Allen–Cahn lattice Boltzmann method. Three mesh pore sizes (115, 150, and 190 μm) are considered, along with variations in surface wettability (contact angles of 55°, 90°, and 120°), Weber number (336, 672, and 1344), and vibration phase angle (80°, 171°, 260°, and 351°). Results reveal that in the non-vibrating case, smaller pores (115 μm) induce extensive spreading on the upper mesh surface but generate fine droplets underneath; larger pores allow liquid ligaments to form before eventually detaching. For Weber numbers above 336, stronger inertial forces initially accelerate penetration through the pores, although final liquid volumes below the mesh become comparable across different Weber values. Vibration significantly alters droplet dynamics: at a 171° phase angle, where the mesh initially moves upward against the droplet, up to 25% more liquid volume transfers below the mesh compared to the non-vibrating case, driven by the combined effects of inertia and mesh motion. Conversely, at 351°, the mesh initially moves with the droplet, reducing early penetration but allowing rapid fluid passage once the mesh reverses direction. Wettability mainly affects droplet behavior after most inertia dissipates: hydrophobic surfaces (120°) promote droplet detachment from the mesh, while hydrophilic ones (55°) foster spreading. These findings offer valuable insights for optimizing industrial processes requiring droplet control on vibrating meshes.

papers.title: Aerodynamics of airfoils in free-surface effect by numerical simulations and regression analysis
papers.abstract: The free-surface effect (FSE) of airfoils is important for wing-in-ground (WIG) vehicles. At low angles of attack (AOAs, α), the lift of the airfoil decreases significantly as the height from the free-surface (h) decreases, called the “negative FSE” phenomenon. This phenomenon needs to be avoided for WIG vehicles, but related mechanisms are limited research. In this paper, the aerodynamic characteristics of the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) airfoils in proximity to the free-surface are simulated using the computational fluid dynamics method. Results show that at low AOAs, the direction of the induced velocity (vi) near the lower surface of the airfoil is consistent with that of the incoming flow. As h decreases, vi increases, resulting in a decrease in the pressure on the lower surface and ultimately leading to the negative FSE. Moreover, the phenomenon is related to the camber of the airfoil. The larger the camber, the smaller the range of AOAs in which negative FSE occurs. For the NACA0012 airfoil, negative FSE occurs when α< 6°, while for the NACA4412 airfoil, this range is α< 2°.

papers.title: A more cost-effective method for calculating two-phase equilibrium: Constrained non-equidistant gray prediction evolution algorithm
papers.abstract: Many existing methods, including traditional direct Newton and indirect thermodynamic methods, as well as new methods based on heuristic optimization algorithms, can provide satisfactory solutions for phase equilibrium calculation problems under specified volume, temperature, and moles (NVT-flash). Nevertheless, traditional methods suffer from initial sensitivity issues and reliance on gradient information of derivatives, and the existing heuristic methods demand large computational overhead. Thus, minimizing computational overhead without compromising accuracy and reliability is essential. Based on the strongly global search capability of gray prediction evolution algorithm, this study proposes a simple constrained non-equidistant gray prediction evolution algorithm (CNeGPE) to solve the NVT-flash problem. The total Helmholtz free energy is used as the objective function, with the molar vector and phase volume as decision variables. Boundary and inequality constraints are handled separately using direct search and feasibility-based resampling methods. High competitiveness of the proposed CNeGPE is demonstrated by comparing its performance with state-of-the-art similar algorithms in computational overhead, stability, and convergence. CNeGPE provides an efficient, accurate, and computationally cost-effective solution for phase equilibrium calculations, capable of advancing the optimization and control of complex thermodynamic calculation problems.

papers.title: Effect of inclination tendency of the channel on the pressure power and energy conversion for regenerative flow pumps
papers.abstract: To quantitatively measure the effect of the channel inclination on the pressure power and energy transport dynamics inside the regenerative flow pump, this paper conducts numerical simulation of three models with different inclination coefficients Ic (−0.25, 0, 0.25) to investigate the exchange flow between the rotating impeller and stationary channel. The results show that, the total pressure power (St) in the impeller is linearly increased along the impeller's rotating direction, while some fluctuations existed in the channel due to the unstable mass exchange. The static pressure power (Ss), rather than the dynamic pressure power (Sd), occupies more in St to increase the pressure potential energy of the fluids. Regardless of the model, both the impeller and the channel's static pressure power account for over 60% of the total power. As the Ic increases, both the St and Sd decrease, and the model with outward inclination presents excellent growth of pressure power. Furthermore, energy transport analysis reveals that pressure propulsion work (PPW) is the dominant contributor to the rate of change of kinetic energy (CKE), accounting for more than 65%. In contrast, the Lamb vector divergence and enstrophy contribute less to CKE. The PPW in the impeller is decreased with the increase in Ic, with its positive values primarily distributed near the impeller's shroud side. Compared with the inward inclination channel in model #3, the model #1 with outward inclination accelerates the growth of pressure power, promotes the formation of positive PPW, and improves the hydraulic performance, hence enhancing the fluid's energy exchange and pump's conveying capacity.

papers.title: Effect of airway geometry and maximum number of generations on droplet generation during coughing
papers.abstract: Infectious respiratory diseases spread via droplets emitted by infected individuals. It is known that the emitted droplets vary from person to person because of geometrical differences. This study aimed to elucidate the influence of airway geometry on droplet generation and the maximum number of generations that should be considered when performing numerical analyses. As models for airway geometry, we chose the symmetric Weibel model and asymmetric Kitaoka model generated by a deterministic algorithm to compare the geometrical characteristics under the same volume, surface area, and other set parameters. The Kitaoka model showed a region of locally high air velocity, which was not observed in the Weibel model. Correspondingly, there were regions with localized high wall shear stress (WSS) values and large detached masses only in the Kitaoka model. Moreover, the locations of these localized regions differed depending on the maximum number of airway generations. Regarding the number of droplets generated, both models generated the same number of droplets of several to several tens of micrometers; however, the Kitaoka model generated more nanoscale-size droplets and large droplets of about 100 μm. This was explained by the WSS distribution and thickness of the airway wall mucosa. The thickness of the airway wall mucosa was attributed to the WSS, suggesting that the asymmetric geometry, which influences cough airflow, is an important indicator of droplet generation.

papers.title: Permeability and gas displacement enhancement analysis on the stimulated coal reservoir by hot flue gas
papers.abstract: Injecting hot flue gas into coal seams can achieve the dual effects of gas production enhancement and greenhouse gas sequestration. However, the gas displacement enhancement effect in coal seams caused by the thermal and chemical effects of hot flue gas is not clear. Therefore, a thermal-hydraulic-mechanical-chemical-damage coupling model was first constructed in this paper for the process of gas displacement by hot flue gas, which considered heat conduction and convection (T), gas–water two-phase flow (H), mechanical deformation (M), chemical reaction (C), and coal damage (D). Then, the model was verified based on the gas displacement experiment of the coal core. The influence of mineral dissolution and damage effects on the gas displacement was analyzed through the verified model. Finally, the temporal and spatial evolutions of coal temperature, mineral content, solution pH, damage, permeability, multi-component gas concentration, and gas content during the injection of hot flue gas into coal seams were analyzed to clarify the mechanism of coal permeability enhancement and gas production enhancement under the coupling of the thermal and chemical effects of hot flue gas. This study can provide theoretical guidance for the engineering of gas production enhancement in coal seams by hot flue gas.

papers.title: Layer analysis of ion transport inside nanomaterials with symmetric internal sources using Poisson–Nernst–Planck equation and mean-field theory
papers.abstract: Poisson–Nernst–Planck equation is employed to describe ion transport disrupted by symmetric internal attractive and repulsive sources on the inner surface of nanomaterials in a vacuum. The present methodology has rapid computation time, where microscopic interactions are incorporated in the macroscopic equation to correct physics. Unlike usual molecular simulation, the present approach only requires static interactions between an ion and the host material, where the evolution of ion density and multi-body interactions between ions are captured by the Poisson–Nernst–Planck equation and Eq. (10), respectively. Both ion transport with and without such internal sources will be scrutinized so that the number of ionic layers can be finely tuned not only by external fields but also internal force sources to modify the charge and thermal capacities of nanomaterials. Last but not least, ion–ion interactions can be identified as ionic correlation functions so that the nonlinearity and the diffusion constant of the ion transport problem can be visualized and updated, respectively.

papers.title: Experimental study on heat transfer between particles and molten salt in gas–solid fluidized bed with immersed tubes
papers.abstract: The fluidized bed heat exchanger with immersed tubes plays a key role in heat transfer in the next-generation concentrated solar power system where low-cost inert particles with outstanding thermal stability serve as the heat-absorbing media. However, due to the lack of heat transfer experiments under real conditions, the heat transfer mechanism of such device is still not fully understood, especially in the case where continuous flow of particles is involved. In this study, a series of experiments was conducted based on our self-developed 20 kWh level fluidized bed heat exchanger and the supporting test system to investigate the fluidizing heat transfer characteristics between inert particles and molten salt for the first time. The variation range of the overall heat transfer coefficient U [17.8–315.8 W/(m2·K)] and the bed-to-tube heat transfer coefficient ho [18.6–439.1 W/(m2·K)] was obtained by experiments with varying particle flow rate ṁp (230–680 kg/h), molten salt flow rate ṁs (1300–3000 kg/h) and fluidization number n, defined as the ratio of the actual fluidization velocity to the minimum fluidization velocity, (1.6–3.3). It was found that 2D numerical simulation may seriously overestimate ho. It was also proved that there exists an optimal fluidization number (n = 1.8) to maximize U and ho, simultaneously. Finally, a modified correlation for predicting ho under continuous feed and discharge conditions was proposed and compared with existing models.

papers.title: Analysis of spatial coupling behavior in gas–liquid two-phase flow within vertical upward pipelines
papers.abstract: Vertical gas–liquid two-phase flows are widely applied in chemical engineering equipment. Investigating the spatial coupling characteristics of flow patterns is essential for revealing the mass and heat transfer characteristics between phases. This paper proposes a novel signal processing method based on multiscale interconnected attention pattern complex networks (MIAPCNs). First, multivariate measurement data of gas–liquid two-phase flow are collected using a resistance sensor array. Based on different combinations of core observations in the measurement data, four types of MIAPCNs are constructed. For each MIAPCN, two correlation indices within the optimal scale range are introduced to quantitatively characterize the spatial coupling behavior during the transition from bubble flow to slug flow. The effect of gas and liquid velocities on the spatial coupling behavior of a single flow pattern is analyzed. Furthermore, a sliding window strategy is employed to investigate the spatiotemporal coupling behavior of two-phase flow, with visualizations provided. In addition, the multivariate multiscale attention entropy, Choi–Williams distribution, and complex network graph energy of the measurement data are calculated to validate the effectiveness of MIAPCN in revealing spatial coupling behavior during the flow process. The results demonstrate that the method successfully reveals the spatial coupling mechanisms of flow pattern evolution.

papers.title: Effects of cylinder shape and spacing ratio on the performance of laminar micromixers with two cylinders based on fluid-induced vibration
papers.abstract: Micromixers are widely used in chemistry, biology, and medicine due to their high mixing efficiency, low cost, and excellent controllability. However, achieving rapid mixing in a laminar flow remains a significant challenge. Fluid-induced vibration (FIV) is a promising method to enhance mass transfer and improve fluid mixing in laminar micromixers. This study investigates the effects of FIV on fluid mixing performance by analyzing four different cylinder shapes (circle, square, trapezoid, and regular triangle) and four different spacing ratios (T/D = 0, 0.4, 0.8, and 1.2) under single-degree-of-freedom conditions. The amplitude-frequency response, flow field characteristics, and mixing index under varying shapes and spacing ratios are examined. The results indicate that both cylinder shape and spacing ratio significantly influence the vibration characteristics of upstream and downstream cylinders. Notably, the downstream cylinder exhibits a significantly larger amplitude, thereby enhancing fluid mixing. The interaction between cross-flow cylinder vibrations and vortex shedding in the downstream region plays a crucial role in promoting mixing. Additionally, while an increase in the spacing ratio (T/D) initially improves mixing performance, an excessive increase suppresses cylinder vibrations, leading to reduced mixing efficiency. Overall, the optimal mixing performance is achieved when U*= 3 and T/D = 0.4, with a laminar micromixer featuring two triangular cylinders reaching a maximum mixing index of 0.82. Furthermore, different vibration modes have minimal impact on the pressure distribution along the flow direction within the micromixer.

papers.title: Motion prediction of planing craft in waves based on two-dimensional plus time method
papers.abstract: Planing craft, as a type of high-performance ship, is mainly supported by hydrodynamic lift. When this type of ship navigates in waves, external disturbance easily leads to motion in big amplitude. In this paper, the forward navigation problem of a planing hull is transformed into the water entry slamming problem of a two-dimensional section based on a two-dimensional plus time (2D+t) potential flow method, and a time-domain model is established to predict the motions of planing hull in waves. The sectional hydrodynamic force is calculated by the modified logvinovich model. The empirical methods are used for correcting the buoyancy and the hydrodynamic force near the stern region because of the three-dimensional effect. Meantime, the improvements are proposed for the geometric characteristics of the keel line curvature at bow. The prediction results of heave, pitch, and acceleration are in good agreement with the experimental results.

papers.title: Effects of perturbation location on the vortical flow over a blunt-nosed slender body at a high angle of attack
papers.abstract: Vortical flow over a slender body at high angles of attack (AoA) is uncertain owing to random surface imperfections. Many investigations have eliminated the uncertainty in vortical flow by introducing a micro artificial perturbation, thereby managing the pattern of vortical flow. Effects of perturbation location (including axial and circumferential location) on vortical flow over a pointed-nosed slender body have been thoroughly investigated. However, for a blunt-nosed slender body, effects of perturbation location are still not systematically studied, and the present work aims to focus on this. The perturbation is a particle with a diameter d/D = 0.004, and numerical simulations and wind tunnel tests have been performed at a subcritical Reynolds number (ReD = 1.54 × 105) and a high AoA (α = 50°). With the perturbation gradually shifted downstream axially from the nose tip, there emerges a critical axial position where the vortical flow switches from one asymmetric flow pattern to another opposite asymmetric flow pattern. Moreover, with the perturbation gradually shifting axially downstream further from this critical axial position, the axial evolution of asymmetric vortical flow is progressively delayed downstream, resulting in a gradual weakening of the flow asymmetry. It is observed that the vortical flow exhibits weaker flow asymmetry if the perturbation is located circumferentially closer to the windward symmetrical plane of the blunt-nosed slender body. Moreover, the vortical flow is varied progressively in the form of a single periodicity as the perturbation is shifted circumferentially from θP = 0° to 360° in sequence.

papers.title: Vortex-induced vibration in lead–bismuth eutectic: High-efficiency coupling framework, stability analysis, and nonlinear effects
papers.abstract: Extensive and in-depth research has been conducted on vortex-induced vibration (VIV) in water and air media, whereas studies on heavy metal media remain scarce. With the emerging interest in lead–bismuth fast reactor development, investigations into VIV in lead–bismuth eutectic (LBE) are of critical importance for structural design. This study presents a unified framework for loose/tight coupling numerical model through secondary development of the Fluent solver via user-defined functions, enabling two-degree-of-freedom VIV simulations in water and LBE. The calculation and analysis show that the proposed numerical model achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement in computational efficiency compared to the classical ANSYS System Coupling module; stability conditions for VIV simulations in LBE are theoretically derived, guiding parameter selection; through the comparison of experiments, the accuracy of the numerical model established is verified; the high density and low viscosity of the LBE amplify nonlinear fluid force effects, leading to pronounced nonlinear dynamic behavior in the fluid–solid interaction system. This research deepens the understanding of VIV mechanisms in LBE and provides an effective numerical model for future investigations into other flow-induced vibrations (e.g., fluid-elastic instability) and industrial rapid simulations.

papers.title: Modeling the generation and growth of single-atom nanoparticle in flame spray pyrolysis
papers.abstract: Supported single-atom nanoparticles synthesized in flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) have recently attracted broad attention due to their special construction and excellent catalytic activities. In the present work, a two-step simulation method combining large-eddy simulation (LES) and population balance Monte Carlo (PBMC) is employed successfully to simulate the spatially resolved generation and growth of supported noble metal-based nanoparticles in FSP. Here, a novel two-component PBMC model is proposed for the first time using the flame fields derived from LES as an input. The model delineates a straightforward yet efficient property space for supported nanoparticles and introduces a new coagulation rule that leverage surface coverage and stochastic process to account for multiple forms of the particle–particle coagulation presented during the flame synthesis process. The proposed two-step simulation method is successfully applied to reproduce the generation and growth details of single-atom Pt/TiO2 nanoparticles in FSP. The spatially resolved loading characteristics of Pt noble metal, as well as the size, morphology, and polydispersed size distributions of both the TiO2 support and the Pt noble metal are attained simultaneously. At the Pt contents of 0.1 mol. %, the experimental measurement and numerical prediction indicate that the Pt is dispersed on the surface of TiO2 supports predominantly as isolated single atoms. However, at the Pt content of 0.5 mol. %, the enhanced coagulation dynamics among Pt species results in a reduction of atomically dispersed Pt, with a corresponding increase in the number of Pt nanoclusters.

papers.title: Mitigation of the pressure fluctuation arising from high-speed train passing through the enclosed noise barrier using ventilation opening
papers.abstract: When a train travels through an enclosed noise barrier at high speed, significant pressure fluctuations are generated, which can result in deformation fatigue damage to the structural components of noise barriers. To address this issue, this study proposes the installation of ventilation openings on the top to mitigate pressure fluctuations caused by a high-speed train entering an enclosed noise barrier. A Re-normalization group k–ε turbulence model and dynamic mesh method were utilized to investigate the mitigation principle of the pressure fluctuation in the enclosed noise barrier using the ventilation opening. The numerical results show that the ventilation opening can significantly alleviate pressure fluctuations within the enclosed noise barrier. The transmission coefficient when the pressure wave passed through the ventilation opening followed a power-law relationship with the opening ratio. Furthermore, the effects of alleviation on the pressure fluctuation amplitudes were not monotonic as the opening ratios increased. The optimal location of the ventilation opening for the total enclosed noise barrier was identified as 2ML/(1 + M). For an opening with a cross-sectional area of 8 m2, the maximum peak-to-peak pressure could be reduced by up to 37%. This study provides insights into the mitigation of pressure fluctuations in enclosed noise barriers and could provide valuable data and a theoretical basis for enclosed noise barrier design when considering the aerodynamic effect of high-speed train passages.

papers.title: Smagorinsky constant distribution and turbulent energy dissipation in high Reynolds Number cavity flow
papers.abstract: This study experimentally investigates lid-driven cavity flow at high Reynolds numbers (Re = 3 × 105–1 × 106) using particle image velocimetry. The spatial distribution of root mean square (RMS) velocity, turbulent kinetic energy dissipation rate, and the Smagorinsky constant is analyzed to reveal key turbulence characteristics. The results show that: (1) the RMS velocity increases significantly in the near-wall region with Reynolds number, reaching a peak of 0.43 m/s on the downstream near-wall surface at Re = 1 × 106, while remaining below 0.1 m/s in the core region due to flow stability suppressing turbulence fluctuations; (2) the turbulent kinetic energy dissipation rate exhibits significant spatial nonuniformity near the wall with a peak value of 0.6 at Re = 1 × 106; as the Reynolds number increases, high dissipation regions extend further into the cavity interior and evolve into multiscale fragmented structures; (3) the Smagorinsky constant is close to zero near the cavity wall, gradually increases with distance from the wall, reaches a maximum, and then decreases to zero at the cavity center. As the Reynolds number increases, the overall Smagorinsky constant increases with a more significant rise in its maximum value at higher Reynolds numbers, indicating stronger eddy viscosity. These findings provide experimental insights for improving the nonuniform parameterization in eddy viscosity models for large-eddy simulations.

papers.title: Effect of surge and sway combined motion on the dynamic stall of floating offshore wind turbine airfoils
papers.abstract: The floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) undergoes six-degree-of-freedom motions influenced by wind, waves, and currents. Surge and sway motions influence the aerodynamic performance of the FOWT by creating variations around the blade flow field, leading to complex dynamic stall mechanisms of the airfoil. This study examines the S809 airfoil, coupling pitching motion with surge and sway two-degree-of-freedom motions in both in-phase and anti-phase scenarios. The study examines the impact of combined surge, sway, and pitching motions on hysteresis response characteristics, surface vortex separation, and load variations during dynamic stall. The results indicate that in-phase motions forward swaying and downward surging significantly enhance lift but induce severe unsteady flow characteristics, increase separation vortex intensity, and hamper flow field recovery. Conversely, backward swaying and upward surging reduce boundary layer kinetic energy and turbulence, decreasing lift and stall severity. In anti-phase motions, forward swaying and upward surging increase boundary layer instability, while backward swaying and downward surging weaken boundary layer energy and enhance disturbances, delaying stall. These findings provide theoretical support for FOWT safety and stability, offering insights into wind turbine design, optimization, and operation.

papers.title: Assessing the influence of design variables on serpentine duct intake performance using surrogate-based sensitivity analysis
papers.abstract: Real-world engineering designs and computational models often incorporate uncertainties introduced by approximations and simplifications. Hence, uncertainty quantification (UQ) and global sensitivity analysis (GSA) are essential tools. UQ assesses the propagation of input uncertainties on quantities of interest (QoIs), whereas GSA decomposes the QoI variance to identify the contributions of individual input variables. Despite extensive studies on diffusing serpentine ducts (s-ducts) in the field of aerospace, the application of GSA has been largely neglected. Existing studies have often employed parameterization techniques that conflate cross-sectional shape and area, making them unsuitable for GSA. This study overcomes this limitation by presenting a novel framework for performing GSA on an s-duct, aligning with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) 2030 vision of UQ-enabled multidisciplinary optimization. The s-duct geometry is parameterized using two design variables: eccentricity, which adjusts the cross-sectional shape, and a control point on a cubic Bezier curve, which modifies the centerline. These variables are treated as random with uniform distributions. Using OpenFOAM, we conduct simulations and compute QoIs on a fully automated grid. Surrogate models are constructed using generalized polynomial chaos expansion, and Sobol indices are calculated to quantify each variable's contribution to the QoI variance. The results reveal that the control point contributes nearly 70% to the variance in circumferential distortion and pressure recovery, while eccentricity accounts for 68% of the variance in radial distortion. The proposed framework lays the foundation for future UQ-enabled s-duct optimization.

papers.title: Hydrodynamics of jet-flapping combinatorial propulsion in a squid-like swimmer: A study on different coordination modes
papers.abstract: This study numerically investigates the hydrodynamic performance of a squid-inspired jet-fin combinatorial propulsion system. This squid-like model integrates mantle motion and fin deformation, using dynamic mesh technology to achieve periodic deformation of the mantle and fins. The study compares hydrodynamic differences between various coordination modes under different Reynolds numbers, with a focus on the distinctions between jet propulsion and fin flapping in thrust generation, energy utilization, and vortex structure formation. The results show that at low Reynolds numbers, the continuous movement mode of the mantle and fins yields larger thrust and propulsion efficiency compared to the intermittent mode, while at high Reynolds numbers, the intermittent fin flapping mode reduces drag and results in higher overall propulsion efficiency. Jet propulsion by the mantle demonstrates significant advantages in terms of high thrust and concentrated momentum, while fin flapping excels in efficient low-speed swimming. Additionally, the mantle jet exhibits high propulsion efficiency during contraction, as the vortex ring structure generated by jetting provides significant advantages in kinetic energy utilization and strength retention. This work offers a comprehensive understanding of the complex dynamics in squid-inspired combinatorial propulsion and may provide valuable insights for the design of efficient bio-inspired underwater vehicles.

papers.title: Research on the spray characteristics of the fan nozzle based on coupled analysis of the internal and external flow fields
papers.abstract: The spray angle and distribution uniformity of fan nozzles mainly determine spray characteristics in precision spraying agriculture. However, unreasonable structural parameters make it challenging to achieve the desired controllability of the spray angle and distribution uniformity. To address this challenge, this study investigates the influence of the four structural parameters on the spray angle and distribution uniformity in terms of the inner chamber diameter and length and grooving angle and depth through the orthogonal and single-factor experimental designs. Results show that the increase in the inner chamber diameter and the grooving angle contribute to an expansion of the spray angle compared with the others. Increasing the inner chamber diameter brings about the reduction of energy dissipation within the internal flow field, and the grooving angle generates the decreased velocity decay of droplets in the external flow field. Compared with the grooving angle, the inner chamber diameter enhances the uniformity of spray distribution due to reduced velocity difference and the uniform velocity distribution in the external flow field. Overall, the inner chamber diameter is the potential parameter for controlling the spray angle and distribution uniformity in precision spraying agriculture.

papers.title: Flow structure, bed morphology, and contaminated sediment transport at the confluences of pipes with an angle 60°
papers.abstract: The convergence of pipes within urban drainage networks introduces the accumulation of sediments and pollutants, significantly impacting operational efficiency and the water environment. Research focusing on the mean and turbulent structures within the shear layer, including parameters, such as the flow field, turbulent kinetic energy, and Reynolds shear stress, yields insight into flow dynamics. The study elucidates that the precise identification of the shear layer position is facilitated by specific values, with spiral flow manifesting under particular conditions, thereby mitigating sediment accumulation. Moreover, the study underscores the pivotal role of the confluence ratio in shaping the confluence bed and influencing sediment transport mechanisms. The temporal evolution of contaminated sediment transport demonstrates a migratory trend toward the downstream bar, signifying the attainment of a state of bed morphological equilibrium. This research imparts valuable insight for addressing sediment reduction in confluence pipes and enhancing overall drainage network efficiency.

papers.title: Comment on “An oceanic basin oscillation-driving mechanism for tides” [Phys. Fluids 37 , 016617 (2025)]
The fluid dynamics of bend
papers.abstract: The fluid dynamics of a bend — an apparently innocuous and abundantly occurring element of a fluid flow network found in engineering applications and in the natural world — is surprisingly complex. The qualitative and quantitative evolution of the primary and secondary flow fields as a fluid progresses through a bend, and its many nuances including the upstream and downstream effects, are documented comprehensively in the present work by invoking the power of high-quality computational fluid dynamics. Large ranges in Reynolds number (100 – 800) and curvature ratio (0.05 – 0.4) are covered, involving 32 separate, three-dimensional computations. The present computations are used to provide extensive new data and to discover substantial amount of new flow physics. As an example, the fluid dynamics of the process of the initiation of the Dean vortices in an initially vortex-free flow field has been established here, for the first time. It is demonstrated through the extensive computations that any two of the three non-dimensional numbers — viz., Reynolds number (Re), curvature ratio (δ), and Dean number (De) — are necessary to characterize the fluid dynamics of a bend; no single non-dimensional number is adequate in this respect. The present paper exposes the hidden consequence of the flow going through a bend on the fluid dynamics and flow loss in subsequent, downstream components.

papers.title: Dam-break-induced shock wave characteristic and bridge pier shape effects on shock wave force
papers.abstract: This study experimentally investigated bridge pier shape effect on the impact force induced by shock wave generated by a dam break, under four different reservoir water depths and dry downstream flow condition. The maximum force, its occurrence time, force intensity, and the impulse were criteria used to evaluate the performance of the bridge piers. Average and wave front celerities were investigated experimentally and numerically and were compared with existing equations in the literature. The time histories of the impact forces were measured using a load cell, and a two-dimensional numerical model was used to determine the shock wave celerities. At a reservoir water depth of 25 cm, the rectangular bridge pier recorded an impact force 2.68 times greater than that of the ogival pier, which had the smallest impact force, and the maximum force occurred 6.23 times earlier than in the case of the upstream facing ogival pier, which recorded the longest time to maximum force. The force intensity for the rectangular pier was approximately 1.8 times higher than that of the ogival bridge pier, which had the lowest force intensity across all studied water depths. It was found that a 2.5-fold increase in reservoir water depth led to an increase in up to 5.51 times the impact force for the rectangular pier.

papers.title: Study on migration and plugging mechanism of knot temporary plugging agent in hydraulic fracturing
papers.abstract: Horizontal well temporary plugging and diversion fracturing are critical for economical and efficient tight oil and gas reservoir development. Researchers have developed a novel degradable knot temporary plugging agent (TPA) to address the challenge of perforation plugging in wellbores. However, current research on this topic remains limited, and the understanding of the mechanism underlying the knot TPA temporary plugging is still inadequate. In this study, a computational fluid dynamics–discrete ball-chain coupled model was developed to investigate the flexible characteristics of the knot TPA. Numerical simulations analyzed the knot TPA's behavior near perforations, showing that it is primarily affected by eccentric drag and inertial forces. The rotational effect induced by the eccentric drag force facilitates the sealing of the knot TPA in the perforation. However, whether the knot TPA successfully seals depends on the resultant direction of the combined eccentric drag and inertial forces. Furthermore, during the numerical simulation process, the variations in flow rate, pressure in the fluid, and knot velocity confirm the knot TPA's temporary plugging effectiveness. A visualization-based experiment validated the numerical simulation feasibility and the rationality of the force analysis.

papers.title: Gas–liquid–solid three-phase flow induced vibration model and experimental verification for mining riser used in deep-sea natural gas hydrate extraction
papers.abstract: The gas–liquid–solid three-phase flow induced vibration model of the deep-sea hydrate mining riser is established using the finite element method and Hamilton's principle. The model considers the dynamic decomposition process of hydrates (during transportation, hydrates continue to decompose, leading to changes in key parameters, such as the content and velocity of each phase in the riser), as well as multiple factors such as large aspect ratio of the structure, vortex induced vibration effect, gas liquid solid three-phase flow induced vibration effect, and ocean platform uplift and subsidence. The vibration model is solved using the combined iterative method of the incrementally applied Newmark-β method and Newton–Raphson method, obtaining the vibration response of the mining riser. Meanwhile, an experimental device for nonlinear vibration of the mining riser under internal and external flow excitation is developed based on the principles of geometric similarity, kinematic similarity, and dynamic similarity. The simulation experiments on three-phase flow-induced vibration of the mining riser are carried out, and the results such as multi-phase flow patterns inside the riser, riser displacement, vibration modes, and frequency response are obtained. Moreover, by comparing the axial and radial solid-phase and gas-phase flow velocities obtained through experiments and theoretical model calculations, the accuracy is higher than 87%, which can verify the correctness of three-phase flow model for gas–liquid–solid in the mining riser. Meanwhile, by comparing the root mean square displacement and dominant frequency of the mining riser obtained through experiments and theoretical model calculations, the accuracy is higher than 89%, which can verify the correctness of the vibration model. The research results provide a theoretically sound guidance for designing and practically sound approach for effectively improving the service life of mining riser.

papers.title: Physics-encoded convolutional neural network to predict the mass flow rates of the holes in double-wall systems
papers.abstract: Novel double-wall effusion cooling system shows a remarkable potential for thermal protection of gas turbine blades due to its high cooling effectiveness. Achieving precise assessment of the mass flow rate across every hole within the double-wall blade is essential for refined design. Compared to existing approaches such as computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods, porous media equivalent methods, and flow network methods, machine learning methods demonstrate superior efficiency and accuracy. However, the commonly used fully connected neural network (FCNN) will suffer from excessive model size and data demand. To address the limitation, a physics-encoded convolutional neural network (PeCNN) is proposed in the present study. By treating all holes as an integral input and performing convolutional calculations on its elements, PeCNN is able to learn the flow interactions among holes, enabling a holistic modeling of the entire system. Additionally, an edge identification feature is added in the input to learn the wall-limited effects at the edge. A customized dot product layer is designed to ensure that the mass flow rates are strictly equal to 0 at positions where the hole diameters are 0. Mass conservation is introduced to the loss function to prompt equal mass flow rates of film holes and impingement holes. These physical constraints are intended to further improve the accuracy and robustness. The models were trained and tested by numerical datasets. For the film holes and impingement holes in the test set consisting of two-dimensional hole clusters, the mean relative errors of the model are only 3.41% and 5.22%, respectively.

papers.title: Analysis of rheological parameter variations in uterine arteries before and after cryptic pregnancy
papers.abstract: Cryptic pregnancy, characterized by the absence of typical gestational indicators, poses significant diagnostic challenges. Current diagnostic tests based on biochemical markers such as Human Chorionic Gonadotropin cannot detect such pregnancies because of hormonal dysregulation. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the variation in different rheological parameters—Pressure, Shear rate, Axial velocity—in the uterine arteries using the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) using the COMSOL. The CFD analysis was performed on the total 24 geometries generated from the two structures: S1, before cryptic pregnancy and S2, after cryptic pregnancy. The CFD studies were performed in no slip condition of the wall and viscosity of flowing fluid (equivalent to blood), which were considered both Newtonian and non-Newtonian in the presence of sinusoidal and pulsatile flow. The different rheological parameters were observed on points P1–P5 at the T cycle. Result indicated that non-Newtonian flows exhibited dominant oscillatory patterns in shear rate, pressure, and axial velocity, especially at points like P2 and P4. Newtonian flows showed linear smooth trends, while non-Newtonian fluids showed complex rheological behavior, indicating their potential role in cryptic pregnancy detection. It had been observed that for the structures S124, S125, and S126, pressure value initially rises at point P1, which is further increased from P2 to P5 (2 × 106 Pa) within the time duration from T/3 to T/2 s. Newtonian models are useful for a simplified description, ignoring non-Newtonian effects that may result in incorrect predictions of flow behavior, which can undermine the efficiency and reliability of fluid transport processes in artificial circulation devices, microfluidic systems, and industrial processes. This research identifies the importance of rheological analysis in providing an alternative, noninvasive early detection test, which improves diagnostic accuracy and maternal health outcomes.

papers.title: Acceleration effect on the drag of a bristled wing at low Reynolds numbers
papers.abstract: Miniature insects use drag to provide the weight-supporting force, and the drag is produced by rapidly accelerating the wing downward at an angle of attack close to 90°. It is known that a membranous wing can generate large drag during rapid acceleration at low and high Reynolds numbers (Re). However, for the smallest miniature insects, the wings become bristled. Here, we consider the case of a bristled wing in rapid acceleration motion. It is found that, when Re is less than approximately 40, the rapidly accelerating bristled wing can generate a large drag peak, similar to that of the membranous wing, but the acceleration effect on the drag of the bristled wing decreases sharply as Re exceeds 40. This is because the interaction among the array of bristles, which causes the large drag peak, becomes weak at high Re. These findings may explain why only the smallest miniature insects (Re below 40) use bristled wings.

papers.title: Hyperchaos in a three-dimensional non-autonomous system
papers.abstract: This paper extends the weakly nonlinear stability analysis reported by Francis et al. [J. Eng. Math. 139, 5 (2023)] to cover post-convective regimes of the gravity-modulated Rayleigh–Bénard convection in a Newtonian liquid, bounded by rigid–free isothermal boundaries. Weakly nonlinear stability analysis is performed by considering second harmonics in the Fourier series expansion of temperature, while the second harmonics in the velocity field is neglected owing to the assumption of small-scale convective motions. The occurrence of hyperchaos within the three-dimensional non-autonomous system is observed, induced by modulation, emerging for varying, random combinations of frequency and amplitude values. This result has not been reported in the literature before, to the best of the authors' knowledge. Bifurcation analysis is carried out for varying combinations of modulation parameters. It is found that gravity modulation, in general, stabilizes the convective system under consideration.

papers.title: Study on the rational layout and control of gas drainage roadways in deep inclined coal seams
papers.abstract: To determine the optimal positioning of the bottom drainage roadway in deep inclined high-gas coal seams, this study investigates mining-induced floor failure mechanisms. Based on the engineering conditions of the bottom drainage roadway in the East Third Mining Area of Dashuitou Coal Mine, a three-dimensional mechanical model of a deep non-uniform pressure roadway was established to investigate the formation mechanism of the excavation-induced plastic zone. Based on the semi-infinite solid theory, the inclined failure depth of the stope floor is calculated considering the distribution characteristics of maximum and minimum principal stresses. Combined with the slip-line field theory, the strike-direction failure depth of the floor is analyzed. A double-yield goaf numerical model is employed to accurately simulate post-mining floor failure behavior. From the perspective of the deviatoric stress second invariant, the distortion energy density distribution in both the floor strata and roadway surrounding rock during mining extraction is investigated. The results indicate that when the coefficient of horizontal pressure exceeds 1, the plastic zone radius expands predominantly along the roadway sidewalls, whereas when it is below 1, the plastic zone develops more significantly in the roof and floor regions. Theoretical calculations determine an optimal depth of 20 m for the bottom drainage roadway positioning. Numerical simulation results confirm the technical feasibility of this 20 m depth with staggered distances 45 m staggered displacement. A composite support system combining anchor cables with shotcrete was developed and successfully implemented in the field application.

papers.title: Sediment transport on sandy slopes under solitary waves
papers.abstract: The sheet-flow sediment transport on sandy slopes under tsunami-like solitary waves is investigated in detail by using a two-phase-resolved Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics model. The model is well calibrated and verified by simulating the run-up and breaking of solitary waves on both immovable and movable slopes as well as the resulted erosion and deposition on sandy beaches. The profiles of water pressure, two-phase velocities and shear stresses, and sediment fluxes on the sandy slope before and after the breaking of solitary waves are examined. The temporal evolution of bed shear stress, thickness of sheet-flow layer, and sediment transport rate at locations before and after wave breaking is compared. During the run-up of solitary waves, the change of pore water pressure in the sandy slope follows closely with waves resulting in a “high-pressure wave front.” Sediment moves mainly in the thin sheet-flow layer, in which the shear stress of sediment phase is much higher than the fluid stress due to the intense interparticle collision and friction. The profile of bed-parallel sediment flux in the sheet-flow layer presents parabolic with the peak at the layer center. Relationships between the sheet-flow sediment transport rate and Shields number at locations below and above the initial water level are compared. Further numerical experiments show that the solitary wave height has a minor effect on the relationships between sediment transport rate and Shields number below the initial water near the wave-breaking point while enhances the relations in the swash zone above the initial sea surface.

papers.title: Ellipsoidal drop impact on inclined superhydrophobic surfaces
papers.abstract: Breaking the circular symmetry commonly seen in typical impact dynamics, by introducing initially ellipsoidal drop shapes, significantly modifies mass and momentum distributions. While previous studies have mainly focused on spherical drops impacting on horizontal surfaces, the current study investigates how the initial drop shape and surface inclination collectively affect drop spreading, retraction, and detachment behaviors. After impacting, drops with positive ellipticities exhibit rapid and symmetrical retraction, leading to shorter residence times. Conversely, drops with negative ellipticities display asymmetric momentum transfer and delayed liquid alignment, prolonging their contact with the surface, which is demonstrated through detailed momentum and rim analyses. The combined effects of drop's ellipticity and surface inclination reveal distinct deformation and detachment mechanisms governed by normal or tangential Weber numbers. The findings emphasize ellipticity and surface inclination as critical parameters controlling bouncing behavior, deformation symmetry, and residence time, providing valuable insights for optimizing applications, such as water repellency control and heat transfer enhancement, through drop shape manipulation.

papers.title: Loss analysis and evaluation of axial compressor with casing treatment based on local entropy generation method
papers.abstract: Casing treatments are widely used to enhance compressor stability, yet their impact on compressor efficiency penalty mechanisms remains incompletely quantified. This study employs control volume entropy generation analysis to evaluate the internal flow loss characteristics induced by slot-type casing treatments in an axial compressor. The axial distributions of entropy generation reveal that casing treatments introduce two distinct peaks: a primary enhancement at the rotor leading edge and a secondary peak near the slot trailing edges. The spanwise distributions demonstrate increased losses above 80% span but modest reductions between 65% and 80% span. Flow field visualization identifies that suction effects deflect the tip leakage vortex toward the suction surface, creating localized high-entropy regions, while injection effects promote radial entropy redistribution. Parametric analysis based on the response surface method establishes slot width and axial overlap as the dominant geometric parameters governing loss generation in the upper end wall region, with slot width exhibiting linear correlations and axial overlap showing nonlinear behavior. Self-organizing maps analysis further confirms a strong correlation between efficiency penalty and upper end wall losses. These findings provide quantitative guidelines for optimizing casing treatment geometries to balance stability enhancement and efficiency preservation in axial compressors.

papers.title: Aeroacoustic investigation of open cavity with rear-wall protrusion using lattice Boltzmann method
papers.abstract: Controlling cavity tones is a critical issue in various engineering applications, such as aircraft landing gears, automobile sunroofs, and train bogies, necessitating the development of effective control techniques. This study investigated the control effects of rear-wall protrusions on the flow and acoustic fields of an open cavity using direct aeroacoustic simulations based on the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM). The research subject was a rectangular cavity with a length-to-depth (L/D) ratio of 2.0. The upstream boundary layer was laminar, and the ratio of the cavity length to the boundary layer momentum thickness was set to L/θ=87. The Reynolds number based on the cavity length was 1.5×104. The LBM simulation results were validated by comparing them with experimental results. The findings showed that optimal values exist for the protrusion height and length: h/L=0.10 and l/L=0.20, respectively. For effective flow and sound control, the protrusions should be placed at a height at which they do not directly interact with the shear layer. Moreover, the installation of the protrusion at heights lower than the optimum height caused active recirculation over the protrusions, diminishing the control effects. Sufficiently, long protrusions can suppress the recirculation within the cavity, stabilize the shear layer, and mitigate the generation of tonal sounds. However, protrusions longer than the optimum length promoted the development of separation vortices on the protrusions, which interacted with the shear layer and generated new tonal sounds different from the standard cavity tones. The optimal protrusion dimensions may vary depending on the Reynolds number, L/D, and L/θ ratios. Future research should aim to systematically investigate these dependencies.

papers.title: Gas-dynamic approach to the nonlinear theory of ion-acoustic waves in nonideal plasma with ions obeying the Van der Waals equation of state
papers.abstract: The authors consider a nonideal plasma. The plasma consists of a mixture of two gases—a gas of inertial electrons and a gas of positive single-charge ions. Electrons in plasma are considered to be Boltzmann distributed, and an ion gas obeyed the Van der Waals equation of state. Ion-acoustic waves (IAWs) in such a plasma are studied. A linear theory of IAWs is developed. Within the framework of this theory, a dispersion equation is derived and an exact expression is obtained for the linear velocity of an ion sound. A non-linear theory of high-amplitude IAWs is developed; it is based on the Bernoulli pseudopotential method. It has been shown that stationary IAWs in the studied plasma can have the form of either a nonlinear periodic wave or the form of solitons. The wave velocity ranges in these two forms are defined. Dependence of the maximum velocity of solitons on the value of plasma thermodynamic nonequilibrium parameter is calculated.

papers.title: Drone anemometry of atmospheric winds—A review
papers.abstract: The low altitude economy presents new opportunities for urban mobility with drones and air taxis offering solutions to traffic congestion and access to hard-to-reach areas. These opportunities come with the same challenges as in civil aviation: the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) gives rise to wind gusts and turbulence, leading to sudden displacements of the low-altitude vehicles from the planned trajectory. Hence, a reliable estimation and prediction of wind conditions is paramount to safe drone and air taxi operations. Drones offer an attractive alternative to expensive stationary platforms for wind monitoring in the lower ABL. This article reviews the status, challenges, opportunities, and alternatives to drone-based wind anemometry. Aspects include the wind measurement and estimation of urban terrain, performance metrics of anemometers, model-based wind speed measurement, and machine learning algorithms for atmospheric wind prediction. Already the attitude of the hovering and cruising drones allows to infer the wind velocity. The accuracy of drone wind measurement may be further augmented with various anemometers such as ultrasonic, thermal, hot wire, and pitot tubes. This article exemplifies the potential of drone anemometry for urban wind prediction, for measuring wind profiles in remote areas of wind turbines as well as a tool for boundary layer meteorology and assessment of gusts in harsh weather conditions.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of force variations in successive high-speed liquid droplet impacts and data-driven modeling
papers.abstract: High-speed liquid droplet impacts were numerically investigated using compressible multicomponent Euler simulations to characterize the time-varying force exerted on each droplet. Successive impacts were examined at three impact Mach numbers in the range of 0.051 < Ma < 0.077. The trailing droplet was consistently experiencing a lower force than the leading droplet. Furthermore, a data-driven framework employing a physics-informed neural network was developed to analyze the influence of droplet spacing on successive high-speed droplet impacts.

papers.title: Effect of strut–lobe combination on combustion characteristics in multimode combustor of innovative ramjet combined-cycle engine
papers.abstract: The Fan Augmented Air-Breathing Ramjet Combined Engine (FABRE), integrating an air-turbo-rocket and a ramjet, emerges as a promising propulsion system for two-stage-to-orbit vehicles and hypersonic aircraft. Central to FABRE is the multi-mode combustor, which should work efficiently in both turbocharged and ramjet modes across the Mach 0–6 range. However, the broad operation conditions and lower length-to-diameter ratio requirements with large scales make it remain a significant challenge for multi-mode combustor. To this end, this study performs a systematic numerical evaluation of several representative combustion organization schemes with different numbers of struts and struts-lobes combinations to explore their wide-operation-range behavior on reactants mixing, thermodynamic, and combustion performances under lean, stoichiometric, and rich conditions. Results indicate that for the strut-only schemes, attributed to improved fuel penetration, an increasing number of struts enhances the mixing efficiency by 8% at Mach 2 and 22% at Mach 6. This enhancement in mixing elevates the average temperature, boosting combustion efficiency by 18% at Mach 2 and 9% at Mach 6, albeit with a slight reduction in total pressure recovery. For the strut/lobe combination scheme, it shows that introducing lobes increases the average mixing efficiency of reactants by approximately 5.5%. This improved mixing environment fosters greater fuel heat release, raising total temperature and enhancing the combustion efficiency by 6% at Mach 2 and 1.3% at Mach 6, respectively, despite a minor decrease in total pressure recovery. These findings offer valuable insights into combustion organization strategies for multi-mode combustors, advancing the development of air-breathing ramjet combined cycle engines.

papers.title: Dynamics of a thin liquid film flowing down a vertical cylinder: Effect of variable fluid properties
papers.abstract: In the present study, the effects of variable fluid properties on the dynamics of a falling liquid film over a solid cylinder are analyzed. Fluid properties, such as density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, and surface tension, are treated as functions of temperature. The mass, momentum, and energy equations are simplified using the lubrication approximation. A film thickness evolution equation is derived, which governs the temporal and spatial variations of the film's shape. Steady state results are presented to show the variation of fluid properties with temperature. Linear stability analysis is performed for various limiting cases. The thin film flow is found to be stable (unstable) for positive (negative) thermoviscous numbers. The growth rate of perturbations increases (decreases) for positive (negative) thermoviscous numbers as the rate of change of thermal conductivity (Λ) rises. The Rayleigh–Plateau instability is dominated by thermocapillary instability for Marangoni number (Ma)>0. Convective heat transfer at the free surface stabilizes the film by suppressing thermocapillary instability through thermoviscous effects. Heat transfer at the free surface and variable density significantly influence the transition from convective to absolute instability. An increase in the value of α (or a decrease in density), which corresponds to a lower flow rate, promotes the transformation of convective instability into absolute instability, consistent with the experimental findings of Duprat et al. [“Absolute and convective instabilities of a viscous film flowing down a vertical fiber,” Phys. Rev. Lett. 98(24), 244502 (2007)]. Furthermore, an increase in heat transfer at the free surface leads to a reduction in the convective regime and an expansion of the absolute regime. Nonlinear computations are also performed, showing good agreement with the results of linear temporal and spatiotemporal stability analyses.

papers.title: Similarity in synthetic jets near an adjacent flat plate
papers.abstract: This study proposes a similarity rule for synthetic jets interacting with an adjacent flat plate. To investigate both the instantaneous and time-averaged flow fields, particle image velocimetry and wall pressure distribution measurements were conducted. A comprehensive analysis was performed by varying the offset height ratio, defined as the ratio of the step height to the slot width, and the dimensionless stroke length of the synthetic jet. Unlike continuous jets, whose flow characteristics are predominantly determined by the offset ratio, the flow pattern and reattachment distance of synthetic jets are primarily governed by the ratio of the step height to the stroke length. Additionally, it was confirmed that the jet reattachment point remains largely unaffected by the Reynolds number within the range of 800–3000 for synthetic jets. By normalizing the coordinates using the stroke length, a similarity in synthetic jets toward an adjacent flat plate was observed, arising from the consistent normalized trajectory of vortex clusters released from the slot.

papers.title: Long-term behavior of high enthalpy reacting flows over double wedges at Mach 7
papers.abstract: The present study focuses on unsteady shock interaction mechanisms in high enthalpy reacting Mach 7 flows of air over double wedges with fixed fore angle of 30° and aft angles of 45°,50°,55°, and 60°. For this purpose, a pre-validated Navier–Stokes finite volume solver, hyperReactingFoam that combines two solvers of OpenFOAM, density-based compressible solver, rhoCentralFoam, and reactingFoam is used. The solver has capabilities of modeling chemical reactions in both thermal equilibrium and non-equilibrium hypersonic flows besides shock interactions. Although there are considerable amount of studies in the literature that focus on short and long-term behaviors of shock interaction mechanisms over double wedges, there is still a need to reveal long-term effects of high enthalpy reacting flows on flow physics and shock interaction mechanisms. The present study has been designed and conducted to address these needs. Our computational results reveal that high enthalpy reacting flows over double wedges differ from those with low enthalpy in terms of aft angle threshold value for periodicity, thickness and length of the separation zone over the compression corner, and the strength of the vortex cores that form over the compression corner. In addition to those, the surface heat flux values can reach 60-fold of the values observed in the low enthalpy flows. Our results also show that reaction zone covers wider area as the aft angle is increased but in contrast to low enthalpy flows this does not affect the period of the flow.

papers.title: Simulation study of the impact of iris-fixated lenses on aqueous flow and ocular structures
papers.abstract: Anterior chamber (AC) phakic intraocular lenses are increasingly used to manage high myopia, particularly in patients with thin corneas. However, the implantation of iris-fixated lenses can slightly alter the aqueous humor (AH) flow within the AC, affecting critical ocular structures. Despite their clinical relevance, the detailed effects of these flow modifications remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we employ advanced computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to comprehensively investigate AH flow in the presence of iris-fixated intraocular lenses. This study reveals previously unexplored features of intraocular flow parameters such as wall shear stress (WSS), skin friction coefficient (SFC), surface Stanton number, strain rate (SR), stream function, and pathline visualizations analyzed in different positions across ocular structures. The findings show how these parameters are influenced by lens implantation, with detailed analysis of the cornea, iris, and trabecular meshwork (TM). Moreover, we also explored how age-related physiological changes can further modulate the dynamics of AH, offering a broader understanding of vision and overall health. To ensure the accuracy of our simulations, we conducted validation using established experimental measurements, analytical result, and existing computational data. This work provides a valuable foundation for optimizing lens design and placement to mitigate postoperative complications.

papers.title: Influence of porous media on the flow field and induced noise characteristics of a hydrofoil
papers.abstract: The challenge of hydrodynamic noise generated by the propulsion systems of contemporary underwater vehicles is increasing. Such noise emissions not only undermine the acoustic stealth capability, but also have adverse effects on the operational ergonomics of on-board personnel. To address this critical issue, this paper proposes a method of installing porous materials at the 20% position of the trailing edge of the NACA66 hydrofoil. Based on this, the research on the influence of this hydrofoil on energy, flow field and acoustic characteristics is carried out. In this study, large eddy simulation and the Ffowcs Williams–Hawkins equation with permeable surfaces were utilized to carry out simulation calculations. The results show that, compared with the original hydrofoil, the total sound pressure level of the porous hydrofoil is reduced by up to 7.45 dB, with the most significant reduction occurring below 500 Hz, reaching 13 dB around 140 Hz. The turbulent kinetic energy in the near-hydrofoil region and the hydrofoil surface's momentum transport is reduced, leading to a more stable flow field. By integrating Lagrangian Coherent Structure analysis and L-vector analysis, the study further reveals that periodically shedding vortices and their interactions are the primary sources of the hydrofoil noise. Notably, while the porous media hydrofoil does not alter the fundamental noise generation mechanism, it effectively stabilizes the surrounding flow field, leading to a significant reduction in far-field noise. These findings provide new insights and methodologies for hydrofoil noise reduction research.

papers.title: Asymmetry in drag reduction and increase via blowing/suction control in compressible channel flows
papers.abstract: This paper employs a high-precision finite difference method to conduct direct numerical simulations on the compressible channel turbulent boundary layer at various Mach numbers (M = 0.8, 1.5, 2.25, and 3.0). The purpose is to examine the variations in drag reduction and enhancement by spatial interval blowing/suction control. The results revealed that the impacts of interval blowing and suction on skin-friction drag, turbulence intensity, and turbulent kinetic energy transport exhibit considerable asymmetry at high Mach numbers. While blowing generates an opposing trend in friction and turbulence intensity compared to suction, the rise in drag caused by suction surpasses the reduction in drag from blowing at the same blowing/suction intensity, and the capacity of suction to mitigate turbulence intensity exceeds that of blowing to augment it. The decrease in the generation term ofturbulent kinetic energy caused by suction is less than the increase in blowing. Nevertheless, owing to the minimal blowing/suction strength employed in this study, the variations in the average and fluctuation characteristics of the turbulent boundary layer at low Mach numbers are significantly less than those observed at high Mach numbers. Consequently, blowing and suction controls demonstrate specific symmetry within the subsonic turbulent boundary layer. Moreover, interval blowing/suction controls exert minimal influence on the peak location of turbulence intensity, the generation term of turbulent kinetic energy, and the streaks of velocity fluctuations. This also demonstrates the stability of the spatial distribution of compressible channel turbulence structures at low blowing/suction intensities.

papers.title: Large-scale turbulence effect on streamwise surface pressures in separated and reattaching flows
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the influence of large-scale freestream turbulence on aerodynamic pressure fluctuations on a rectangular cylinder based on large eddy simulation (LES) and wind tunnel experiments. The integral length scale of the freestream turbulence is up to 40 times the characteristic length of the bluff body. The LES computational model is validated through pressure measurements and particle image velocimetry (PIV) experiments. The study reveals a convergence phenomenon in turbulence length scale effects and identifies three key convergence characteristics in (1) spectral-spatial properties of wind pressures, (2) the non-Gaussian nature of negative peak pressures, and (3) the spanwise correlation of lift forces. These findings provide a reference for estimating the most unfavorable wind loads in engineering practice when the turbulence scale is uncertain. Furthermore, the paper explores the specific interactions between flow field fluctuations and wind pressure fluctuations on the rectangular cylinder. The results show that large-scale vortices outside the time-averaged shear layer induce significant low-frequency fluctuations in wind pressures, which, in turn, modulate the low-frequency flow fluctuations within the shear layer near the wall. This insight clarifies research priorities in turbulence blockage effects within wind engineering. Additionally, this study investigates the mechanism behind the elevation of fluctuating wind pressure under turbulent inflow conditions. It is found that this elevation stems from intensified momentum exchange outside the time-averaged shear layer, primarily driven by the upward convection of low-speed momentum near the shear layer and its intensified mixing with large-scale vortices in the incoming turbulence.

papers.title: Faraday waves in an annular cell with a crossing baffle
papers.abstract: An experimental investigation on the effect of the baffle crossing the width of an annular cell is conducted to determine if its existence can alter the Faraday instability and characteristics. The results indicate that while the baffle introduces additional viscous dissipation, raising the instability threshold, it also generates dominant perturbations that reduce the energy barrier for wave formation. The relationship between wavenumber and angular frequency agrees well with theoretical predictions accounting for surface tension. The presence of the baffle slightly increases the wavenumber with respect to forcing acceleration but has no significant impact on wave steepness. Measurements of wave crest positions reveal that for the annular cell with a baffle, the crests remain nearly unchanged, while they do not align for a clean annular cell. This suggests that the meniscus induced by the baffle crossing the width of the cell plays a more significant role in Faraday instability than the influence of the inner circular wall, which lies along the wavelength direction.

papers.title: Dust migration law in the “Y” ventilation pattern of the roof cutting and pressure relief goaf
papers.abstract: This study delves into the dust migration patterns under the “Y” type ventilation system in coal mine top-coal caving faces to address the increasingly severe underground dust concentration issues. By establishing a mathematical model for the motion of gas–solid two-phase flow and employing numerical simulation methods, the study reveals the uneven distribution characteristics of airflow in the goaf and the reserved entry of the tail section of the working face, particularly the significant impact of airflow direction near the mining machine on dust migration. The research findings clarify the concentration distribution patterns of dust generated by drum cutting and support movement in the working face and the reserved entry, identify the high-concentration areas of respirable dust formed at the breathing height on the downwind side of the mining machine, and pinpoint the central and downwind areas of the working face as key regions for dust control. Based on these findings, the study proposes an integrated dust control strategy, emphasizing the synergistic application of multiple technological measures such as source control, ventilation optimization, and wet dust suppression, providing a scientific basis for the formulation of effective dust control measures. This research contributes to the theoretical foundation of dust migration patterns in top-coal caving faces and provides practical guidance for dust control in engineering applications, thereby demonstrating significant theoretical and practical value.

papers.title: Failure characteristics of sandstone containing a single flaw under different σ 2 and σ 3 conditions
papers.abstract: In deep underground geotechnical engineering, flaws emerge as a critical factor influencing the stability of engineering rock masses. This study delves into the macroscopic mechanical behavior and fracture characteristics of sandstone specimens containing a single flaw under true triaxial stress states. The main objective is to systematically elucidate the impact of the intermediate principal stress σ2 and minimum principal stress σ3 on the stress–strain response, triaxial strength, brittleness index, and cracking pattern. The results demonstrate that the stress–strain curves of flawed sandstone specimens exhibit multiple fluctuations with rises and falls, and the post-peak recovery stresses are significantly influenced by σ3. The peak strength, crack initiation stress, and crack damage stress under true triaxial compression initially increase and then decrease as σ2 increases, while the increase in σ3 has a pronounced enhancement effect on the characteristic strength of flawed sandstone specimens. Based on the total stress–strain curve, an evaluation index of rock brittleness characterized by fracture energy is established to determine the quantitative relationship between principal stress and brittleness of flawed sandstone specimens. The flawed sandstone specimens typically fail due to flaw-dominated tensile-shear mixed cracks, regardless of σ2. Conversely, when σ3 is low, the failure of the flawed sandstone specimen is dominated by tensile-shear mixed cracks with a tensile-dominated mechanism. As σ3 increases, the failure mode gradually transitions to flaw-dominated tensile-shear mixed failure. When σ3 is high, the failure mode is characterized by stress-dominated tensile-shear mixed cracks. Compared with σ2, the failure mode of flawed sandstone specimens is more sensitive to σ3.

papers.title: Research on performance prediction of a small sample centrifugal pump based on a pre-processing approach for imbalanced regression and key hyperparameters optimization
papers.abstract: This article proposes a method for optimizing key hyperparameters and its application in predicting the performance of centrifugal pumps.
