Centrifugal pumps, as essential equipment widely utilized in diverse engineering perspectives such as construction, industry, and water treatment, play a crucial role in both product design and engineering practice, and their performance prediction has been a widespread concern and should be critically looked at. Meanwhile, the traditional numerical simulation methods have limitations regarding computational complexities and time consumption, hence emanating to a growing interest in machine learning methods based on neural networks. By combining a genetic algorithm and a synthetic minority over scaling technique for regression with Gaussian noise and using a simple back propagation neural network, higher prediction accuracy and stability have been achieved in small sample sets, the average absolute percentage error of the head is 7.22%, and the efficiency is only 1.38%. To verify the adaptability of the method, we build a new dataset and compare it with experimental results, and the maximum relative error of the head is 5.06%, while the maximum error of the efficiency is only1.93%. Finally, the reasons for the higher accuracy of efficiency prediction were analyzed.

papers.title: Experimental study on hydrodynamic characteristics of offshore seabed-fixed cylinder with truncated porous shells
papers.abstract: The impermeable shells in collision protection systems installed on seabed-mounted offshore structures alter the hydrodynamic profile and may amplify wave loadings, resulting in hydrodynamic penalties. Surface-pierced porous designs are proposed as potential solutions, yet their efficacy in reducing these penalties remains insufficiently explored. To bridge this gap, model tests are conducted for a seabed-fixed cylinder with truncated porous shells. The shells feature various parameters including diameter, porosity, submerged depth, and opening shape to investigate their influence on the cylinder's hydrodynamic characteristics. Regular and irregular wave conditions are tested, with base shear forces, moments, and wave surfaces recorded. The results indicate that non-porous shells introduce hydrodynamic penalties to the model, increasing base shear by 24%–27% and base moment by 21%–25%. Larger shell diameters yield more severe amplifications, particularly under high wave heights. Porous shells significantly minimize these penalties, with merely 5% porosity reducing the increases to 7% for base shear and 13% for base moment. For practical engineering applications, shells with 10% porosity offer a potential balance between protective functionality and hydrodynamic performance. Furthermore, increasing porosity beyond 10% shows gradually converged hydrodynamic performance approaching that of the original cylinder without shells. The submerged depth of porous shells plays a secondary role in affecting hydrodynamic performance, while the opening shape exhibits even more minimal influence. Analysis of diffraction waves demonstrates that porous shells interfere with diffraction by diminishing diffraction wave amplitude and exacerbating phase lag between incident and diffracted waves, suggesting that porous shells effectively suppress wave diffraction forces.

papers.title: Axial auxiliary fluid injection on the internal flow of the draft tube of Francis turbine
papers.abstract: With the gradual increase in the proportion of clean energy, the demand for load regulation in hydro-generator units is growing. Taking a real Francis turbine unit as the research object, this paper conducts a numerical study by employing auxiliary fluid injection (water and air injection) through the main shaft's central hole when the unit operates at 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% of the rated load. The results show that both water and air injection through the central hole can effectively suppress draft tube cavitation, reduce airfoil cavitation, and create more uniform streamlines in the straight conical section. These methods also contribute to reducing draft tube losses and improving turbine efficiency. Both injection types suppress pressure pulsation at 0.2 times the natural frequency (fn, the rotation frequency). Comprehensive analysis of turbine efficiency, output, cavitation, and draft tube losses suggests that under the conditions of 80% and 100% of the rated load where the flow pattern quality is inherently good, the injection volume for both fluids should not exceed 0.02 times the rated flow rate (Q). Furthermore, under the conditions of 40% and 60% of the rated load with relatively small flow rates, an injection range of 0.02Q to 0.03Q is recommended to balance efficiency enhancement with effective cavitation and loss control, thereby optimizing the overall unit performance.

papers.title: Time-invariant characteristics of evaporating thin film during droplet evaporation
papers.abstract: An evaporating thin film (ETF) plays a critical role in heat dissipation due to the substantially enhanced evaporation flux. Despite its fundamental importance in interfacial evaporation dynamics, direct experimental characterization of the ETF has remained a major challenge, resulting in a limited understanding of its temporal evolution. This study provides the first direct experimental evidence demonstrating the time-invariant nature of ETF profiles during the pinning stage of droplet evaporation, offering novel insight into interfacial evaporation mechanisms. The ultra-thin liquid film profiles are measured under varying surface wettability conditions through a self-assembled monolayer (SAM) on a gold substrate. A theoretical model incorporating kinetic theory and the augmented Young–Laplace equation is also employed to quantitatively examine the finite evaporation flux in the ETF region. The findings reveal that the ETF profile remains time-invariant during the pinned stage, exhibiting local equilibrium characteristics, and theoretical predictions show good agreement with experimental observations. Notably, it is found that surface wettability has a minor influence on variations in ETF profiles, and the disjoining pressure is found to be higher on hydrophilic substrates, contributing to further thinning of the ETF.

papers.title: Enhancing the aerodynamic performance of fling kinematics through wing deformation and phase overlap
papers.abstract: The study investigates the impact of wing deformation in insects employing clap-and-fling kinematics specifically during the peel phase. In this regard, the curvature parameter (γ) is introduced to mimic bending patterns observed in fruit flies, while the sweep-pitch overlap (ξ) is also explored. Numerical simulations performed using an in-house solver reveal complex and intriguing interactions between wing deformation, overlap, and vortex dynamics. Increasing wing deformation enhances mean lift, despite a delayed leading edge vortex (LEV) pair formation. Unlike lower curvatures, where circular LEVs remain attached, higher γ produces detached, non-circular LEVs, expanding the low-pressure region across the entire chord. However, excessive wing straightening at high γ and wing–wake interaction disrupt new LEV formation also responsible for lower lift toward the end of peel. Mean lift increases with overlap due to stronger vortex-pin structures extending from root to tip, diminishing the high-pressure region near the trailing edge. The deforming wing's Pareto front achieves significantly higher lift with lower input power, enhancing fling aerodynamics and reveals ideal range of γ and ξ that maximize lift. These findings emphasize the importance of LEV and trailing edge vortex dynamics in efficient lift generation during wing deformation, offering insight for bio-inspired flapping-wing designs.

papers.title: Feature attention-based deep neural operator for solving seepage flow equations in porous media reservoir simulation
papers.abstract: The porous media seepage problem is a key area of reservoir fluid simulation, which aims to solve multifield partial differential equations. With the increasing adoption of machine learning to solve partial differential equations, the solver for this problem is becoming ever more intelligent. However, current intelligent partial differential equation solvers for solving this problem commonly lack the ability to generalize across multiple parameters and conditions. In the context of porous media seepage, existing solvers face challenges in capturing the local effects of geological parameters on fluid flow. This limitation necessitates repeated targeted calculations under varying geological conditions, leading to high spatiotemporal costs and reducing the model's capability to draw generalizations among distinct scenarios. To overcome this barrier, a deep operator neural network based on the feature attention mechanism is proposed. The auxiliary fitting network of deep operators is used to encode information about the complex geological conditions affecting flow in porous media. Then, the feature attention mechanism is used to identify and select the crucial local features from the encoded auxiliary and spatiotemporal information. Finally, the model aggregates these features to fit the pressure and saturation fields under the spatiotemporal variations of the fundamental flow problem in porous media. The model's capacity to address two-phase porous seepage problems was substantiated under three distinct heterogeneous geological conditions. The experimental outcomes substantiate the model's superiority in terms of robustness and generalization, and the feature attention mechanism notably enhances the model's prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Assessment of thermal conductivity of unsaturated frozen soils based on three-dimensional numerical models
papers.abstract: The thermal conductivity of unsaturated frozen soil is a critical parameter influencing a wide range of engineering applications, including geothermal energy systems, radioactive waste disposal, and infrastructure development in cold regions. As a typical multiphase medium comprising solid, gas, ice, and water, the thermal behavior of unsaturated frozen soil is highly complex, with each constituent phase affecting the overall thermal conductivity. This complexity poses significant challenges for accurate prediction. To address this issue, a novel three-dimensional (3D) identification-reconstruction-mesoscale-simulation model is proposed to evaluate the thermal conductivity of unsaturated frozen soils. The modeling process consists of three key steps: feature identification, mesostructure reconstruction, and thermal conductivity calculation. The first step is implemented by computed tomography scanning, contacting angles testing as well as nuclear magnetic resonance to determine the input parameters. Following this, the identified characteristic parameters are utilized to reconstruct mesostructured. Thermal conductivity is then calculated by the finite-element method coupled with the Monte Carlo simulation. To verify the accuracy of the proposed model, numerical data are compared with the results obtained from experiments and empirical models. The comparison demonstrates that the proposed approach offers strong predictive capability for the thermal conductivity of unsaturated frozen soils. Furthermore, a parametric study is conducted using the 3D model to explore the effects of phase composition on thermal conductivity. This study provides new insights into the influence of internal structure on thermal behavior and offers practical guidance for engineering applications in cold regions.

papers.title: Slip boundary condition on self-affine fractal surfaces via molecular dynamics
papers.abstract: This study utilizes molecular dynamics simulation to examine the slip boundary conditions of self-affine fractal rough surfaces. The findings suggest that decreasing the Hurst index and increasing the cutoff wave vector augment the power spectral density values. This in turn amplifies the high-frequency (small-scale) rough components of the self-affine fractal surface, thereby increasing resistance to fluid motion on the rough surface. Enhancing the interaction between solid and liquid molecules by raising the interfacial energy and augmenting the overall roughness of the self-affine fractal surface by increasing the root mean square roughness, both contribute to an increased resistance of the rough surface to fluid motion. The increase in the resistance to fluid motion results in a decrease in the overall slip velocity of the fluid, an increase in the inhomogeneity of the density profile, an improvement in the ordering of the fluid motion at the solid–liquid interface, and an increase in the intensity of the main peak of the in-plane structure factor, as well as a suppression of the slip behavior. In addition, we find that the relationship between the slip length and the peak intensity of the normalized in-plane structure factor can be fitted to a curve. As the peak intensity of the in-plane structure factor increases, the effect of the fluid ordered layer being “anchored” becomes stronger, and the slip length decreases.

papers.title: Turbulent flow characteristics and drag crisis in aerodynamic optimization of non-uniform cross section: A combined computational fluid dynamics and wind tunnel study
papers.abstract: As telescopic booms in all-terrain cranes increasingly adopt high slenderness ratios, investigating the blunt-body flow characteristics of special cross section booms is critical for achieving wind resistance reduction and ensuring operational stability under complex wind conditions. Combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and wind tunnel experiments, the research focuses on the blunt-body flow characteristics of a non-uniform cross section boom. Two optimization approaches, response surface methodology (RSM) and direct optimization methodology, were employed to refine critical geometric parameters while maintaining structural integrity. Numerical results demonstrated that both methods effectively reduced the drag coefficient, with RSM achieving a maximum reduction of 12.04% at 10 m/s, while direct optimization minimized lift fluctuations by up to 34.58%. A scaled model was tested in a wind tunnel under Froude number similarity to measure drag parameters, and a derived correction formula was applied to account for Reynolds number discrepancies between experimental and numerical conditions. The optimized designs exhibited consistent drag reduction trends with experimental deviations from CFD results reduced to below 7% at low wind speeds (10 m/s) after correcting for three-dimensional end effects. Wind tunnel experiments identified a “drag crisis” regime at a critical Reynolds number of 2.11 × 105, underscoring the destabilizing effects of turbulent boundary layer transitions. By integrating numerical simulations, multi-objective optimization, and experimental validation into a unified framework, this study establishes a robust theoretical foundation for analyzing blunt-body flow dynamics and developing aerodynamically efficient crane designs tailored to extreme wind environments.

papers.title: Acoustic emission response characteristics and energy evolution laws of sandstone under stepwise cyclic loading with “loading–stress maintaining–unloading”
papers.abstract: The analysis of damage evolution during the dynamic process of stress accumulation–brief stabilization–stress transfer is crucial for ensuring the stability of underground engineering projects. In this study, sandstone specimens were subjected to a cyclic loading regime consisting of loading–stress maintaining–unloading phases. Mechanical data and acoustic emission (AE) signals were collected simultaneously throughout the experiments. The outer envelope of the stress-strain curves during loading resembles that of continuous loading, with both elastic energy and dissipated energy increasing as input energy increases in each cycle. During the stress maintaining phase, variations in elastic energy and input energy conform to linear energy storage laws. AE signals show a strong correlation with the loading process, effectively reflecting the internal damage evolution characteristics of the samples. Specifically, during the stress maintaining phase, the decay of AE hit rate follows an exponential decay form expressed as At=A0⋅e−tτ+I. An increase in characteristic parameters A0, τ, and I can serve as precursors for disaster warnings under this stress path.

papers.title: Flow redirection dynamics in mature reservoirs: Low-viscosity gel-polymer synergy for conformance control
papers.abstract: Following three cycles of intensive reservoir development, the increasing permeability in oil layers has led to the formation of preferential seepage channels, resulting in inefficient circulation, elevated pressure differentials, and dispersed residual oil. To address these challenges, an integrated “profile control-flooding-water shutoff” framework was developed, comprising three critical stages: (1) precise identification of seepage pathways using advanced diagnostic techniques; (2) injection of a low-initial-viscosity (LIV) gel system to optimize flow distribution and mitigate channeling effects; and (3) implementation of a tailored polymer-surfactant displacement system to enhance oil recovery efficiency. Core flooding experiments demonstrated that the LIV gel-assisted polymer flooding system (polymer molecular weight: 25 × 10−6 Daltons; concentration: 1800 mg/L) achieved an incremental recovery rate of 13.6% following conventional polymer flooding, surpassing standalone high-concentration polymer flooding by 4.4% while reducing polymer consumption by 24%. Key operational parameters were optimized as follows: LIV gel system: a slug size of 0.1 times pore volume (PV), an injection rate of 0.18 PV/a, with an operational period of 172 days; polymer flooding: a slug size of 0.7 PV, an injection rate of 0.18 PV/a, with an operational period of 1420 days. Over a total operational duration of 1592 days and a cumulative chemical injection volume of 218.152 × 104 m3, field predictions indicate an 8.08% increase in recovery for test zones (initial water cut: 96.5%), corresponding to an incremental oil production of 12.72 × 104 tons. These findings confirm that the synergistic approach combining LIV gel and polymer flooding not only enhances recovery efficiency but also reduces costs, thereby strengthening the economic viability of mature oilfields.

papers.title: Scaling of mixed velocity-temperature derivative skewness in stationary homogeneous isotropic turbulence with a uniform mean scalar gradient
papers.abstract: Transport equations for the mean squared scalar derivatives in stationary homogeneous isotropic turbulence with a uniform mean scalar gradient are derived from the transport equations for the second-order scalar derivative tensor. After some manipulation of the equations, it is shown that the large-scale forcing caused by the mean scalar gradient can be recast in the form RiSθ*Peλθ−1 (Sθ* is the non-dimensional mean scalar gradient, Peλθ is the turbulent Péclet number, and Ri(i=1,2,3) are the normalized mixed velocity-scalar derivatives). The effect of the large-scale forcing gradually disappears as Peλθ becomes sufficiently large, implying a gradual approach toward a constant value of the mixed velocity-temperature derivative skewness with increasing Peλθ. The trend of available data for the dependence of this mixed skewness, both with respect to the Reynolds number for a fixed Sc and with respect to Sc for a fixed Reynolds number, is consistent with the analysis.

papers.title: Theoretical and intelligent studies of critical hydraulic gradient for piping erosion
papers.abstract: Piping erosion is one of the most common reasons for the failure of hydraulic engineering structures, and determining the critical state of piping erosion is crucial. In this study, a theoretical model of piping erosion is established that considers the coupling between non-Darcy and Darcy flow. The analytical solution of the critical hydraulic gradient of piping erosion (CHGPE) is derived under the velocity slipping interface condition. Additionally, a new intelligent expression of CHGPE is proposed based on existing experimental data consisting of 41 measurements, using gene expression programming (GEP). The proposed intelligent model achieved the coefficient of determination, root mean squared error and mean absolute error values of 0.912, 0.107, and 0.090, respectively. The results showed that the proposed intelligent model's errors with the existing experimental data were within 15% (CHGPE values ranged within ± 0.2), indicating that the model can be reasonably applied in engineering. Moreover, many CHGPE values were within the predicted ranges of the proposed theoretical model. Further comparison with several other theoretical or empirical formulas was conducted. The proposed theoretical model has a similar expression form to some existing models, and both the proposed theoretical and intelligent models have higher accuracy than those formulas. According to parametric analysis, the GEP model can reasonably reflect the influence patterns of the input parameters on the critical hydraulic gradient. The analysis identified d10, d20, and d60 as the most important factors, with their contributions being consistent with the physical understanding of the piping erosion process.

papers.title: Mechanism of water adsorption and penetration at the coal interface under methane pressure and temperature
papers.abstract: Injecting water into coal seams serves as an effective approach for mitigating coal mine disasters, with its effectiveness largely determined by the wettability of coal seams to aqueous solutions. This study integrates physical experiments with molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the macro and microscopic wettability characteristics of the coal–water–methane interface, focusing on the effects of high gas pressure and temperature in deep coal seams. Physical experiments measured the coal–water contact angle under a methane atmosphere, revealing that increased methane pressure elevates the contact angle, reducing water's wettability on coal, whereas higher temperature decreases the contact angle, enhancing wettability. Molecular dynamics simulations, employing a large-scale rough-wall coal–water–methane model, examined the adsorption and diffusion behaviors of water and methane molecules under varying methane pressures and temperatures. Increased methane pressure led to higher contact angles, decreased coal–water interaction energy, reduced hydrogen bond counts, lower relative concentrations of water molecules, and diminished mean square displacement of water molecules, collectively weakening the interaction between water molecules and coal macromolecules. Conversely, elevated temperature resulted in the opposite trends, promoting adsorption and diffusion of water molecules. Higher methane pressure hampers water molecule adsorption and penetration into coal pores due to methane occupying adsorption sites, thereby weakening water-coal interactions. In contrast, increased temperature suppresses methane adsorption, facilitating methane desorption and diffusion, thus creating space for water molecule adsorption and penetration. This study enhances the understanding of coal–water interface wettability, providing theoretical support for water injection technology in deep coal seams.

papers.title: Particle dynamics analysis of hydraulic collecting for deep-sea mining based on overlapping mesh method
papers.abstract: Submarine mining represents a pivotal yet intricate endeavor, encompassing a spectrum of challenges that span technological innovation, ecological stewardship, and regulatory compliance. The precision of collecting is profoundly influenced by the nozzle height and particle size, with considerable variability observed across terrestrial and marine trials. Leveraging the dual-jet phenomenon, we have engineered a dual-row jet collector's physical prototype. Through the overlapping mesh technique, the dynamic characteristics of a single particle under various nozzle height and particle size have been investigated with a particular emphasis on the trajectory and force exerted on individual particles. The initial surface pressure and the ensuing dynamics of spherical particles have been assessed to elucidate the particle–fluid coupling mechanism. Concurrently, the interaction between particle size and nozzle height on lifting has been dissected utilizing the π-theory. The function curve of force coefficients had been unveiled through model reduction and functional approximation. The findings suggest that the collection efficacy is markedly enhanced when the particle size is 20 mm and the nozzle height from the ground is 40 mm. However, the particles become uncollectible as the nozzle height surpasses 80 mm. Principal force reaches its zenith when the ratio of nozzle height to particle diameter is 0.875. These insights provide a theoretical framework for the optimization of engineering mining operations, potentially optimizing the design of hydraulic collectors.

papers.title: Multiple flow modes in CO2 geological storage fluid dynamics and reactive transport in saline aquifers
papers.abstract: Global carbon emissions are a major contributor to climate change, highlighting the urgent need for effective carbon reduction and removal strategies. Geological storage of carbon dioxide (CO2) in saline aquifers has emerged as a promising and secure approach for long-term carbon sequestration. This study systematically investigates the influence of key process parameters on the efficiency of CO2 mineral trapping through calcite dissolution. First, the effect of particle size distribution on the dissolution dynamics is examined using five calcite structures with identical porosity (30%). The results reveal that neither highly uniform nor highly heterogeneous particle size distributions yield optimal performance. Instead, an intermediate level of particle size variation maximizes dissolution efficiency by balancing reactive surface area and flow accessibility. Subsequently, the effects of injection rate and acid concentration are evaluated under fixed structural conditions. It is found that higher injection rates facilitate the formation and elongation of dissolution channels, while increased concentrations accelerate reaction kinetics and enhance the widening of existing pathways. However, a saturation threshold exists beyond which further increases in injection rate or concentration offer diminishing returns. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the interplay between pore structure, transport conditions, and reaction kinetics in CO2 storage systems. The study highlights the importance of optimizing particle size distribution and injection parameters to enhance storage efficiency, offering valuable guidance for the design of effective geological carbon sequestration strategies.

papers.title: An efficient method to determine conjugate heat transfer in moving bodies on parallel computing systems
papers.abstract: An efficient numerical method to simulate the conjugate heat transfer between a fluid and moving bodies is presented. The numerical approach is based on hierarchical Cartesian meshes and formulated for immersed boundaries such that simulations can be performed for solid bodies of arbitrary shape and without interpolation assumption on parallel high-performance computing systems. To ensure a consistent temperature and heat flux across the fluid–solid interface, a direct iterative procedure incorporating the solid and the fluid domains is used such that a fully energy conserving method is obtained. The method is validated by comparing simulation results for generic three-dimensional problems of stationary and moving geometries with reference data, for which also the conservation properties and the accuracy of the method are demonstrated. Results for the heat transfer of a sphere at a fixed position in an adiabatic domain, the flow over a backward-facing step, and a shape-transforming body are shown. Additionally, results for moving bodies are presented, which demonstrate the accuracy and versatility of the developed method. Finally, the efficient implementation of the algorithm for usage on parallel computing systems is shown by scaling and benchmark plots.

papers.title: Effects of high and low temperatures on gas adsorption under high pressure
papers.abstract: The present study sets out to address the dynamic imbalance of gas adsorption and transportation in the context of the “three highs and one disturbance” phenomenon observed in deep wells of kilometers scale. To this end, a high-pressure adsorption model has been constructed for the entire temperature range of −30–110 °C. This model aims to reveal the characteristics of gas adsorption under the action of high-pressure temperature fields. The 7 MPa high-pressure isothermal adsorption–pressure mercury joint test of anthracite in the Guhanshan Mine yielded the following findings: The adsorption process conforms to the Langmuir model, and the adsorption intensification effect is evident in the low-temperature region. This is due to the lowering of the kinetic energy of methane molecules, which leads to the preferential occupation of the low-energy adsorption sites. Consequently, the limiting adsorption amount (Qm) is increased, and the adsorption capacity is enhanced by 6% for every 10 °C decrease in temperature. Conversely, at elevated temperatures, desorption is hindered, and although the increase in molecular kinetic energy leads to an enhancement in the rate of desorption, the effect of thermal compaction causes a decrease in the volume of macropores, thereby forming a transport barrier in which the specific surface area increases and the permeability decreases. The effect of entropy increase in supercritical adsorption is significant; the high-pressure environment weakens the temperature sensitivity by filling the micropores and fluctuating the density of supercritical methane, while the nonlinear amplification of the response characteristics of the excess adsorption capacity. The research findings provide a theoretical foundation for the optimization of engineering parameters in the context of deep coal seam freezing core technology, as well as for the prevention and control of gas outbursts.

papers.title: Planar vibrations of a slightly curved simply-supported piping system subjected to pulsating flow
papers.abstract: In this paper, the dynamic characteristics of a slightly curved simply-supported pipeline system subjected to pulsating flow were investigated. Considering the nonlinear effects introduced by the initial curvature of the pipeline and the influence of pulsating parameters on the system, a nonlinear model equation for pipeline vibration was constructed and discretized using the Galerkin method. The Floquet theory and the fourth-order Runge–Kutta method were employed to analyze the effects of pulsating parameters, flow velocity, and curvature on the system's stability and nonlinear vibration characteristics. The results show that the geometric nonlinear effect induced by bending presents a two-way regulation law on the system stability in different flow velocity intervals. Under subcritical conditions, this effect can enhance the system stability; while under supercritical conditions, it makes the system more prone to chaotic motion. In addition, under supercritical flow velocity conditions, the system can be restored to a stable state by rationally selecting pulsating parameters. The instability of the low-curvature system is caused by the harmonic and subharmonic resonances of the first- and second-order modes, and the system generates quasi-periodic and chaotic motions under harmonic resonance conditions. The instability of the high-curvature system is due to the subharmonic of the first-order mode and the combined-parameter resonance of the first- and second-order modes.

papers.title: Aerodynamic heat and drag reduction for hypersonic rarefied flow around a bipyramid–type bluff body
papers.abstract: Severe thermal environment and drag are among the major challenges for the aerodynamic design of hypersonic spacecraft operating in the atmosphere. Rarefied gas is encountered when flying at an altitude of 85 km or above for reentry spacecraft. Numerical computations are performed to study the aerodynamic heat and drag reduction in rarefied flow regime. Direct Simulation Monte Carlo approach is adopted to solve the Boltzmann governing equations based on the OpenFOAM platform. A two-stage pyramid–type bluff body is selected as a basic configuration, based on which an aerospike and its combinations with aerodisk and opposing jet are, respectively, studied. A parametric study is performed under the freestream Mach numbers of 6–20. Statistical aerodynamics including the wall temperature, heat flux, pressure, drag coefficient, and rarefied gas velocity around the surface of the bluff body are compared. The heat flux dramatically drops by 35%–44% while the drag drops by 4.1%–7.8% on the bluff body wall when the pure aerospike is used. The heat and drag on the bluff body wall are further decreased when an aerodisk is added, but they are slightly increased when a jet is injected reverse to the freestream in front of the aerospike. Moreover, the total heat and drag on all walls show minor variation. The heat and drag reduction rates generally decrease or tend to be stable with increased inflow Mach number.

papers.title: Dynamics of cylindrical bubble driven by two same-sided shock waves
papers.abstract: The dynamics of cylindrical bubble driven by two same-sided shock waves is examined through numerical simulations across three characteristic regimes: the second shock strength weaker than, equal to, and stronger than the first shock. Under matched total pressure ratios, comparisons with equivalent single-shock scenarios highlight distinct downstream jet evolution and vorticity generation mechanisms. Key findings reveal that the second shock-induced transmitted waves effectively suppress the first shock-generated diverging waves, inhibiting outward jet formation. Moreover, both positive and negative vorticity emerge at the downstream interface, and their mutual competition further suppresses the jet development. To characterize the vorticity deposition in dual-shock configuration, the classic one-dimensional circulation model is revised by incorporating the shock transit time correction and velocity correction, and the revised model achieves prediction errors ≤5% (single-shock) and ≤6% (dual-shock) across our parameter space. Finally, the mixed mass dynamics under second shock impact is examined. The second shock amplifies mixing efficiency between the test gas and ambient air, and stronger second shock yields proportionally greater increase in mixed mass at fixed total pressure ratios.

papers.title: Quantitative characterization of oil–water occurrence states in organic-rich, high-clay, and multi-lithofacies shale reservoirs using vacuum-imbibition and two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance
papers.abstract: Quantitative characterization of oil–water occurrence states is of great significance to the evaluation of shale oil mobility and the selection of sweet spot. Chang 73 shale reservoir is characterized by organic-rich, high-clay contents and multi-lithofacies, which makes the fluid distribution and occurrence state characterization more complicated than conventional reservoirs. In this paper, the organic/inorganic porosity and saturation with different lithofacies were characterized by vacuum-imbibition experiment. Then, considering the adsorption of clay minerals and kerogen to shale oil, two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance (2D NMR) maps of each hydrogen-bearing component of three different lithofacies were established. Based on vacuum-imbibition combined with 2D NMR, a new method for calculating the contents of fluid occurrence states was proposed. The results indicate that lenticular laminated shale (LLS) and horizontal laminated shale (HLS) have higher TOC (total organic carbon) content, which results in organic porosity being greater than that of massive mudstone (MM). However, MM has a higher clay content, which leads to its inorganic porosity being higher than that of HLS and LLS. From the T1-T2 spectra, HLS and LLS are primarily composed of movable oil and movable water, while MM is mainly composed of kerogen adsorbed oil and movable water. Ad/absorbed oil content is positively correlated with TOC and clay content. High TOC and low clay content can reduce the amounts of bound water and adsorbed water, promoting the mobilization of movable oil.

papers.title: Numerical study on the impact of structural flexibility and platform motions on the dynamic behaviors and wake characteristics of floating offshore wind turbine
papers.abstract: Structural flexibility and six degrees of freedom (6-DOF) platform motions influence the dynamic behaviors and wake characteristics of the floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT). However, current quantitative studies on these effects remain insufficiently comprehensive. In this study, fluid–structure interaction simulations are conducted to investigate the impact of structural flexibility and 6-DOF motions on FOWT using the coupled computational fluid dynamics software SOWFA and turbine simulation tool OpenFAST. Various cases are analyzed, including rigid and flexible structures, as well as configurations with different DOF activated. The dynamic behaviors and wake characteristics, including rotor power, platform motions, wake velocity deficit, and vortex structures, are comprehensively compared. The results indicate that structural flexibility has a stronger impact on power reduction than 6-DOF motions, and blade flexibility has a greater overall impact compared to tower flexibility. Specifically, blade flexibility leads to a power decrease in 166.31 kW, while tower flexibility leads to 17.62 kW. Among the 6-DOF motions, pitch causes the largest power decrease in 96.06 kW. Moreover, coupling effects between different 6-DOF motions are identified, with roll motion inducing low-frequency components in sway motion, emphasizing the necessity of considering such interactions for accurate motion predictions.

papers.title: Aerodynamics of gas transport induced by buoyant releases in inclined narrow spaces: Helium–air analogous experiments
papers.abstract: When combustible buoyant gas leakage or fire occurs in a narrow space, harmful gases spread rapidly due to buoyancy, which could lead to disasters and severe injuries or fatalities. In inclined narrow spaces, buoyancy could become a significant driving force in the transport of harmful gases. This study investigates the effects of source buoyancy flux and the height difference between the buoyant release source and the downstream outlet on the transport of buoyant hazardous gases, using reduced-scale helium–air analogous experiments. Predictive models are proposed to describe the key aerodynamics properties such as downstream buoyant gas layer thickness, back-layering length upstream of the source and the outlet velocity of the downstream stratified flow. Results indicate that as the source buoyancy flux and height difference between the release source and downstream outlet increase, both downstream buoyant gas layer thickness and outlet velocity of downstream stratified flow tend to increase. The back-layering length upstream of source decreases as the height difference between the release source and downstream outlet increases. As the source buoyancy flux increases, the back-layering length upstream of source initially decreases and then increases. Relationships between these parameters and dimensionless mixing-control parameter are proposed based on experimental data. These findings help in understanding leakage-induced or fire-induced harmful buoyant gases transport in emergency scenarios and formulating personnel evacuation plans.

papers.title: Atmospheric interaction with wildland dual-fires: Flame dynamics and fire-induced flow structures
papers.abstract: Understanding the atmosphere-fire interaction is of vital importance for the fire management and fire-induced synoptic flow prediction. This work aims to reveal the mechanism of fire dynamics and its interaction with atmospheric boundary layer by considering the complex dual-fires condition that is rarely studied. Thus, the numerical simulations were performed with a detailed analysis of flame geometry, fingering structure, turbulence spectrum, Richardson (Ri) number. The results show that the flame morphological parameters changed significantly as increasing Nc number with the flame drag length reduced from 6.2 to 2.5 m and the flame inclination angle increased from 13.9° to 36.6°, especially an opposite trend of change was observed at buoyancy-driven regime when the dual-fire was considered. A lognormal distribution was indicated for fingering structure spacing, where the average spacing is between 1.4–0.9 m, which was apparently affected by dual-fires when Nc number is high. The profile of Ri also demonstrated the enhanced natural convection and the resulting forces imposed on the upstream flame for dual-fire cases, for which different fire-wind interaction mechanisms can be drawn at different magnitudes. The proper orthogonal decomposition analysis was developed to further reveal that the coherent structures in dual-fires condition were a strong perturbation of the downstream fire induced by the fire-fire interaction.

papers.title: Energy conversion analysis for behavior transition in binary droplet collision at high Weber number
papers.abstract: Studying energy conversion provides critical insights into the abnormal behavior transition from separation to coalescence following fingering (CFF) in binary droplet collisions at high Weber numbers (We). This study investigates the energy conversion dynamics of binary droplet collisions with an Ohnesorge number (Oh) of approximately 0.001 and We=30–650 through three-dimensional phase-field lattice Boltzmann simulation. Key findings reveal that the classical spreading theory [Jiang et al., “An experimental investigation on the collision behaviour of hydrocarbon droplets,” J. Fluid Mech. 234, 171–190 (1992)] leads to a significant overestimation of viscous dissipation by approximately 25% at high We, primarily due to the neglect of kinetic energy of internal flow at the spreading end point. A crucial finding reveals that the ratio of viscous dissipation rate to surface energy release rate during most of the merging stage is maintained at one-third, contrasting with the established value of one-half observed in soap film rupture studies. Based on this finding, a quantitative analysis for CFF further found that the additional dissipation caused by fingering needs to reach about onefold of the initial surface energy to cause the reflexive separation behavior to transform into coalescence behavior. Furthermore, this study attributes the low onset We of CFF in the gallium–indium–tin (GaInSn) droplets–gas system to its properties of significantly high density ratio and oscillation-induced surface tension reduction, challenging prior explanations based solely on low Oh.

papers.title: Flow and thrust characteristics of rectangular expansion–deflection nozzles
papers.abstract: To enhance the thrust performance of single-stage-to-orbit (SSTO) vehicle nozzles across wide nozzle pressure ratio (NPR) ranges while mitigating thrust degradation in annular expansion–deflection nozzles under low NPR conditions, a systematic investigation was conducted on the flow characteristics of rectangular expansion–deflection nozzles (REDNs). Numerical and experimental methods were used to investigate the flow field of the REDN under different NPR conditions and demonstrate the altitude compensation mechanism of the nozzle. The results indicate that the main factors affecting the thrust and flow characteristics of the REDN are the external airflow entering the nozzle at low-NPR conditions and the mode transition process. A higher external airflow rate into the nozzle results in a higher thrust, whereas an early mode transition reduces the thrust performance. The designed REDN has a thrust coefficient of 0.913 at NPR = 10 and 0.962 at the designed state NPR = 288.667. In addition, the thrust coefficients of the designed REDN are higher than 0.88 in the NPR range of 10–530. The effects of nozzle width and pintle sidewall deflection angle on the performance are further investigated. The results show that the nozzle width affects the NPR at which the mode transition occurs and the unit flow rate of the external air entering the nozzle. The deflection angle of the pintle sidewall has a significant influence on the operating mode of the nozzle. With excellent thrust performance over the wide range of NPRs, the REDN demonstrates the potential for application on an SSTO vehicle.

papers.title: Stable upstream swimming of a swarm of puller microswimmers
papers.abstract: Recent experiments have revealed that puller-type Janus microswimmers exhibit upstream swimming in the presence of an externally applied flow [Sharan et al., “Upstream rheotaxis of catalytic Janus spheres,” ACS Nano 16, 4599–4608 (2022)]. Previous theoretical studies had shown that hydrodynamic interactions with adjacent walls can stabilize the upstream motion of puller-type microswimmers. A thermodynamically admissible model that allows coupling fuel consumption with the swimmer's motion is used here to study a swarm. We show that hydrodynamic interactions between the swimmers in the swarm can also stabilize the upstream swimming of puller-type microswimmers. Moreover, stability is maintained for a longer time when the volume fraction of microswimmers is larger.

papers.title: Deep learning-driven physics-informed neural networks for rotating fluid flow over a vertical cylinder with Hall currents and thermal effects
papers.abstract: This paper presents a physics-informed neural network approach to solve the coupled system of partial differential equations governing the three dimensional transient flow of a rotating fluid over an infinitely long vertical cylinder in the radial direction. The flow distribution is influenced by thermal buoyancy forces, external thermal effects, and Hall currents resulting from an externally applied radial magnetic field. The study begins by transforming the governing equations of the mathematical model into their dimensionless forms using appropriate nondimensional parameters. These equations are then solved using the advanced deep learning framework known as physics-informed neural networks and validated through numerical methods. This study revels a noteworthy behavior regarding Hall current parameter, where the primary velocity initially diminishes. However, after reaching a critical value (m=0.6) at time t=3, it suddenly rises within the boundary layer region. Furthermore, we observe contrasting effects on both velocities as the rotation parameter increases, leading to a reduction in primary velocity while simultaneously enhancing secondary velocity. The skin friction coefficient in the axial direction increases by 5.80% as the Hall parameter is raised from 0.4 to 1.0, while in the θ− direction, this coefficient rises by 91.61%.

papers.title: Machine learning-based prediction of turbulent flows over backward-facing steps with varying step angles using large eddy simulation data
papers.abstract: A convolutional machine learning (ML) model was developed to predict flow fields over backward-facing steps (BFS) with varying step angles. The model was trained on flow data from three-dimensional large eddy simulations for specific step angles and tested on unseen step angles. The loss function incorporated both the mean-squared error and boundary loss to handle geometric changes. Numerical results used for ML model training were validated against experimental data, showing good agreement regarding the velocity profiles, turbulence intensity, and reattachment lengths. The ML results were consistent with the numerical results of the velocity and turbulence intensity profiles although ML model predicted a slightly delayed reattachment point due to the broader predicted flow patterns in the separation zone. Additionally, the ML model and numerical simulations exhibited similar trends in continuity and momentum. The ML results aligned well with the experimental data, albeit with a slight overprediction of the turbulence intensity. Nevertheless, the model achieved high performance and strong generalization capability across different BFS angles. Overall, it was verified that a convolutional ML model trained using a loss function that combines the mean-squared error and boundary loss can effectively predict BFS flows with varying step angles.

papers.title: Beyond primitive bionic surfaces: Bionic structures coupled surface with superhydrophobicity and programmable directional adhesion
papers.abstract: The Cassie state surface, exemplified by lotus and rice leaves, and the Wenzel state surface, exemplified by rose petals, are both superhydrophobic due to their unique structures. The objective is to expand the primitive wettability function of a single bionic structure by coupling various bionic structures in the corresponding wetting state region on an entire surface. The rice leaf–rose petal structures coupled (RRSC) aluminum surfaces were fabricated by micro-milling. The rice leaf wall substrate forms an air layer in the Cassie state. The Wenzel roughness is controlled by the rose petal crown. The RRSC surface is more hydrophobic than a single bionic surface, and it can also be programmed for adhesion and directional diffusion. An augmentation of up to 0.57° in contact angle and 3.34° in run-off angle per micrometer of rose petal crown width is exhibited. A model for identifying the wetting states on rough surfaces is developed, and the effect of two bionic structures on wetting states is analyzed quantitatively. The rose petal crown is observed to retain the air layer by impeding droplet penetration. By determining the free energy and adhesion work, the superhydrophobicity and programmable adhesion originate from the cooperative interaction and internal competition between two wetting states, respectively. This article presents a new theoretical thermodynamic model for analyzing wetting states, wettability, and adhesion on rough surfaces. The bionic structures coupled strategy is proposed to exceed the primitive wettability of bionic surfaces by coordinating natural surface characteristics in different wetting states.

papers.title: Improving dynamic mode decomposition of tandem cylinder flow with nonlinear dictionaries
papers.abstract: This paper examines algorithmic nonlinear dictionary enhancements for dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) based analysis of an industrially relevant flow problem. Several nonlinear variants of DMD are used to analyze flow interacting with two tandem cylinders in a bi-stable configuration. This study investigates the coexistence of two vortex shedding regimes, distinguished by their characteristic frequencies. Using DMD, we extract coherent structures associated with each regime and consider their relation to surface pressure and far-field noise at these frequencies. Simultaneous experimental measurements of velocity fields, unsteady surface pressure, and far-field acoustic pressure are performed using high-speed particle image velocimetry, a remote microphone technique, and a far-field microphone. Two DMD algorithms are applied to investigate the flow. First, we apply kernelized extended DMD to demonstrate how a nonlinear dictionary can improve modal reliability compared with the usual linear alternative. The extracted modes are validated by analyzing their modal residuals, which are further used to explore phenomena at other frequencies and harmonics while examining the impact of dictionary depth and characteristics. Second, we study the flow physics of each shedding frequency via the Rigged DMD algorithm, which provides detailed spectral insights for dynamical systems with continuous spectra. A new kernelized Rigged DMD is introduced, showing improved accuracy in resolving generalized eigenfunctions and spectral measures compared to linear dictionaries.

papers.title: Erratum: “Numerical study on the flow characteristics of a start supersonic inlet using direct numerical simulation” [Phys. Fluids 37 , 036131 (2025)]
Impact of ladle plug clogging on multiphase flow and refining efficiency in ladle furnace
papers.abstract: Ladle plug clogging, a widespread challenge in ladle refining, profoundly influences various stages of the process. However, existing numerical simulations and water model experiments primarily assume an idealized non-clogging condition, posing a significant constraint on the comprehensive understanding and optimization of refining operations. This study comprehensively investigates the impact of porous plugs on refining efficiency under various clogging conditions, with a focus on gas–liquid flow, mixing time, and slag eye behavior to establish a full-size three-dimensional mathematical model of 135 t ladle and offers practical solutions to mitigate the negative effects. A 1:4 water model experiments were carried out to verify the accuracy of mathematical models. The results indicate that plug clogging influences refining efficiency by altering the initial bubble characteristics. As the degree of clogging increases, the initial bubble diameter distribution shifts toward larger diameters. The overall stirring energy is reduced by approximate 10%, and the axial velocity in the slag-molten steel interface and bubble plume area is significantly reduced. At flow rates of 300 and 450 NL/min, mixing time exhibits a positive correlation with the degree of clogging. However, when the flow rate increases to 600 NL/min, mixing time fluctuates unpredictably with clogging severity. When the initial flow rates are 300 and 450 NL/min, following clogging, increasing the flow rate to 600 NL/min may offset the negative impact of congestion on mixing time. Post-clogging, the slag eye area decreases by up to 18%, and the instability in slag eye fluctuation increases with higher clogging severity. This mathematical model can also be employed to investigate the clogging issues of slot-type plugs.

papers.title: Compact elastic mooring configurations for semi-sub wind platforms
papers.abstract: A compact mooring configuration for a semi-sub platform with an inelastic vertical cable connected to inclined elastic cables anchored to the sea bed is tested using an efficient hydrodynamic/mooring/wind thrust model. The elastic stiffness is determined by the tension in the upper cable to satisfy the maximum strain constraint (20% for nylon). The established 15 MW Volturn platform in 200 m of water is used as a test case. The maximum excursions, important for electric cable efficacy, and tensions occur at rated wind speed giving maximum thrust. The smallest excursions and tensions occur with the cables' connection point near the platform base and they increase as this point is lowered to about 20 m from the bed, but excursions remain within acceptable limits. Reducing anchor footprint diameter reduces surge excursion and increases heave excursion slightly; maximum tension in the upper cable also decreases while tension in the lower elastic cables reduce markedly. It is demonstrated that compact configurations minimizing water column obstruction are a practical option, but the optimum configuration depends on many factors.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic interaction and energy-saving mechanisms of two three-dimensional parallel swimmers with synchronous and asynchronous undulation
papers.abstract: The hydrodynamic performance and wake structures of three-dimensional (3D) fish are distinct from those of two-dimensional (2D) models. To reveal the hydrodynamic interaction and energy-saving mechanism of 3D fish school, this study numerically simulated swimming of two 3D parallel fish, using a robust ghost cell method. The hydrodynamic benefits and wake structures were examined under different transverse spacings, Strouhal numbers, and phase differences. The results showed that the swimming efficiency at a narrow spacing was enhanced by 33.8% compared with the single-fish case. It can be further enhanced by 15.4% in the anti-phase undulation compared to the in-phase state. The critical spacing where the apparent hydrodynamic benefit occurs is wider than that obtained in 2D simulations because the vortex row induced by transverse velocity can obliquely approach that generated by the adjacent fish. The thrust enhancement can be attributed to the channeling effect in the general synchronous and asynchronous undulations. This channeling effect occurs in the wake centerline instead of in the gap between the two fish bodies in the 2D simulations. The wake is redirected downstream in the streamwise direction owing to the transverse obstruction, which strengthens the thrust. Additionally, vertical expansion with vorticity dissipation can be induced, compromising the channeling effect. Both the channeling effect and vertical expansion are more significant at narrower spacings and higher Strouhal numbers. Notably, the wall effect contributes to the thrust enhancement in the antiphase undulation. Also, the disorderly small-scale vortex contrails appearing in other phase states are not observed, further improving thrust.

papers.title: Coal damage and failure from shaped charge blasting with an empty hole under high ground stress
papers.abstract: The effectiveness and safety of blasting operations used to increase gas permeability in the coal seam are compromised by the high crustal stress in deep coal mining. In order to increase the effectiveness of blasting cracking and reflection enhancement of coal seams, the crack propagation law and damage characteristics of high ground stress coal bodies under the action of shaped charge blasting coupled with empty holes are studied through the method of theoretical analysis combined with blasting simulation tests. The results demonstrate that shaped charge blasting can generate a directional cutting impact on coal via shaped charge jets, improve the efficiency of explosive energy utilization, and focus energy in a particular direction. The free surface impact from the void amplifies damage and promotes crack propagation in the coal body over a distance. In the blasting simulation experiment, elevated ground stress results in the re-compaction of the ruptured fissure, especially when the coal body undergoes significant crushing from standard blasting methods. Shaped charge blasting with vacant holes yields an average damage value that is 1.26 times and 2.1 times larger than that of conventional blasting, as determined by damage assessments by resistivity and ultrasonic wave velocity measurements. The results of this study have significant social consequences for safeguarding mining production safety. Theoretical and experimental principles are established to enhance the permeability of coal seams subjected to elevated ground stress, augment blasting efficiency, and optimize blasthole use.

papers.title: Prediction of fine particle retention at the pore-scale using deep learning
papers.abstract: In subsurface flow, the transport and retention of fine particles often lead to pore blockage and reduced permeability, posing significant challenges. This alteration of pore space can occur in various fields, including pollutant transport, geothermal systems, underground carbon and hydrogen storage, and subsurface energy systems. The conventional pore scale modeling approach for predicting particle deposition in porous media is too time consuming. Thus, the deep machine learning approach, for the first time, is implemented to predict the transport and retention of fine particles in subsurface flow. Two deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures built on an encoder-decoder framework (i.e., autoencoder and U-Net) are implemented to predict deposition patterns within porous media. An Eulerian–Lagrangian computational fluid dynamics (CFD) scheme is employed to predict particle retention at the pore scale and create a large dataset, composed of 16 000 training porous media images, 3000 validation images, and 500 testing images. The evaluation metrics of similarity index (SSIM) provide a quantifiable measure for comparing predicted against ground truth porous media images, derived from pore-scale simulations. The precision of these deep learning approaches in predicting reservoir properties due to fines deposition is highlighted by SSIM accuracy metrics of 0.93 and 0.95 for the autoencoder and U-Net, and R-squared values of 0.93 and 0.72 for porosity and permeability for the autoencoder, and 0.97 and 0.88 for the U-Net, respectively. This evaluation enhances the credibility and predictive efficiency of these machine learning models in forecasting porosity and permeability alterations caused by fine particle migration.

papers.title: Aluminum particle combustion dynamics and critical conditions in solid rocket motors
papers.abstract: To elucidate aluminum particle combustion behaviors and establish the critical conditions for efficient combustion within solid rocket motors, this study develops a numerical simulation framework utilizing the Eulerian–Lagrangian method and the detailed aluminum combustion model. The proposed model incorporates convective heat transfer, phase transitions, detailed combustion processes of aluminum particles, and heat/mass transfer interactions between particles and the gas phase. Validation of the numerical model was achieved by comparing the simulated condensed-phase particle size distribution at the nozzle exit. Subsequently, comprehensive numerical analyses were performed for representative configurations, systematically examining distributions of gas-phase temperature, species concentrations, particle temperature, and alumina mass fraction throughout the combustion chamber, nozzle, and plume regions. Specifically, the effects of aluminum particle initial diameter, particle injection location, and motor dimensions on particle evolution characteristics and combustion efficiency were explored. Results reveal notable radial temperature and species concentration gradients attributed to dispersed aluminum particle combustion. Particles injected from the front and rear end-faces of grain exhibit prolonged residence times and correspondingly higher combustion efficiencies, whereas particles introduced along the inner port demonstrate reduced efficiency as axial injection distance increases. Additionally, this study investigates the influences of combustion chamber size and pressure on particle combustion dynamics, highlighting the critical role of motor characteristic length in determining particle residence time and combustion efficiency. A practical criterion enabling rapid estimation of aluminum particle combustion efficiency is proposed. The outcomes presented herein offer valuable insights for the efficient evaluation of aluminum combustion in solid rocket motors, facilitating improved motor design and optimization practices.

papers.title: Physics-informed super-resolution and forecasting method based on inaccurate partial differential equations and partial observation
papers.abstract: Physics-informed machine learning has emerged as a promising approach for modeling physical systems. However, real-world applications often face significant challenges due to the limitations of partial observations and inaccuracies in governing partial differential equations (PDEs). In this work, we propose a novel physics-informed machine learning method named Physics-Informed method based on Inaccurate PDEs and Partial Observation (PIPO), to overcome the above two challenges under the real-world scenario, which aims to address the problems of super-resolution and forecasting simultaneously in physical systems characterized by partial observations and inaccurate PDEs. The proposed method is motivated by two key considerations. First, despite the inherent inaccuracy of PDEs, the differential terms (such as diffusion and advection terms) contain valuable information that can effectively reduce the hypothesis space, thereby enhancing the model's generalization capability. Second, while the data only provides partial observations, it offers crucial supervised constraints at the observed points. These constraints not only facilitate model optimization but also help prevent the degeneracy of PDE loss, where the PDE loss could yield multiple solutions. PIPO integrates an interpolator, encoder, forecaster, decoder, and parameters learner, which are jointly optimized using data loss and PDE losses to reconstruct high-resolution states and forecast future states using only partial observation data and inaccurate PDEs. We leverage the proposed PIPO method to address a real-world problem in air pollutant concentration fields and wind fields, specifically PM2.5 transport dynamics, which are governed by the advection-diffusion equation with unknown diffusion coefficients and the source term. The results in super-resolution reconstruction, forecasting, and multi-hour forecasting highlight the effectiveness of PIPO in capturing complex spatial and temporal dynamics despite the limitations of partial observations and inaccurate PDEs.

papers.title: Hydrodynamics and flow field of a 6:1 prolate spheroid in maneuvering state: Numerical simulation and experimental investigation
papers.abstract: To address the critical issue of hydrodynamic and flow field dynamic response in predicting the maneuverability of underwater vehicles, a hydrodynamic analysis method for maneuvering motion is developed, utilizing numerical simulation and comparison with towed pool tests, focusing on a 6:1 prolate spheroid as the subject of investigation. The dynamic pressure response of a prolate spheroid subjected to pure sway, pure yaw, and coupled sway-yaw motions (including in-phase coupling, IPC, and quadrature-phase coupling, QPC) is systematically examined through experimental validation of an adapted novel horizontal motion mechanism, revealing the correlation between the peaks and troughs of pressure coefficients and the flow field structure. The results indicate that (i) hydrodynamic variations under pure sway, pure yaw, and IPC conditions exhibit a notable positive correlation, in which IPC amplifies the angle-of-attack effect via phase synchronization. (ii) The QPC condition demonstrates distinct nonlinear hydrodynamic properties resulting from the periodic disruption of the yaw-induced vortex structure by the sway motion: the pressure differential is positively correlated with yaw amplitude and negatively correlated with sway amplitude, while the peak-to-valley pressure difference increases sharply with a sudden frequency change (0.3 Hz). (iii) The flow separation method mainly influences the disparity in pressure response; the IPC condition is likely to generate significant transient shock loads, whereas the QPC condition emphasizes the nonlinear effects of motion coupling. The research findings establish a theoretical foundation for modeling fluid–solid interactions in underwater vehicle maneuvers.

papers.title: Velocity responses of the supersonic turbulent boundary layer to streamwise vortices
papers.abstract: Velocity responses of the supersonic turbulent boundary layer to streamwise vortices are experimentally investigated. A vortex-induced S-shaped boundary layer deformation is observed, characterized by upwash-side thickening and downwash-side thinning. Quantitative analysis further reveals velocity deficits in the upwash region and enhancements in the downwash region. However, an unexpected near-wall acceleration adjacent to the location of maximum boundary layer thickness on the upwash side is clearly visualized, which has been seldom presented before. The velocity deficits and enhancements cause the velocity profiles to lie above and below the undisturbed profiles, respectively. Moreover, the velocity profiles on the upwash side exhibit greater sensitivity to the vortex-to-plate distance than the downwash-side profiles. Results show that the turbulent boundary layer retains its stratified characteristics despite the impact of vortex.

papers.title: Critical instability characteristics and crack propagation process of sandstone containing two non-connected fissures under uniaxial compression
papers.abstract: Fissures, the weakest components in jointed rock masses, always reduce overall strength, induce stress concentration, and ultimately undermine stability. The study combines acoustic emission (AE) and digital image correlation techniques to monitor the critical instability and damage process of defective sandstone under uniaxial compression. As the inclination angle (α) of fissure ① increases, the average peak strength and elastic modulus rise accordingly. α has pronounced influence on crack type and number, with the Gaussian mixture model revealing that shear cracks gradually decrease while tensile cracks increase with increasing α, indicating a transformation from shear failure to tensile failure. The ratio of rise angle (RA) to average frequency (AF) was more sensitive to microcracks and exhibited better anti-interference capabilities against attenuated AE signals. Both a sudden increase in the coefficient of RA/AF variation and a sudden decrease in the b value can be identified as precursor information for sandstone failure. Based on the critical slowing down theory, the autocorrelation coefficient shows stronger early warning capability than variance, while the critical damage precursor point (D point) determined by energy variance significantly lags behind the stable crack propagation stage. Compared to amplitude, RA, RA/AF, and energy, peak frequency demonstrates the highest sensitivity and timeliness in responding to rock failure precursors. Besides, as α increases, the interaction of strain field between the two fissures transforms from symmetry to asymmetry, influencing crack propagation patterns. This study deepens the understanding of the relevant standards for damage evolution and failure precursors of defective rocks in engineering applications.

papers.title: Research on sediment erosion and jet flow characteristics of Pelton turbine's injector
papers.abstract: The Pelton turbine frequently operates in environments characterized by high head and heavy sedimentation, where the flow containing sediments can cause erosion on the surfaces of flow components, affecting the stability and safety of the unit. To investigate this phenomenon, present study applies the standard k-ε turbulence model and the Discrete Phase Model to conduct a three-phase unsteady numerical simulation of flow with sediment. The straight pipe erosion simulation results align with previous experimental findings, verifying the accuracy of the methods employed herein. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) Severe erosion predominantly occurs at the spray needle and nozzle outlet. The maximum velocity is achieved at the nozzle outlet. There is a “velocity deficit zone” at the needle tip, which can somewhat protect the tip from erosion. (2) Increasing opening (ΔS) reduces internal flow velocity, decreasing sediment transport capacity and erosion severity. The erosion rate at ΔS = 0.62 decreased by about 95% compared to ΔS = 0.07. (3) An increase in sediment concentration CV enhances the interaction between particles and the surface, leading to severe erosion at both the needle and nozzle. The erosion rate at CV = 5% is about 2.5 times that at CV = 1%. Additionally, sediments with smaller diameters and lower densities exhibit better flowability, resulting in more severe erosion on the injector. (4) Analysis results from machine learning (XGBoost) reveal that sediment concentration, diameter, and nozzle opening affect erosion more significantly than sediment density. The results can provide some guidance for the safety maintenance and erosion prediction of Pelton turbine.

papers.title: Experimental investigation of vortex-induced flow field dynamics in oscillating water column converters with various front wall drafts
papers.abstract: Oscillating water column (OWC) converters represent a promising technology for wave energy extraction, with the flow dynamics playing a critical role in optimizing their performance. This study employs particle image velocimetry to investigate the vortex-induced flow field dynamics in an OWC wave energy converter with various front wall drafts. The effects of the front wall draft on water surface amplitude, vortex evolution, and oscillation patterns are analyzed under various wave periods, highlighting the decisive role of vortices near the front wall. The results reveal that increasing draft reduces water surface amplitude, particularly under short-period wave conditions. A strengthening leeward vortex is observed with increasing draft, contributing to enhanced mixing and turbulence near the front wall. The influence of front wall draft variations on the oscillation patterns is more pronounced under short-period wave conditions, while the impact diminishes for longer wave periods. The increasing front wall draft leads to an increased proportion of outflow near the front wall and decreased inflow in the deeper region. These findings provide crucial insights into the mechanisms by which draft variations impact OWC performance, offering a framework for the design and optimization of OWC converters.

papers.title: Fluid–structure interactions of a high-aspect-ratio flexible wing in steady and unsteady flows
papers.abstract: The aeroelastic stability of high-aspect-ratio flexible wings constitutes a fundamental challenge in aerospace engineering, where flutter phenomena impose critical limitations on the aerodynamic performance and structural safety. To investigate these fundamental fluid–structure interaction mechanisms, we present an experimental study focusing on a flexible cantilever wing with a beam-shell elastic structure (aspect ratio = 7.5). The wind tunnel investigation systematically examines both steady and unsteady flow conditions across Reynolds numbers ranging from 3.54×104 to 1.53×105 and angles of attack (α) from 0° to 22°. The structural deformations and the corresponding flow field are measured simultaneously by distributed strain gauges and fiber Bragg grating sensors and particle image velocimetry, respectively. The results show that aeroelastic behavior is strongly depended on α and wind speed. At a low α (0°–5°), as the wind speed increases, the flexible wing transitions sequentially through (1) no limit cycle oscillation (no LCO) regime, (2) unsteady amplitude LCO regime, (3) classical flutter, and ultimately (4) stall flutter, while at a higher α (5°–20°), the wing transits directly from (1) no LCO regime to (4) stall flutter. Classical flutter results from interactions between the coupled bending-torsion mode and fluid mode, characterized by periodic shedding of vortex pairs in the wake with a shedding frequency of fv*=1.29, which exhibits strong frequency synchronization with the structural coupled bending-torsion (fh**=fθ*=1.31). Conversely, stall flutter arises from coupling between the torsional mode and fluid mode, dominated by periodic shedding of leading-edge vortices and trailing-edge vortices at fv*=1.49, which is locked to the torsional frequency (fθ*=1.53). Gust-induced structural divergence mechanisms before stall flutter exhibit distinct characteristics. At α=0°, both bending and torsional instabilities contribute to the structural divergence with the delayed onset of stall flutter, whereas at α=12°, pure torsional instability triggers immediate divergent vibrations.

papers.title: Exploiting high gas content in lubricants to enhance drag reduction on lubricant-infused surfaces
papers.abstract: Lubricant-infused surfaces (LISs) have emerged as an innovative technology to reduce frictional drag between fluids and solids. Recent studies proposed that a nanoscale gas layer at the lubricant–working fluid interface is crucial for high drag reduction (DR) of LISs. However, most previous studies have focused on inducing bubble nucleation by controlling gas concentration in the working fluid. This study proposes a new approach to leverage the inherently high gas content of lubricants. A new LIS, denoted as PiCCS, was fabricated by infusing a gas-rich lubricant, 1-bromoheptadecafluorooctane (PFOB), into a carbon nanotube (CNT)-coated surface. The micro-/nanoscale hierarchical structures formed by coating CNTs imparted high photothermal and hydrophobic properties, enabling rapid surface heating under solar irradiation while repelling water droplets. The fabricated PiCCS was compared to a silicone oil (SO2)-infused surface with an identical viscosity but significantly lower gas content. X-ray micro-imaging was employed to directly visualize microscale bubble formation at the PFOB–water interface with increasing temperature. In channel flow experiments, PiCCS achieved up to 50% DR, outperforming SO2-infused control surface under identical conditions. This study shows that the gas content of the infused lubricant, alongside temperature elevation, plays a pivotal role in enhancing DR. Therefore, the use of a gas-rich lubricant in LISs with temperature regulation might offer effective DR beyond conventional LISs, paving the way for effective drag reduction across diverse applications.

papers.title: Time-dependent diffusion in one-dimensional disordered media decorated by permeable membranes: Theoretical findings backed by simulations and a new disorder class
papers.abstract: As the diffusion of fluids is hindered by semipermeable membranes, the long-time behavior of the diffusion coefficient is influenced by the arrangement of the membranes. We develop methods that predict this long-time instantaneous diffusivity from bulk diffusivity, the membranes' locations, and their permeabilities. We studied this problem theoretically and expressed the instantaneous diffusivity analytically as an infinite sum. An independent numerical scheme was employed. Several types of disorder in the membranes' positions were considered including a new disorder family that generalizes hyperuniform and short-range disorders. Our theoretical and numerical findings are in excellent agreement. Our methods provide an alternative means for studying time-dependent diffusion processes.

papers.title: Effects of a top opening on pressure transients caused by the high-speed train passing through the enclosed noise barrier
papers.abstract: Enclosed noise barriers have been gradually applied in railway engineering owing to their excellent noise reduction performance. However, when a high-speed train passes through an enclosed noise barrier, significant pressure transients are generated because the walls of the barrier restrict the flow of the internal air. These pressure transients can adversely affect both the structural safety of the train and noise barrier. The present study proposes a pressure relief scheme featuring an opening at the top to mitigate the pressure transients within the enclosed noise barrier.
