(3) A degradation model coupling AE cumulative ringing count and stress under different dry–wet cycles was established based on a continuous damage mechanics theory. These findings provide a scientific reference for understanding the mechanical behavior of tuff under dry–wet cycling and provide theoretical support for engineering safety and slope disaster prevention.

papers.title: Advances in multiscale numerical simulation of gas–liquid two-phase flows in liquid metals
papers.abstract: The gas–liquid two-phase flow of liquid metals has important applications in extreme industrial scenarios such as nuclear reactor cooling, aerospace thermal control, and additive manufacturing. However, its complex gas–liquid interface dynamics, coupling of phase change heat transfer, and interactions among multiple physical fields pose challenges to traditional numerical methods. This review comprehensively surveys recent advances of multiscale numerical simulations in this field, covering macroscopic, mesoscopic, and microscopic scale methods. At the macroscopic scale, the improvements and optimizations of the finite volume method, finite difference method, and custom numerical algorithms in phase interface tracking, porous medium coupling, and complex boundary treatment are analyzed with emphasis. At the mesoscopic scale, the mesoscopic modeling methods for the coupling of gas–liquid phase change heat transfer in porous media and microchannels are discussed. At the microscopic scale, the latest achievements of interface dynamics and molecular scale simulations are summarized. The limitations of current research are further analyzed, including issues such as insufficient accuracy of porous medium modeling, large errors in phase change heat transfer models, and limited ability to analyze interface dynamics. This review proposes future research directions: developing high-precision interface and phase-change models, achieving multiscale-method coupling, and optimizing numerical algorithms through machine-learning integration. It aims to offer theoretical references and technical support for the multiscale simulation of gas–liquid two-phase flow in liquid metals.

papers.title: Three-dimensional characterization of autoignition kernel development under varied jet velocity and coflow temperature conditions
papers.abstract: This study utilizes three-dimensional (3D) tomographic CH* chemiluminescence imaging to characterize the spatiotemporal evolution of autoignition kernels in turbulent jet-in-hot-coflow (JHC) configurations, with particular focus on kernel morphology and growth dynamics under varying thermo-kinetic conditions. By implementing the multiplicative algebraic reconstruction technique (MART) for 3D flame tomography, we systematically quantified autoignition kernel growth dynamics across parametric variations in fuel jet velocity (93–186 m/s) and coflow temperature (923–1311 K), while maintaining constant coflow oxygen concentration. The tomographic reconstruction enables extraction of five fundamental ignition kernel characteristics: (1) morphokinetic parameters including volumetric expansion rates and 3D three-component (3D3C) velocity vector fields; (2) geometric evolution metrics quantifying principal axis development; and (3) combustion topology descriptors comprising flame surface density (FSD) distributions and reaction progress variable (RPV) gradient fields. The experimental results reveal two distinct thermo-kinetic modulation regimes: (1) a 40%–50% reduction in volumetric expansion rate with increasing jet velocity (93→147 m/s, 147→186 m/s) due to enhanced turbulent dissipation, and (2) a 70% growth rate enhancement under coflow temperature elevation (923→1311 K) through Arrhenius-dominated kinetics. The analysis reveals that, among the extracted 3D kernel properties, the co-varying trends of FSD and RPV quantitatively manifest the coupled effects of coflow temperature and jet velocity on kernel growth dynamics, demonstrating 3D morphology descriptors (FSD/RPV) as robust indicators for kernel evolution mechanisms.

papers.title: Tail cavity kinematic characteristics and in-tube pressure behavior induced by pressure difference and pressure ratio
papers.abstract: The development of the tail cavity is recognized as a critical factor affecting motion stability during vehicle water-exit. Investigations on tail cavity evolution and in-tube pressure characteristics under varying conditions are essential for water-exit studies. Based on experimental studies of high-pressure gas-ejected vehicles during water-exit, research was conducted on free water-exit tail cavity evolution and in-tube pressure characteristics under varying front pressure, pressure difference, and pressure ratio conditions. The pull-off formation mechanism of the tail cavity was revealed to be jointly influenced by the entrainment effects of starting vortices and necking effects during vehicle axial motion. Results indicate that tail cavity development was found to be influenced by two competing mechanisms: reentrant jet suppression effects and environmental pressure enhancement effects. Specifically, increased front pressure was observed to elevate vehicle velocity while intensifying in-tube pressure oscillations. Vehicle velocity showed a negative correlation with pressure ratio but a positive correlation with pressure difference. A positive correlation was also identified with gas average flow velocity in the gas chamber. When either pressure difference or pressure ratio was maintained constant, equivalent changes in pressure difference demonstrated a greater impact on vehicle motion velocity compared to pressure ratio adjustments.

papers.title: A soft particle collision model based on the immersed boundary method for smooth strictly convex bodies
papers.abstract: A novel collision model for strictly convex particles in granular flows is presented. The model is implemented into the framework of a sharp interface immersed boundary method with unstructured triangular immersed boundary grid systems. The points of common normals among different particles are calculated with a hybrid distance calculation algorithm. Stability problems arising from the flatness of the grid faces are mitigated by smoothing the motion of the contact points over discrete time, utilizing quadratic Bézier surfaces. The model is validated using existing experimental data, and our comprehensive comparative analysis illustrates a more accurate distribution of the resting points for naturally shaped convex particles relative to ellipsoidal particles. The findings of this study reveal that the realistic approximation of the particle shapes significantly enhances the accuracy of the collision model's simulation results.

papers.title: Numerical research and experiment on the thermal protection characteristics of opposing jets for rudder leading edge
papers.abstract: During the flight of hypersonic aircraft, severe aerodynamic heating occurs at critical regions such as the nose and the leading edge of rudders, presenting significant challenges to the design of hypersonic vehicles. This paper systematically investigates the flow field characteristics and aerodynamic force/heat properties of the leading edge of a hypersonic aircraft's air rudder with active jet cooling, employing numerical simulations and experimental studies. The thermal protection mechanism of the multi-hole opposing jet at the rudder leading edge is explored by varying the position, spacing, and sweep angle of the jet holes. The thermal protection effectiveness under different jet total pressure ratios is also experimentally validated, providing critical data references for engineering applications. The results demonstrate that, under a constant jet total pressure ratio, a larger sweep angle enhances the cooling effectiveness of the jet, and the effective cooling length exhibits a quadratic relationship with the sweep angle. At a sweep angle of 60°, the jet hole position closer to the flat plate wall slightly enhances overall cooling performance but may intensify localized overheating upstream of the jet hole. Increasing the spacing between jet holes expands the effective cooling length for a constant position of the bottom jet hole while reducing the localized heat mitigation effect upstream of the holes. This study reveals that dual-hole configurations provide a cooling effect more than twice that of single-hole systems. It reveals that the cooling effect becomes more pronounced with higher total jet pressure ratios, but the efficiency ratio decreases.

papers.title: Existence and characteristics of soliton-like coherent structures in a transitional mixing layer
papers.abstract: Laminar-to-turbulent transition in shear flow can be complicated and may follow many possible routes. The scenario based on the soliton-like coherent structure (SCS) [Lee and Wu, “Transition in wall-bounded flows,” Appl. Mech. Rev. 61, 030802 (2008)] has drawn much attention to the role of hairpin vortices and their origin. This Letter reports the existence of such SCSs in a compressible mixing layer and explores how their interactions with the background shear flow generate streamwise vorticity. Lagrangian particle tracking based on direct numerical simulation data is employed to trace the dynamic evolution of such structures. Evidence shows that localized three-dimensional waves travel coherently during the early transition stage, in good agreement with the behavior of SCSs in boundary layer transition. Through visualization of disturbance amplification and statistical analysis of locally distributed high-strain rate regions, it is suggested that SCSs originate from local oblique resonance effects in mixing layers, with the motion of these structures along the mean shear flow contributing to the generation of hairpin vortices.

papers.title: Tunable droplet generation with particle suspension via impact on lubricant-infused surfaces
papers.abstract: Conventional droplet generation techniques often rely on complex nozzle-based systems that demand precise actuation, sophisticated fabrication, and suffer from clogging issues under high particle mass-loading, making them unsuitable for particle-laden applications and cost-sensitive settings. In this study, we present a passive, low-cost method to generate tunable daughter droplets through the partial rebound of a macro-droplet impacting a lubricant-infused surface (LIS). The method enables the formation of a protruded liquid column that pinches off into sister droplets without requiring external actuation. The size and outcome of the generated droplets are controlled by varying the Weber number. Systematic experiments and simulations are conducted to elucidate the retraction dynamics and pinch-off behavior. The proposed approach enables droplet generation with a wide range of volumes ranging from tens of nanoliters to microliters, well below the capillary length and high particle mass-loading (up to 30% w/w) with 5 μm particles, overcoming limitations of nozzle-based and patterned surface methods. This study introduces a novel LIS-assisted droplet generation using nonfluorinated, soot-based LIS, which enhances economic and environmental viability along with potential applications in printing, biochemical assays, and material synthesis, particularly in resource-limited environments.

papers.title: A modified theoretical model coupled with the nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) for performance prediction of centrifugal pumps
papers.abstract: The accuracy of theoretical models for performance curve prediction has been a persistent challenge, particularly when operating conditions deviate from the rated values. Furthermore, improving the prediction accuracy for centrifugal pumps remains a focal point in this field of research. This research proposes a novel theoretical model that employs the energy-flow variation theory to derive the characteristic curve equation for centrifugal pumps. By utilizing the nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II for multi-objective optimization, the model optimizes the coefficients in the theoretical model, enabling precise calculation of the performance curves for head, power, and efficiency. Notably, the proposed model offers enhanced generality and effectiveness as it is not restricted by the geometric parameters of the pump's overcurrent components. Experimental validation was conducted on two centrifugal pumps with specific speeds of 64.1 and 128.2, yielding mean absolute relative errors of 1.44% and 0.59% for head, 2.9% and 4.13% for power, and 6.41% and 3.91% for efficiency, respectively. This research significantly contributes to the field of pump performance prediction models, aligning well with the requirements of engineering practice.

papers.title: Wind-induced response characteristics of reduced-scale aeroelastic models for cooling towers: Comparative analysis of shell model and beam-net model
papers.abstract: Wind tunnel testing of aeroelastic models is a widely adopted approach for evaluating the wind-induced response characteristics of cooling towers. Two primary similarity methods for modeling the aeroelastic behavior of cooling towers are the Continuous Shell (CS) model and the Equivalent Beam-Net (EBN) model. The CS model is a replica that simulates reduced-scale stiffness and mass by using isotropic, continuous materials with density, and Poisson's ratio similar to those of concrete. The EBN model simulates reduced-scale stiffness using spatially arranged orthogonal beams and replicates the mass and aerodynamic configuration by incorporating additional lumped mass blocks and an elastic membrane over the beam-net framework. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the design methodologies for both types of aeroelastic models and compares their wind-induced response characteristics. The results show that wind-induced background responses are predominant in the CS model, while resonant responses are more pronounced in the EBN model. This is mainly because the natural frequencies of the CS model are significantly higher and beyond the effective frequency range of the turbulent flow generated in the boundary layer wind tunnel, thereby limiting the excitation of resonant modes. Conversely, the frequency ratio of the EBN model to its prototype structure can be adjusted by altering the width and thickness of the orthogonal beams, allowing its natural frequencies to align with the effective frequency range of turbulence flow in the wind tunnel. Additionally, both field measurements and numerical simulations confirm the existence of distinct resonance components in the wind-induced fluctuating response of cooling towers.

papers.title: Manipulation of surface pressure fluctuations for a tandem symmetric airfoil configuration using the trailing-edge treatments
papers.abstract: Noise pollution is a critical issue in urban and industrial areas, particularly those near airports. This study experimentally investigated brush and serration edge treatments as passive methods to control wake-leading-edge interaction noise in a tandem symmetric airfoil configuration using surface-mounted unsteady pressure sensors in a subsonic wind tunnel. Surface pressure fluctuations, a key source of aerodynamic noise, were examined on the rear airfoil surface at a relatively low angle of attack and a Reynolds number of 185,000. The results demonstrate that the brush increases the surface pressure fluctuation power spectral density (PSD) levels at low frequencies, whereas its performance at medium and high frequencies varies depending on the relative positioning of the airfoils. The highest PSD reduction (up to 5.5 dB) was achieved when the downstream airfoil leading-edge was aligned with the upstream airfoil chord line. In contrast, the serration performs satisfactorily at low frequencies for negative vertical distances between the rear airfoil leading-edge and the front airfoil trailing-edge (yg < 0); however, its effectiveness is minimal for positive distances, except when the rear airfoil leading-edge aligns with the front airfoil chord line, where it performs optimally. Although serration can sometimes increase PSD levels, it generally reduces pressure fluctuations over a broader frequency range than the brush. Both treatments can be effective for wake-leading-edge interaction noise control, particularly in configurations where the downstream airfoil leading-edge aligns with the upstream airfoil chord line, providing valuable insights for mitigating aerodynamic noise in practical applications.

papers.title: A coupled non-saturated model for cohesionless sediment transport
papers.abstract: A continuous formulation and a suitable finite element numerical method are introduced for simulating interactions between fluid flow and evolving bedforms. Sediment transport is modeled by solving the non-equilibrium saltation dynamics of non-cohesive grains. The approach integrates the Navier–Stokes equations for incompressible fluid flow, a conservation equation to track the evolution of the fluid–solid interface, and mass and momentum equations governing sediment dynamics. The latter conservation laws are depth-integrated over the saltation layer, resulting in a reduced-dimensional framework that improves computational efficiency. A built-in explicit procedure enables a straightforward two-way coupling between sediment and fluid dynamics. To stabilize flow computations and ensure the positivity of key variables, such as saltation layer density and sediment thickness, the numerical algorithm is a non-oscillatory finite element method; its positive definite characteristic is essential for flows in combined erodible/non-erodible scenarios. Numerical experiments assess the model response for transient conditions, including wind tunnel environments and sand dune–atmospheric boundary layer interactions. Among other features, test setups are designed to explore the advantages of the proposed model under severe transient conditions in comparison with the results of standard saturated flow based models.

papers.title: Computational study of electrohydrodynamic regimes on planar films
papers.abstract: Two-phase flow can be affected under sufficiently strong electric fields, giving rise to various electrohydrodynamic (EHD) regimes. Among these, the formation of Taylor cones at curved (meniscus) interfaces is one of the most prominent and well-studied phenomena. However, EHD regimes emerging from planar interfaces remain less explored, particularly in liquid–liquid systems, where interfacial deformations become significantly more complex. In these systems, cone structures form along dimple rims, and Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities occur under specific conditions. This work presents a numerical investigation of the diverse structures formed at planar liquid–liquid interfaces under varying conditions. Numerical results reveal that viscous forces initially dominate the interface deformation; however, as the Taylor cone elongates, inertial forces become significant, indicating that EHD shear stress alone cannot deform the liquid film interface. Instead, the normal EHD force is primarily responsible for the observed deformation. Moreover, this study revealed that onset voltage and conductivity ratio are critical factors influencing interfacial deformation. Higher electric fields accelerate the development of Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities, leading to more pronounced surface perturbations. Conversely, elevated conductivity in the suspending medium facilitates the formation of dimples at the interface. These findings shed light on the intricate interplay between electric fields, fluid properties, and interfacial dynamics, contributing to a deeper understanding of EHD-flow behaviors at planar interfaces.

papers.title: Simulation of multi-fracture interference and optimization of stimulated reservoir volume in layered shale using finite element and response surface method
papers.abstract: Staged multi-cluster fracturing in horizontal wells is essential for developing shale oil reservoirs. The stress shadow caused by competitive fracture propagation and bedding interactions is highly complex. A three-dimensional flow-stress-damage coupled numerical model based on the finite element method was developed. It is used to simulate the non-planar propagation behavior and stimulated reservoir volume (SRV) of hydraulic fractures (HFs) when they encounter bedding planes. The HFs may experience arrest, deflection, penetration, and combined bifurcation under different conditions such as cluster spacing, number of clusters, in situ stress, bedding tensile strength, and construction factors in layered shale. The response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to analyze the sensitivity and coupling effects on SRV and identify optimal parameter combinations. The results indicate that the bedding structure and stress interference lead to transverse asymmetric propagation. Intermediate fractures tend to deflect or arrest due to stress superposition, while adjacent fractures commonly exhibit vertical reverse propagation patterns. Reduced cluster spacing and an excessive number of clusters increase fracture interference, thus limiting vertical propagation. A moderate vertical stress difference and bedding tensile strength promote the formation of complex fractures. RSM analysis reveals that injection rate and cluster spacing are the most sensitive factors affecting SRV, while the number of clusters has the least sensitivity, with each factor's influence being nonlinear. Optimizing the interrelationships between cluster spacing, injection rate, and viscosity is crucial for enhancing SRV and fracture network efficiency. These findings provide insights into fracture geometry control mechanisms and SRV optimization strategies in Jiyang Depression's layered shale reservoirs.

papers.title: Liquid ammonia in-nozzle flow: Effects of aspect ratio and surface roughness on the flash boiling
papers.abstract: Liquid ammonia, a promising carbon-free fuel with a significantly high saturation pressure, frequently exhibits flash boiling during its spray processes. The nozzle configuration plays a crucial role in flash boiling by altering the in-nozzle flow states. To gain deeper insight into the underlying physics, this study conducts numerical simulations of liquid ammonia in-nozzle flow. Six cases are examined to assess the effects of nozzle aspect ratio and surface roughness, including L/D = 2.5, 5, 10 and k-type rib roughness. The distributions of liquid volume fraction α and pressure p reveal that the enhancing effects of high aspect ratios on flash boiling predominantly manifest in rough nozzles due to the linear loss of pressure. However, a non-linear behavior emerges from the competing effects of cavitation and flash boiling, resulting in the lowest α at the nozzle outlet for L/D = 5 rather than L/D = 10 condition. Additionally, the observed drop in local temperature and saturation pressure indicates that, in smooth nozzles, this enhancing effect is offset by the cooling effect caused by the large latent heat of liquid ammonia. Regarding surface roughness, this study finds that roughness-induced turbulent flow generates eddies of various scales. These eddies detach and convect into the central flow, promoting bubble development through energy dissipation. Furthermore, surface roughness increases both the local velocity and velocity fluctuations at the nozzle outlet. As a preliminary study, the results are anticipated to guide the practical applications of liquid ammonia injection.

papers.title: Experimental study on film cooling in hypersonic flow with different coolant gases
papers.abstract: An experimental study was conducted to assess the effectiveness of nitrogen (N2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) as coolant gases for mitigating aerodynamic heating in a hypersonic flow at 2.1 km/s. The tests employed a flat-faced cylinder with a 2 mm diameter orifice at the stagnation point for coolant injection. The performance of both gases was evaluated at pressure ratios of 5 and 8.3. Schlieren imaging was used to analyze the flow field characteristics, while convective heat transfer rates were obtained using coaxial surface junction thermocouples. CO2 showed better cooling performance close to the injection point at a pressure ratio of 5, reducing heat transfer by 31% as opposed to 26% for N2. Additionally, CO2 maintained a more stable flow field. However, at all other downstream locations, N2 outperformed CO2 in heat transfer reduction due to its lower molecular weight and higher diffusivity. At the higher pressure ratio of 8.3, both coolant jets exhibited increased flow unsteadiness and failed to achieve significant heat transfer reduction.

papers.title: Pseudo-boiling of supercritical CO2 in horizontal tubes: the influence of tube diameter
papers.abstract: Supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) is a promising working fluid to improve the efficiency of advanced power systems. Relevant to the use of sCO2 in parabolic trough solar receivers, heating sCO2 in a horizontal tube is investigated numerically. The ranges of tube diameter, pressure, mass flux, and heat flux are 8–12 mm, 10–20 MPa, 700–1300 kg/m2 s, and 66.7–300 kW/m2, respectively. When heat transfer deterioration occurs at high heat flux, there are not only overshoot wall temperatures along the flow direction but also non-uniform wall temperatures in the circumferential direction. Temperature difference ΔT between the top and bottom generatrix of the tube wall reaches 199.7 K, maximally. To suppress ΔT, the influence of tube diameter on supercritical heat transfer is analyzed based on pseudo-boiling theory. The result shows that the heat transfer coefficient (HTC) at the top generatrix decreases while HTC at the bottom generatrix exhibits nonlinear variation with reducing diameter. Heat transfer performance at both the top and bottom generatrix is determined by the thermal resistance of a vapor-like film on the tube. It can be characterized by a supercritical K number, involving the balance of evaporation momentum force and inertia force on the vapor-like film. Thus, ΔT is determined by the ratio of K number at the tube top to that at the tube bottom and ΔT significantly decreases with reducing tube diameters. In addition, increasing pressure and mass flux can also reduce ΔT. This paper not only advances the pseudo-boiling heat transfer theory of supercritical fluids, but also provides guidance for the safety design of sCO2 heat exchangers in advanced power systems.

papers.title: Permeability evolution in variably saturated shales controlled by bimodal organic/inorganic pore structure and surface wetting characteristics
papers.abstract: Moisture is distributed heterogeneously within shale with distinctive features in both organic and inorganic pores. Importantly, this influences gas flow, impacts reservoir dynamics, and affects the accuracy of production forecasts. We establish a variable pressure gradient-bimodal pore structure (VPG-BPS) model to capture these characteristics of methane transport in partially water-saturated shale. We determine permeability in both organic and inorganic pores by matching estimated to actual gas production. Dynamic production experiments are conducted on variably saturated shales from the Sichuan Basin to determine permeability. Methane adsorption capacities are categorized into three stages, delineated by two intermediate threshold moisture contents—lower (MLc) and upper (MUc) threshold moisture contents, respectively. We demonstrate that the moisture content significantly influences shale transport dynamics by controlling adsorption–desorption properties and thereby gas-water distribution and permeability. Ultimate gas production decreases with increasing moisture content (Mc). Gas permeability (Kin and Ko) and gas desorption rate coefficients (kads,in and kads,o) in inorganic and organic pores range from 1 × 10−8 μm2 to 1 × 10−7 μm2, and 1 × 10−4 to 1 × 10−3, respectively. With Mc increasing from 0% to 3.5% (MUc), Kin, Ko, and kads,in exhibit a consistent trend of initially increasing before decreasing although kads,in shows no definitive trend above the threshold peak (MLc). When Mc increases from 0% to 2.2% (MLc), the desorptive hysteretic effect gradually weakens and adsorption kads,in increases with increasing Mc, subsequently prompting an increase in the other three flow parameters. As Mc further increases to MUc, kads,in remains constant but the other three flow parameters decrease as the gas flow channel is occupied by the invading water. Even when moisture migration ignored, the VPG-BPS model provides superior predictions of time histories of gas production over existing models and thus provides a theoretical foundation for dynamic evaluation of shale gas production.

papers.title: Characteristics of sodium p-styrenesulfonate modified polyacrylamide at high temperature under dual scale boundary
papers.abstract: In deep oil and gas operations, as well as in carbon capture, utilization, and storage, the temperature resistance of polyacrylamide is becoming increasingly critical. This paper investigates the temperature resistance of polyacrylamide from both microscopic and mesoscopic perspectives. Molecular dynamics simulation results indicate that the incorporation of sodium p-styrenesulfonate can increase the radius of gyration of polyacrylamide at high temperatures (increased by 2.97% at 180 °C) and decrease its diffusion coefficient (decreased by 33.94%) in water, effectively enhancing its temperature resistance. However, the decrease in hydrogen bonding was 17.39%. Additionally, the spatial network structure of the polymer obtained from scanning electron microscope images is parameterized using ImageJ software. The average values of area, perimeter, and width increased by 6.5%, 97.52%, and 275.86%, respectively, compared to the initial values, while the average value of skeleton width increased by 61.48% and 412.6%, respectively. Parameters such as pore area and width, along with an increase in fluctuation level, lead to a decrease in viscosity. The parameterization of the spatial network structure serves as a bridge between material structure and performance and also expands the application of spatial network structures in fields such as materials science and chemistry.

papers.title: Effects of sound on aerodynamics of a square cylinder in smooth and turbulent flows
papers.abstract: The interaction between sound and wind flow likely influences the aerodynamic characteristics of bluff bodies, highlighting the need for in-depth investigation. This study explores the coupling between the sound wave and wind flow and its influence on the aerodynamics of a two-dimensional (2D) square cylinder. This paper presents an experimental study of how sound affects the pressure distributions on the 2D square cylinder in smooth and grid-generated turbulent flows, considering a wider range of sound frequencies (1–2000 Hz) and sound pressure levels (60–100 dB) compared to previous research. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and spectral analysis provide insights into the sound effects through dominant flow structures and frequency characteristics. The results show that both sound frequency (fs) and sound pressure level (SPL) can modulate aerodynamic forces and vortex-shedding dynamics of the cylinder, with the effects of acoustic resonance identified. Audible sound impacts the pressure distributions on the side and leeward faces in two distinct patterns, resulting in opposing influences on drag and lift forces. The increase in sound pressure level leads to enhancement and progression of the sound frequency effects. Additionally, turbulence in the oncoming flow weakens these sound-induced effects, with the degree of attenuation depending on turbulence intensity and integral length scales.

papers.title: Using graphitic carbon nitride nanosheet/magnesium oxide for preventing asphaltene precipitation in carbonate reservoirs based on atomic force microscopy and core flooding tests
papers.abstract: Numerous industrial problems are related to the deposition of asphaltene in oil and gas reservoirs. Recently, different researchers used asphaltene inhibition using different types of nanoparticles. In this study, new nanocomposites named carbon nitride nanosheet/magnesium oxide nanocomposites (MgO/CN) were used for asphaltene inhibition in carbonate porous media, and a comparison was made with magnesium oxide nanoparticles (MgO). After performing characterization tests, a series of ultraviolet–visible spectrometer (UV–vis), CO2/oil interfacial tension, and atomic force microscopy (AFM) tests were performed at real reservoir carbonate conditions to see asphaltene adsorption on MgO/CN and MgO. Finally, as MgO/CN had better results for asphaltene adsorption in the mentioned tests, a series of natural depletion tests observing asphaltene deposition in porous media were designed using MgO/CN. The Langmuir isotherm was fitted better than Freundlich for maximum asphaltene adsorption on MgO/CN and MgO. Moreover, comparing MgO MgO/CN demonstrates superior asphaltene adsorption capacity in CO2/oil interfacial tension testing, especially at 5200, 4900, and 4600 psi, which were chosen to conduct natural depletion tests. Roughness data from AFM tests were in line with adsorption tests. Average roughness, peak to valley roughness, and root mean square roughness for carbonate sheets dropped from (46.70 ± 1.38 nm, 335.71 ± 2.64 nm, and 57.21 ± 1.98 nm) to (15.36 ± 1.25 nm, 131.5 ± 2.62 nm, and 19.24 ± 1.2 nm), and (5.42 ± 0.25 nm, 23.37 ± 1.62 nm, and 17.52 ± 0.86 nm) using MgO/CN and MgO, respectively. Finally, MgO/CN decreases asphaltene deposition and improves permeability/porosity reduction in carbonate formation.

papers.title: Unsteady numerical simulation of the icing process on oscillating airfoils
papers.abstract: Rotor blade icing degrades aerodynamic characteristics, affecting helicopter flight safety. The rotor blades under the forward flight state of a helicopter perform periodic variable pitch motion, which is the oscillation process of the rotor airfoil. Compared to fixed-wing icing, the unsteady characteristic of oscillating airfoil icing is a complex problem. To address this, numerical simulations of the unsteady airflow field in an unstructured overlapping grid system and the impact characteristics of supercooled water droplets based on the Euler method are carried out. An improved unsteady icing calculation method based on the Myers icing model is proposed. A dynamic mesh generation method based on Delaunay graph mapping and radial basis function is developed for multi-stage icing simulation. A set of unsteady numerical simulation methods for oscillating airfoil icing is synthesized. Accordingly, icing wind tunnel test conditions are numerically simulated, and the predicted ice shape is compared to that of the icing wind tunnel test. The data on macroscopic characteristics, including icing limit, ice angle position, and maximum thickness of icing, are in good agreement, verifying the accuracy and reliability of the calculation method. Furthermore, the influence of oscillation amplitude, oscillation frequency, and icing temperature on the icing process of oscillating airfoils is investigated. The icing limit of the airfoil pitching motion is higher than that of static airfoil icing. The oscillation frequency and amplitude of the airfoil pitching motion have a lesser effect on rime ice than on glaze ice. The glaze ice angle feature gradually disappears with increased frequency and amplitude, making the ice shape smooth.

papers.title: High in-droplet particle concentration on one-plate electrowetting-on-dielectric-based microfluidic devices by dielectrophoresis
papers.abstract: In recent years, parallel-plate electrowetting-on-dielectric (EWOD)-based digital microfluidic (DMF) devices have been used in many medical applications. However, few medical applications have used coplanar electrodes for droplet manipulation on one-plate EWOD-based microfluidic devices since digital microfluidic (DMF) manipulation on coplanar electrodes requires high operation voltage for droplet cutting. In this study, the first in-droplet particle concentration and droplet cutting on coplanar electrodes were demonstrated by integrating dielectrophoresis (DEP) and EWOD technologies. In our one-plate device, particles are concentrated on one side of the droplet by DEP, and then droplet cutting is performed by EWOD. The effects of alternating current electrothermal (ACET) and DEP on particle manipulation were investigated by simulation and experiment; effects of voltage, frequency, and electrode geometry on droplet cutting on coplanar electrodes were also investigated by the experiment. Compared to parallel-plate EWOD-based devices and other methods of particle concentration, our device can provide high concentration efficiency (95.2%) and a simple structure (no cover-plate, microchannel or external pump) in the microfluidic device. This novel method of in-droplet particle concentration and the droplet cutting method on a one-plate device could be integrated into particle assays and digital microfluidics so as to extend their applications.

papers.title: Laboratory observation of impact pressure, fluid velocity, and air fraction during dam-break impacts on a square prism
papers.abstract: This study experimentally investigates the fluid kinematics and dynamics of dam-break wave impacts on a square prism under a wet-bed condition. The incident of interest was a plunging breaker generated by the wet-bed dam break. Four impact scenarios were established by varying the distance between the wave impingement point and the prism's frontal face. Gate motion, fluid velocity, impact pressure, and air fraction were measured, with ensemble-averaged data obtained from repeated tests. Velocity fields in aerated and non-aerated regions were revealed using bubble image velocimetry and particle image velocimetry, respectively, while local air fractions were measured using fiber-optic reflectometry. Beyond serving as a benchmark for validation purposes, the present datasets support in-depth analysis of flow characteristics, pressure and air fraction distributions, and the correlations among fluid velocity, impact pressure, and aeration level. Maximum horizontal and vertical velocities reached 1.67 C and 2.14 C, respectively, where C is the wave celerity. Peak impact pressures reached to 12.652 ρwC2, with the highest values occurring just above the still water level. The generalized extreme value distribution is recommended for estimating peak impact pressures based on their probability density at specific occurrence frequencies. A dimensionless envelope curve was established to relate peak impact pressure to pressure rise time. Impact coefficients (0.846–7.647) were identified, allowing peak pressure to be estimated from local fluid velocity. A positive correlation between aeration and peak pressure was observed, indicating that existing pressure–aeration models are inadequate for capturing this behavior under wet-bed dam-break conditions.

papers.title: A stabilized reduced integration cell-based smoothed finite element method for incompressible laminar flow
papers.abstract: In this work, a cell-based smoothed finite element method (CS-FEM) empowered by reduced integration (CS-RI) is proposed to more efficiently solve incompressible laminar flow problems than previous CS-FEM. The proposed method incorporates the characteristic-based split scheme to deal with pressure check-board and hourglass control for instability caused by reduced integration. The reduced integration techniques can significantly save computational costs by treating each four-node quadrilateral (Q4) element or eight-node hexahedral (H8) element as a single smoothing domain (SD). However, previous CS-FEM takes 4 SDs for Q4 element and 6 (or 8) SDs for H8 element, respectively. Through carefully selected two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) benchmark examples, the stability, accuracy, and efficiency of the proposed CS-RI method are compared with reference results and original CS-FEM. The results show that the proposed method can substantially improve the computational speed while still maintaining comparable accuracy and stability, making it particularly promising for fluid dynamics applications.

papers.title: Modeling of the dewetting of ultra-thin liquid films on chemically patterned substrates: Linear spectrum and deposition patterns
papers.abstract: Liquid films of nanometric thickness are prone to spinodal dewetting driven by disjoining pressure, meaning that a non-wetting liquid film of homogeneous thickness in the range of tens of nanometers will spontaneously break into droplets. The surface energy of the underlying solid substrate heavily influences the dynamics and resulting droplet configurations. Here, we study the dewetting of thin liquid films on physically flat but chemically heterogeneous substrates using the thin film equation. We use linear stability analysis (LSA) to describe and predict the system's behavior until the film ruptures and compares it to numerical simulations. The good agreement between the numerical solutions and the LSA allows us to propose a method for measuring surface energy patterns from early time step film height profiles with good precision. Furthermore, we study the non-linear dynamics and the eventually formed droplet pattern by numerical simulations. This offers insight into the dependency of the resultant droplet arrays on shape, feature size, and magnitude of the chemical patterning of the underlying substrate.

papers.title: Surfactant effects on deformable drop motion in a slit
papers.abstract: The effect of insoluble surfactants on drop motion and deformation in a pressure-driven flow between two parallel plates at low Reynolds numbers is simulated by a combination of three-dimensional boundary-integral and flow-biased least squares methods to solve the coupled hydrodynamic and surfactant transport equations for the deforming drop surface. The external flow induces droplet motion and deformation that result in subsequent surfactant redistribution along the interface, which ultimately gives rise to tangential Marangoni stresses. In general, drop steady-state velocity decreases and drop deformation increases with increasing drop diameter, though increasing velocity with increasing diameter occurs for small drop viscosities. In the convection-dominated regime, i.e., in the limit of high surface Péclet number, Marangoni stresses partially immobilize the surface of the drop, leading to a significant decrease in the steady-state velocity of a low-viscosity drop. The accumulation of surfactants at the rear tips of the drop lowers the local interfacial tension, thereby inducing larger deformations to satisfy the normal stress balance. For an initially off-centered drop position, a surfactant-laden drop is observed to migrate to the channel centerplane either faster or slower than a clean drop does, depending on the drop-to-bulk viscosity ratio and the capillary number. Moreover, it is found that higher surfactant concentration values on the drop surface delay the cross-stream migration of nearly spherical droplets, while for deformable droplets, higher surfactant concentration facilitates faster migration.

papers.title: Predicting Pelton turbine bucket free-surface flow with an attention-based temporal convolutional network: A data-driven surrogate model
papers.abstract: Accurately resolving free-surface flow over Pelton turbine buckets is essential for efficiency optimization but remains prohibitively expensive when using conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) or smoothed particle hydrodynamics. To overcome this bottleneck, we proposed a data-driven deep learning model, the attention-enhanced temporal convolutional network (TCN), for predicting transient free-surface flow on buckets through convolutions in temporal and spatial dimensions. A surface-point-cloud sampling (SPCS) strategy was applied to the CFD results of a micro-Pelton turbine prototype, yielding 30 complete free-surface flow patterns that mirror the off-design operating condition. Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) was applied to free-surface flows under both design and off-design operating conditions, revealing modal similarities across flow patterns. Attention-enhanced TCN model was subsequently trained on 30 complete flow patterns under off-design condition. Model parameters including input and prediction horizons and channel configuration were evaluated to ensure model reliability and generalization. Ablation studies show that the temporal layer delivers the bulk of the error reduction, while the attention layer supplies the remaining improvement margin. The attention-enhanced TCN model attains mean squared error (MSE) below 2%, mean absolute error (MAE) below 7%, and coefficient of determination (R2) exceeding 0.9 on untrained flow patterns, delivering a 58% improvement in MAE over Bayesian-optimized four baselines models. Compared with full CFD strategy, the attention-enhanced TCN model compresses the flow data in ratio 1005 and successfully enables learns the evolution of the free-surface flow with high accuracy, which offers a practical pathway for integrating data-driven models into digital-twin frameworks for hydropower optimization.

papers.title: Air circulation effects on airborne particles aboard cruise ships
papers.abstract: Virus outbreaks on cruise ships pose significant challenges due to their enclosed environments and high passenger densities. Managing these outbreaks has become even more critical as cruise ships have increased in size and passenger capacity. This study uses numerical simulations to investigate the dispersion of airborne respiratory droplets and aerosols within a passenger cabin on a cruise ship, focusing on the angle of the mechanical ventilation jet's influence. Although previous research primarily focused on larger respiratory droplets that quickly settle, this study emphasizes aerosols under 10 μm that can remain airborne for extended periods. The findings demonstrate that variations in the inflow angle from the ventilation unit can significantly affect aerosol dispersion. The results show that the travel distance of the larger droplets is more effectively restricted at the larger 75° inlet angle. Smaller droplets with a diameter ranging between 1–10 and 10–50 μm can remain airborne 1.4 m above ground 20% and 40% longer, respectively. These insights underscore the importance of tailored air circulation strategies to reduce transmission risks in confined spaces, such as cruise ship cabins, highlighting the need for optimized ventilation design to manage infectious disease outbreaks.

papers.title: Three-dimensional high-lift configuration simulation using data-driven turbulence model
papers.abstract: Traditional Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes equations often struggle to predict separated flows accurately. Recent studies have employed data-driven methods to enhance predictions by modifying baseline equations, such as field inversion and machine learning with symbolic regression. However, data-driven turbulence models exhibit limited adaptability and are rarely applied to complex engineering problems. This study examines the application of data-driven turbulence models to complex three-dimensional high-lift configurations, extending their usability beyond previous applications. First, the generalizability of the shear-stress transport model for conditioned field inversion (SST–CND) is validated, where CND is the abbreviation for conditioned. Then, the spatially varying correction factor obtained through conditioned field inversion is transferred to the three-equation k−v2¯−ω model. The 30P30N three-element airfoil, the Japan aerospace exploration agency standard model, and the high-lift version of the common research model (CRM–HL) are numerically simulated. The results indicated that the SST–CND model significantly improves the prediction of stall characteristics, demonstrating satisfactory generalizability. The corrected k−v2¯−ω−CND model accurately predicts the stall characteristics of CRM–HL, with a relative error of less than 5% compared to experimental results. This confirms the strong transferability of the model correction derived from conditioned field inversion across different turbulence models.

papers.title: Frequency characterization of a sweeping jet actuator with internal geometry modification
papers.abstract: An unsteady simulation method was conducted to investigate the internal flow mechanism of a sweeping jet actuator, with a focus on the influence of varying the ratio of the first and second chambers on the oscillation frequency. The time histories of the oscillations under seven distinct working conditions were simulated to reveal the law of frequency change. A detailed comparison involving the variation of the deflection angle, pressure, and vorticity fields under three specific working conditions was conducted from both qualitative and quantitative perspectives to explore the underlying oscillation mechanism. The results indicated that the asymmetric expansion and contraction of the vortex activated the feedback flow to generate oscillation, and the frequency of the oscillation was related to the speed of vortex expansion in the first and second chambers. The length of the second chamber determined the oscillation frequency, which could change, ranging from 1.9% to 26.9% compared to the prototype with the variation of this length scale. The internal flow dynamics had a direct impact on the characteristics of the jet within the external flow field. Furthermore, equipping the actuator on the end wall of a compressor cascade, using this actuator with only 0.11% of the cascade mass flow, the total pressure loss, factoring in the additional energy input, was reduced by 3.7%.

papers.title: Gas drainage optimization via fracture network characterization in coal mining
papers.abstract: The collapse of overlying strata in the goaf creates fractures that facilitate gas migration and accumulation in the upper corner, increasing the risk of gas overlimit. This study used physical simulations to analyze the distribution of the “three vertical zones” in the 11308 working face. The caved zone height is 28.5 m, and the fractured zone height is 54.4 m. The “voussoir beam” structure of mining-induced fractures was identified as the primary gas migration channel. An innovative fracture classification method was proposed to clarify their development and distribution, revealing that the low-level “rectangular terrace” acts as a gas accumulation “sweet spot,” guiding borehole extraction. Numerical simulations indicated that gas mainly accumulates in the high-level of the fracture zone (7–10 times the mining height). Based on these findings, a “low-level interception-high-level extraction” directional long borehole layout was designed, along with a dynamic balance model of “airflow-borehole extraction-gas migration.” Field application in the 11308 working face showed a 123% increase in gas extraction and a stable gas concentration of 0.08% in the upper corner, significantly reducing the risk of upper corner gas exceeding the limit. These results provide valuable guidance for managing gas risks in similar geological conditions in coal mines.

papers.title: Numerical analysis on wind pressure characteristics of a rectangular beam under the moving thunderstorm downburst wind
papers.abstract: To study the wind pressure characteristics of a rectangular beam under the action of a moving thunderstorm downburst wind, the large eddy simulation method was used to simulate the thunderstorm downburst wind field at different moving speeds. After verifying the accuracy of the wind field, the wind load characteristics of a 2:1 rectangular beam under the action of a moving thunderstorm downburst wind were investigated. The wind pressure distribution and flow field characteristics on the surfaces of the rectangular beam, as well as the fluctuating wind pressure spectrum and coherence function, were analyzed. The results show that the maximum wind pressure coefficient on each surface of the rectangular beam decreases as the spanwise distance increases. When the thunderstorm downburst wind is approximately 0.5 m from the left and right surfaces of the rectangular beam, the wind pressure coefficients at the center measurement points of the left and right surfaces reach their maximum. When the thunderstorm downburst wind is directly above the rectangular beam, the wind pressure coefficients at the center measurement points of the upper and lower surfaces reach their maximum. As the thunderstorm downburst wind approaches the rectangular beam, vortices are created on the upper, lower, and right surfaces of the beam, resulting in the wind pressure coefficients on the left surface remaining positive. As the thunderstorm downburst wind is above the rectangular beam, vortices form on the left, lower, and right surfaces, and due to the asymmetry of the moving thunderstorm downburst's center, the main vortex on the lower surface shifts to the right, leading to relatively higher wind pressure on the right side of the lower surface. The moving speed of the thunderstorm downburst wind has a significant impact on the low-frequency values of the fluctuating wind pressure power spectrum at measurement points on the surfaces of the rectangular beam. Specifically, when the dimensionless frequency is below 0.02, the dimensionless power spectra at the low-frequency range increase with the moving speed, while at higher frequencies, the dimensionless power spectra at different moving speeds overlap. During the movement of the thunderstorm downburst wind, the coherence function values on the left, lower, and right surfaces of the rectangular beam are relatively larger than those on the upper surface across the entire frequency range.

papers.title: Working state analysis and structure optimization of blast furnace copper cooling stave with numerical simulation
papers.abstract: Cooling stave is one of the key equipment of the blast furnace cooling system, and its working condition is vital to determine the long-term stable operation of the blast furnace. Based on the computational fluid dynamic, this paper established a three-dimensional model of blast furnace copper cooling stave. The temperature and stress distribution characteristics of the cooling stave under normal and abnormal working conditions are first simulated and analyzed. The influences of the distance between the cooling water pipes and the shape of the cooling water pipes on the cooling capacity of the cooling stave are then investigated. The damage characteristics of a practical cooling stave are also clarified by constructing an integrated model of the copper cooling stave. Results indicate that the bending area of the cooling stave bears high pressure and tends to deform. Lowering the cooling water temperature can improve the cooling performance of the cooling stave. Compared with the small water pipe, the maximum stress of the cooling column is reduced by 625.41 MPa, and the deformation is reduced by about 0.12 mm, which can further reduce the damage of the cooling stave. When the cooling stave is well fixed, the central part is squeezed due to the high stress at the edge, resulting in its depression. On the contrary, the edge of the cooling stave is seriously damaged by curling. Therefore, improving the connection between the cooling staves can greatly improve the working conditions and service life of the cooling stave.

papers.title: Experimental and numerical investigation into the effects of tip configurations on the aerodynamic performance and loss structure of turbine blade tip
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of blade tip configurations on the aerodynamic performance and loss structure of turbine cascades, aerodynamic measurements incorporating blade tip coolant ejection are conducted on a transonic cascade test rig. A comparative aerodynamic analysis is conducted between four tip configurations: (1) classical squealer tip (REF) as the reference case; (2) pressure-side inclined rim modification (IR); (3) IR configuration with partitioned cavity via a divider wall (IRDW); and (4) IR configuration integrated with suction-side cutback rim (IRCR). Results indicate that at all three exit isentropic Mach number conditions, as for the aerodynamic performance, IRCR slightly surpasses IR, which outperforms IRDW, with REF performing the lowest. Quantitatively, in the terms of experimental results, compared with REF, area-averaged total pressure loss coefficient of IRCR decreases by 13.11%, 16.62%, and 18.14% at exit isentropic Mach number equal to 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9, respectively. The influencing regions of different tip shapes primarily concentrate on the loss of tip leakage vortex (TLV) and upper passage vortex (UPV). For three improved shapes, the limited development of tip leakage flow and the weaker interaction between the mainstream and secondary flow lead to the lower TLV loss. The swirling and consumption of TLV to UPV and their interaction impact the UPV development. Overall, three improved tip shapes can enhance the cascade aerodynamic performance significantly and offer a meaningful reference for the progression of gas turbine design.

papers.title: Physical-properties-preserving space fourth-order numerical scheme for the coupled damped nonlinear Schrödinger equations with fractional Laplacian
papers.abstract: Fractional differential equations have found extensive applications in modeling various physical, biological, and engineering phenomena owing to their nonlocal characteristics. However, theoretical and numerical analysis of fractional differential equations presents a substantial challenge. The current manuscript aims to provide rigorous theoretical analysis and detailed study about the numerical solution for the coupled damped nonlinear fractional Schrödinger equations involving the fractional Laplacian. To obtain physically faithful numerical solution, we first transform the original non-structure-preserving system into a new one that preserves several important physical properties. Then, we conduct a thorough analysis about the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the solution to this new system, accompanied by the boundness and conservation. These theoretical results are the first time to be presented for such a system. Next, a novel fourth-order numerical differential formula for approximating the space fractional Laplacian operator is constructed by an indirect method. Different from existing direct methods, the coefficients of our constructed formula have exact expressions, and the corresponding matrix is symmetric, which is beneficial to the stability and convergence analysis and the subsequent fast algorithm design of the corresponding numerical schemes. Considering the use of the modified Crank–Nicolson method in the time direction, the corresponding numerical scheme for the new system is developed. Meanwhile, we have conducted rigorous theoretical studies on the established difference scheme, including its unique solvability, stability, and convergence under different norms. Furthermore, an iterative algorithm for the difference scheme with a proof of the convergence is also given.

papers.title: Numerical study on the development length of thermal counterflow in superfluid helium
papers.abstract: The entrance effect in the thermal counterflow of superfluid helium (He II) plays a crucial role in understanding its heat transfer behavior and in designing effective flow channels to minimize experimental uncertainties. This study investigates the development process of He II counterflow in a two-dimensional channel through numerical simulations that couple the two-fluid model with Vinen's equation. Our findings identify three distinct flow regions and highlight the significant impact of mutual friction on flow development characteristics. The dimensionless development length exhibits a strong dependency on temperature and Reynolds number. A critical channel width for the superfluid component is observed below which the development length increases markedly. Notably, a Poiseuille velocity profile at the inlet necessitates a longer development length compared to uniform or “M”-shaped profiles, likely due to a more uneven distribution of mutual friction force near the inlet. These insights enhance our understanding of quantum fluid behavior and provide valuable guidance for experimental design in thermal counterflow studies.

papers.title: Expanding wet-capillary-thinning for microrheology: Framework for stable core–sheath extensional flows of miscible fluids
papers.abstract: For complex fluids such as polymer solutions, biofluids, and colloids, microrheology plays a critical role in evaluating shear and extensional properties, especially when sample volumes are limited to a few microliters. Traditional methods often require separate experiments for each property, often involving complex setups, large sample volumes, or macroscale conditions incompatible with sensitive materials. Here, we establish a microrheological technique that enables simultaneous measurement of extensional viscosity, nonequilibrium interfacial tension, effective diffusion coefficient, and osmotic pressure under confined microscale flow using as little as 50 μl of sample. The method forms a stable, lubricated viscous thread of a complex fluid within a microchannel using a co-flowing miscible sheath fluid. Upon stopping the core flow, the arrested thread undergoes capillary thinning under extensional stress from the sheath, while osmotic suppression preserves a sharp interface. We termed this technique wet-capillary-thinning (WCT). In this study, we expand WCT using a wide array of aqueous polyethylene oxide solutions (M¯w: 2 × 105 to 4 × 106 g/mol; 0.1–1.0 wt. %), spanning dilute, semi-dilute, and entangled solution regimes to demonstrate versatility and define the operating framework. A smooth converging–diverging channel was designed to enhance thread symmetry, and stable lubricated core flow was verified. Using the Buckingham Pi theorem, we identified key dimensionless parameters—viscosity ratio (≤ 5.6), Péclet (104 to 105), Capillary (0.01–1), and Elasticity number (≈ 58)—which define operational limits. We also extracted osmotic pressure from WCT, consistent with Flory–Huggins predictions, supporting the method's thermodynamic accuracy. These results establish WCT as a robust microrheometer for low-volume extensional characterization of complex fluids.

papers.title: Microscopic mechanism of wettability alteration at the coal–water–CO2 interface under extreme conditions
papers.abstract: Injecting hot flue gas from power plants into coal seams is a key strategy for promoting green and low-carbon coal mining. This study investigates the mechanisms underlying changes in coal–water interfacial wettability under high-temperature and high-pressure flue gas injection, with a specific focus on the coal–water–CO2 interface. Experimental results indicate that, under CO2 conditions ranging from 323 to 443 K and 2 to 8 MPa, the surface tension of de-ionized water decreases notably with increasing temperature and pressure. The coal–water contact angle decreases linearly with temperature but increases exponentially with CO2 pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that elevated temperatures enhance the spreading of water molecules on the coal surface, whereas increased CO2 density inhibits this effect. The concentration of water molecules in the strong adsorption layer, the interaction energy between coal and water, and the mean square displacement of water molecules all increase with temperature but decrease as CO2 density rises. Therefore, increasing temperature improves the wettability of the coal–water interface, while the introduction of CO2 impairs interfacial wettability. This change results from the competitive adsorption between water and CO2 molecules on the coal surface. These findings offer mechanistic insight into coal–water interfacial behavior under extreme conditions and support the application of hot flue gas to enhance permeability in coal seams.

papers.title: Flow characteristics and structural optimization of multiple heterogeneous self-excited oscillatory pulse structures
papers.abstract: To enhance the potential for diversified field applications of self-excited oscillatory pulse structure devices, this paper compares the velocity and pressure fields of the original structure (PSOS) with those of heterogeneous structures (return channels RCOS, diffusion angles ANOS, wall folds WCOS, and rectification blocks RBOS) using the standard k-ε model and large eddy simulation (LES), which reveals the variation rules of vortex structure evolution, perturbation oscillation range, and pulsation pressure value during the dynamic development of the jet. It turns out that the standard k-ε model has limitations in describing the vortex fragmentation and dissipation processes. In contrast, the LES model can capture the flow details more accurately and agrees well with the results of high-speed camera experiments. The different oscillatory structures show significant differences: the PSOS structure has a symmetric velocity field distribution with a large outlet pressure amplitude, the RCOS has a significant wall-attachment effect, the inlet is significantly diverted by the feedback channel, the ANOS has faster velocity decay and the most extensive sweeping range, and the WCOS has a wall folding corner structure that induces wall-vortex generation and less energy dissipation; the RBOS increases the flow resistance in the cavity and generates significant pressure fluctuations. The optimized PSOS-O structure exhibits high-frequency oscillatory flow with both high mean peak pressure and maximum pulsation pressure. This study provides a reference for the optimization of the oscillatory flow field and the design of engineering-assisted efficiency enhancement devices.

papers.title: Surrogate-assisted optimization of fluid-dynamic descaling systems using a hybrid Kriging-non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II framework
papers.abstract: To address the challenges of steel material loss (9%–12%) caused by iron oxide sheet formation and environmental contamination from conventional pickling rust removal methods, this study investigates mixture flow descaling (MFD) device as a potential alternative. While abrasive waterjets demonstrate descaling potential, their structural optimization mechanisms remain insufficiently explored. A Kriging-assisted modified non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II optimization framework is proposed to enhance the descaling efficiency of the MFD device. Parametric analysis systematically evaluated how blade length, jet distance, and flow velocity collectively influence the descaling performance of the MFD device, with particular emphasis on quantifying interaction effects between these operational variables. Simulation and experimental validation were performed to verify these optimized results. After optimization, the simulation demonstrated that the erosion rate increased by 72.76%, and the descaling width increased by 81.97%. Additionally, the experimental results for surface roughness and rust curve provided further validation of the proposed algorithm's effectiveness. This research provides actionable design principles for optimizing water-slurry blasting systems in steel strip descaling applications.

papers.title: Numerical features of the fifth-order nonlinear Kawahara equation for modeling shallow water waves
papers.abstract: In the present study, numerical solutions of the important type of the fifth-order Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation for modeling shallow water waves, namely, Kawahara equation, are investigated. With the solutions of the higher order Kawahara equation used in the modeling of shallow water waves, the behavior change of the wave with parameter changes is revealed. Unlike the classical numerical methods, two effective numerical methods are combined and used together. One of the components of the scheme is differential quadrature method (DQM) that approaches the derivative of the mesh points in the solution domain. In other words, space discretization is completed by using DQM. The other component is the Crank–Nicolson scheme, which is the effective type of the finite difference method. By using the advantages of the DQM and Crank–Nicolson scheme with effective linearization technique together, high accurate solutions are obtained. Four different test problems and their various forms are solved numerically. Error norms, central processing unit times, rate of convergence, and three invariants are calculated and reported.

papers.title: Numerical simulation of the interaction between shock trains and flame in hypersonic crossflow for various fuels
papers.abstract: Ethylene (C2H4) and hydrogen (H2), serving as crucial intermediate species in hydrocarbon oxidation and pyrolysis processes, constitute practical propulsion system fuels. This paper conducted an analysis of the typical flow field structures, combustion characteristics, and performance of scramjet engines operating under high Mach number inflows with H2/C2H4 fuel combustion. The numerical methodology incorporates a 9-species, 27-step H2/O2 chemical kinetics mechanism and an 8-species, 10-step C2H4/O2 reaction scheme, implemented with wall function formulation and k–ω shear-stress-transport turbulence model, utilizing Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes computations, demonstrating excellent correlation with experimental measurements. The results show that (1) compared with H2 fuel, the shock wave in C2H4 fuel combustion flow field is more pronounced, and the Mach number decreases more slowly along the flow direction. (2) The spatial distribution patterns of engine heat release zones and premixed/non-premixed combustion modes under supersonic crossflow conditions were obtained, with H2 fuel showing larger premixed combustion zones in the boundary layer upstream of the combustor than C2H4, while other combustion areas were non-premixed. (3) Comparative analyses of stagnation pressure losses along the flowpath revealed that C2H4 combustion exhibits greater total pressure loss and lower combustion efficiency than H2, while generating approximately 70% higher thrust output. The research results provide important basis for further detailed flow field calculation and multi-scale combustion process research under high Mach number incoming flow conditions.

papers.title: Study on the effect of surfactant functions on invasion–flowback and interaction depth based on online computed tomography and numerical simulation
papers.abstract: Surfactants can enhance imbibition processes; however, water invasion also affects oil-well productivity during depletion development. Nonetheless, it remains unclear how the various functions of surfactants affect oil-well performance. In this study, core displacement experiments based on online computed tomography scanning, together with numerical simulations considering multi-field coupling, are employed to investigate the invasion–flowback characteristics. The results show that the regained permeability drops to 24% after distilled water invasion, whereas the wettability alteration and ultra-low interfacial tension (IFT) systems increase that to 30% and 43%, respectively. Due to the Jamin effect, the solubilization and the self-emulsification systems maintain high water saturation at fracture face after flowback, reducing regained permeability to 11.3% and 14.5%, respectively. The invasion depth of distilled water reaches 65 mm, whereas the addition of surfactants reduces it to approximately 50 mm. The water saturation at invasion front of the wettability alteration system is approximately 0.45; however, due to the ultra-low IFT, the water saturations of the ultra-low IFT, self-emulsification, and solubilization systems reach 0.6–0.7. Numerical simulations show that surfactant adsorption confines its effective action zone to a region much smaller than the water invasion depth. The ultra-low IFT system maintains high surfactant concentrations and the originally low IFT only within 0–10 mm, beyond which the concentration decreases exponentially. This study provides a deeper insight into the surfactant–matrix interactions, thereby facilitating the design of fracturing completions.

papers.title: A novel meshless simulation for stress-sensitive fractured reservoirs
papers.abstract: This paper has developed a novel meshless numerical simulation method for fractured reservoirs with stress-sensitive effects. This method breaks through the limitations of traditional grid methods by employing meshless node technology to discretize the reservoir computational domain, thereby more accurately simulating the complex fracture network geometry. In the simulation of two-phase oil–water flow, the method uses the generalized finite difference method to discretize the pressure equation with stress-sensitive and calculate the transmissibility between matrix nodes, fracture nodes, and the control volume of nodes. The pressure and saturation equations are solved using a fully implicit method. This approach can directly apply nonlinear solvers in reservoir simulation, simplifying the process of developing a universal simulator. Through case studies, we found that an increase in the stress-sensitive coefficient leads to a decrease in the micropores of the rock framework as pressure changes, resulting in a decrease in formation permeability, and consequently reducing daily oil production and cumulative oil production. This method demonstrates the flexibility of meshless nodes in simulating irregular reservoir boundaries and fracture geometries, as well as their high-precision computational capabilities.

papers.title: Assessing morphology of Jhelum river and prediction of centerline shifting using autoregressive integrated moving average model
papers.abstract: Jhelum River originates from the Verinag Spring. It shows meandering characteristics in its alluvial plains. The course of the Jhelum River is continuously changing, and the people residing near the river are mostly affected. This study investigated the Jhelum River's morphological changes and centerline shifts over several decades using Landsat images and ARIMA (autoregressive integrated moving average) modeling. The river was systematically divided into multiple reaches and cross sections (17 reaches and 37 cross sections) to evaluate the meander parameters, including meander length, meander width, meander ratio, sinuosity, wavelength, and radius of curvature. The study reveals spatial variation in channel migration with maximum shift (63 m) at Reshipora, Pulwama, and minimum shift (1 m) at Goripora, Pulwama. A considerable variability in the sinuosity was observed across the study area, indicating a highly meandering river. It was also observed that meander length, meander width, and wavelength show a decreasing trend. In order to understand the forecasted future trends, a statistical time series forecasting approach was applied using the ARIMA model. The outcome of the model successfully generated the predicted values of the centerline for different time intervals, with a good correlation value of R2.

papers.title: An efficient modified Lax–Wendroff/interpolation approach with finite element method for a three-dimensional system of tectonic stress and deformation model: Example of landslides in Cameroon
papers.abstract: This paper develops an efficient computational technique to assess the landslide responses to tectonic deformation and to predict the implications of large bedrocks landslides on the short and long-term development of the disasters. The considered equations represent a three-dimensional system of geological structure deformation subject to suitable initial and boundary conditions. The space derivatives are approximated using the finite element procedure while the approximation in time derivative is obtained using the Lax–Wendroff and interpolation techniques. The new approach is so-called a modified Lax–Wendroff/interpolation method with a finite element method. The modified Lax–Wendroff/interpolation scheme is employed to efficiently treat the time derivative term and to provide a suitable time step restriction for stability. Under this time step requirement, both stability and error estimates of the new algorithm are deeply analyzed using a constructed strong norm. The theory suggests that the developed computational technique is second-order accurate in time and spatial convergent with order O(h3), where h denotes the space size. A wide set of numerical examples are carried out to confirm the theoretical results and to demonstrate the utility and validity of the proposed numerical scheme. Some examples of landslides observed in west and center regions in Cameroon from 29 October 2019 to 5–7 November 2024 are also considered and discussed.

papers.title: Toward stable multi-jet formation in ionic liquids for annular slit-type electrospray thrusters
papers.abstract: This study achieves stable multi-jet formation in annular slit-type electrospray emitters, focusing on the effects of viscosity and electric potential. Using water–glycerin mixtures, the transition from Taylor cone formation to multi-jet generation is analyzed. Higher viscosity is found to enhance the jet stability, enabling up to a maximum of seven stable jets at optimal conditions. Key parameters are identified as the capillary number (Ca) and Reynolds number (Re), and insights into the interplay between surface tension and viscosity are reported. The annular slit design demonstrates superior scalability and efficiency compared to the capillary emitter. Higher flow rates allow stable multi-jet formation at lower voltages, while voltages above 18.5 kV trigger instability. The reported findings provide design guidelines for optimizing electrospray systems by balancing jet stability and pulsation frequency. Sustained multi-jet formation at lower voltages improves efficiency by reducing power consumption, a critical factor for nanosatellite propulsion. High pulsation frequencies enhance thrust stability, making annular slit-type emitters viable for low Earth orbit operations in microgravity environments.

papers.title: Effects of acoustic coupling across compact flames with heat capacity variations on entropy generations and thermoacoustic modes
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the effect of heat capacity variations across the compact flame, calculated using detailed chemical reactions in combustion processes, on the acoustic coupling and thermoacoustic modes in a general combustor. For thermoacoustic analyses, the acoustic jump conditions across compact flames are recast to account for changes in heat capacities and specific heat ratios at a non-zero Mach number. Two coefficients defined by heat capacity and specific heat ratio in jump conditions show a strong dependence on temperature jump ratios and equivalence ratios within premixed flames.
