papers.abstract: The purpose of this study is to assess the steady natural convection behavior of Williamson fluid flow between two concentric cylinders, factoring in the influence of the Soret effect, magnetic field, and a first-order chemical reaction. The complex interplay between fluid dynamics, thermal diffusion, and magnetic influences is modeled to understand the behavior of the Williamson fluid under varying conditions. The outer cylinder rotates, keeping the inner cylinder fixed. This rotation leads to the generation of flow. A magnetic field is introduced in the radial direction. The appropriate transformation allows for the conversion of the non-linear partial differential equations associated with the Williamson fluid model into ordinary differential equations. Artificial neural networks (ANN) are adopted to analyze the Williamson fluid model. A neural network output with adjustable parameters (biases and masses) is used in the trial functions. The adjustable parameters of the trial solution are determined using the ADAMS (adaptive moment estimation algorithm) optimization technique to satisfy the Williamson fluid model. The findings demonstrate that using an ANN based method for solving the equations provides substantial accuracy and efficiency in contrast to other numerical techniques. Moreover, the ANN results are validated against spectral quasi-linearization method solutions, achieving an error margin of 10−4, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed method. Comparison with related optimizers like SGD, RMSProp, and LBFGS is also explored in this study. The impact of the loss function on various neural network parameters, including learning rate, number of hidden neurons, and activation functions, is depicted through graphs. The findings show that the Adam optimizer offers faster convergence and higher accuracy. The findings indicate that higher magnetic parameter values result in lower velocity and temperature profiles. The current study has significant applicability in industries such as food, pharmaceuticals, and petroleum, enhancing process optimization and product quality.

papers.title: Simulation and mechanism study of cavity collapse of small angle conical projectile entry into water
papers.abstract: The issue of structural water entry represents a significant topic in mechanics, with extensive applications in both military and civilian sectors. Despite its importance, relatively limited research has been conducted on the cavity collapse mechanism associated with complex head-shaped projectiles' entry into water, and the relationship between cavity and spatiotemporal load remains inadequately understood. This study introduces an enhanced methodology within the framework of the compressible Eulerian finite element method. This approach integrates an improved penalty immersed boundary method and a pressure-truncated cavitation model, enabling the resolution of transient nonlinear fluid–structure coupling problems. The discussion of the results begins by presenting the fundamental characteristics of the physical process based on experimental findings, followed by an examination of the effects of head shape, velocity, and gravity parameters. The proposed numerical model can accurately simulate structural water entry loads and the evolution of multi-phase, multi-interface processes. In addition, it establishes the correlation between the cavity and various head shapes. The findings indicated that higher velocities result in more rounded cavity shapes, reduced local cavity surface pressures, and nonlinear cavity closure times. In addition, the gravity intensifies cavity collapse, producing local load pulses acting on the projectiles.

papers.title: Multi-objective optimization of bionic guide vanes for flow rectification in elbow pipes based on convolutional neural network—Second-generation genetic algorithm
papers.abstract: Pipeline systems constitute essential structural components in marine vessels, primarily responsible for fluid transportation. Elbow pipes, being the most prevalent configuration in these systems, serve dual functions of flow direction alteration and pipeline spatial arrangement optimization, while simultaneously exhibiting complex hydrodynamic characteristics. The inherent flow separation phenomena and vortex generation within these components frequently induce substantial pressure fluctuations, ultimately leading to pipeline vibrations and acoustic emissions. Thus, flow channel optimization for pressure fluctuation mitigation holds critical importance in marine engineering applications. This investigation focuses on a 90° elbow pipe (radius-to-diameter ratio R/D = 4). Computational Fluid Dynamics simulations were first implemented to characterize the internal flow field, with subsequent experimental validation confirming model accuracy. A bionic guide vane, inspired by the hydrodynamic morphology of whale fins, was then parametrically designed. A systematic optimization framework integrating Convolutional Neural Network and the Second-generation Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm was developed to simultaneously minimize pressure pulsations and energy loss through multi-objective parameter optimization. The results indicate that vorticity concentration regions form downstream of the elbow pipe. After multi-objective optimization, the bionic guide vane significantly reduces the vorticity in this downstream region. Additionally, the total pressure level at all monitoring points decreases by over 4.7 dB. This study offers a theoretical foundation for the rectification and drag reduction of ship pipeline systems, as well as for reducing pressure pulsation intensity and suppressing vibration and noise.

papers.title: DrivAer transformer: A high-precision and fast prediction method for vehicle aerodynamic drag coefficient based on the DrivAerNet++ dataset
papers.abstract: At the current stage, deep learning-based methods have demonstrated excellent capabilities in evaluating aerodynamic performance, significantly reducing the time and cost required for traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. However, when faced with the task of processing extremely complex three-dimensional (3D) vehicle models, the lack of large-scale datasets and training resources, coupled with the inherent diversity and complexity of the geometry of different vehicle models, means that the prediction accuracy and versatility of these networks are still not up to the level required for current production. In view of the remarkable success of transformer models in the field of natural language processing and their strong potential in the field of image processing, this study innovatively proposes a point cloud learning framework called DrivAer transformer (DAT). The DAT structure uses the DrivAerNet++ dataset, which contains high-fidelity CFD data of industrial-standard 3D vehicle shapes. Enabling accurate estimation of air drag directly from 3D meshes, thus avoiding the limitations of traditional methods such as 2D image rendering or signed distance fields. DAT enables fast and accurate drag prediction, driving the evolution of the aerodynamic evaluation process and laying the critical foundation for introducing a data-driven approach to automotive design. The framework is expected to accelerate the vehicle design process and improve development efficiency.

papers.title: Implosion impact behavior and damage mechanism of titanium alloy pressure hulls under deep-sea conditions at submerged plate boundaries
papers.abstract: When the deep-sea pressure hull is subjected to hydrostatic pressure exceeding its ultimate bearing capacity, it experiences a catastrophic underwater implosion. The resulting implosion shock wave exhibits an extremely high peak value and releases a significant amount of energy, posing a serious threat to the structural integrity of the entire submersible. It is essential to investigate the pressure hull implosion at the boundaries of adjacent structures in deep-sea environments. First, an experiment investigating the underwater implosion of a spherical pressure hull at a submerged plate boundary is conducted. Then, the arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian method is developed to study the implosion fluid-structure interaction characteristics of titanium alloy spherical pressure hulls under both variable-spacing and variable-thickness plate boundary conditions. The dynamic deformation and failure mechanisms of spherical pressure hull implosion, along with the impact behavior and damage mechanisms of submerged circular plates, are analyzed. The extent of the fracture in the spherical pressure hull decreases as the distance from the boundary increases. In addition, when the spherical pressure hull implodes at variable-spacing circular plate boundaries, the implosion center exhibits a significant migration effect.

papers.title: Swinging pressure reducing valve in a real water distribution network: Where is the catch?
papers.abstract: To reduce leakage in water distribution networks, several strategies have been developed, each addressing different aspects of the problem. Alongside advanced leak detection technologies, pressure control has proven to be one of the most powerful and widely implemented strategies to reduce leakage. In this perspective, a key technology in pressure management is the use of pressure reducing valves (PRVs). This paper presents field measurements showing significant instability (swing) of a PRV installed in a real pressure management area in Trieste (Italy). Such instability is characterized by very frequent and significant pressure variations. The various factors influencing this feature are pointed out, finding the catch of the problem and suggesting effective solutions.

papers.title: Coupling mechanisms of thermoacoustic instability in downward-propagating biogas–hydrogen flames
papers.abstract: The stability of biogas–hydrogen combustion is critical for advancing hydrogen-enriched fuel applications in sustainable energy systems. This study investigates the downward propagation dynamics of biogas–hydrogen premixed flames in a vertical tube, focusing on thermoacoustic instabilities under varying hydrogen fractions (0–40 vol. %) and equivalence ratios (0.8–1.2). Four distinct flame propagation regimes were identified, transitioning from continuous oscillation to Helmholtz-driven pulsations as hydrogen content increased. Spectral analysis revealed secondary frequency components (≈2 × primary frequency), attributed to acoustic resonance modes. A novel criterion for flat-flame instability was established by correlating laminar burning velocities (SL) with equivalence ratios, proposing a critical SL threshold of 24 cm/s for regime transition. Theoretical analysis further quantified the role of the Lewis number (Le) in combustion instability: higher Le amplified oscillatory intensity, while elevated SL increased dimensionless frequencies across modes. Growth rate calculations demonstrated that acoustic losses (1/τloss ≈ 24 s−1) and the combined Zel'dovich–Mach parameter (βM ≈ 0.009) are pivotal in suppressing flat-flame instabilities.

papers.title: Cascaded PhyFormer-SRNet: A physics-informed transformer-based framework with cascaded refinement for spatiotemporal super-resolution of turbulent flows
papers.abstract: Reconstructing high-resolution turbulent flow fields from sparse low-resolution data remains a significant challenge for conventional data-driven methods, primarily due to the added difficulty of resolving the spatiotemporally coupled multi-scale dynamics inherent in turbulence. We propose a novel framework, named as Cascaded PhyFormer-SRNet, that provides a comprehensive solution through improved model architecture design, imposition of physical constraints, and a method for enhanced fine-scale refinement. First, an end-to-end spatiotemporal transformer-based super-resolution model is developed to integrate spatial feature extraction and attention mechanism for temporal enhancement. Unlike conventional methods that separately construct spatial and temporal super-resolution models, a unified architecture enables simultaneous spatiotemporal super-resolution, allowing more effective learning of the spatiotemporal multi-scale interactions present in turbulence. Second, finite difference-based physical constraints are imposed on the reconstructed flow fields to ensure physically consistent predictions of fine-scale turbulence characteristics. Building on the proposed physics-informed transformer-based super-resolution model, a cascaded refinement strategy to improve multi-scale spectral reconstruction is further applied to complete our proposed Cascaded PhyFormer-SRNet framework. Through these three innovations, the Cascaded PhyFormer-SRNet achieves superior spectral accuracy across scales and facilitates high-fidelity turbulence reconstruction in space and time. Experiments show that our framework outperforms conventional methods in reconstructing multi-scale channel turbulence from highly compressed data, even at compression ratios over 99%. Separate experiments show effective reconstruction of Kolmogorov flow from both regularly and randomly distributed noisy observations, with a reduction in reconstruction error exceeding 32% for the former compared to conventional methods.

papers.title: Integrated numerical and experimental validation on optimal sail angle for unmanned sailboat
papers.abstract: Unmanned sailboats offer a sustainable solution for long-term marine operations by utilizing wind energy for propulsion. This study focuses on the optimal sail angle determination for unmanned sailboats under varying wind conditions through an integrated modeling and validation approach. A lightweight three-degree-of-freedom velocity prediction program (VPP) model was developed specifically for unmanned sailboats, enabling accurate prediction of sailing performance and optimal sail angle across a wide range of apparent wind conditions. To verify the VPP results, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were conducted, demonstrating strong consistency in sail angle predictions and validating the rationality of the proposed aerodynamic model. Furthermore, the “FanHai T1” unmanned sailboat was independently assembled and tested in a towing tank experiment. Twelve test cases across two wind speeds and six apparent wind angles were performed, each repeated three times, resulting in an average relative error of 7.86% between the predicted and measured sailing speeds. In addition, the experimentally determined optimal sail angle under a selected condition was found to align closely with VPP predictions, further confirming the model's accuracy. This study presents a reliable and efficient framework for sail angle optimization in unmanned sailboats, with promising applications in autonomous marine observation and environmental monitoring.

papers.title: Numerical study on wind load characteristics of photovoltaic modules with sand barriers
papers.abstract: Sand barriers have been extensively applied to reduce sandstorm hazards in Desert Photovoltaic (PV) systems, but their effects on the aerodynamic performance of ground PV modules are seldom addressed. In this study, the effects of sand barriers on PV modules investigated by computational fluid dynamics have been investigated. The results demonstrate that as the tilt angle is increased, the positive pressure area on the front surface shifts from the center to the sides, while the maximum negative pressure on the rear surface intensifies toward the edges. It is evident that increasing the height of the sand barrier results in the elevation of the maximum negative pressure region on the rear surface. Additionally, when the tilt angle increases from 15° to 60°, the drag coefficient (CD) increases significantly, peaking at a 900% rise. In the cases of 45° and 135° wind direction angles, the moment coefficients (CMX/Y) also increase significantly. Wind loads under the case of sand barrier height of 1 m are the highest, while the drag coefficient CD and lift coefficient (CL) are minimized at the spacing of 10.5 m. Finally, a sand barrier with a porosity of 0.5 yields an optimal distance of 10.5 m. These results can provide critical insights for wind-resistant design of PV modules, ensuring the stable operation of PV power plants in desert environments.

papers.title: Poiseuille flow-induced vibration of two tandem cylinders with different diameters in a confined channel
papers.abstract: Poiseuille flow-induced vibration of two tandem cylinders with different diameters in a confined channel flow is numerically examined by the lattice Boltzmann method. We explore how the Reynolds number (Re), cylinder distance (S/d), and cylinder blockage ratio (β) affect the drag force, the phase angle, and fluid velocity on the motion of tandem cylinders. The cylinders rest at the channel centerline (CR mode), oscillate near one side of the wall (OSL mode), and vibrate around the channel centerline (OCL modes) are discovered. It is interesting to find that when the upstream cylinder is larger than the downstream cylinder with a small distance, two cylinders can be considered as a single entity that keeps the significant oscillations even under low fluid inertia, then the vibration mode is changed with increasing Re and S/d. Sidewall amplifies shear layer interactions, enabling significant vibrations at low Reynolds numbers. As the diameter ratio of the upstream cylinder to the downstream cylinder increases, the Reynolds number corresponding to the formation of the OCL mode continuously decreases. Thus, by controlling the cylinder blockage ratio and distance, the OCL mode can be achieved at low fluid inertia. This study offers potential use in enhancing the fluid and mass transfer in a confined channel.

papers.title: Linear instability of power-law liquid jets with heat and mass transfer in a swirling gas
papers.abstract: This study investigates the instability and breakup mechanism of power-law liquid jets subject to heat and mass transfer and swirling gas in a confined environment. A mathematical model is established, and the dispersion relation between the dimensionless instability growth rate and the dimensionless wavenumber is derived by linear instability analysis. The results show that swirling gas enhances jet instability by amplifying azimuthal velocity and promoting Kelvin–Helmholtz instability. It can divide the jet into multiple species. Heat and mass transfer effect varies with the Weber number, suppressing instability at low values and enhancing it at high values. Additionally, as the heat and mass transfer increases, the jet develops toward a large azimuthal wavenumber. It is obtained through sensitivity analysis that increasing the gas velocity and wall constrains can effectively promote the jet instability. Finally, it is concluded that shear-thickening fluids are more prone to destabilization due to the dominant effect of swirling gas.

papers.title: Numerical simulation of horizontal particle jets in a supercritical water environment based on an improved coarse-grained computational fluid dynamics–discrete element method
papers.abstract: Horizontal particle jets are critical to supercritical water (SCW) reactors, as their flow behavior directly impacts reaction efficiency, heat transfer, and system stability. However, the rapid variation in fluid properties near the critical point and the complexity of particle–fluid interactions have hindered a comprehensive understanding of their kinetic characteristics. This study employs an advanced coarse-grained computational fluid dynamic–discrete element method to simulate horizontal particle jets in a SCW environment. By integrating the kinetic theory of granular flow with turbulence modeling, the proposed approach effectively captures rapid fluid property changes and complex particle–jet interactions. This study systematically analyzes the effects of transcritical and supercritical conditions on particle diffusion, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer, alongside sensitivity analyses of coarse-grained ratios on particle flow and thermal properties. The results demonstrate that higher fluid temperatures stabilize jet behavior, enhance mixing, and create more uniform temperature and density distributions. Particle diffusion is significantly influenced by temperature with increased fluid temperatures accelerating diffusion velocities. While translational velocity fluctuations decrease with rising temperatures, rotational perturbations and particle temperatures intensify before stabilizing. The coarse-grained method shows high accuracy in predicting particle behavior and heat transfer with deviations below 1%. These findings provide critical insight into the hydrodynamics of horizontal particle jets in SCW environments and offer valuable guidance for optimizing reactor design and improving operational efficiency.

papers.title: Normal rheological behavior and theoretical modeling of sepiolite shear thickening fluid
papers.abstract: Recently, the majority of studies on shear thickening fluid (STF) have considered shear rheology and viscosity, while the normal force has been neglected. Notably, investigation of the normal force is essential for elucidating the shear-thickening mechanism and expanding the practical applications of STF. Hence, in this study, a rotating rheometer was used to examine the variation in the normal force on sepiolite shear thickening fluid (Sep-STF) under different loading rates since Sep-STF exhibited a high shear-thickening performance in a prior study. The results show that the normal load-bearing capacity and energy absorption ability of Sep-STF exceeded those of pure STF. Specifically, the energy absorption capacity of Sep-STF increases by an impressive 857.40% compared with pure STF under a loading rate of 60 μm/s. An extrusion flow model derived from a piecewise power-law viscosity function coupled with the Navier boundary slip condition was proposed to analyze the velocity field and shear stress gradient distributions of Sep-STF. The normal force results obtained from this model were consistent with experimental data. Therefore, this study provides a platform allowing researchers to investigate more high-precision vibration-damping devices.

papers.title: A novel physically motivated Zener model for magnetohydrodynamics viscoelastic fluids with differential–integral fractional operator
papers.abstract: Based on the mechanism of physical memory effects, an improved fractional Zener constitutive model is proposed to describe the boundary layer characteristics of viscoelastic fluids in magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) environments. The model employs a mixed-order structure where instantaneous elastic response maintains integer-order characteristics, while delayed elastic response and viscous flow introduce fractional operators. This design simultaneously captures the stress relaxation and strain lag characteristics of the fluid. The established model is numerically solved using the finite difference method together with a fast algorithm, and the regulatory mechanisms on the fluid boundary layer characteristics are investigated. The research reveals that the proposed model achieves more comprehensive characterization of boundary layer behavior compared to conventional models, while exhibiting unique saturation effects in magnetic field regulation. The fractional parameter α governs stress relaxation, with larger values enhancing viscous behavior and producing thicker boundary layers. Parameter β controls strain memory intensity, promoting greater flow mobility. Rheologically, a larger stress relaxation time λ1 enhances elastic character and compacts boundary layers, while an increased strain lag time λ2 extends microstructural adjustment time, manifesting as thicker boundary layers. This study establishes correlations between model parameters and physical phenomena, providing a theoretical framework for understanding MHD viscoelastic fluid boundary layer behavior.

papers.title: Simulation study on permeability characteristics of shale reservoirs considering multi-scale rough fracture network
papers.abstract: The actual reservoir fracture network has multi-scale characteristics, is the main channel for gas flow in shale reservoirs, and determines the seepage capacity of the reservoir. Therefore, it is of great significance to conduct research on reservoir permeability characteristics considering multi-scale features of fractures. In this paper, a multi-scale fracture network generation algorithm is proposed. Then, considering millimeter-, centimeter-, and meter-scale multi-scale fractures in shale reservoirs, a multi-scale fracture network seepage simulation model is established to analyze the seepage characteristics of the fracture network under the influence of multi-scale features. The results show that both the fracture network structure and modeling parameters significantly affect the gas flow. The increase in mesoscale fractures has a more significant effect on the seepage capacity of the multiscale fracture network than that of small-scale fractures. The gas flux increases by about 1.5 times when the number of mesoscale fractures increases by a factor of 1, while the gas flux increases only by a factor of 0.1 when the number of small-scale fractures increases by a factor of 2. The increase in mesoscale and small-scale fractures enhances the topological connectivity of the multiscale fracture network, and the gas fluxes subsequently increase to —four to six times of the original ones. When the large-scale fractures are connected to the gas outlet boundary, the seepage performance of the multiscale fracture network is greatly improved. When the large-scale fractures are connected to the gas inlet boundary only, the seepage performance of the multiscale fracture network is not significantly improved or even decreased. Compared to when the boundary is unconnected, the gas flux of the multiscale fracture network after connecting the boundary is enhanced by about four times.

papers.title: Generalized Riemann problem method for the Kapila model of compressible multiphase flows
papers.abstract: The Kapila model, reduced from the Baer–Nunziato model, is becoming increasingly popular for numerical simulations of compressible multiphase flows. In the Kapila model, the volume fraction equation includes a stiff source term containing velocity divergence, posing significant challenges for numerical schemes. Most existing numerical methods employ Runge–Kutta time stepping strategies and Riemann solvers. The effect of the source term is not fully resolved in Riemann solutions. In this paper, a robust second-order finite volume scheme is developed for the Kapila model of compressible multiphase flows. The scheme is developed using the generalized Riemann problem (GRP) solver as the cornerstone. Besides Riemann solutions, the GRP solver provides time derivatives of flow variables at cell interfaces, achieving second-order accuracy in time within a single stage. The use of the GRP solver enhances the capability of the resulting scheme to handle the stiffness of the Kapila model in two ways. First, Riemann solutions and time derivatives give the cell interface values of flow variables at the new time level, yielding an approximation to the velocity divergence at the new time level in a computational step. This allows a semi-implicit time discretization to the stiff source term in the volume fraction equation. Second, the effect of the source term is included in numerical fluxes by considering time derivatives. The resulting numerical flux is able to capture the interactions between phases. The robustness of the scheme is, therefore, further improved. Several challenging numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the good performance of the proposed scheme.

papers.title: The gas interchange between bubble and emulsion phases in a negative pressure bubbling fluidized bed by computational fluid dynamics simulations
papers.abstract: This paper employs an Eulerian–Eulerian two-fluid computational model to simulate and analyze the effects of negative pressure, superficial velocity, and temperature on gas exchange between the bubble phase and emulsion phase in a large-scale negative pressure bubbling fluidized bed. During the validation phase, we integrated experimental methods with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, systematically comparing the simulation results with experimental data to assess the model's accuracy and reliability. In the second step, based on the CFD simulations, we used a statistical method for bubble boundaries to calculate the gas exchange coefficient. The results indicate that the gas exchange coefficient increases with increasing negative pressure (i.e., decreasing absolute pressure) and correlates significantly with increases in superficial velocity and temperature. Notably, an increase in superficial velocity also results in a decrease in the average diameter of the bubbles. Furthermore, this paper introduces a correction term to account for the influence of negative pressure on the gas diffusion coefficient and calculates the gas exchange coefficient between the bubble phase and emulsion phase in the negative pressure bubbling fluidized bed. The outcomes of this study contribute to a better understanding of interphase gas dynamics under negative pressure conditions, offering valuable insights for industrial applications in fluidized bed reactor optimization and scale-up.

papers.title: Dynamic prediction of nano-milk transport in a parabolically elevated electromagnetic channel with parabolic thermal ramping: A Python-based machine learning approach
papers.abstract: This study analyzes the fluctuating dynamics of milk flow containing silver and magnesium oxide nanoparticles in a parabolically elevated electromagnetic channel exposed to a parabolic thermal ramp-up, employing artificial intelligence (AI)-based machine learning algorithms in Python. This study unifies key physical phenomena comprising thermal heat flux, heat sinks, and porous medium's impendence. Employing rigorous mathematical and computational methods such as the Laplace transform for streamlined solutions to dynamic flow equations, we analyze milk flow dynamics, concentrating on variables like shear stress (SS) and rate of heat transfer (RHT), and presenting results through detailed graphical representations. The findings indicate that nanoparticles significantly enhance thermal conductivity and viscosity, thereby improving heat transport efficiency and modifying flow dynamics. Notably, an elevation in milk momentum is observed with a higher modified Hartmann number, while wider electrode widths help mitigate this effect. In milk flow, escalated pressure oscillation frequencies intensify SS, and elevated heat source parameters enhance RHT. The AI-based machine learning algorithms in Python, reinforced by artificial neural networks, achieves 100% precision in SS prediction on both training and validation datasets and maintains 99.974% accuracy on testing datasets and 99.93% during cross-validation for RHT predictions. The model findings highlight the potential of nanoparticle-enhanced milk for efficient heating, crucial to improving pasteurization and sterilization. Python AI algorithms enable real-time control, boosting efficiency, quality, and sustainability in dairy processing.

papers.title: The gas-oil minimum miscibility pressure variation patterns and prediction for associated gas reinjection in the J oilfield
papers.abstract: To elucidate the miscibility mechanisms of injection gas and crude oil during the reinjection of associated gas with a high CO2 content, the slim tube method was employed to determine the minimum miscibility pressure (MMP) of the injected gas and crude oil. A correlation analysis was conducted to establish an MMP prediction model for associated gas reinjection. The results indicate that the reinjection of high-CO2-content associated gas in the studied block is feasible, and removing CH4 and N2 from the associated gas can significantly improve the recovery efficiency. There are notable differences in the displacement efficiencies and miscibility potentials of different gases with C1 exhibiting the lowest oil displacement efficiency and C4 the highest. To predict the MMP in the context of associated gas reinjection, this study utilized 46 sets of experimental data and applied linear regression and gray relational analysis to identify key influencing factors, including reservoir temperature, light components in crude oil (N2, CH4), and C2–C4 concentrations. Based on this analysis, a novel MMP prediction model using nonlinear fitting was proposed for the first time. The correlation coefficient (R2) of the model was 0.913 37, indicating a high prediction accuracy. Experimental validation revealed that the model achieved an average relative error of only 4.8% when predicting the MMP for associated gas reinjection in the J oilfield. This study demonstrates that the proposed model effectively addresses the challenges of MMP prediction under associated gas injection conditions, providing a reliable reference for an optimized design in practical oilfield development.

papers.title: Emerging perspectives in non-Newtonian fluid dynamics: Research gaps, evolving methods, and conceptual limitations
papers.abstract: This paper primarily focuses on areas within non-Newtonian fluid mechanics that remain underexplored or inadequately investigated. It highlights research domains that have not received sufficient attention or detailed study, while also considering the emergence of new areas unexplored by recent scientific and technological advancements. For example, this study explores research directions and innovative modeling and theoretical strategies for understanding fluid dynamics in complex, deformable, and branched flow systems across multiple scales. The elastoviscoplastic behavior of fluids under external forcing is used to model droplet spreading, coalescence, and filtering over porous and soft substrates. Wall slip and junction resistance effects of the flow are in a tree-like structure. The study also highlights and explores research directions in the flow physics of non-Newtonian fluids that exhibit odd viscosity and odd elasticity, focusing on their unconventional stress–strain responses and the resulting unique flow behaviors. The objective of this paper is to raise awareness about these relatively neglected or unexplored areas of research, encouraging researchers to put efforts toward these promising domains. By doing so, they can contribute to advancing the field in ways that diverge from which have already been sufficiently explored and may lead to breakthroughs and novel discoveries by generalizing the existing laws or creating new models and laws. Moreover, addressing these under-explored areas could have far-reaching implications for both theoretical and practical applications in non-Newtonian fluid mechanics. Investigating these areas more deeply could uncover new insights, enhance existing models, and drive forward technological advancements that were previously overlooked. In addition, this paper will briefly discuss the potential introduction of novel tools, techniques, and methodologies that could be applied to these research areas, as well as to the broader field of non-Newtonian fluid mechanics. Furthermore, we also discuss the current and upcoming applications using non-Newtonian fluids. These innovations could open up new avenues of exploration and help overcome some of the existing limitations in past and current research.

papers.title: Nonlinear spin-up flow in magnetic colloidal suspensions under high-frequency rotating magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We investigate the spin-up flow dynamics of dilute ferrofluids under a rotating magnetic field with a focus on high frequencies. Three models are compared: the first- and second-order approximations of the orientational probability density function and the full Smoluchowski equation. The first-order approximation, while computationally simple, has not been tested for its validity in high-frequency regimes, nor has it been compared with experimental data in such regimes. A parametric study explores the effects of magnetic field intensity, nanoparticle concentration, and particle diameter in the clusterless regime. Two types of ferrofluids—water-based and oil-based—are considered, each with different behaviors at high frequencies. The results show a transition in spin-up behavior from increasing torque and velocity with frequency to a regime where torque flattening causes flow attenuation. While the full Smoluchowski model captures additional nonlinear effects, the second-order approximation offers a computationally efficient and accurate alternative. It provides a good balance between accuracy and efficiency, especially when additional phenomena, such as the Kelvin body force, come into play.

papers.title: Effect of surface wettability on liquid water freezing behavior in the gas diffusion layer of proton exchange membrane fuel cells
papers.abstract: During the operation of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), particularly under low-temperature cold-start conditions, the freezing of liquid water within the gas diffusion layer (GDL) can significantly impair both the performance and structural stability of the cell. Therefore, effective water management strategies are essential. This study combines high-fidelity numerical simulations and in situ cryo-microscopy to systematically investigate the impact of carbon fiber structure on the dynamic transport characteristics of liquid water on the GDL surface. Additionally, the influence of GDL surface wettability and carbon fiber structure on the freezing behavior of liquid water is explored. The results show that by adjusting fiber spacing and surface wettability, it is possible to control the diffusion behavior of liquid water within the GDL and reduce the risk of flooding. Hydrophilic GDLs promote a uniform water distribution throughout the pore structure and facilitate a continuous freezing process. In contrast, hydrophobic GDLs result in discrete droplet freezing and abrupt pore blockage. The hydrophobic GDL reaches a peak ice coverage of 18% at −15 °C, while the hydrophilic GDL shows a sharper increase, reaching 26% at −30 °C after steadily increasing to −20 °C. These differences are attributed to variations in surface wettability and fiber-scale wetting interactions between the two materials. The findings emphasize the critical role of wettability in directing ice growth pathways and maintaining the structural integrity of the GDL. This study offers valuable theoretical insights for optimizing GDL design and provides experimental evidence for improving the cold-start performance of PEMFCs.

papers.title: A comparative study on the application of phase transition theory analytical method and phase plane method to strain localization in brittle rocks
papers.abstract: The initiation and propagation of strain localization can lead to degradation of intergranular cementation, local strength loss of materials, and accelerated deformation instability, which can induce underground engineering disasters. Describing the strain localization process from the perspective of phase transition theory is reasonable. When solving the theoretical model, two analytical methods, the perturbation method and the phase plane method, are used for analysis. Both calculation results can effectively describe the strain localization process in rock masses. This study compares and analyzes the two solution methods, describing the strain localization process in rocks separately to determine which method is more reasonable for describing the evolution of strain localization. The research finds that the phase plane analysis method can describe the strain localization evolution phenomenon in materials, offering both rationality and simplicity. Through a multi-objective optimization algorithm (NSGA-II), the optimal numerical solution for the phase plane is matched, demonstrating speed and intelligence compared to traditional approximate analytical methods.

papers.title: Stress-fracture-migration field coupling characteristic in gas-water bearing coal under the influence of mining activity
papers.abstract: Coal damage and gas conductivity under mining conditions govern the gas drainage and mining safety, which concerns the coupling results of in situ stress, fracture, and fluid seepage. In this study, the evolution behaviors of damage and conductivity in coal ahead of the mining face were investigated using a novel true triaxial loading apparatus with a function of nuclear magnetic resonance monitoring. The multifield coupling mechanism and its influence on gas drainage were analyzed based on experimental data and field measurements. The results reveal that the stress-dependent coal undergoes four stages: a homogeneous compression stage with a large number of gas desorptions, anisotropic fracture growth stage with limited desorption gas, a homogeneous crack penetration stage with abundant desorption gas, and a mature pore-fracture stage with abundant gas channeling. Permeability varied from 0 to 0.17 mD throughout the compression-failure process as “X-shape” shear fracture formed with localized tension crack. Coal damage morphology transitioned from multi-winged to single-wing with increasing distance from the roadway. Elevated intermediate principal stress enhanced the crack compaction, with a mature state conductivity of pore-fracture (fractal dimension of 1.015) at the intermediate principal stress of 5 MPa. In contrast, a well-developed pore-fracture network with a fractal dimension of 0.998 was observed at 10 MPa. The gas migration was limited by the surface tension, capillary effect in micropore and mesopore, but promoted by the gas slipping effect in macropore. The maximum relative gas permeability occurred at the developed pore-fracture stage, and lower relative gas permeability was present at the compression and maturation pore-fracture stages. The desorption-migration zone, desorption zone, compression zone, and free gas zone were divided ahead of the mining face, and a relatively higher gas discharge of 0.12–1.15 m3/min and concentration of 12%–83% was present at the roadway side. Fracture development promoted the gas desorption, and efficient pore connectivity combined with low water saturation benefits gas migration. The findings provide significant insight into the coal mining of coal and gas in engineering practice.

papers.title: Crude oil mobilization enhanced by nano-emulsion in the full fracturing process for tight oil reservoirs
papers.abstract: The Chang 8 tight sandstone reservoir in the Ordos Basin is primarily developed using a nano-variable-viscosity fracturing fluid. However, the contribution of the fracturing fluid to crude oil mobilization and the mechanisms of oil–water interaction during the three stages of “fracturing–soaking–flowback” remains unclear. A full-process simulation device for “fracturing–soaking–flowback” is constructed based on nuclear magnetic resonance technology. Two types of crude oil mobilization fracturing fluids, nano-amphiphile and nano-emulsion, are compared and studied. Quantitative analysis of the distribution and changes of crude oil in core pores at different stages leads to the development of a new technology for calculating oil–water relative permeability. Results indicate that: (1) Rapid wettability modification by nano-emulsions enhances sweep efficiency, imbibition displacement, and flowback efficiency, increasing the total oil recovery factor to 87.71%. (2) A particle size of approximately 10 nm facilitates crude oil mobilization in nanopores. (3) Relative permeability movement, driven by rock wettability modification, is a key mechanism for enhanced oil recovery with residual oil saturation reduced to about 7% during the flowback stage. (4) A decrease in the degree of emulsification between the fracturing fluid and crude oil may also significantly improve crude oil mobilization. This study provides a scientific foundation for optimizing fracturing development and oil mobilization processes in tight oil reservoirs.

papers.title: On the spatiotemporal dynamics of multi-mode fluid resonance in moonpools with recess
papers.abstract: Wave-induced nonlinear fluid resonance in moonpools with a recess is numerically investigated in this work based on a two-dimensional multiphase viscous flow solver. The objective is to explore the spatiotemporal dynamics of wave resonance, with a particular emphasis on identifying modal contributions, characterizing nonlinear harmonic interactions, and revealing frequency-dependent mode transitions. This study aims to provide new insight into the fundamental mechanisms governing multi-modal fluid resonance under nonlinear and viscous conditions. Two distinct temporal evolution regimes of resonant fluid oscillations, i.e., piston-mode and sloshing-mode resonance, are clarified via time-resolved wavelet spectra and phase dynamics analysis. The piston mode exhibits linear, coherent oscillations characterized by phase locking state, whereas the sloshing mode demonstrates strong nonlinearity, higher-order harmonic generation, and nonlinear phase trapping behavior. A mode displacement superposition mathematical approach is employed to quantify the modal contributions, revealing frequency-dependent energy exchange between piston and sloshing modes, particularly near superharmonic resonance conditions. Spatial analysis further shows that resonant amplification is highly localized, with certain modal responses absent at nodal positions. Harmonic decomposition confirms the critical role of nonlinear energy redistribution at or around the superharmonic resonant frequencies. The physical insight gained from this study advances the understanding of the dynamic establishment of the complex multi-mode moonpool resonance and offers valuable guidance for future modal analysis.

papers.title: Construction of a self-excited foam dust suppression system and study on gas–liquid regulation mechanism in coal mining face
papers.abstract: Coal mining faces persistently face the challenge of excessive dust concentrations, posing significant occupational health risks. This study proposes a self-excited foam dust suppression system integrated with a gas–liquid regulation mechanism. Through a combination of numerical simulations and experimental validation, the research focuses on three aspects: compound optimization of fine wet foam dust suppressants, multi-parameter collaborative regulation of bubble generation devices, and on-site application efficacy evaluation. Orthogonal experiments identified the optimal dust suppressant formulation as 0.01% dioctyl sulfosuccinate sodium salt + 0.05% alkyl polyglucoside + 0.1% alcohol ether sulfate. Numerical and experimental results demonstrated that under a water supply pressure of 3.0 MPa, a suction pipe diameter of 10 mm, and an L-shaped tee structure, the system achieved an optimal negative pressure of −753.02 Pa, a jet velocity of 9.627 m/s, and a gas–water ratio (λ) improvement of 9.73 compared to conventional configurations. Field application at the 823 coal mining face in Yuandian No. 1 Coal Mine showed total and respirable dust suppression efficiencies of 78.1% and 81.7%, respectively, representing 35.7% and 42.3% enhancements over traditional spray systems. This study innovatively integrates gas–liquid directional regulation and composite wetting enhancement technologies, providing theoretical and technical insights for dust control in coal mining environments.

papers.title: Prediction of cavitation inception number around axisymmetric bodies based on nuclei dynamics mutation
papers.abstract: Cavitation inception is a critical phenomenon significantly impacting the performance of hydraulic machinery, while traditional prediction criterion is constrained by neglecting the gas nuclei effect, leading to inaccurate estimation of cavitation inception number. In this paper, we proposed a more physical criterion based on the mutation of nuclei dynamics across cavitation numbers. To obtain the information of nuclei dynamics in realistic flow, we employed a Euler–Lagrange model. The feasibility of the nuclei dynamics mutation criterion is examined in the cavitation inception case around axisymmetric bodies with different head configurations. Compared with the measured cavitation inception number, the new criterion reduces the error from 158.9% and 63.1% to 4.1% over the traditional criteria based on minimum pressure or vapor volume. This research provides a more precise criterion for predicting cavitation inception number, conducive to the structural optimization of high-speed underwater vehicles and advanced prevention of negative effects caused by cavitation.

papers.title: Effects of through-draught on the transmission and distribution of droplets within double-formation subway carriages
papers.abstract: The situation of mass infections caused by respiratory diseases in public places continues to pose a significant threat to public health, particularly in the context of the subway, which is characterized by its high passenger density. While there exists a modicum of research on the transmission and spread of droplets within the subway compartment, these studies primarily focus on the environment of a stationary subway and a single carriage. There is a paucity of research on the specific flow field environment formed during subway operation, particularly in the case of through-draught. This study utilizes numerical simulation to analyze the transmission and distribution of droplets within the two-formation subway carriages under the influence of through-draught. The findings reveal that through-draught substantially augments the transmission distance of droplets in the direction of through-draught, reaching up to approximately 24 times the baseline value. Concurrently, through-draught suppresses the maximum transmission distances in the transverse and vertical directions, reducing them by approximately 29.7% and 22.0%, respectively. Furthermore, through-draught has been observed to reduce the suspension time of droplets and to augment the distribution range of their ultimate deposition positions within the passenger compartment. With the increase in the air volume of through-draught, droplets spread downstream in the passenger compartment, with more than 80% of the droplets depositing downstream of the release source. These findings elucidate the impact of through-draught on droplet transmission in the passenger compartment and further reveal the migration mechanism and distribution law of droplets in the carriages of an operating subway.

papers.title: Numerical investigation on bubble dynamics and pressure wavelet characteristics of the four-opening seismic airgun
papers.abstract: The seismic sources generated by airguns have long been used for the marine resources and seabed geological exploration. This work investigates seismic bubble dynamics and pressure wavelet features using detailed numerical simulations of full-scale, four-port airguns within the OpenFOAM framework. The Navier–Stokes equations are spatially discretized via the finite volume method, with the volume of fluid method employed to capture the evolving bubble interface. Gas emission from the ports initially creates four separate bubbles, which subsequently merge into a single, larger bubble. Some flow details including coalescence features of the bubbles and mass throttling of the opening port are discussed. Meanwhile, it is observed that the coherent interaction induced by the four expanding bubbles can suppress the initial pressure wavelet attenuation, which might provide an innovative way to optimize the performance of the single four-opening airgun. In addition, the results from our studies on airguns with different configurations indicate that the airgun parameters including firing pressure, opening size and form, airgun volume are primary to the pressure wavelet characteristics, though some minor details outside the airgun wall can slightly affect the bubble evolution.

papers.title: Settling of U-shaped rods at low Reynolds numbers
papers.abstract: The low Reynolds number settling of U-shaped and straight rods in a quiescent fluid was experimentally investigated in this study. It was shown that the U-shaped rods adopt an oblique orientation and horizontal drift at Reynolds numbers above a critical value and middle arm length ratios below a critical value. Due to the non-zero inclination angle of a U-shaped rod, it consistently settles faster than a straight rod with the same diameter and aspect ratio. The vertical component of the U-shaped rod terminal velocity reaches a maximum at an intermediate value of aspect ratio and middle arm length ratio or remains nearly constant as these geometric parameters change, indicating a trade-off between the length and orientation of the side arms. Furthermore, the horizontal velocity ratio of a U-shaped rod is strongly correlated with the inclination angle, either increasing or remaining constant with an increase in aspect ratio, depending on the Reynolds number. Finally, a new model for the vertical component of a U-shaped rod terminal velocity was developed using the experimental results of this study.

papers.title: Evaluating the performance of a solar-geothermal heat pump system for heating a greenhouse
papers.abstract: This study examines the simultaneous utilization of geothermal and solar energy for a greenhouse during the four coldest months of the year. The performance factor and exergy efficiency will be assessed throughout this period, and the variations in these parameters will be analyzed in relation to the temperature of the water entering the geothermal heat exchanger and the surrounding ambient temperature. In this study, the use of R22 (chlorodifluoromethane) with a mass flow rate of 0.1 (kg/h) provides important insights into their performance in an integrated system. This research presents a new method for optimizing a hybrid system by strategically integrating solar and geothermal energy, which results in increased power output and energy efficiency, and consequently reduced exergy efficiency. To achieve this objective, a suitable thermodynamic cycle is examined for greenhouse heating. By analyzing the laws of thermodynamics in relation to this cycle, the performance factor and exergy efficiency values are determined for the four coldest months of the year. The results show that the performance factor in January, February, March, and December was 4.136, 3.050, 3.048, and 4.205, respectively, and the exergy efficiency was 78.58%, 78.01%, 78.00%, and 78.62%. By examining the effect of the temperature of the water entering the geothermal heat exchanger on the coefficient of performance and exergy efficiency, it was found that by increasing the temperature from 6.7 °C to 9.5 °C, the efficiency of the geothermal system increases by 1.3%, which increases the efficiency of the entire system by 1.45%.

papers.title: Maximum density effects on the stability of thermal convection in a vertical Brinkman layer with uniform horizontal throughflow
papers.abstract: This study examines the impact of the maximum density property on the instability of thermal convection in a vertical Brinkman layer under uniform horizontal throughflow. Deviating from the classical Boussinesq approximation, the density relationship is modified to a quadratic polynomial. The Navier–Stokes equations are converted to the Orr–Sommerfeld eigenvalue problem by linear stability analysis and solved numerically by the Chebyshev collocation method. The results show that the maximum density effect will cause the buoyancy to reverse, counteract some disturbances, and enhance the stability of the system. Moreover, the presence of throughflow has a significant impact on the basic state and instability. At low Pe, increasing throughflow enhances stability; however, beyond a critical range, further increase in Pe amplifies inertial effects and vertical temperature non-uniformity, which destabilize the stability. Meanwhile, PrD also has dual effect on system stability, with low PrD promoting instability and high PrD enhancing viscous diffusion to suppress instability. Particularly, the pure and modified quadratic density models exhibit similar stability behavior in certain regions.

papers.title: Influence and mechanism analysis of spatial heterogeneity on the propagation characteristics of near-limit detonation
papers.abstract: The present work numerically investigates the effects of periodic sinusoidal and more realistic random spatial heterogeneities on near-limit detonation propagation in a thin explosive slab confined by inert layers and analyzes the mechanisms of these effects. Random heterogeneity is modeled by superimposing sinusoidal ripples with random center coordinates. Results demonstrate that sinusoidal and random heterogeneities with appropriate sizes, particularly 5–50 times the half-reaction zone length, produce clear regular and irregular cellular-like complex shock structures, respectively, and enhance propagation velocity, thus narrowing the critical thickness corresponding to the thinnest reactive layer for self-sustained detonation. Larger amplitudes or random distributions, representing higher degrees of heterogeneity, further extend propagation limits. In contrast, heterogeneities with wavelengths smaller than the reaction zone are rapidly averaged out, and the detonation characteristics converge to those of the homogeneous case. When the size of individual perturbations is comparable to the charge thickness, a velocity deficit occurs. The mechanisms of the impact of appropriate-sized and large-sized heterogeneities on detonation propagation are explained from the perspectives of energy release and loss. Appropriate-sized heterogeneities cause localized energy release inhomogeneity, inducing unstable transverse waves and triple-point structures that accelerate reaction rates, while elevated inert layer impedance mitigates lateral losses. The influence mechanism of large-scale heterogeneities lies in the alteration of sonic surface positions. As the detonation wave passes through the high-density zone, a significant portion of the heat is released outside the sonic surface, and more explosives at the edge of the high-density zone are driven into the inert layer.

papers.title: Sequential drop impacts onto horizontal fiber arrays
papers.abstract: We experimentally investigate liquid infiltration into horizontally oriented fiber arrays imposed by sequential drop impacts. Our experimental system is inspired by mammalian fur coats, and our results provide insight to how we expect natural fibers to respond to falling drops and the structure innate to this multiscale covering. Two successive drop impacts are filmed striking three-dimensional-printed fiber arrays with varying densities, surface wettability, and fixed fiber diameter. The penetration depth and the lateral width of drop spreading within fiber layers are functions of drop displacement relative to the liquid already within the array as well as the drop Weber number. Hydrophobic fibers more effectively prevent an increase in penetration depth by the second impacting drop at low impact Weber numbers, whereas hydrophilic fibers ensure lower liquid penetration depth into the array as the Weber number increases. Impact outcomes, such as penetration depth and lateral spreading, are insensitive to impact eccentricity between the first and second drops at high experimental Weber numbers. As expected, denser, staggered fibers reduce infiltration, preventing the entire drop mass from entering the array. Fragmentation of the first drop, which is promoted by hydrophobicity, larger inter-fiber spacing, and higher drop impact velocity, limits increases in lateral spreading and penetration depth of the liquid mass from a subsequent drop.

papers.title: Modular fine-tuning of physics-informed neural networks for natural convection in eccentric geometries
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as promising tools for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) in complex domains, yet their adaptation to geometrically varying configurations remains computationally demanding. This work introduces a modular transfer learning framework for PINNs that combines boundary-aware pretraining, intermediate fine-tuning, and a lightweight geometry-specific correction layer. The method enforces Dirichlet boundary conditions through hard constraints to ensure physical consistency across geometries. Natural convection in eccentric annuli is selected as a benchmark case to assess performance against computational fluid dynamics ground truth over a range of geometric perturbations. Lightweight fine-tuning achieves temperature prediction errors below 2% in moderately perturbed cases while preserving coherent flow and thermal structures under significant domain shifts. Compared to full fine-tuning, the proposed approach reduces trainable parameters and training time by a substantial margin, making it suitable for rapid deployment in surrogate modeling and digital twin applications. The results underscore the framework's capacity for efficient and accurate generalization across geometrical variations in PDE-based simulations.

papers.title: Drag reduction of turbulent boundary layer flow with traveling wavy wall on flexible rubber sheet
papers.abstract: An effect of a traveling wavy wall deformation generated on a flexible rubber sheet for the drag reduction of turbulent boundary layer flow was investigated. The traveling wave was generated by oscillating the upstream end of the rubber sheet in the wall-normal direction using a piezoelectric actuator so that the wave travels in the streamwise direction. The parameters of the traveling wave, e.g., amplitude, wavelength, and wave speed, are given in the range where fully developed turbulent flows could be relaminarized in Nakanishi et al. [“Relaminarization of turbulent channel flow using traveling wave-like wall deformation,” Int. J. Heat Fluid Flow 35, 152–159 (2012)] and Mamori et al. [“Effect of the parameters of traveling waves created by blowing and suction on the relaminarization phenomena in fully developed turbulent channel flow,” Phys. Fluids 26, 015101 (2014)]. A two-component laser Doppler velocimetry was used to measure the streamwise and the wall-normal velocities. The flow was measured at two streamwise points where the Reynolds numbers based on the momentum thickness without control were 620 and 880. The momentum in the boundary layer was evaluated using the von Kármán momentum integral equation considering the momentum defect, the fluctuating momentum, and the pressure gradient in the boundary layer. The total drag between the measurement points quantified by the momentum equation was reduced by 9.4% due to the traveling wave. The modification of the turbulence was discussed in terms of a velocity fluctuation decomposed into periodic and random components. The wavy wall directly induced the periodic forcing in the near-wall region while secondarily reducing the turbulent fluctuation in the wide range of the boundary layer. The reduced turbulent fluctuations result in a reduction in the momentum defect, which contributes to the reduction in the drag quantified by the momentum equation.

papers.title: Effect of various mountainous terrains on the aerodynamic characteristics of high-speed trains under cross wind
papers.abstract: The non-uniform wind fields generated by complex mountainous terrains pose significant challenges to train operation safety. A validated numerical method was adopted to explore the effects of various mountainous terrains on the aerodynamic performance of high-speed trains under crosswind. Specifically, the wind flow characteristics, flow field around trains, and aerodynamic loads acting on trains under five typical mountainous terrain configurations were thoroughly investigated. The results indicate that variations in wind field along the railway line are primarily caused by the airflow acceleration at the side edge and wake disturbance at the wake of the mountains. Among these five mountainous configurations, saddle terrain demonstrates more pronounced flow acceleration and an extended wake region due to the smaller inter-gap distance between the two mountains. Although the trailing car experiences the smallest aerodynamic forces, it exhibits the highest sensitivity to terrain configurations. Under saddle terrain conditions, the lateral force and overturning moment of the tail car increase by 279.0% and 140.7%, respectively, compared to the flat ground case. The aerodynamic peaks are observed at the critical moment when the trailing car emerges from the mountain's sheltering effect. This substantial aerodynamic load increase stems from a longitudinal vortex initiating at the train's head. The vortex develops downward to the rear while maintaining close alignment with the body surface. Such persistent attachment induces a marked negative pressure surge specifically on the tail nose. The research provides a theoretical basis and identifies critical risk parameters for wind hazard prevention in mountainous railway operations.

papers.title: Experimental investigation on characteristics of pressure fluctuation and vibration under hump instability of a pump-turbine
papers.abstract: For pump-turbines, the hump region in a head curve under the pump mode is an extremely unstable zone that severely restricts the stable operating range. This study proposes a fractal theory-based framework that integrates quadratic mode decomposition for non-intrusive early warning and mechanistic analysis of hump instability in pump-turbines. A warning coefficient Wh = 2, derived from relative variations in the multifractal intensity of vibration, serves as a robust threshold for identifying critical rotating stall. Systematic investigations reveal that pressure fluctuation dominates vibration excitation during stability degradation. Under relatively stable conditions, strong linear coherence between pressure fluctuation and vibration is concentrated at rotor–stator interaction frequencies. However, as hump instability develops, the interaction shifts from a linear correlation dominance to nonlinear-dominant mode—linear coherence decreases, while nonlinear energy transfer efficiency increases, as evidenced by a more than 25% rise in transfer entropy. Moreover, hump instability induces divergent variation trends between long-range cross correlation and coupling intensity. During the transition from the critical stall to the hump region, a long-range cross correlation decreases, whereas multifractal cross correlation intensity increases by over 40%, indicating intensified multiscale interactions driven by flow destabilization. These findings provide theoretical foundations for instability mitigation and operational optimization in pumped-storage hydropower systems.

papers.title: Acoustics of permeable media with active internal heat sources
papers.abstract: Acoustics of permeable media with active internal heat sources is investigated in this paper. A macroscopic non-homogeneous Helmholtz equation, established by using the two-scale asymptotic method of homogenization, is found to describe the propagation and emission of sound waves in the studied permeable media. We study two classes of permeable materials in which external energy is injected. In one of them, the heat sources act in the material solid skeleton, while in the other class of materials they act in the pore fluid network, with the generalization to the case of heat sources acting in both constituents also provided. The derived macroscopic description shows that the general properties of the effective parameters of the fluid equivalent to the permeable medium are not altered by the internal heat sources. However, these sources determine the non-homogeneous term in the upscaled Helmholtz equation. Through theoretical analyses and analytical models, the key characteristics of acoustic wave propagation and emission in the studied media are illustrated. Additionally, a generalized impedance matching condition, enabling the control of the active apparent sound reflection and absorption coefficients of rigidly backed finite layers of the materials, is first introduced. The results of this work provide fundamental insights on the role of active internal heat sources on the linear long-wavelength acoustics of permeable media and lay the foundation for the development of active thermoacoustic porous materials for acoustic wave control applications.

papers.title: Anomalous behavior of Taylor bubble rise in glycerol solutions–mechanistic insights and numerical simulations
papers.abstract: The present study reports a hitherto unexplored phenomenon during Taylor bubble rise through glycerol solutions of different concentrations. There are numerous studies on Taylor bubble rise through aqueous glycerol. These primarily focus on concentrated glycerol solutions (> 50%v/v) and report a decrease in rise velocity with increasing concentration. In the present study, experiments over 0–80%v/v glycerol solution reveal an anomalous trend. An increase in concentration from pure water results in a higher bubble rise velocity up to around 40%v/v, beyond which the rise velocity decreases with increasing concentration. The counterintuitive observation is investigated through extensive visualization using particle image velocimetry and videography, along with numerical simulations using COMSOL Multiphysics v6.0 and a theoretical analysis. We attribute this to the piecewise-linear variation of viscosity with concentration, with the point of inflection ∼ 40%v/v concentration. Thus, below this concentration, the more pronounced effect of density (through buoyancy effect) and surface tension compared to viscosity results in a higher radius at the bubble tip, implying a flatter nose, which leads to the unanticipated phenomenon. The increase in liquid film thickness with concentration is also sharper beyond the inflection point due to the combined effect of increasing viscosity and decreasing surface tension. The anomalous range of glycerol concentration is identified in terms of capillary and bond numbers. The anomaly is also rationalized based on its quantitative behavior. The findings deliver a fresh perspective on the intricate interplay of forces governing Taylor bubble motion in Newtonian media and contribute to a broader understanding of bubble dynamics.

papers.title: Intelligent optimization of sealing system based on reciprocating sealing soft elastohydrodynamic lubrication theory
papers.abstract: Aiming at the problem that the reciprocating seals of hydraulic systems under extreme working conditions can hardly meet the low leakage requirements, the sealing system is prone to failure. A high-precision seal performance analysis method is proposed considering surface roughness and cavitation effect and a multi-objective optimization design method combining deep learning algorithms. By introducing the average flow factor and cavitation factor into the Reynolds equation, a reciprocating seal soft elastohydrodynamic lubrication model with careful consideration of surface roughness and fluid cavitation effect is established to analyze the influence of key structural parameters and working conditions on the sealing performance. The accuracy of the numerical model is verified by comparing it with the literature. With the optimization objectives of minimum leakage, the minimum and maximum equivalent stress of the seal, and minimum friction force, a representative sample library is obtained using the Latin hypercube sampling method. The A time series forecasting model based on the fused sine-cosine and Cauchy variant of the Sparrow optimization algorithm for bidirectional long- and short-term memory networks was used to establish an agent model of the mapping relationship between the design variables and the objective function with high fitting accuracy and combined with the second-generation non-inferiority-ranked genetic algorithm, a set of optimal solutions considering the importance of the objective function was obtained. The results show that the seal leakage is reduced by 12.5%, the maximum equivalent force is reduced by 10.56%, and the friction force is reduced by 11.48% compared with that before optimization. This paper provides an efficient optimization design method for seal structure design.

papers.title: Optoelectronic tweezers induced electroosmotic vortex for manipulating microparticles swarm
papers.abstract: Microparticle swarms have wide applications, such as targeted delivery, biosensing, and micro-scale cleaning. Effective control of these swarms is, therefore, crucial. This study reports an approach for manipulating the microparticles swarm by utilizing optoelectronic tweezers induced dynamic electroosmotic vortex. Through combined numerical simulations and experimental investigations, we confirmed that patterned light virtual electrodes create electroosmotic vortex effect at illuminated edges, since the non-uniform electric field caused by the light pattern forms a strong tangential electric field component working on an electric double layer. Subsequently, microparticles were trapped by the vortex. The results indicated that microparticles self-assemble into chain-like structures in vortex, executing stable orbital motion controlled by light pattern geometry. The orbital range reached 279.2 μm. Finally, we demonstrated that, after captured by the light-induced electroosmotic vortex, microparticle swarms can be effectively transported across a microfluidic chip. The light pattern transporting speed can reach to 154.6 μm/s. Moreover, applying different light patterns can achieve different manipulating effects. This approach offers a versatile, non-contact method for potential applications in microparticle manipulation and microscale assembly.

papers.title: Research on the fracture propagation mechanism of multi-directional radial boreholes fracturing
papers.abstract: Radial boreholes fracturing is a kind of reservoir stimulation technique, which can guide fractures to extend directionally in multiple directions and realize multi-fracture stereoscopic reconstruction of reservoirs. Current research on radial boreholes fracturing mainly focuses on single, single row or double row radial boreholes, but investigations into the multi-directional radial borehole fracturing remain relatively sparse, its fracture propagation mechanism as well as stereoscopic reservoir stimulation effect are still unclear. This paper established a fracture propagation model of multi-directional radial boreholes fracturing based on the discrete lattice method, and the fracture propagation mechanism and the stereoscopic reservoir stimulation under effect of multiple parameters are analyzed. The results indicate that through multi-directional radial boreholes fracturing, multiple main fractures extending deep into the formation can be formed, which can realize multi-fracture stereoscopic reservoir stimulation. The radial borehole azimuth should be set at 45° and the inter-borehole angle at 90°, at which time the fracture area is the largest, the fracture propagation is the most uniform, and the effect of stereoscopic reservoir stimulation is the best. As the radius increases, the fracture area increases, the area difference coefficient decreases significantly, and the effect of radial boreholes to guide the directional propagation of the fracture increases; if the radial boreholes spacing is too large, the fracture may show a nonunion state and the effective fracture cannot be formed, so the spacing should be ≤ 1 m; the multi-directional radial boreholes fracturing is more suitable for the formation with low level stress difference, but it still has a certain degree of stimulation effect under high stress differential conditions. As elastic modulus increases, Poisson's ratio decreases, the degree of fracture uniformity decreases, the fracture complexity increases, and the radial boreholes have a weakened role in guiding fractures. Within the range allowed by the field operation, appropriately increasing the fracturing fluid injection rate and viscosity is conducive to enhancing the guiding effect of radial boreholes on fractures and improving the effect of stereoscopic reservoir stimulation.

papers.title: Analysis of Bragg reflection phenomenon induced by an array of submerged twin-wing breakwaters
papers.abstract: The interaction of gravity waves with an array of submerged twin-wing breakwaters (STWBs) is investigated based on the assumption of the linear water wave theory. A numerical solution utilizing the boundary element method is employed to solve the boundary value problem. In this study, we considered three types of twin-wing breakwater shapes, such as convex, inclined, and concave, to improve the effectiveness of wave attenuation. The proposed method is validated by comparing its numerical results with experimental and analytical findings from the literature, demonstrating its efficiency. The characteristics of Bragg reflection, including the conditions for its occurrence 2d/λ≈m (where λ is the wavelength of the incident wave, m is an integer, and d is the distance between the centers of any two contiguous breakwaters), the primary reflection peak, the phase downshift, and zero reflections are thoroughly discussed under various influencing factors, including length, draft, and array size in three STWB configurations. This analysis contributes to the efficient design of Bragg breakwaters, facilitating the creation of a tranquil wave environment in harbor areas. Furthermore, the Taguchi optimization technique is employed to optimize the response variable (i.e., the reflection coefficient) with respect to the influencing parameters.

papers.title: Impact of an oblique electric field on Rayleigh–Taylor instability in perfect and leaky dielectric fluids
papers.abstract: In this study, we present a comprehensive analysis of Rayleigh–Taylor instability (RTI) in systems involving perfect and leaky dielectric Newtonian fluids under the influence of an oblique electric field. Using linear stability analysis and mathematical theorems, we determine the number and nature of the solutions with respect to the dispersion relation. Our findings demonstrate that the RTI can be effectively controlled by applying a uniform electric field that is not necessarily aligned with the principal axes of the interface that separates the two fluids. In the leaky dielectric model, the orientation of the electric field can be adjusted to either suppress or enhance the instability, depending on the system parameters such as the permittivity and conductivity ratios of the two fluids. In particular, when the permittivity and conductivity ratios coincide, the leaky dielectric model seamlessly reduces to the perfect dielectric model. Moreover, for the perfect dielectric model, we confirmed that an oblique electric field can stabilize the interface.
