The design space is extensively explored with 68 configurations, applying the constraints of pressure recovery (PR) > 0.97 and distortion coefficient (DC60) < 0.06. This process yields 16 feasible designs, from which the best performing model in terms of PR and DC60 is selected as the optimized EMWB. The electromagnetic model and experimental setup are then established. Radar cross-sectional measurements of the optimized EMWB model demonstrate significant improvements: aerodynamic performance is increased by 8.1% for PR and 14% for DC60, while the radar cross section is decreased by 51%. These results suggest that the optimized EMWB in a straight duct configuration offers a promising alternative to S-shaped ducts for reducing aircraft engine signatures while maintaining aerodynamic performance.

papers.title: Local momentum ratio-dominated stability control in a throttleable liquid oxygen/methane pintle combustor
papers.abstract: This study examines how local momentum ratio (LMR) governs combustion stability in a pintle combustor through liquid oxygen (LOX) flow throttling experiments. Rough combustion occurs and its severity is governed by operational conditions. When the LMR decreases from 0.85 to 0.25 during the regulation stage, the chamber pressure amplitude decreases by 52%, and its standard deviation decreases by 50%. Based on the topology of spray and flame acquired by the spray–flame synchronous observation method, it is found that the spatial decoupling of the heat release zone and the oscillation zone is the key to improving combustion status. A reconstruction mechanism from “wall-impacting combustion” to “gas-confined combustion” is proposed. At high LMR, the momentum of the LOX spray dominates, causing the strong heat release zone near the wall to overlap with the strong oscillation zone. At low LMR conditions, the gas film encapsulation effect promotes the movement of the heat release core, realizing the spatial decoupling of the two zones. The dual-threshold criteria of flame area/brightness precisely locate the critical interval of the combustion status transition at LMR = 0.60–0.65, characterized by the disappearance of the liquid spray wall-impingement phenomenon and the reconstruction of the heat release rate distribution. The regulation process can be divided into three substages. Mode1 dominates both rapid- and slow subphases, accounting for 34.9% and 28.2% of the energy distribution, respectively. That suggests the regulation process avoided triggering notable coherent structures and the robust flame stabilization within the recirculation zone effectively suppresses combustion instability.

papers.title: Insights of flow transition over converging-diverging riblets using large-eddy simulation
papers.abstract: High-fidelity large eddy simulations are used to demonstrate the boundary layer transition over herringbone riblets exhibiting alternating converging and diverging patterns. Two variations of riblets' shape are considered: One with a blade profile having zero thickness (defined as HB) and the other with a conventional triangular cross section (defined as HBth). Large-scale counter-rotating vortices are observed over HBth, leading to the formation of low- and high-speed streaks aligned with the converging and diverging lines, respectively. These low-speed streaks lift up, and thereby, they interact with background disturbances, culminating in the proliferation of hairpins, which eventually undergo breakdown into small-scale eddies. In contrast, HB-riblets exhibit multiple longitudinal streaks that undergo secondary instability via the varicose mode, with an earlier onset of transition compared to HBth. An imbalance between production and dissipation in the outer layer persists in the transition region, while the turbulent kinetic energy budget becomes balanced downstream, except near the riblet crests. The observed delay in transition over these riblets against the smooth surface, and thus an increase in the critical Reynolds number, demonstrates lower frictional drag over a wider range of Reynolds numbers until the onset of instabilities. This study makes a significant contribution by elucidating the flow transition over herringbone riblets inspired by bird feathers.

papers.title: Coupled shear and magnetic effects on Rayleigh–Bénard convection in liquid metals
papers.abstract: This study investigates Rayleigh–Bénard convection in liquid metal characterized by a low Prandtl number (Pr=0.03) within a rectangular cavity (aspect ratio 5), under the combined effects of surface shear and strong magnetic fields, using two-dimensional numerical simulations. With a fixed Rayleigh number (Ra=106), we vary the Hartmann number (Ha = 2000–8000) and shear Reynolds number(Rew = 0–20 000) to assess their effects. The results show that the shear effect exhibits a non-monotonic variation in heat transfer efficiency. When Rew < Rew(Numin), buoyancy dominates the flow, and shear disrupts vertical vortex structures through horizontal momentum transport, fragmenting thermal plumes and reducing heat transfer efficiency. Here, Numin is the minimum Nusselt number within Rew = 0–20 000, with Rew(Numin) being the corresponding shear Reynolds number, denotes the critical threshold of transition from buoyancy-dominated to shear-dominated flow. When Rew > Rew(Numin), the flow transitions to shear-dominated, with enhanced primary circulation driving a linear increase in Nu(Nu∼0.0001Rew), where the coefficient varies with Pr. The Prandtl number plays a key role in the transition between buoyancy-dominated and shear-dominated states, with low-Pr fluids requiring higher shear Reynolds numbers for this transition to occur. Furthermore, at a fixed Rew, as Ha increases from 2000 to 8000, the magnetic field dampens the intensity of buoyancy-driven convection, rendering the flow more susceptible to shear effects, and the critical shear Reynolds number scales as Rew(Numin)∼Ha−1/2, indicating that a stronger magnetic field accelerates the flow transition to the shear-dominated regime.

papers.title: Three-dimensional finite element modelling of chemical environment in droplet-based microfluidic systems for drug therapy applications
papers.abstract: This study presents a novel computational fluid dynamics-based optimization framework for enhancing mixing efficiency in droplet-based microfluidic systems. The key innovation lies in systematically linking microchannel geometry, flow parameters, and material properties to internal mixing dynamics, providing new insights into how microfluidic design can be tuned for improved solute distribution within droplets. Such optimization is particularly relevant for applications in single-cell analysis and on-chip therapeutic drug screening. Using water and a solution of fluorescently dyed bovine serum albumin (BSA) as the dispersed phase within a silicone oil-based continuous phase, we generated quasi-monodisperse droplets and analyzed how mixing behavior responds to specific design choices. Simulations revealed that serpentine channels enhanced mixing efficiency by up to 17% compared to straight channels, primarily due to Dean vortices that promote homogenization. Flow rate manipulation further influenced droplet formation and internal mixing: initial flow conditions (0.2 μl/s water, 0.2 μl/s BSA, 0.02 μl/s oil) resulted in stable but poorly mixed droplets, while increasing the oil flow rate to 1.4 μl/s triggered a droplet-generation regime that significantly improved internal mixing. Experimental measurements of droplet behavior and internal intensity profiles were conducted to validate the simulation results, showing strong qualitative agreement and confirming the predictive capability of the proposed model. These findings highlight the potential of droplet microfluidics as a platform for miniaturized chemical reactors, enabling precise control over solute concentration and distribution. This approach provides a foundation for precise drug delivery for studying therapeutic agents and supports the development of advanced lab-on-a-chip systems for optimized drug formulation within controlled microenvironments.

papers.title: Subsonic side-blown bubbles' unstable oscillatory behavior in a side-blown smelting furnace
papers.abstract: In order to ensure the long service life and safe operation of superlarge side-blown smelting furnaces, the unstable oscillatory behavior of side-blown bubbles was studied through a combination of experiments and numerical simulations. This research focused on the evolution process of bubbles, their oscillation instability and intensity, and the reverse impact phenomenon. The results show that bubbles oscillation manifests as their growth and detachment, i.e., expansion and contraction. The shape, generation frequency, and breakup state of the bubbles change with the increase in the modified Froude number. Oscillation instability is quantitatively analyzed based on the time evolution of the bubble root radius and is associated with the balance between surface tension and turbulent shear force. Therefore, the standard deviation follows different power function laws with Weber and Reynolds number for bubbly flow and jet. Allan deviations describe the random differences and increases on different time scales with the modified Froude number. Continuous wavelet transform indicates that the increase in instability appears as the appearance of high-frequency, high-intensity peaks in the time evolution results. Oscillation intensity is quantitatively analyzed by using average bubble root radius and a dimensional analysis relationship with the modified Froude, Weber, and Reynolds numbers is established within ±10% error. Numerical simulation identifies the reverse impact caused by bubble unstable oscillation, which leads to non-uniform damage to the nozzle base and manifests sudden increase in pressure around the bubble during the contraction phase. Both the frequency and intensity of the impact increase with the modified Froude number.

papers.title: Fractal-based modeling of permeability evolution during CO2–brine–rock interactions in sandstone reservoirs
papers.abstract: The CO2–brine–rock interaction can significantly alter rock permeability during CO2 storage in saline aquifers. However, quantitatively characterizing the effects of this interaction on the correlation between the microstructure of pores and permeability is still a challenge. To address this issue, this study focuses on sandstone core sampling from the CO2 saline aquifer storage field test site in the Dezhou subdepression, China. The microscopic pore structures of samples before and after CO2 injection were analyzed using x-ray micro-computed tomography imaging, and laboratory experiments simulating CO2–brine–rock interactions were conducted under normal temperature and pressure conditions. Additionally, permeability coefficients were evaluated by integrating fractal theory with numerical simulations. The results indicate that mineral dissolution caused by CO2–brine–rock interactions significantly enhanced pore connectivity by 233.50%, increased the maximum pore radius by 28.46%, and expanded the maximum throat radius by 60.81%. These microstructural modifications also led to a 9.87% increase in mean fractal dimension and a 213.25% improvement in mean permeability. Furthermore, the dynamic variation of fractal dimension was found to be a reliable indicator of interaction intensity. By coupling the evolution of fractal dimension with connected porosity, a new permeability prediction model was established to quantitatively assess the impact of CO2–brine–rock interactions. The model showed good agreement with experimental measurements. This study provides a practical methodology for quantifying permeability evolution driven by geochemical alteration and offers theoretical insights for enhancing the predictive accuracy of reservoir performance under reactive flow conditions in CO2 geological storage.

papers.title: Study on dynamic mechanisms and frequency characteristics of self-pulsation in gas-centered liquid-swirl coaxial injectors with recess
papers.abstract: This study examines self-pulsation spray oscillations in a gas-centered swirl coaxial (GCSC) injector using high-speed photography and numerical simulation. For the first time, high-speed photography captured the unsteady gas–liquid flow inside the GCSC injectors' recess chamber, revealing three spray modes: stable liquid-film breakup, intermittent oscillatory breakup, and purely aerodynamic breakup. Mid- to high-frequency oscillations are governed by the gas–liquid momentum flux ratio and the recess ratio (RR). The core mechanism is a “pressure-relaxation” cycle triggered by periodic gas–liquid blockage in the recess. In this cycle, high-speed airflow expands and compresses the liquid film, causing pressure to build up and then release through the nozzle as a closed-loop oscillation. In stable film-breakup mode at M < 0.1, high-frequency oscillations can arise from Kelvin–Helmholtz waves and viscous shear, even without gas–liquid blockage. Frequency analysis shows that oscillation frequency is closely related to momentum ratio, liquid Reynolds number, and gas Weber number. High-frequency oscillations occur when 0.1 ≤ M < 0.8 and Rel >15 000 (J < 10, Weg < 6000) but disappear when M ≥ 0.8 and Rel < 20 000 (J ≥ 10, Weg ≥ 6000), leaving low- and medium-frequency instabilities. A Strouhal number correlation shows a peak at a recess ratio of 1.4 (∼2–4 kHz), a drop to ∼0.5–2 kHz at RR = 1.7, and no high-frequency oscillations at RR ≈ 1. These findings offer insight into self-pulsation mechanisms and provide guidance for optimizing injector design to mitigate high-frequency combustion instabilities in rocket thrust chambers.

papers.title: Multiphysics modeling of microwave heating-induced moisture and methane transport in shale gas reservoir
papers.abstract: To advance shale gas extraction, this study investigates the potential of microwave irradiation, an auxiliary technique for hydraulic fracturing to exploit methane resources sustainably. A coupled multiphysics model with dual-porosity media theory is proposed to capture this complex evolution, considering the characteristics of two-phase flow within shale gas reservoirs. The model incorporates the interactions among electromagnetic effects, solid deformation, fluid and moisture transport, and heat transfer, which enables effective evaluation of the change of various reservoir parameters under microwave irradiation, along with the analysis of different factors' influences on water–gas transport properties and gas extraction efficiency. The findings indicate that relative humidity is crucial to water–gas flow dynamics, specifically, the increase in relative humidity enhances the contribution of adsorbed methane to cumulative methane production. Microwave heating considerably raises the water–gas exchange rate between matrix and fracture, and boosts shale gas' desorption efficiency during the later extraction stages. Improving reservoir permeability is a key to strengthening productivity; however, its impact on cumulative production becomes less significant beyond a threshold. Additionally, the decrease in the gas adsorption decay factor enhances cumulative production.

papers.title: Particle deposition in colloid-polymer suspensions: Complex interplay between flow characteristics and polymer interactions
papers.abstract: The addition of polymer to the particulate suspension provides several functionalities, such as tuning rheological properties and ensuring uniform dispersion. However, the effect of polymers on particle deposition has not been systematically investigated in the previous literature. In this study, we perform microfluidic observation and image processing analysis of particle deposition in colloid-polymer suspensions, focusing on the interplay between flow characteristics and polymer interactions. Polystyrene particles are selected as model particles, while polyethylene oxide is dissolved in de-ionized water at varying polymer concentrations. Higher polymer concentrations enhance colloidal interactions, as evidenced by zeta potential measurements and depletion interaction analysis. Consequently, in the semi-dilute unentangled regime, increased polymer concentration promotes particle deposition. On the other hand, in the semi-dilute entangled regime, the trend reverses, with higher polymer concentrations leading to reduced particle deposition. In the cavity region, stagnant flow facilitates particle retention, further reinforced by polymer interactions. When the zero-shear viscosity is matched, the deposition behavior in the semi-dilute entangled regime is reversed, indicating that particle motion is primarily governed by flow behavior and particle-polymer interactions. Our findings highlight the role of polymers in deposition dynamics under flow, providing valuable insights for optimizing industrial processes involving complex channel structures.

papers.title: Direct numerical simulation and prediction model construction for flow and heat transfer characteristics of particle clusters in supercritical water
papers.abstract: Particles tend to aggregate locally and form clusters in supercritical water (SCW). The absence of constitutive relations for accurately predicting the interphase interaction of SCW-particle cluster systems restricts the orderly energy conversion efficiency and the scale-up of reactor in supercritical water gasification technology. In this work, a mesoscale particle cluster model considering particle position random distribution and size dispersion is constructed. By using the particle-resolved direct numerical simulation method, the flow and heat transfer characteristics of clusters containing 20–100 sub-particles, with sizes of 3.2–8 times the diameter of a single particle and local particle phase fractions of 10%–35% in SCW are investigated under particle Reynolds number 0.1–100. The research results indicate that the increase in local particle phase fraction and cluster size will enhance the stagnation effect inside the cluster, thereby hindering the interphase interaction. The characteristic distribution of sub-particle within the cluster is emphatically correlated with its position. Due to the synergistic effect of cluster structural parameters and fluid dimensionless parameters, the momentum and energy exchange efficiency between particle clusters and SCW are suppressed by 17.27%–87.26% and 8.25%–94.49%, respectively. Finally, the simulation results across various conditions are used to construct prediction models for the overall flow and heat transfer characteristics of SCW-particle cluster two-phase flow under a wide parameter range. Note that SCW is used as the fluid in this work, but the prediction models constructed are universal for different two-phase flow systems within the given physical model assumptions and dimensionless conditions.

papers.title: An efficient vortex-resolved direct discontinuous Galerkin method with adaptive mesh refinement
papers.abstract: Vortex-resolved simulations often require fine grids to capture multi-scale vortices, which leads to extremely high computational costs. This work proposes a direct discontinuous Galerkin method (DDGM) integrated with adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) for effectively reducing the expensive computational overhead of vortex-resolved simulations. First, a symbolic regression inspired vortex indicator is developed and generalized to arbitrary incompatible grids, enabling the concentration of computational grid resources on vortex regions. The most attractive advantage of this vortex indicator lies in its theoretically analyzed capability to capture dissipative small-scale vortices even on coarse grids, which is naturally compatible with AMR. Second, by integrating the AMR strategy guided by the present vortex indicator, an efficient and vortex-resolved DDGM is established. Numerical results validate that the vortex-resolved DDGM with AMR is able to resolve vortices of different scales in complex flows with a slight increase in computational overhead, providing a promising numerical method for exploring vortex-induced lift mechanisms and underlying flow physics in aerospace applications.

papers.title: Electrokinetics of concentrated suspension of fluid droplets under applied electric field or electrolyte concentration gradient
papers.abstract: This article presents a detailed theoretical investigation into the electrokinetic behavior of concentrated suspensions of dielectric and hydrophobic fluid droplets. We examine two common scenarios: movement of suspension of the droplets under an applied electric field (electrophoresis) and movement driven by a bulk electrolyte concentration gradient (diffusiophoresis). Recognizing the significance of analytical results, we have performed a mathematical study on the electrophoresis and diffusiophoresis of undertaken suspension. We model the suspension system with Kuwabara's unit cell model. Under the conditions of weak applied potential fields (e.g., voltage drop or concentration gradient) and employing the Debye-Hückel electrostatic framework, we have linearized and integrated the governing equations to derive general formulas for electrophoretic and diffusiophoretic mobilities. Furthermore, we deduced approximate expressions for both the electrophoretic and diffusiophoretic mobilities of the studied suspension, which are free from cumbersome integrals and, thus, very convenient for practical uses. Notably these findings are applicable to electrokinetic behavior of various systems, including concentrated suspension of hydrophobic and dielectric oil droplets, perfectly conducting mercury droplets, nanoemulsions, air bubbles, to name a few.

papers.title: Numerical study of CO2 utilization technology in shale gas reservoir: Implications for enhancing gas recovery and optimizing fracture scheme
papers.abstract: CO2 fracturing technology shows innovation and strategic value in both economy and environment. This study proposes a novel CO2 utilization strategy to restore production-induced stress fields and enhance infill well fracturing. A fully coupled fluid–solid model was developed, incorporating complex transport mechanisms and dynamic fracture propagation in shale. The model was solved using a discontinuous discrete fracture approach, enabling continuous simulation of production and fracturing. Two oilfield scenarios were simulated: (1) direct CO2 fracturing of the infill well, and (2) CO2 injection into the parent well to restore the stress field prior to infill fracturing. The simulation results revealed that CO2 injection effectively reestablished the stress field without reservoir damage, increased effective fracture length, and enhanced CH4 production from both infill and parent wells. One-year cumulative gas production improved by up to 23.2%. Additionally, the method offers significant potential for reducing carbon emissions in shale gas development.

papers.title: Computational study of gastric emptying in microgravity: The role of density and viscosity variations
papers.abstract: Space exploration represents a major scientific endeavor, and the microgravity encountered in space can significantly affect gastrointestinal function, and consequently, the health of astronauts. However, stomach function in microgravity, including gastric emptying, is not yet fully understood. In this study, we employed computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to investigate the effects of microgravity on gastric emptying for liquid meals across a range of densities and viscosities. Specifically, we introduced a food bolus in an aqueous medium and assessed its emptying rates. Our results indicate that the total gastric liquid emptying rate remains largely unchanged across gravity levels (∼0.087 ml/s), except when the bolus exhibits both high density and high viscosity, in which case the pylorus becomes partially obstructed and the emptying rate decreases under normal gravity. In contrast, the food bolus emptying rate varies significantly depending on density, viscosity, and gravity. Zero gravity may enhance, maintain, or reduce bolus emptying relative to normal gravity depending on food properties. For instance, a low-density, low-viscosity bolus exhibits nearly zero emptying under normal gravity, while emptying efficiently in microgravity. Conversely, a high-density, high-viscosity bolus experiences reduced emptying under microgravity due to ineffective propulsion and increased viscous resistance. These findings underscore the interactions between gravitational stratification and peristaltic transport, highlighting the need to consider fluid properties when evaluating digestive processes in microgravity. Overall, the CFD framework presented provides a valuable and cost-effective tool for understanding gastrointestinal function under microgravity, with implications for both space missions and terrestrial healthcare.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of coarse particle conveying with a non-mechanical feeder: Process interruption, restart, and wear
papers.abstract: Pneumatic conveying is an important operation used in many industries to transport granular materials. This study, for the first time, numerically investigated the conveying interruption and restart process as well as the erosive wear of coarse particle conveying with a non-mechanical feeder using an improved computational fluid dynamics coupled with the discrete element method and an impact energy erosion model, aiming to advance our understanding of complicated coarse particle dynamics in the narrow vertical pipes. The specific research content includes (i) pressure drops, particle acceleration characteristics, and solids mass flow rate at the steady-state conveying stage, (ii) particle falling and pile characteristics after conveying interruption, (iii) initial particle motion and restart pressure drop during conveying restart, and (iv) erosive wear of conveying devices. The interested parameters, including particle acceleration height, pile height, and restart pressure drops, were quantitatively evaluated and analyzed. Two newly defined threshold velocities, referred to as minimum entrainment velocity and initial motion velocity, were discussed. An important phenomenon after conveying interruption, i.e., plug stagnation, was found under different operating conditions. The erosive wear simulation of the conveying system also gave a quantitative prediction on the wear of the feeder, riser, and storage bin, including cutting and deformation wear. The findings and numerical framework used in this study have the potential to contribute to the optimal design, operation, and maintenance of the conveying system.

papers.title: Distance-based collocation sampling for mesh-free physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a powerful mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations by embedding physical laws into the loss function of deep learning models. Their flexibility, particularly in data-scarce or noisy environments, has enabled a wide range of applications in computational physics and engineering. However, one of the persistent challenges in training PINNs lies in the accurate enforcement of boundary conditions, especially for domains with irregular geometries. Conventional collocation point sampling methods, including mesh-based and uniform random strategies, pose limitations in the context of PINNs. The mesh-based sampling strategy contradicts the mesh-free feature of PINNs, while the uniform sampling makes it a challenge to account for the geometric structure of the domain. A geometry-aware, distance-based sampling (DBS) strategy is proposed in this study to select collocation points using a signed distance function (SDF). The SDF provides geometric information by which the structured sampling is aligned with the domain shape, without requiring explicit meshing. SDF information is used to promote selective sampling in the region near domain boundaries based on the concept of proximity. This proposed approach facilitates the treatment of boundary conditions while fully preserving the mesh-free nature of PINNs. Furthermore, the proposed DBS strategy provides high flexibility in the selection of collocation points and supports the incorporation of diverse sampling methods.

papers.title: Investigation of spontaneous imbibition of de-ionized water into heterogeneous porous rock by continuous weighing and in situ X-ray computed tomography observation
papers.abstract: Spontaneous imbibition (SI) of water driven by capillary forces within underground reservoir is recognized as a key mechanism influencing the oil and gas recovery. A comprehensive investigation at both the pore and core scales is essential for a deeper understanding of the SI behavior. This study employs continuous weighing measurement and in situ computed tomography (CT) scanning to quantitatively characterize the SI of de-ionized water into a dry synthetic rock sample with a permeability of 124 mD. At the core scale, the co-current SI weighing data showed two-stage imbibition behavior. Detailed analysis indicated that the imbibition rate slowed after the imbibition front advanced to the top of the sample. Pore-scale observations using in situ CT imaging confirmed that the imbibed masses at the end of the two stages were consistent with the weighing data. At the end of the first stage, the imbibed de-ionized water was distributed throughout the pore space. Subsequent imbibition in the second stage was attributed to increased saturation within the pores. Notably, the central region of the sample imbibed less de-ionized water than its peripheral counterpart of equivalent volume in the first stage, which was caused by the heterogeneous distribution of pores and rock matrix in the central region. The integration of core-scale measurements and pore-scale imaging provided insights into the mechanisms governing SI in porous rocks.

papers.title: Flow evolution and fingering instability of a thin water film on an inclined plate under shear airflow
papers.abstract: One of the key issues affecting aircraft safety in the field of aircraft icing and anti-icing is the stability of shear-driven runback water films on component surfaces. This study investigates the flow evolution and fingering instability of thin water films on inclined plates under shear airflow, elucidating the coupled multi-physics mechanisms governing film rupture. A theoretical model, which integrates airflow shear stress and contact line forces, is established through the long-wave approximation of Navier–Stokes equations, enhanced by the precursor film model and dynamic contact angle model. A numerical solver (rivuletFoam) is developed to simulate interfacial evolution. The results of linear stability analysis combined with numerical simulation show that increasing inclination angle amplifies Kapitza instability by strengthening gravitational components, expanding the cutoff wavenumber by 24%. The airflow shear stress enhances the maximum temporal growth rate by 17 times and reduces the film rupture time by 96% through capillary ridge acceleration. Contact angle augmentation intensifies disjoining pressure gradients, decreasing maximum continuous film length by 92% while reducing rivulet count by 43%. Precursor film thinning amplifies intermolecular forces, extending the cutoff wavenumber range by 44%. The proposed model effectively captured the fingering-to-rivulet transitions and provided critical insights for interfacial instability prediction in multiphase flows, which is of significant engineering value for the optimization of the design of aircraft anti-icing systems.

papers.title: Aerodynamic noise optimization of a voluteless centrifugal fan with biomimetic blades inspired by eagle-owl wingtip morphology
papers.abstract: Inspired by the low-noise characteristics of the eagle-owl nocturnal flight, two novel designs for blades of the voluteless centrifugal fan are proposed to improve the aerodynamic performance and reduce the noise. A serrated structure inspired by the eagle-owl wingtips at the trailing edge is adopted to design and optimize the blade. Based on the computational fluid dynamics methods and the Ffowcs Williams–Hawkings equation, the impact of the serrated leading and trailing edges on the aerodynamic performance and acoustic characteristics of a fan is investigated. The optimal geometric parameters of the bionic sawtooth are determined. Subsequently, a comprehensive comparison of the flow characteristics and noise spectra among the fan with the original blade (OBLE), the serrated leading-edge blade (SLBE), and the serrated trailing-edge blade (STBE) is conducted, revealing the control mechanism of the SLBE and STBE on the flow properties and noise optimization principles. Results demonstrate that the SLBE fan not only mitigates pressure fluctuations and optimizes vortices but also increases the maximum flow rate by 1.76%. Although the STBE fan also optimizes pressure and vortices, its efficiency slightly decreases due to reduced blade lift. However, the STBE fan achieves outstanding noise suppression, reducing the sound pressure level (SPL) by 6.42 dB compared to the OBLE fan. While the SLBE fan yields a limited SPL reduction of only 1.97 dB. Additionally, the noise energy shift at 1364 Hz demonstrates frequency modulation caused by the serrations. The blade trailing edge is identified as the primary noise source, and the STBE fan significantly attenuates broadband and tonal noise by optimizing the airflow disturbance suppression at the impeller outlet. These findings validate the feasibility of using biomimetic serrated designs to optimize the performance of voluteless centrifugal fans.

papers.title: Study on the effect of hydraulic transport erosion and deposition of fine sand in rough fractures
papers.abstract: The hydraulic transport and deposition dynamics of fine sand in fractured media have garnered growing attention due to groundwater over-exploitation-induced geological concerns. While previous studies predominantly focused on proppant transport in vertical fractures for oil or gas applications, significant knowledge gaps remain regarding hydrodynamic erosion-deposition mechanisms of fine sand particles in horizontal fracture systems. This investigation employs numerical modeling to systematically examine particle transport, surface erosion, and deposition characteristics in rough-walled fractures. Results demonstrate three dominant controlling factors on erosion-deposition processes: fluid velocity (v), particle diameter (d), and mean fracture aperture (a). Fracture surface erosion rate exhibits a positive correlation with both v (R2 = 0.96) and d (R2 = 0.99), while showing an inverse relationship with a (R2 = 0.99). The proposed Particle Uniformity Index (Pu) effectively elucidates the diminishing erosion intensity associated with increasing fracture aperture. Three distinct empirical relationships were established through data fitting to quantify these interdependencies. They are E=71.052a−1.285;E=10.944v−8.384;E=0.284×163 313d, respectively. (E is the average erosion rate.) Deposition patterns reveal dual control mechanisms: fluid velocity governs particle retention through shear transport dominance, while aperture dimensions regulate deposition through gravitational settling effects. A derived nonlinear regression model m=0.000 204⋅a0.539⋅v−2.15 quantitatively predicts deposition capacity (m is the mass of deposited particles), highlighting fluid velocity as the predominant controlling factor (p < 0.01).

papers.title: Hydrothermal analysis of turbulent heat transfer across various twisted elliptical tube configurations
papers.abstract: High-performance heat exchangers are critical components in numerous industrial sectors, including power generation, chemical processing, automotive, and air conditioning systems, where efficient thermal management is essential for energy conservation and process optimization. The adoption of twisted elliptical tubes (TETs) and twisted tri-lobe tubes (TTT) in heat exchangers induces secondary flows, enhancing heat transfer performance. Also insertion of helical twisted tape (HTT) to twisted tube can induce stronger secondary flow compared to twisted tubes alone. This numerical study examines turbulent flow and heat transfer characteristics in TETs and TTTs within a Reynolds number range of 8000–20 000. The k–ω shear stress transport turbulence model was employed to simulate flow behavior. Key geometric parameters investigated include uniform twist pitch, alternate twist direction, and non-uniform twist pitch configurations. Results indicate that TETs and TTTs achieve up to 32% and 37% greater heat transfer compared to circular tubes, respectively, accompanied by a 64% and 75% increase in pressure drop. Reducing the uniform twist pitch (increasing the number of turns) yields a 22% and 26% improvement in TET and TTT, respectively, albeit with a respective 63% and 73% rise in pressure drop. Non-uniform twist pitch configurations can achieve a suitable balance between increased heat transfer and reduced pressure drop, making them a structure of significant interest. In both TET and TTT with non-uniform twist configurations, particularly the 100–200–400 mm arrangement exhibits the highest performance evaluation criterion of 1.135and 1.163, respectively, at Re = 8000, achieving an optimal balance between heat transfer enhancement and pressure drop. The insertion of a HTT into twisted tubes is an innovation that can significantly enhance heat transfer. Applying a HTT in TET and TTT can increase heat transfer by up to 28% and 32%, respectively, compared to twisted tubes alone. These enhancements make TTTs preferable for compact heat exchangers despite higher pressure drops.

papers.title: Study on the influence mechanism of solid particles on the flow field characteristics in centrifugal slurry pumps
papers.abstract: The solid–liquid two—phase flow characteristics within a centrifugal slurry pump are closely related to its performance. In this paper, a combined experimental and numerical simulation method is adopted to conduct a detailed analysis of the flow field characteristics of the flow—through components of the centrifugal slurry pump. The results indicate that at the rated flow rate, the particle distribution in the impeller passage is relatively uniform, with particles mainly aggregating on the pressure surface and the volute wall. When the flow rate has not reached 1.0QBEP (Best Efficiency Point, BEP), particles mainly cause wear at the inlet and the suction surface. After exceeding 1.0QBEP, the impact on the pressure surface becomes more significant. When the particle size is 1 mm and the particle mass fraction is 15%, the head is 6.807 m, and the head is reduced by 17.243%; when the particle mass fraction is 15%, the efficiency is 41.849%, and the efficiency is reduced by 10.45%. Meanwhile, the wear at the impeller outlet and the volute continues to increase. In addition, the increase in particle mass fraction also makes the volute deformed, and the inlet of the blades are prone to stress concentration, and the safety factor also decreases, resulting in fatigue damage. This study has certain guiding significance for the optimized design of slurry pump impeller.

papers.title: A hybrid machine learning framework for rotor performance prediction
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in electric propulsion technology have created significant demand for rotor performance models that can be used for preliminary design and optimization of new class of electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft. Existing high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics models, while accurate, are computationally expensive and too slow for real-time and optimization applications. This paper presents a novel approach, NN-BET, which combines neural networks (NN) with blade element theory (BET) to predict rotor loads based on rotor geometrical features, operational parameters, and airfoil characteristics. This hybrid surrogate model employs a neural network to estimate an intermediate aerodynamic parameter (mean inflow), which is then integrated into the BET framework to calculate aerodynamic loads. Incorporation of NN architecture inside a blade-element framework makes it an order of magnitude faster than a traditional blade element momentum theory model, one of the fastest physics-based models, while maintaining similar accuracy. To assess the influence of integrated physical principles, the performance of the developed NN-BET model is compared to that of a conventional neural network model. Both models are trained on the same dataset with identical neural network architectures and hyperparameters to maintain a fair and consistent comparison. The results show that the NN-BET model surpasses the conventional NN model in terms of predictive accuracy. Given the rapid computational speed and reliable accuracy of the developed machine learning-based model, it is well suited for optimization and design applications, as well as multidisciplinary frameworks requiring efficient rotor dynamics modeling.

papers.title: Solutal Marangoni effect and chemical reactions on interfacial instability of droplet driven by surface acoustic waves
papers.abstract: Aerosol droplets of micrometer and sub-micrometer sizes may be produced quickly using surface acoustic wave (SAW) atomization. This study theoretically investigates the influence of the solutal Marangoni effect and chemical reactions on the instability of SAW-driven droplets. By applying lubrication theory to the governing equations, a droplet evolution equation is formulated, which is influenced by parameters such as the acoustic capillary number E, solutal Marangoni number M, and Damköhler number Da. In addition, the droplet evolution process is numerically simulated using the method of lines. When the SAW-induced capillary waves on the droplet reach a critical amplitude, atomization is triggered. Increases of M and Da lead to decreases in the droplet height profile h(x, t) and increases in the characteristic length L. Moreover, droplet atomization may result from an increase in the number of wave peaks, which is brought on by increases in M and Da. It is noteworthy that M and Da can regulate the atomization of droplets. However, the initiation of droplet atomization is only dependent on E. As M, Da, and E increase, the rate at which aspect ratio ε diminishes accelerates and the duration of the transition phase contracts, thereby precipitating an earlier onset of the quasi-stable stage. Moreover, increases in M and Da result in a reduction in the final ε.

papers.title: Investigation on the stagger angle adjustment and loss mechanism of the supersonic through flow variable pitch tandem cascade
papers.abstract: The supersonic through-flow variable-pitch tandem fan offers significant potential to expand the acceptable inflow range of the fan. However, owing to its higher degree of freedom, the adjustment relationship between the front and rear blades needs further clarification. This study uses numerical simulations to explore the adjustment and loss mechanisms of the rear blade stagger angle in a variable-pitch tandem cascade across different operating modes. In the transonic mode, cascade performance changes monotonically with the rear blade stagger angle. A larger stagger angle can significantly reduce the shock boundary layer interaction on the suction side of the rear blade, while weakening the maximum boost capacity of the cascade. In the supersonic through-flow mode, the favorable pressure gradient enables the rear blade to operate at a smaller positive incidence, improving its flow turning ability and alignment between the inlet metal angle of the rear blade and the inflow angle of the front blade under positive incidence conditions. In the high-speed windmilling mode, it is crucial to achieve a balance between the separation at the trailing edge of the suction side of the rear blade and the shock-induced separation on the pressure side. Notably, the optimal trend of the rear blade stagger angle adjustment in these two modes shows an inverse relationship.

papers.title: Dynamics of viscous flow induced in a linearly viscoelastic channel by peristaltic forcing
papers.abstract: A mathematical model is developed to investigate the effect of wall viscoelasticity on the flow induced by peristaltic forcing in a viscous fluid occupying a two-dimensional channel. The main objective of the work is to investigate the role played by viscous damping of the channel wall on the net flow rate. To that end, the resistance of the walls to deformation is modeled using a Kramer-type linearly viscoelastic model. Numerical results are presented for periodic waves in wave frame at arbitrary wavelengths and amplitudes of the peristaltic forcing for parameter values typical of the human digestion system. The viscous behavior of the channel wall is predicted to reduce the flow rate. It also gives rise to a phase lag between the applied force and the wall deformation, with its severity depending on the wave parameters and fluid/solid properties. The peristaltic forcing mechanism is predicted to be better suited for long waves, but it is shown that beyond a threshold amplitude, the effect of wavelength saturates when trapping occurs. For highly viscous fluids such as chyme flowing in human colon, the viscous normal stress exerted by the fluid on the inner side of the wall is shown to play a key role in the deformation of the walls and thereby the flow rate. It is predicted that competition between the fluid internal forces and the external peristaltic forcing causes the flow rate to initially decrease with the Reynolds number before starting to increase beyond a threshold.

papers.title: Experimental study of closed loop control of cross-flow instability driven transition by plasma actuator
papers.abstract: A closed-loop control was implemented to mitigate stationary cross-flow instability vortices in the boundary layer of a swept wing. Control was achieved using a multichannel plasma actuator and a flow velocity sensor based on a particle image velocimetry system. The optimal control strategy was determined using a gradient descent method, which minimized the root mean square of the steady velocity modulation. The excitation of the boundary layer by a single section of barrier discharge was investigated, with key actuator characteristics, such as linearity limits and noise levels, measured during the experiment. The system's performance was evaluated in a wind tunnel experiment, with various roughness patterns used to force the initial vortices. For isolated roughness elements, substantial transition delay was achieved.

papers.title: Linear instability analysis of an annular liquid jet with swirl air
papers.abstract: Airblast nozzles are widely applied in advanced aeroengine combustors, and their crucial physical phenomena can be simplified to the disturbance and breakup of an annular liquid jet with swirl air. Therefore, the performance of the nozzle is closely related to the primary breakup process, and the linear instability theory provides a theoretical framework for elucidating the primary breakup process. The research focuses on the swirling airflow interacting with the annular liquid jet and derives the dispersion equation for the annular liquid jet based on the linear instability. Through numerical solutions of this dispersion equation, a detailed parametric analysis is conducted. The parametric study shows several key findings. Increasing air density, axial gas velocities (both inner and outer flows), and the rotational Weber numbers promote breakup efficiency. Reducing the liquid jet thickness also enhances breakup efficiency. These changes result in a decrease in primary breakup length and mean droplet diameter. In the process of the decrease in the liquid jet thickness, the dominant force of primary breakup will be changed from the surface tension of the liquid to the aerodynamic force. The swirl air will make the dominant modes of primary breakup change from the axisymmetric modes to the helical modes.

papers.title: Laplace-based physics-informed neural networks for solving nonlinear coefficient inverse problem for acoustic equation with fractional derivative
papers.abstract: As physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) continue to evolve, the limitations of traditional PINNs are becoming increasingly apparent. One major drawback is their reliance on automatic differentiation, which imposes constraints on solving partial differential equations, especially for those with fractional derivatives. For fractional-order equations, automatic differentiation cannot be directly applied, making it a challenge to use PINNs effectively. To address this, we propose a novel Laplace based physics-informed neural networks (L-PINNs) that combines PINNs with the Laplace transform to solve the coefficient inverse problem for acoustic equation with fractional derivative. This approach transforms fractional derivatives, enabling efficient handling of time-fractional inverse problems. Moreover, the nonlinear coefficient functions can be determined efficiently by the L-PINNs for the inverse problem of acoustic equations or time-fractional differential equations. We validate the effectiveness of the L-PINNs method by solving the one-dimensional and two-dimensional coefficient inverse problem for the acoustic equation with a fractional derivative, demonstrating its ability to solve the time-fractional coefficient inverse problem efficiently.

papers.title: Electrophoresis of non-uniformly charged particles in viscoelastic fluids: The weak field limit
papers.abstract: Electrophoresis of charged particles in polymeric (viscoelastic) fluids remains important in various separation processes, although their theoretical analysis is rather scarce in the literature. The ones which do investigate this topic use simplifying assumptions, especially that of thin Electrical Double Layers (EDLs) and weak surface charge on the particles, which are often assumed to be uniform in nature. In contrast, this article seeks to move beyond such conventional analytical boundaries, by probing the electrophoretic motion of a non-uniformly (but axisymmetrically) charged particle in an Oldroyd-B fluid, accounting for arbitrary EDL thickness and surface potential. The only restriction is that of a weak external electric field (the so-called “weak field limit”), which enables us to use regular perturbation expansions to deduce the particle's electrophoretic velocity. Our results reveal that the excess polymeric stresses in a viscoelastic medium tend to significantly impact the particle's velocity only when the EDL is sufficiently thin. At the same time, increasing the magnitude of the surface potential (or charge) tends to augment the impact of viscoelasticity. We find that depending on the precise distribution of the particle's surface potential, the medium's viscoelasticity may either speed up or slow down the particle, when compared to a Newtonian fluid. Overall, the inhomogeneity in the surface potential enhances the influence of viscoelasticity, and this enhancement is more pronounced for smaller particles as compared to larger ones.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization of curved grooves for reducing flow-induced loads on a circular cylinder
papers.abstract: A novel passive flow control for flow-induced load reduction on a circular cylinder is introduced by incorporating two symmetrically arranged curved grooves. Here low Reynolds numbers (Re, based on the cylinder diameter D) ranging from 100 to 180, where the flow remains two-dimensional, are investigated numerically by solving two-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations using a finite volume method with 2nd order accuracy both in time and space. The Bayesian Optimization with Gaussian Process Regression method has been successfully applied to this flow configuration for the first time, demonstrating high efficiency in identifying the optimal angular width (θw=90.9°) and angular position (θp=88.8°) of the groove for maximum drag reduction. These optimal values were found within the broad admissible ranges of θw∈[20°,120°] and θp∈[65°,115°], measured clockwise from the cylinder front. We found that i) the optimized groove configuration generates two small corner vortices near groove corners, which effectively weaken vortex shedding and displace the wake farther downstream compared to a smooth cylinder, mainly contributing to a large pressure drag reduction; ii) the upstream corner vortices result in significant viscous drag reduction and decrease in the pressure difference between cylinder top and bottom, thus leading to a significant lift reduction; iii) both drag and lift reductions relative to a smooth cylinder grow monotonically with increased Re, peaking at 16.7% and 42%, respectively. These findings provide fundamental insights in designing effective passive flow control devices with simple geometric modifications.

papers.title: Aerodynamic ablation of dust grains in ambient gas under hypervelocity impact
papers.abstract: During hypervelocity impacts, the ablation of dust grains constitutes a significant source of impact flash and electromagnetic radiation. This study presents, for the first time, an investigation into the coupled mechanisms of dust grain ablation and ionization under hypervelocity impact conditions, employing the electrostatic parallel particle-in-cell (EPPIC) method in conjunction with a Monte Carlo collision model. The analysis evaluates the spatial and temporal characteristics of potential distributions arising from charge separation. Our findings reveal that, in hypervelocity impact conditions, the ablation of dust grains releases high-temperature atoms, which undergo rapid ionization due to gasdynamic effects, resulting in plasma formation. The ions and electrons generated through ablation ionization exhibit pronounced directionality and spatial-temporal inhomogeneity, forming a distinctive trail structure behind the dust grains. The rapid diffusion of electrons induces charge separation, creating distinct regions of positive potential surrounding the dust grains. Variations in field boundary conditions, ablation rates, and ambient gas pressure influence the distribution of ionization products and the evolution of the electric potential. Furthermore, the differences between ablation-induced ionization and impact ionization were analyzed, and the potential electromagnetic radiation from ablation-induced ionization was estimated. This study provides theoretical insights into the physical mechanisms governing dust grain ablation and ionization in hypervelocity impact environments, while also offering valuable guidance for the design of related experimental investigations.

papers.title: Stability analysis of discrete Boltzmann simulation for supersonic flows: Influencing factors, coupling mechanisms, and optimization strategies
papers.abstract: Supersonic flow simulations encounter challenges in threefold: trans-scale modeling, numerical stability and complex field analysis, which arise from inherent nonlinear, nonequilibrium, and multiscale characteristics. The discrete Boltzmann method (DBM) provides a multiscale kinetic modeling framework and analysis tool for capturing complex discrete/nonequilibrium states and effects. Despite its fundamental role in DBM simulations, a comprehensive stability analysis is still lacking. Similar to the lattice Boltzmann method, complexity in DBM lies mainly in the intrinsic coupling between velocity and spatiotemporal discretizations, which distinguishes it from traditional computational fluid dynamics. This study conducts von Neumann stability analysis to examine factors influencing DBM simulation stability, including approaches for determining equilibrium distribution functions, thermodynamic nonequilibrium (TNE) levels, spatiotemporal discretization schemes, initial conditions, and model parameters. Key findings include: (i) among the equilibrium distribution discretization methods considered, the moment-matching approach outperforms the expansion- and weighting-coefficient-based methods in the test simulations. (ii) Increased TNE intensity/Knudsen number enhances the system's nonlinear behavior and the intrinsic nonlinearity embedded in the matching model equation, thereby amplifying the instabilities in simulations. (iii) Although additional viscous dissipation based on distribution functions improves stability, it distorts flow fields and alters constitutive relations, highlighting the need for careful trade-offs between stability and accuracy. (iv) Larger Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy numbers and relative time steps significantly degrade stability, necessitating appropriate time-stepping strategies. To assess the stability regulation capability of DBMs across different TNE levels, stability-phase diagrams and stability probability curves are constructed within the moment-matching framework using morphological analysis. These diagrams identify common stable parameter regions applicable across various TNE orders. Finally, the effects of discrete velocity configurations on achieving both physical functionality and numerical stability are assessed through comparisons between numerical and analytical TNE solutions, as well as statistical properties of distribution functions. This study reveals key factors and coupling mechanisms governing numerical stability in DBM simulation and proposes general strategies for optimizing equilibrium distribution function discretization, discrete velocity design, and stability parameter selection across supersonic regimes.

papers.title: Roof disaster analysis and prevention technology of mining in the thick conglomerate coal pillar area
papers.abstract: Coal bursts from irregular coal pillar mining beneath thick conglomerate layers pose significant challenges in deep mining. This study analyzed overburden structure evolution and stress distribution at the coal pillar working face through theoretical modeling, numerical simulations, and field monitoring. It revealed coal burst mechanisms and roof failure prevention strategies. The results show that the mining process is influenced by the spatial structure of the surrounding stope, transitioning through stages of unilateral gob-side mining to bilateral gob-side mining, with the overburden structure evolving from C-type to S-type configuration. The coal body of the working face exhibits multi-level stress distribution characteristics. The coal pillars on the left and right sides are stress concentration areas, and the peak vertical stress increases with advancing distance. The main and sub-key strata II are the primary disaster-inducing layers during mining. The main controlling factors of coal burst are the dynamic loads from roof instability and high static stress in coal pillars. Accordingly, ground acid fracturing is proposed to weaken the disaster-causing strata, reducing the accumulation of roof elastic energy, improving the coal body stress environment, and enhancing buffering and energy absorption. After fracturing, the total fracture length is 380 and 275 m. Resonance exploration reveals extensive fractures in the rock strata with a 50% decrease in wave impedance. Microseismic events are characterized by high frequency and low energy with 103 J events decreasing by 63%. The results provide references for preventing coal bursts with similar roof conditions.

papers.title: Modeling of transport and interfacial properties for saturated quantum liquid hydrogen, deuterium, helium-4, argon, and neon using a dimensionless calorimetric parameter
papers.abstract: In this work, a method integrating reduced parameter scaling, quantum corrections, and machine learning has been established to predict the transport and interfacial properties of saturated quantum liquids Ne, D2, H2, Ar, and 4He below the critical point (T < 0.99Tc). The dimensionless calorimetric parameter (DCP), derived from Helmholtz free energy residuals, and the quantum length-scale ratio (L), quantifying thermal de Broglie wavelength relative to interparticle spacing were employed. Analysis reveals that DCP exhibits an exponential dependence on L near the critical point. Scaled properties (η̃, D*, and σ*) systematically deviate from classical trends at high L, underscoring the necessity of quantum corrections. An 8-node artificial neural network trained on high-precision datasets (NIST REFPROP 10.0) achieves exceptional accuracy with a mean squared error of 3.207 × 10−5 and high correlation coefficient R = 0.99962. The model's generalization capability is further confirmed by an external test on krypton (Kr), demonstrating reliable prediction accuracy. This work offers a computationally efficient alternative to complicated methods, validated for Bose–Einstein fluids (Ne, D2, H2, Ar, and 4He), and highlights potential applications in cryogenic engineering and quantum fluid system optimization.

papers.title: A review of methods to optimize hydraulic design and cavitation suppression of centrifugal fire pumps
papers.abstract: In modern firefighting scenarios, centrifugal fire pumps require enhanced hydraulic efficiency, cavitation resistance, and operational reliability while demanding accelerated development cycles. This study systematically investigates advancements in the hydraulic optimization design and cavitation suppression of centrifugal fire pumps. For performance enhancement, gradient-based optimization methods are analyzed, with emphasis on the adjoint method for fast iterative solution through the coupled solution of flow and adjoint equations. In the application of optimization methods based on intelligent optimization algorithms, the collaborative optimization method integrating intelligent optimization algorithms and surrogate models is explored, introducing how ensemble learning enhances nonlinear relationship modeling accuracy. In the cavitation suppression, the active methods and passive methods are reviewed, and the mechanism of the bionic structures, superhydrophobic surfaces, and other methods to delay the flow separation is analyzed. Future research priorities include multidisciplinary collaborative optimization methods, material structure, and gas–liquid two-phase flow, providing theoretical foundations for next-generation high-performance centrifugal fire pumps.

papers.title: Study on optimization of fracturing timing based on geological-engineering integration: A case study of water injection development area in the Ordos Basin
papers.abstract: The Ordos Basin is a typical low-pressure tight oil reservoir, which has been effectively developed through the advanced water injection + hydraulic fracturing technology model. Advanced water injection enhances formation energy and thereby improves recovery efficiency. However, from the perspective of fracturing, advanced water injection alters the in situ stress field of the reservoir, affecting hydraulic fracture propagation. This study proposes optimizing the fracturing timing to mitigate the negative impacts of advanced water injection on fracturing. By comprehensively considering reservoir physical and mechanical properties, a heterogeneous integrated geological-engineering model was established. Model calibration was performed using three methods: actual field fracturing treatment curves, microseismic monitoring results, and single-well production data to ensure model accuracy. Taking the square inverted nine-spot well pattern in the X341 well area as an example, the four-dimensional evolution patterns of pressure, stress, and saturation during the full-cycle advanced water injection–fracturing–production process were investigated. The study revealed the influence of advanced water injection on fracture morphology and identified the optimal fracturing timing for reservoirs with varying advanced water injection volumes and physical properties. Key findings include the following: (1) Advanced water injection induces changes in reservoir pore pressure, in situ stress, and water saturation, with diffusion ranges ranked as pressure field > stress field > saturation field. (2) Advanced water injection increases horizontal principal stresses and causes stress direction deflection (less than 3°). The maximum horizontal principal stress increases faster than the minimum horizontal principal stress along the sediment source direction, resulting in a bidirectional stress difference increase of ∼1 MPa. Conversely, perpendicular to the sediment source direction, the stress difference decreases by ∼1.6 MPa. (3) Fracturing timing significantly affects the reservoir injection-production pressure field. Excessive pre-fracturing water injection reduces fracture length and conductivity and may cause water breakthrough in new wells. Post-fracturing water injection disrupts reservoir pressure equilibrium, impairing waterflood efficiency, indicating the existence of an optimal fracturing window. (4) When permeability exceeds 1.5 mD, advanced water injection may lead to early high water cut in wells, suggesting pre-fracturing water injection should be avoided. This study provides guidance for similar advanced water injection development models.

papers.title: Investigation on the oscillatory dynamics of liquid slugs under pressure fluctuations in a capillary tube
papers.abstract: Liquid slug maldistribution can deteriorate mass and heat transfer efficiency of microfluidic slug flow. Among the dominant factors, pressure fluctuations have significant influence on uniformity of slug length and stability of the meniscus morphology. This paper experimentally investigated the hydrodynamic characteristics of an individual liquid slug of different lengths and pinning positions under imposed pressure fluctuations at multiple frequencies. An analytical model was also developed revealing that the liquid slugs behave as a mass–spring–damper system, which corresponds well with the experiment data. The second-order oscillatory dynamic characteristics of liquid slugs revealed in this paper, including the resonant frequencies of liquid slugs and the pressure magnification by a liquid slug, can be useful in optimizing the microfluidic design for overcoming slug flow maldistribution. The findings related to hydrodynamic characteristics of an individual liquid slug can also provide new insights into the pressure transmission inaccuracies in the pinholes of a pressure gauge, as well as sonocrystallization and atomization processes of an acoustic resonant slug in a microreactor.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of vibrational and misaligned effects on atomization characteristics of impinging jets
papers.abstract: To investigate the individual and combined influences of vibration and misalignment on the atomization characteristics of the impingement, this study employs the polyhedral mesh adaptive refinement algorithm and volume of fluid to discrete phase model (VOF-to-DPM) method to simulate impinging jet atomization. The numerical simulation results are validated through comparison with experimental data, ensuring calculation accuracy. The findings indicate that increased vibration frequency deteriorates atomization performance, with the back-splash phenomenon becoming particularly pronounced at a vibration frequency of 1000 Hz. In contrast to previous research, which typically addresses vibration and misalignment independently, this research concurrently evaluates their combined effects in a single numerical framework, and the results demonstrate that when the misaligned degree is small, low-frequency vibrations can mitigate the adverse effects of misaligned impingement, enhancing atomization performance. However, when the degree of misalignment is large, low-frequency vibrations amplify the deflection angle of the liquid film, shortening breakup length and degrading atomization performance. Consequently, this research provides novel insights into the dynamics of impinging jet atomization and contributes valuable implications for propulsion system design.

papers.title: On Prandtl's turbulent flow expressions for arbitrary power-law and shear-stress exponents
papers.abstract: This work overviews two forms of Prandtl's power-law representation for turbulent motions that have been frequently used throughout the literature. After clarifying the difference between these two power-law expressions and their sources, a unified formulation is provided that enables us to recover the solutions for all boundary-layer properties and wall-normal velocity for arbitrary power-law and shear-stress parameters. This is accomplished over a broad range of Reynolds numbers by leveraging closed-form relations that accompany Kármán's momentum-integral approach. The availability of a generalized formulation helps to streamline the process of determining the most suitable combinations of power-law exponents and shear-stress coefficients for a given application and Reynolds number. Our findings indicate that both power-law and shear-stress exponents have an appreciable bearing on boundary-layer characteristics. Specifically, decreasing the overall power-law exponent leads to a larger disturbance thickness coefficient but lower skin friction, displacement, and momentum thickness coefficients. Conversely, increasing the overall shear-stress exponent results in systematically larger boundary-layer coefficients. By connecting classical power-law models to modern turbulence analyses, this work may provide a flexible tool for evaluating boundary-layer properties with added degrees of freedom and controlled accuracy. The resulting framework offers a simple avenue to reconcile empirical observations with basic power-law representations, thereby reinforcing Prandtl's fundamental formulation.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic and energy capture analysis of oscillating water column wave energy converter arrays with shared mooring under concentrated wave action by parabolic breakwater
papers.abstract: The energy capture efficiency of oscillating water column (OWC) wave energy converters can be enhanced through the focusing effects of waves by a parabolic breakwater. Additionally, a shared mooring system for positioning the floating device arrays is considered an effective approach to reduce mooring costs. In this paper, a numerical wave tank was established to simulate the hydrodynamic performance of the OWC arrays based on the computational fluid dynamics methods. A mooring numerical model was developed to simulate mooring lines' behavior subject to axial elasticity, hydrodynamic forces, and vertical contact forces with the seabed based on the discrete element method. The numerical model and setup have been validated against experimental results. The motion responses, energy capture performances, and mooring lines' tensions of the floating OWC array under a shared mooring system with and without the parabolic breakwater were compared and analyzed. Results show that the parabolic breakwater significantly enhances the heave and surge motions of the OWC arrays. The central OWC deployed at the theoretical focal point of the parabolic breakwater demonstrates a substantial enhancement in energy capture capacity. Parabolic breakwater leads to an increase in the average mooring force on the leeward side of the OWC arrays system, while reducing the fluctuation in mooring force of the shared polyester ropes. This article can provide favorable reference data for the placement of floating OWC arrays under parabolic breakwater and the design and simulation of the shared mooring system in the future.

papers.title: Capture of hydrophobic particles by freely rising buoyant bubbles
papers.abstract: Buoyant bubbles rising through a suspension of particles can remove hydrophobic particles and carry them upward, leaving hydrophilic particles in the slurry. Here, the passage of a layer of buoyant bubbles through a suspension of hydrophobic particles is examined using fully resolved numerical simulations. Particles colliding with the bubbles are attached, using a simple attachment model. The particles move into the bubble until the contact angle of the triple line is equal to the static angle and slide toward the back of the bubbles, where they accumulate and reduce the rise velocity of the bubbles due to their weight. The passage of the bubbles reduces the volume fraction of the freely suspended particles, as the captured particles are carried upward with the bubbles. A simple averaged drift flux model is introduced to model the rise of the bubbles and their scavenging of hydrophobic particles, and it is shown that relatively simple closure models capture the evolution reasonably well.

papers.title: Using large language models for parametric shape optimization
papers.abstract: Recent advanced large language models (LLMs) have showcased their emergent capability of in-context learning, facilitating intelligent decision-making through natural language prompts without retraining. This new machine learning paradigm has shown promise in various fields, including general control and optimization problems. Inspired by these advancements, we explore the potential of LLMs for a specific and essential engineering task: parametric shape optimization (PSO). We develop an optimization framework, LLM-PSO, that leverages an LLM to determine the optimal shape of parameterized engineering designs in the spirit of evolutionary strategies. Utilizing Claude 3.5 Sonnet as the default LLM, we evaluate LLM-PSO on three flow-involved PSO problems: (1) lift-to-drag maximization of a two-dimensional airfoil in laminar flow, (2) drag minimization of a three-dimensional axisymmetric body in Stokes flow, and (3) thermal resistance minimization of a heat exchanger's fin profile in a conjugate thermal-hydraulic setting. Across all cases, LLM-PSO reliably recovers the reference solutions while converging rapidly, matching—and occasionally surpassing—the performance of conventional optimizers. Experiments with three additional LLMs exhibit similarly robust behaviors, with newer models exhibiting better performance. Our preliminary exploration may inspire further investigations into harnessing LLMs for shape optimization and engineering design more broadly.

papers.title: Large eddy simulation of inflow velocity effects on flow characteristics in a square-section diffuser
papers.abstract: Diffusers are essential for flow deceleration and pressure recovery, but the adverse pressure gradient often induces boundary layer separation that degrades performance. This study employs large eddy simulation (LES) to investigate how inflow velocity influences the internal flow structures of a square-section diffuser with emphasis on separation phenomena. Three inflow velocities—5, 10.5, and 30 m/s—are considered, and the flow characteristics are analyzed in terms of time-averaged, instantaneous, and fluctuating behavior. Results show that increasing inflow velocity significantly enhances static pressure recovery and exponentially reduces total pressure loss, improving diffuser efficiency. Two types of separation are identified: (1) a centerline bubble near the diverging section entrance and (2) large-scale three-dimensional corner separations. The centerline bubble triggers shear layer instability and separation-induced transition, leading to the formation of hairpin vortices. In contrast, corner regions experience earlier instability accompanied by vortex leg crossover due to vortex interactions from adjacent walls. With higher inflow velocity, vortices become smaller and more coherent, and corner separation zones shrink, reducing interference with centerline vortices. Corner separation also weakens in the mid-to-downstream regions. Turbulent kinetic energy and Reynolds stresses increase, but relative kinetic energy decreases, suggesting enhanced main flow stability despite increased asymmetry and localized instabilities. This study provides high-fidelity insights into the mechanisms of flow separation and vortex formation in square-section diffusers. These findings contribute to the development of turbulence models and the optimization of diffuser performance.

papers.title: Active yaw control optimization of wind turbines in wind farms considering multi-scenario wind speed and direction
papers.abstract: Active optimization of the yaw angle of wind turbines can improve overall power generation for the wind farm. In this paper, an active yaw control strategy with a yaw-angle exceedance penalty is proposed, and the feasibility of the approach is verified by four cases of single-scenario and multi-scenarios. First, the double Gaussian model with the yaw deflection method is utilized to predict the wake loss of a single turbine. Then, a sum-of-squares superposition model is utilized to evaluate the superposition effect of multiple turbine wake flows. Then, the particle swarm optimization algorithm with a time-varying inertia factor is optimized for single-scenario wind turbine yaw optimization, and the results are used as the initial solution for multi-scenarios. Finally, a penalty system for yaw-angle exceedance is established to globally optimize turbine yaw angle for multi-scenarios. The results show that the single-scenario yaw optimization can improve the power efficiency by 3.13%–8.61%, and the multi-scenarios active yaw optimization can improve the power efficiency by 0.58%–0.63%. The proposed method can be used for multi-scenario yaw optimization in real wind farms to achieve a balance between power generation enhancement and fatigue load reduction.

papers.title: Prandtl's mixing-length model is unsuitable for turbulent Bödewadt flow
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the suitability of various turbulence models in simulating flow within the turbulent Bödewadt boundary layer. Four progressively more realistic models are investigated; models B and C have diffusivity prescribed and models D and E have diffusivity determined in part by Prandtl's mixing-length theory. Model B is known to produce reasonable results for vortical outer flow. Using models B or C, solutions are obtained using a spectral/iterative procedure for 0.01<ρ<100, where ρ=ϵr/z0 is the dimensionless radius, r is the radial coordinate, z0 is the thickness of a rough layer adjoining the boundary, and ϵ≪1 is an inverse critical Reynolds number. Using models D and E, solutions are increasingly difficult to find as ρ becomes small; practical lower limits are ρ=0.035 for model D and ρ=0.15 for model E. All models produce the same radial structure: nearly linear variation with ρ. Boundary-layer thickness decreases as the magnitude of the turbulent diffusivity is decreased. Models D and E, based on Prandtl's theory, have serious flaws that make them unsuitable. Using model D, radial variation of the mixing length becomes large as ρ becomes small, leading to an unphysical axial velocity structure. Using model E, the Prandtl mixing length has an unphysical axial structure for ρ<1.

papers.title: Numerical investigation on energy harvesting of four submerged cylinders with different cross-sections in tandem arrangement
