papers.abstract: Efficient liquid transport in conventional capillary structures is often hindered by a fundamental trade-off between capillary pressure and permeability, as well as the absence of a built-in driving force for guided flow. These limitations restrict their applications in heat transfer, water/energy harvesting, and microfluidics. Here, we propose a hierarchical gradient dendritic mesh (HGDM), where micro-nano dendrites with density and composition gradients are selectively formed on the warp (longitudinal) copper wires aligned with the flow direction. This architecture creates aligned microchannels that serve as preferential pathways for fluid transport, significantly enhancing permeability. Meanwhile, micro-dendrites with nano-branches increase the effective surface area and reduce the local radius of curvature, generating strong capillary pressure. Additionally, the dendritic gradients induce unbalanced capillary forces, enabling direction-preferred liquid transport and further improving transport efficiency. As a result, the HGDM achieves a capillary performance parameter (ΔP·K) of 4.14 × 10−7 N and a 242% increase in liquid transport velocity compared to a dendritic copper plate. This design is projected to increase the maximum capillary limit of heat transfer devices by ∼170% over conventional configurations. This highly efficient liquid transport platform provides new insights into capillary-driven water manipulation and opening avenues for advanced applications across multiple disciplines.

papers.title: Heat transfer characteristics of supercritical CH4-H2 mixed working fluid based on Rankine cycle in horizontal tubes
papers.abstract: Based on Rankine cycle, the heat transfer characteristics of supercritical CH4-H2 mixture flowing through horizontal pipes were analyzed. The Re-Normalization Group k-ε turbulence model was adopted for numerical simulation and theoretical analysis to explore the effects of different hydrogen proportion (5%–15%) and pressures (6–10 MPa) on the physical properties of the working fluid. The influences of hydrogen proportion (0%–15%), mass fluxes (150–250 kg/(m2 · s)), and heat fluxes (150–250 kW/m2) on the heat transfer characteristics were analyzed. The results showed that as the hydrogen proportion increased, the pseudo-critical pressure rose, while the pseudo-critical temperature initially increased slightly and then decreased. When the pressure rose, the pseudo-critical temperature shifted to the right, the hydrogen proportion increased, and the overall thermophysical properties decreased. Increasing the proportion of hydrogen, mass flow rate and heat flux density all enhanced heat transfer coefficient. In the Rankine cycle system, hydrogen-doped working fluid as a mixed refrigerant effectively reduced the logarithmic mean temperature difference and improved the heat exchange efficiency of the heat exchanger in the cycle. Furthermore, a Nusselt number correlation formula based on the concentration weight factor (ηα) applicable to a certain working condition range (α = 0%–15%, Tin=130–170 K, G = 150–250 kg/(m2 · s)) was proposed, and the prediction error was within ±10%. This research provided a technical support and theoretical basis for the optimal design of hydrogen-blended natural gas transmission and power cycle systems.

papers.title: Finite element analysis of natural convection and entropy generation under the influence of magnetic field in a wavy enclosure
papers.abstract: Numerical analysis of the combined effects of natural convection exchange of thermal, entropy generation, and the existence of a warmed elliptical cylinder in a wavy enclosure stuffed with ferrofluid under an inclined uniform magnetic field. The left and right wavy walls of the enclosure are actively cooled at a temperature (Tc), while its horizontal boundaries are thermally adiabatic. Inside the cavity, an inner elliptical cylinder is heated at a constant temperature (Th). The governing equations for the system under assessment are computed using the Galerkin finite element method. The ferrofluid's flow behavior and exchange of thermal energy are investigated for relevant non-dimensional values, such as the number of sinusoidal (N=6, 12, 18), the Hartmann numbers (Ha=0, 10, 20), the number of Rayleigh (Ra=103, 104, 105), the volume fraction (ϕ=0.00, 0.03, 0.06), and the thermal transport features and entropy production variables. The outcomes show that as the Hartmann number (Ha) amplifies, the Nuavg drastically decrease, while the augmentation of both Rayleigh number (Ra) and volume fraction rise (ϕ), the average thermal transport rate of the ferrofluid increases. Additionally, when the intensity of the magnetic field is (Ha=0), with ϕ=0.06, the velocity field exhibits a more pronounced, while by applying a magnetic field with higher intensity (10≤Ha≤40), the convective heat transfer drops drastically. The application of a magnetic field significantly influences the velocity profile, effectively reducing the stream function from |ψ|max=42.54 to |ψ|max=23.09 as the Ha enhances from 0 to 20. Furthermore, the Beavg declines with the enhancement in Ra and ϕ, while it grows with the rise in Ha.

papers.title: Facilitating droplets detachment in microchannels via surface acoustic wave
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic waves (SAW) emerge as an attractive approach for droplet detachment due to unique acoustic radiation force and acoustic streaming effects. The effect of SAW on droplet detachment primarily focused on open platform, where acoustic streaming serves as the principal driving force. However, when droplet is adhered within microchannels, the acoustic radiation force would be the primary actuation for the oil–water interface, also significantly enhanced by flow shear forces, leading to more complex detachment behaviors. To reveal the mechanisms of droplet detachment under these circumstances, we integrated SAW at the microchannel to investigate the detachment dynamics of sessile droplet. Our results indicated that: (1) with increasing capillary number under SAW actuation, droplets exhibit four distinct dynamic states: pinning, sliding, detachment, and pinch-off; (2) SAW induces pinning, and facilitates the earlier onset of detachment, with the effect intensifying at higher acoustic Weber numbers; and (3) SAW suppresses pinch-off, promoting a transition from pinch-off to detachment. This study advances the understanding of droplet detachment dynamics and provides new insights for addressing droplet adhesion challenges in microfluidic systems.

papers.title: Bubble growth on a single artificial nucleation site near saturation conditions in microgravity
papers.abstract: We analyze pool boiling experiments with single bubbles realized on the International Space Station (ISS) as part of Reference mUltiscale Boiling Investigation (RUBI). Fluorinert FC-72 (pure component) is used as a working liquid. For a fixed liquid pressure (here 500, 600 or 750 mbar), upon initial thermalization, a joule heater coated atop a transparent BaF2 substrate is on. Following a “waiting time” of a few seconds (here 2 or 5 s), a pre-prepared nucleation site is activated by a laser pulse. The resulting bubble growth up to a centimetric size is diagnosed for 9 s by a side-view camera (shape, contact angle) and a bottom-view infrared camera (temperature). Here, we specifically focus on “smooth growth” cases such as low heater power and near-saturation conditions inasmuch as available in RUBI. Although our 500 fps of the camera misses a “zeroth” growth stage (the bubble being of a size of hundreds of micrometers in the first image it appears), the subsequent (first, etc.) stages are well explored. Strong shape oscillations, up to detachment, due to an initial explosive growth (first stage) are followed by a quasi-spherical-cap growth (second and third stages) with different power laws. An efficient minimalistic numerical model based on a spherical-cap approximation is developed. This helps to elucidate the physics behind each observation. A strongly disproportionate contribution of a near-contact-line zone to the evaporation flux is quantified in passing. Upon a limited calibration, in conjunction with a classical “microregion” model, the simulation reproduces well the overall measurements including the evaporation-induced contact angle.

papers.title: Conditional diffusion inversion for Darcy flows in heterogeneous porous media with random parameters
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have recently become powerful tools for solving inverse problems in scientific and engineering applications. Many existing approaches treat pre-trained diffusion models as priors and employ additional sampling or correction strategies to incorporate observations. In this work, we consider a Bayesian inverse problem arising in subsurface flow, where the goal is to reconstruct spatially heterogeneous permeability fields from noisy flow rate observations governed by transient Darcy flow. We propose a two-stage conditional diffusion framework that explicitly separates the denoising of observations and the inversion of the quantity of interest. The first stage involves training a supervised conditional diffusion model to learn the mapping from noise-free simulated flow rates to the corresponding permeability fields. The second stage employs an unsupervised diffusion model to recover noise-free flow rates from noisy observations. This two-stage structure enables robust posterior sampling by producing permeability fields that match the observed flow rates. Numerical experiments on a synthetic reservoir model demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of reconstruction accuracy, uncertainty quantification, and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Dynamics and predictive modeling of vertically rising bubble motion in rotating shear-thinning fluids
papers.abstract: This study investigates the dynamics of a rising bubble in Newtonian and shear-thinning fluids under both stationary and rotating conditions using fully resolved direct numerical simulations. In stationary shear-thinning environments, the temporal evolution of rise velocity reveals a previously unreported negative drag regime, where the net hydrodynamic force assists upward motion, an effect absent in Newtonian cases. Despite similar trajectories, early-time velocity evolution remains indistinguishable between the two rheologies, highlighting a delay in the manifestation of non-Newtonian effects. Under rotation, centrifugal and Coriolis forces compete with buoyancy to reverse the bubble's ascent. While Newtonian bubbles exhibit earlier deflection, shear-thinning fluids show enhanced trajectory stability due to rheology-induced damping. Finally, this work develops a novel closed-form predictive model, based on force balance, that accurately estimates the critical time of reversal across a range of Rossby numbers. These results offer new physical insights and a reduced-order framework for bubble dynamics in complex multiphase systems.

papers.title: Temporal evolution of scour depth and hydrodynamics around T-shaped spur dikes
papers.abstract: This study investigates the temporal evolution of scour depth and hydrodynamics around T-shaped spur dikes. The study includes 12 physical experiments with four different T-shaped spur dike sizes and three distinct velocities of 0.23, 0.28, and 0.34 m/s. Additionally, numerical modeling is performed with four different T-shaped spur dike sizes at velocity of 0.34 m/s. The effects of the densimetric Froude number, dimensionless time, and spur dike length on the scouring process are analyzed using the experimental data. Furthermore, a relationship is proposed to estimate the development of scour depth, and statistical sensitivity analyses are performed to assess the consistency of the proposed relationship with the observed data and identify the most influential parameters in the scouring process. The result of numerical modeling is validated against experimental results with an error margin of less than 7%. The simulated results provide insights into the evolution of local scour and flow field evolution, such as velocity vector fields, streamline patterns, turbulent kinetic energy, turbulence intensity, and Q-criterion. The scour evolution is analyzed for all the cases at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of equilibrium conditions, which reveal the essential features of the scouring dynamics. The study provides insights into the hydrodynamics and scour process and will be useful in the design of T-shaped spur dikes for riverbank protection.

papers.title: Diffusion mechanism and scope estimation for splitting grouting in deep rock plates: A case study based on microseismic inversion and numerical simulation
papers.abstract: Geological conditions for resource mining become more complicated with depth increasing. Grouting technique is important for preventing hazards in deep floor plates. Accurate slurry diffusion ranges have been challenging for invisibility of rock medium. In addition to geo-stress and water pressure, new grouting-induced fractures affect slurry flowing. Therefore, a hybrid model integrating microseismic (MS) sources and finite element simulation is proposed. First, MS fractures generated by grouting are embedded considering hydro-mechanical coupling. Second, this model was applied to Xieqiao coal mine, China. Diffusion ranges were statistically analyzed based on simulated data. Subsequently, to verify estimated scopes, cement hydration products contained in rock samples were detected by x-ray diffraction (XRD) mineral analysis. A novel strategy based on XRD is proposed correspondingly. Finally, laboratory tests were compared to numerical estimation. Results show that slurry diffusion patterns are more complex and show significant heterogeneous distribution and MS monitoring can help estimation closer to real scopes. Fractures provided dominant channels from 0.5 to 14.5 h. Slurry pressure can reach 9.5 MPa at 0.5 h and 16.2 MPa at 14.5 h. Influence of direction was superior to quantity for penetration. Diffusion distance in regions (45–95 m) without MS fractures (about 10 m) is smaller than regions (215–295 m) with multiple fractures (up to 50.5 m). In addition, it was revealed that the average error rate of estimated ranges along the grouting hole is limited within 6.03%. To guarantee mining safety, secondary reinforcement measures are recommended. This study provides a scientific and reliable reference for evaluating grouting effect in underground engineering.

papers.title: Investigations on the influence of high-enthalpy nonequilibrium on turbulent flows: Exploring similarities through direct numerical simulation and a priori analysis
papers.abstract: During hypersonic flight in low-altitude, vehicles encounter a complex phenomenon at their surfaces: the coupled interaction between turbulence and high-enthalpy (HE) nonequilibrium effects. This work utilizes DNS (Direct Numerical Simulation)-generated data to reveal similarities between high-enthalpy and low-enthalpy (LE) turbulence, aiming at garnering critical insights that could enhance Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) modeling. Overall, this research reveals fundamental statistical similarities between HE and LE turbulent flows, with mean velocity profiles conforming to the law of the wall, yet significant deviations in the von Kármán constant κ raise challenges for its use in RANS modeling. The Reynolds stress anisotropy tensor shows minimal sensitivity to enthalpy effects, providing potential for constructing turbulence models. Notably, Bradshaw's coefficient a1 shows a low dependence on enthalpy but reveals increased near-wall values in both HE and LE conditions compared to the incompressible scenario. Turbulent Prandtl and Schmidt numbers exhibit variations in the buffer layer (5 < y+ < 30), requiring consideration in future turbulence modeling efforts. The turbulent kinetic energy budget highlights differences in production and dissipation rates, confirming the non-negligible compressibility effects present in the viscous sublayer (0 < y+ < 5).

papers.title: Data-physics sequentially driven deep neural network for predicting flow and acoustics fields
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a data and physics sequentially driven method (D-PDM) for training neural networks to predict flow and acoustics fields, addressing the limitations of existing approaches. Traditional data-driven methods, though effective, are often black-box models that require high-accuracy and large-scale sample data, while physics-driven methods, despite their interpretability, are computationally expensive and time-consuming. The proposed D-PDM innovatively combines the strengths of both approaches through a sequential training strategy. Initially, the neural network is trained using a data-driven approach with a small number of low-accuracy data samples to rapidly reduce the prediction error. Subsequently, the model is fine-tuned using a physics-driven method to further minimize the prediction error. This sequential training process significantly reduces the reliance on high-accuracy and large-scale sample data while dramatically shortening the overall training time. The innovation of D-PDM lies in its ability to achieve lower prediction errors compared to purely data-driven methods with limited data samples and faster training times compared to purely physics-driven methods. Additionally, it outperforms methods that simultaneously integrate data and physics in both prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Three case studies on flow and acoustics field predictions validate the effectiveness of D-PDM, highlighting its potential to improve the training of neural networks in physical simulations.

papers.title: Satellite droplets suppression through trampoline effect of ring-shaped electrode during droplet flight process
papers.abstract: Pulsed voltage-driven electrohydrodynamic (EHD) drop-on-demand (DOD) printing is a promising micro- and nanoscale additive manufacturing technology. However, end-pinching mechanism can lead to the formation of tiny satellite droplets during the droplet formation process, which blurs the printed patterns and bring challenges for industrial production. This paper proposes a method to suppress satellite droplets by applying a constrained electric field from a ring-shaped electrode during the droplet flight process. The constrained electric field acts like a trampoline, cushioning the droplet's descent and facilitating the fusion of satellite droplets. First, a numerical model of EHD printing was established, and the accuracy and reliability of the numerical results were experimentally verified. Subsequently, the mechanism of electric field confinement using a ring-shaped electrode was analyzed in detail, and the “trampoline” effect was proposed. The influences of different process parameters on the trampoline effect were studied, and the process window for suppressing satellite droplet formation was identified. The study reveals the mechanism of the trampoline effect in suppressing satellite droplet formation. This provides a method to eliminate satellite droplets during flight and achieve satellite-free printing, advancing its application in high-resolution additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Machine learning meets hydrodynamics: Unraveling the nonlinear influence of aft body diameter on cavitation across varying ventilation coefficients
papers.abstract: While artificial supercavitation serves as a viable method for minimizing skin friction in underwater vehicles, there is a notable lack of comprehensive research into ventilated cavitation with constant temperature and its repercussions on such vessels. Additionally, Machine Learning models stand out as a contemporary approach for addressing complex issues in today's landscape. In the current study, the effect of increasing the aft body diameter on ventilated supercavitation flow with constant temperature using experimental, numerical, and optimized machine learning methods has been studied. In this study, incompressible air with a constant temperature was used for injection into the cavity. The data was used to validate the numerical simulation and machine learning model. The machine model used is optimized random forest model, with acceptable accuracy (About 10%) predictions and validated by numerical and experimental results. Also, using machine learning interpretability techniques, the importance and impact of parameters on cavity length have been investigated. The results show that in an aerated cavity with a constant temperature, the cavitator aft body diameter ratio affects the length of the cavity in a nonlinear way. First, it increases the length due to body-cavity interactions, and then decreases the length. Also, by increasing the ventilation coefficient, the maximum cavity length is achieved at a smaller aft body diameter ratio. Specifically, in low ventilation coefficients, doubling the rear body diameter results in an increase in cavity length by more than 70%. In high ventilation coefficients, the length of the cavity increases by more than 20%. After reaching the maximum cavity length, further increasing the rear body diameter by 50% can decrease the cavity length by up to 30%, depending on the Froude number and the ventilation coefficient.

papers.title: Evolution mechanisms of near-field noise in cylinders with varying aspect ratios
papers.abstract: This study constructs a model of near-field noise for cylinders with a single free end using Large Eddy Simulation and the sound potential fluctuation equation. This model is employed to explore the evolution mechanisms of near-field noise at a Reynolds number (Re) of 14000. The results indicate that the flowfield structure of finite-length cylinders predominantly consists of three layers: a top flowfield dominated by washdown flows, a middle flowfield governed by periodic vortex shedding from the cylinder surface, and a bottom flowfield dominated by ground boundary layers. The proportion of these three flowfield layers on the cylinder surface determines their contribution rate to aerodynamic noise. In cylinders with a short aspect ratio, the direct interaction of washdown flows with the ground, coupled with boundary layers and vortex shedding, generates significant noise at the cylinder base. For cylinders with a large aspect ratio, the total height of the washdown flows and ground boundary layers is considerably less than the height of vortex shedding on the cylinder surface, leading to vortex shedding dominating the aerodynamic noise generation mechanisms. As the aspect ratio increases further, there is a slight variation in the maximum near-field sound pressure levels. This study provides new insights into the flow-acoustic coupling for active control of aerodynamic noise in cylindrical structures.

papers.title: Sparse feature extraction-based flowfield reconstruction and prediction in a supersonic isolator
papers.abstract: The reconstruction and prediction of the flowfield within the scramjet isolator serve as the foundational elements for the surveillance and regulation of the power system in the realm of supersonic flight. An important method for doing so accurately is feature extraction. In this study, a sparse feature extraction-based supersonic flowfield reconstruction and prediction methodology is proposed. Ground experiments are performed on a supersonic isolator with variable Mach number and backpressure: sparse features of the flowfield therein are obtained by subjecting experimental schlieren to discrete orthogonal transformation and sparse processing, then reconstruction is accomplished via inverse transformation. To predict the flowfield via only a small number of wall pressure sensors, a sparse prediction model is established by combining a convolutional neural network and a fully connected network: the trained model predicts the sparse features, from which the predicted flowfield is derived. Analysis results show that the flowfield reconstructed from the sparse features has almost all the characteristics of the original one. The reconstruction accuracy exceeds 90% with fewer than 10% of the sparse features, and the predicted sparse features accurately represent the key local ones and the global structure.

papers.title: Buoyancy effect of front plate perforated brush seal based on transient fluid-solid interaction
papers.abstract: To tackle the buoyancy effect of bristles in traditional brush seal (TBS) induced by airflow, which leads to bristles disturbance instability, the construction of front plate perforated brush seal (FPBS) was proposed. Based on the Arbitrary Lagrange-Eulerian fluid-solid interaction method, three-dimensional transient solution model of the floating disturbance effect of FPBS was established. The leakage characteristics and flow field velocity characteristics of the FPBS were analyzed, and the influence of different structural parameters of the suppression disturbance (SD) hole on the buoyancy effect was researched. Additionally, the bristle tip deformation characteristics were further quantitatively investigated. The results indicated that the FPBS reduces bristles bending deformation caused by airflow by setting SD hole in front plate. This novel structure can effectively suppress the bristles buoyancy effect and improve the sealing performance. Compared to TBS, which is prone to the buoyancy effect, increasing the angle, diameter, and height of the SD hole can effectively reduce the leakage rate. When the SD hole diameter reaches 2.00 mm, the leakage rate decreases by 19.57%. The bending deformation of the bristles induced by the airflow can be effectively reduced by setting the SD hole in the front plate. When the angle of the SD hole is 60°, the diameter is 2.00 mm, and the height is 5.10 mm, the average deformation of the bristle tip can be reduced by 41.39–49.07% compared with the TBS.

papers.title: Numerical investigation on phase change heat transfer performance of a two-phase closed thermosiphon with mixed wetting patterns
papers.abstract: In this study, we investigate the phase change heat transfer performance (HTP) of a two-phase closed thermosyphon (TPCT) with mixed wetting surfaces composed of a hydrophobic condenser and a hydrophilic evaporator. The phase-change behavior and the HTP of TPCT with the mixed wetting surfaces are mainly examined under different values of input power numerically. It is discovered that the wettability has a significant impact on the HTP of the evaporator, while the input power has a significant impact on the HTP of the condenser. For a given input power, the vapor volume fraction decreases, and more liquid films are formed on the evaporator wall with the increase in the wettability of the evaporator wall. On the other hand, as the hydrophobicity of the condenser wall increases, the nucleation density gradually decreases, making it difficult for the coalesced droplets to stay on the wall. Both the boiling rate at the evaporator and condensation rate at the condenser decrease as the hydrophilicity of the evaporator increases for the medium and superhydrophobic surface of the condenser. They are almost constant as the hydrophobicity of the condenser increases. As the input power increases, evaporator thermal resistance rises modestly by an average of 13.1%, whereas condenser thermal resistance declines significantly by an average of 91.3% for all the considered mixed wetting patterns. Furthermore, the TPCT with a combination of a medium hydrophilic θe=40° evaporator and a moderately hydrophobic (θc=140°) condenser could achieve better HTP for almost all of the input power conditions taken into consideration.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of supersonic jet-induced cratering in the Martian surface based on compressible multiphase particle-in-cell method
papers.abstract: The process of perpendicular jet impingement on a particle layer, such as the Martian surface, causes complex particle craters. A comprehensive understanding of particle evolution characteristics under shock wave influence is necessary for spacecraft operation safety. A compressible multiphase particle-in-cell (CMP-PIC) method with varied particle force models was applied to numerically reveal the inherent physical mechanisms of shock wave-particle layer interactions. The reliability of this method was demonstrated by the good agreement of the crater's depth and shape between the numerical and experimental data. It was found that the shear flows and entrainment vortices are induced by bow-shaped incident shock wave–reflected shock wave interactions, which influence the spatial distribution of drag force and pressure gradient force in the upper particle region. In the particle compaction region, the collision forces of the interior particles are shown to be dominant in influencing the motion of particles. Also, the formation mechanism of cratering was quantitatively studied from the Lagrangian perspective. The momentum input from the gas phase to the surface particles, due to its sustainability, was found to be significantly greater than the momentum input caused by interior particle interactions. Since the collision force waves propagated deeper but did not reflect from the bottom wall, surface particles were subjected to an unbalanced resultant downward force in the perpendicular direction, leading to the occurrence of initial craters. This study lays a theoretical basis for further accurate flow control of the Mars landing process at high exhaust jet conditions.

papers.title: Lattice Boltzmann-based subgrid-scale modeling of fully developed turbulent pipe flow
papers.abstract: In this paper, large eddy simulations based on the volumetric strain-stretching (VSS) model and nonequilibrium moments (NM) are carried out to present the simulation of pressure-driven turbulent pipe flow at Reτ=180 (based on pipe radius and friction velocity) within a Cartesian coordinate framework. In the formulation of the subgrid-scale model, which can be called the “NM-VSS” model, the shear-strain rate tensor in the VSS model is locally derived through Chapman–Enskog expansion analysis of the NM in the D3Q27 discretization scheme. As the core numerical solver of fluid fields, the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) is implemented to resolve momentum transport, coupled with a sharp-interface immersed boundary method for the no-slip boundary at curved walls. Through comparisons with prior direct numerical simulation data, the proposed NM-VSS model shows good performance in terms of accuracy and consistency. In addition, the numerical dissipation of the near-wall region is reduced by using the NM-VSS model as compared with the typical Smagorinsky model, and the isosurface of the viscosity of the former shows better consistency with the vortex structures than the latter. Because of the specificity of the constructed form, the NM-VSS model is suitable for complex boundaries while fitting the parallelism of the LBM itself. Overall, the present work offers a useful extension and detailed information of the current LBM in dealing with turbulent flow with curved boundaries.

papers.title: Optimization of centrifugal compressor impeller with splitter blades based on secondary flow suppression mechanism
papers.abstract: The complex secondary flow inside the centrifugal compressor impeller increases internal flow loss and deteriorates the internal flow state, thereby affecting the overall performance of the compressor. To improve the internal flow conditions of the centrifugal compressor, reduce unsteady pressure fluctuations, suppress secondary flow within the impeller, and enhance compressor performance, this study investigates the optimization design of centrifugal compressor impellers with splitter blades based on the secondary flow generation mechanism. First, a parametric modeling approach is employed for the splitter blade design and main blade wrap angle distribution, the leading-edge position of the splitter blade, and the mid-plane offset of the splitter blade as optimization variables. A quantitative analysis method based on the secondary flow coefficient (Csec−VA) is established, which serves as the optimization objective for developing an automatic optimization platform for high-speed centrifugal compressor impellers. The internal flow fields of both the original and optimized impellers are analyzed through flow visualization, quantitative energy loss analysis, and comparative analysis of unsteady pressure fluctuations to reveal the suppression mechanism of secondary flow in the optimized impeller. The results indicate that the optimized impeller achieves a 2.03% reduction in pressure ratio, an 8.04% increase in isentropic efficiency, a 30.16% reduction in average pressure fluctuation amplitude, and a 17.1% decrease in the average secondary flow coefficient within the impeller flow domain. Under the condition of maintaining nearly unchanged overall performance, the proposed optimization effectively suppresses secondary flow within the centrifugal compressor.

papers.title: Interpolation-based parametric reduced-order models via Galerkin projection and dynamic mode decomposition
papers.abstract: Since dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) Galerkin reduced-order models (ROMs) have been developed and successfully applied across various fields, they hold great potential for constructing parametric reduced-order models (PROMs). By integrating the DMD-Galerkin framework with different interpolation methods, accurate and efficient DMD-Galerkin PROMs are effectively constructed. Specifically, two interpolation methods—Grassmann manifold interpolation (GMI) and mode-realigned pointwise interpolation (MRPWI)—are employed to obtain complex-valued, non-orthonormal DMD modes at target (unseen) parameters. The interpolated DMD modes are then incorporated into the Galerkin projection to build the DMD-Galerkin PROMs. It is noteworthy that the GMI, rigorously derived based on the complex Grassmann manifold via the noncompact Stiefiel manifold representation, and the MRPWI, which relies on Kasner's pseudo-angle, are both directly applied to interpolate complex-valued, non-orthonormal DMD modes, making them particularly suitable for this interpolation process. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed DMD-Galerkin PROMs, flow over a cylinder is adopted as a canonical benchmark for assessing their predictive fidelity. The results show that for target parameters within the parameter space, the DMD-Galerkin PROMs yield sufficiently accurate predictions compared to DNS and DMD-Galerkin ROMs, while providing computational efficiency over high-fidelity simulations. Furthermore, the DMD-Galerkin PROMs constructed with GMI and MRPWI exhibit comparable accuracy, while those with the latter are more efficient due to its theoretical simplicity.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of coupled drag reduction mechanism of loach mucus trapped by flexible V-microgrooves
papers.abstract: Biomimetic mucus-lubricated surfaces are highly effective in reducing drag, but achieving stable mucus adsorption on microstructures remains a challenge. The loach (Paramisgurnus dabryanus) can reduce frictional resistance during swimming. Using the water tunnel experimental platform, it was calculated that loach skin with mucus achieves a 28% drag reduction compared to mucus-free skin. Inspired by the ultra-smooth and flexible body surface of loach skin, this study establishes a novel biomimetic lubricating surface design that utilizes flexible V-microgrooves (FV) to firmly trap the mucus, thereby enhancing lubrication and reducing friction. The mucus and flexible V-microgrooves (M&FV) aim to effectively reduce drag while improving the durability of self-lubricating surfaces. To explore the drag reduction mechanism of the model, the V-microgrooves, the high viscosity of the mucus, and the low interfacial tension with water were studied. Through numerical simulations, the optimal configuration was identified using the drag reduction rate (DRE) as the primary evaluation criterion. Within 1.5 s, at the flow rate of 1 m/s, the M&FV3 achieved a maximum DRE of 34.64%, and the effective slip length was 3.2 μm. Inside the FV, the mucus volume fraction reached 32.72%, which significantly reduced surface pressure resistance by 31.57% and viscous resistance by 40.83%. Additionally, the increased boundary layer thickness promoted velocity slip, further enhancing drag reduction. These findings highlight the potential of integrating bionic mucus and microgrooves into self-lubricating surfaces, providing valuable insights for advancing biological lubrication in engineering applications.

papers.title: Influence of pressure fluctuations on the sealing performance of a spiral groove mechanical seal in different phase states
papers.abstract: To investigate the impact of internal pressure fluctuations on the performance of multiphase flow mechanical seals in high-speed rotating equipment, this study focuses on a spiral groove mechanical seal and establishes a transient continuous boiling model that comprehensively considers centrifugal inertia and phase transition. The transient Reynolds equation, energy equation, and heat transfer equation are solved using the finite difference method, and the small perturbation method is employed to analyze multi-variable perturbations of film pressure, viscosity, and density. The study examines the influence of pressure fluctuations at the inner and outer diameters on the phase state of the fluid film and the steady-state and dynamic performance of the seal when the fluid film is in different phase states. The results indicate that the location of pressure fluctuations significantly affects the phase transition ratio of the fluid film and the sealing performance. Compared to inner diameter pressure fluctuations, outer diameter pressure fluctuations exhibit a more pronounced effect on the response curves of fluid film phase transition ratio, opening force, and axial stiffness coefficient, while showing a weaker influence on leakage rate and axial damping coefficient. When outer diameter pressure fluctuations stabilize, the restored stable response times of sealing performance and dynamic characteristic coefficients are significantly longer than those for inner diameter pressure fluctuations. Large-scale and rapid changes in the vapor mass fraction of the fluid film can significantly alter the pressure distribution, causing strong oscillations in the response curves of sealing performance and dynamic characteristic coefficients, and transient increases in leakage rate.

papers.title: Offshore wave energy converter array poses threat to coasts causing significant rip currents
papers.abstract: The deployment of wave energy converters (WECs) in arrays is promising for the exploitation of sustainable marine energy under the overwhelming pressure of global warming. The far-field influence of these arrays can alter nearshore hydrodynamics and environment. Existing studies focus on the change of wave actions while little attention is paid to nearshore circulation patterns. Using a fully nonlinear Boussinesq-type wave model, this paper investigates the influence of WEC array in wave-dominated beach environment. It is shown that significant rip currents will form in the lee of the array despite the original circulation pattern. In the longshore non-homogeneous beach environment, the array-related rip current can be comparable to the natural one in terms of magnitude. The extension length is dependent on the deployment location. The generation mechanism is similar to that of a shadow rip, with an exception for a specific incident angle. This study raises concern of nearshore circulation changes to ensure nearshore environment safety.

papers.title: Microwave-liquid nitrogen synergy on granite fracture surfaces induced by Brazilian splitting
papers.abstract: The efficient fracturing of deep hard rock remains a critical challenge in resource exploration. To enhance the upper limit of mechanical rock-breaking capacity for polycrystalline diamond compact bits, microwave heating and liquid nitrogen cooling (LNC) are receiving increasing attention due to their superior auxiliary rock-breaking effectiveness. This study investigates the synergistic effects of microwave-LNC on the mechanical properties, fracture morphology, and energy evolution of granite. Brazilian splitting tests are conducted on granite specimens subjected to varying microwave durations (0–16 min) and thermal cycles (1–20 cycles). Three-dimensional scanning and fractal analysis are employed to quantify the roughness and anisotropy of fracture surfaces. The results reveal that microwave-LNC pretreatment significantly reduces tensile strength (up to 79.5% after 15 cycles) and alters fracture morphology. The fracture surfaces exhibit an inverse proportionality between surface undulation (maximum peak to valley height Z and root mean square slope Z2) and geometric complexity (fracture dimension D), while demonstrating anisotropic characteristics. The anisotropy of the fracture surface has larger roughness at 15°–45° and 105°–165°. Energy analysis highlights strong correlations between dissipated energy and roughness parameters, particularly along the loading direction. Microstructural analysis identifies five distinct thermal damage stages, governed by intergranular crack propagation, mineral expansion anisotropy, and crack tip blunting.

papers.title: Effect of temperature-dependent viscosity on molten steel behavior in ladle stirring: A numerical simulation and industrial practice
papers.abstract: Ladle stirring plays a crucial role in improving the homogeneity of alloying elements and temperature distribution in molten steel. Due to the high-temperature nature of the process, numerical simulations have been widely used in the study of ladle stirring. However, previous numerical simulations have generally assumed viscosity as a constant parameter. In this study, viscosity is considered as a temperature-dependent variable, and its impact on temperature distribution, fluid flow, alloy melting, and alloying element diffusion is analyzed. The results show that in industrial practice, the average temperature decrease rate in molten steel is 1.31 K·min−1. When viscosity is assumed constant, the numerical simulation predicts a temperature decrease rate of 1.12 K·min−1, while when viscosity varies with temperature, the predicted temperature decrease rate is 1.312 K·min−1. The industrial alloy homogenization time is 140 s, and when the viscosity of molten steel changes, the numerical simulation predicts an alloy homogenization time of 138.6 s, which is more consistent with the industrial experimental results. The findings demonstrate the significance of incorporating temperature-dependent viscosity in simulations, as opposed to assuming viscosity as a constant parameter.

papers.title: Exact solutions of the Beaufort Gyre in the presence of ice
papers.abstract: Based on the Navier–Stokes equation and the mass conservation equation in a rotating frame, combined with appropriate stress boundary conditions at the air–ice–water interface, we select suitable parameters and invoke the thin-shell approximation to establish a mathematical model describing the ice and ocean surface flow problem in the central Arctic Ocean, governed by the Beaufort Gyre. Using knowledge of differential equations and mathematical analysis, we provide exact solutions for the equations when the eddy viscosity is either a constant or a quadratic function or a power function. The angles between the wind stress covering the ocean and the generated current at the ocean surface, between the wind stress and the floating ice, and between the floating ice and ocean surface currents are calculated, respectively. Under the conditions of additional pressure exerted by the weight of floating ice and given atmospheric pressure at the surface, the analytical expression of the pressure variation with the depth of the flow is obtained. The analytical solution for the vertical velocity component of the surface ocean current is calculated and used to describe the upwelling/downwelling associated with horizontal motion.

papers.title: A low-cost singular value decomposition-based data assimilation technique for analysis of heterogeneous combustion data
papers.abstract: This article applies low-cost singular value decomposition (lcSVD) for the first time, to the authors' knowledge, on combustion reactive flow databases. The lcSVD algorithm is a novel approach to SVD, suitable for calculating high-resolution two-dimensional (2D) or three-dimensional (3D) proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) modes and temporal coefficients using data from sensors. Consequently, the computational cost associated with this technique is much lower compared to standard SVD. Additionally, for the analysis of full n-dimensional datasets, the method reduces data dimensionality by selecting a strategically reduced number of points from the original dataset through optimal sensor placement or uniform sampling before performing SVD. Moreover, the properties of data assimilation of heterogeneous databases of this method are illustrated using two distinct reactive flow test cases: a numerical database modeling an axisymmetric, time-varying laminar co-flow flame with a fuel mixture of 65% methane and 35% nitrogen, using air as the oxidizer, and experimental data generated from a turbulent bluff-body-stabilized hydrogen flame. The computational speed-up and memory gains associated with the lcSVD algorithm compared to SVD can reach values larger than 10, with compression factors greater than 2000. Applying lcSVD for data assimilation to reconstruct the flow dynamics combining data from sensors with simulation measurements, we found errors smaller than 1% in the most relevant species modeling the flow.

papers.title: Suppression mechanism of pressure oscillations in solid rocket motors based on the flow control technology of dielectric barrier discharge plasma
papers.abstract: This study introduces dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma flow control technology into solid rocket motors with finocyl grain configurations to suppress pressure oscillations induced by flow instabilities in the combustion chamber. By coupling a DBD plasma excitation model with large eddy simulation, a three-dimensional numerical method for analyzing internal flow fields was established. Numerical calculations were performed to investigate the flow characteristics and pressure oscillation behaviors under DBD plasma excitation. The results show that compared with experimental data, the dominant frequency and amplitude errors are 3.09 % and 3.60 %, respectively. The velocity gradient curves predicted under plasma excitation also agree well with literature results. This validates the accuracy of the proposed method. An appropriate DBD plasma excitation reduces the amplitude of pressure oscillations at the nozzle inlet by approximately 69.6 %. This, in turn, effectively inhibits the amplification of acoustic-vortex coupling. The suppression mechanism involves plasma-induced vortices disrupting the corner vortex structures, enhancing the rotational intensity and energy dissipation in the anterior segment of the step downstream region, and inhibiting the periodic shedding of large-scale vortices. This prevents periodic energy supply to the downstream coherent structures and eliminates cyclic acoustic feedback with the nozzle wall. The observations provide a novel approach for suppressing pressure oscillations in finocyl-grain solid rocket motors.

papers.title: Migration of gyrotactic micro-organisms in surface gravity waves
papers.abstract: Many micro-organisms such as phytoplankton commonly inhabit the upper layers of aquatic environments, where surface waves are prevalent. In this study, we investigate the migration of gyrotactic micro-organisms in surface gravity waves using two complementary approaches: a wave-averaged simplified continuum theory specific to spherical micro-swimmers, which combines Lagrangian Stokes drift with generalized Taylor dispersion theory, and a wave-resolved random walk simulation. We begin with a parametric analysis of gyrotaxis and swimming on dispersion. While both methods show that stronger gyrotaxis enhances gravitactic focusing near the surface, the random walk simulation additionally reveals a regime in which gyrotactic swimmers exhibit a mean vertical position below that of passive solute particles. The migration of non-spherical micro-swimmers is analyzed using the random walk simulation. Rod- and disc-like micro-swimmers display distinct transport behaviors due to their shape-induced orientation preferences, which either enhance or inhibit vertical focusing. Incorporating non-linear wave effects shows that all swimmer types experience increased drift velocities, but only disc-like swimmers exhibit significantly amplified longitudinal dispersion. Finally, the addition of a background current weakens gravitactic focusing in spherical swimmers, while inducing opposite responses in rod- and disc-like ones. Our findings highlight the crucial role of swimmers' taxes and morphology and wave–swimmer interactions in shaping vertical distributions and dispersion characteristics, offering insight into the prevalence of elongated forms among motile phytoplankton.

papers.title: Stability analysis of viscoelastic fluid flow between two parallel plates, modeled by linear and exponential Phan–Thien–Tanner models
papers.abstract: A temporal linear stability analysis of three-dimensional viscoelastic fluid flow between two parallel plates is performed using the linear and exponential forms of the Phan–Thien–Tanner (LPTT and EPTT) constitutive models. The study systematically investigates the influence of key dimensionless parameters—Reynolds number (Re), Weissenberg number (Wi), viscosity ratio (βnn), spanwise wavenumber (β), elongational parameter (ε), and mobility parameter (ξ)—on the onset of flow instability. Neutral stability curves in the α−Re plane are constructed to delineate stable and unstable regions for a wide range of these parameters. The results show that, for both models, two-dimensional waves (β=0) are found to be the most unstable mode. An increase in the Weissenberg number consistently destabilizes the flow, while a higher viscosity ratio (larger solvent fraction) has a strong stabilizing effect. The influence of the elongational parameter, ε, is shown to be model-dependent, exhibiting a destabilizing effect in the LPTT model and a more complex, dual role in the EPTT model that reverses from destabilizing at low Wi to stabilizing at high Wi. The mobility parameter, ξ, is consistently destabilizing for both models. A direct comparison reveals that the LPTT model consistently predicts a larger unstable region than the EPTT model, highlighting that the choice of the constitutive stress function is a critical factor in determining flow stability characteristics.

papers.title: Flow separation-induced cavitation dynamics and pressure pulsation in mixed-flow pumps
papers.abstract: In dynamic marine environments, transient flow separation and cavitation–vortex coupling phenomena induced by frequent operational transitions of mixed-flow pumps pose significant threats to the reliability of marine equipment. This study employs high-speed visualization and synchronous pressure monitoring experiments, combined with image analysis and spectral diagnostics, to initially identify a special operating regime dominated by high-swirling flow within mixed-flow pumps. This condition can be quantitatively recognized through anomalies in energy flux density values. Then, the research systematically investigates the coupling mechanism between flow separation and cavitation evolution, along with their dynamic influence on pressure pulsations. High-speed photography visually shows for the first time the amplification effect of discrete bubble clusters on vortex cavitation. Under specific flow conditions, rotating leakage vortices entrain discrete bubble groups, resulting in significant expansion of cavitation zones and intensification of impact loads. Through comprehensive pressure spectrum analysis across all operating conditions, this study establishes frequency signatures of cavitation-induced pressure fluctuations in mixed-flow pumps. Low-frequency broadband energy dominates under atmospheric pressure, while high-frequency broadband energy becomes significantly enhanced due to cavitation effects when pressure drops to critical values. This enhanced energy distribution is closely correlated with vortex dynamic evolution.

papers.title: A data-driven evaluation of solution strategies for nonlinear parabolized stability equations
papers.abstract: Parabolized stability equations (PSE) have been widely employed to understand the development of perturbations in fluid flow and predict laminar-to-turbulent transition since their introduction in the 1990s. The parabolic structure of the PSE framework enables efficient and cost-effective computations. This framework relies on the assumption of “slowly varying shape functions,” implemented through a wavenumber iteration formula typically designed to minimize the streamwise gradient of disturbance kinetic energy for the primary mode. However, it remains unclear whether an iteration strategy effectively mitigates the influence of elliptical terms in the harmonics, thereby affecting both the applicability and accuracy of the equations. To address this concern, we propose a global magnitude analysis combined with a balance model framework utilizing a Gaussian mixture model and sparse principal component analysis. This methodology systematically assesses the relative significance of retained and neglected elliptical terms across the entire flow field and Fourier space, verifying the physical relevance and predictive accuracy of PSE-based analyses.

papers.title: Propagation laws of complex fracture networks in cleated thin-layer coal rocks
papers.abstract: With the continuous advancement of coal resource extraction and coalbed methane (CBM) development, revealing the propagation laws of hydraulic fractures in cleated thin-layer coal rocks has become particularly important. This study establishes a three-dimensional complex fracture propagation model considering the cleat system based on the Block Discrete Element Method, systematically investigating the influences of geological, engineering, and perforation factors on hydraulic fracture propagation in coal seams. The results show that: (1) the thickness of coal seams affects the expansion pattern of hydraulic fracture networks by regulating stress distribution, showing a positive correlation with hydraulic fracture length and width, and a negative correlation with fracture height. (2) Cleat spacing significantly affects the fracture network in cleated thin-layer coal rocks; smaller spacing leads to more frequent interactions between fractures and cleat surfaces, resulting in a more complex network. (3) Cleat angle exerts a notable guiding effect on the propagation direction of fractures in thin coal seams; the maximum fracture deflection angle and higher fracture complexity index occur at a cleat angle of 45°. (4) A high injection rate (16–20 m3/min) effectively increases fracture width and stimulated reservoir volume in cleated thin-layer coal rocks, while reducing the risk of fracture penetration into the roof and floor, thus improving CBM recovery efficiency. The findings provide a theoretical basis and technical support for efficient CBM development.

papers.title: Influence of slot radial skew angle on performance of a transonic fan with arc-shaped casing treatment
papers.abstract: Demanding operational requirements for modern aero-engines necessitate enhanced compressor stability, often limited by tip flow instability. Casing treatments can significantly increase the stall margin, but this benefit often involves efficiency trade-offs. This work employs combined experimental and numerical methods on a transonic fan to investigate arc-shaped slot casing treatment, focusing on the influence of slot radial skew angle. A key finding is that a larger skew angle can dramatically improve the stall margin by achieving better flow alignment near the stall boundary, offering a direct and effective strategy for extending the stable operating range. Stabilization enhancement is attributed to a dual momentum replenishment mechanism (injection disrupting tip leakage vortex, suction mitigating shock-induced boundary layer separation). A critical stability limit involves a mismatch between the actual radial flow angle (αr) and designed skew angle (γ); stall occurs when increasing αr exceeds γ. The skew angle influences the performance trade-off: larger angles (e.g., 55° vs 35°) yield a larger stall margin by improving matching near stall. Conversely, at high flow rates, a larger angle mismatch reduces slot activity, leading to slightly lower efficiency penalties in that regime. Efficiency losses stem from rotor tip mixing and flow redistribution-induced stator hub separation.

papers.title: Structural optimization study of anti-water hammer air valves
papers.abstract: This study addresses the limitations of traditional air valves used in water hammer protection, such as low exhaust efficiency, poor anti-water hammer performance, and the difficulty in accurately modeling dynamic air intake and exhaust behaviors. The research focuses on the anti-water hammer air valve and proposes innovative dynamic air intake and exhaust coefficient models (Cin(p), Cout(p)) based on differential pressure variation. The research examines the structural characteristics of the throttle plug, considering different positions, shapes, and center orifice diameters. Fluent simulations were performed to evaluate the impact of these parameters on the valve's air intake and exhaust performance, identifying the optimal throttle plug design. The results demonstrate that optimizing the throttle plug position to h = 80%, improves the minimum negative pressure by 6.48% to 46.01% compared to the original design. A funnel-shaped throttle plug improves the minimum negative pressure by 11.20% to 29.03%, and an orifice ratio between 10% and 16% enhances the minimum negative pressure by 3.65% to 27.35%. The dynamic air intake and exhaust models, supported by high-precision numerical simulations (R2 = 0.99), overcome the limitations of traditional fixed coefficient models, significantly enhancing transient pressure prediction accuracy. The optimized structure was validated using the mathematical model of an actual AL water conveyance project in Xinjiang, effectively reducing the risk of negative pressure. This study provides a framework for optimizing the structural design of anti-water hammer air valves and a solid theoretical basis for the safe operation of long-distance water conveyance systems.

papers.title: Evaluation of linear and nonlinear methods for predicting the dynamic behavior of plain and textured water-lubricated bearings
papers.abstract: In this study, a transient mixed elastohydrodynamic lubrication (mixed-EHL) model coupled with a rotor dynamic model to analyze the dynamic behavior of water-lubricated bearings. The hydrodynamic pressure in the transient mixed-EHL model was computed using two commonly used methods in dynamic analysis: the linear method and the nonlinear method. Both methods were validated through comparison with experimental and numerical results from existing literature. A comprehensive evaluation is then conducted to assess their applicability in predicting the dynamic responses of both plain and textured bearings subjected to rotor unbalance. This evaluation covers key aspects such as transient mixed lubrication performance, rotor dynamics, and axis trajectory. Furthermore, the effects of rotor unbalance, mass-conserving cavitation, and rotational speed on the dynamic responses obtained using the two methods are systematically investigated. The results indicate that the differences in dynamic responses obtained using the linear and nonlinear methods are more pronounced for textured bearings compared to plain bearings. These differences primarily arise from variations in transient contact and friction forces. Therefore, the nonlinear method is recommended for the dynamic analysis of textured bearings, especially under large rotor unbalance. However, this inevitably increases the computational cost, highlighting the need for developing acceleration strategies in future work. In contrast, the linear method is not recommended for analyzing transient contact and friction behaviors of rotor-bearing systems. Interestingly, the study also finds that mass-conserving cavitation has a limited impact on dynamic analysis and can be neglected without significantly compromising accuracy. Additionally, the linear method may become unsuitable for accurate dynamic predictions at high rotational speeds.

papers.title: Experimental and numerical investigation of the inhibition mechanism of deep-sea mining sediment plume based on fluid flow characteristics
papers.abstract: The commencement of commercial deep-sea mining activities is contingent upon minimal environmental disturbance, which is a mandatory and stringent criterion. In this research, a novel active separation type sediment disturbance inhibition device, termed the Y-shaped separation device, is proposed based on the solid–liquid flow motion characteristics. The numerical model was primarily utilized to characterize the motion of the sediment plume through the discrete element model methods. Subsequently, the device underwent numerical optimization by means of the selection of structural characteristic parameters (b1, b2, L1, L2, D). The optimized flow field has been shown to reduce the accelerated region of local velocity and form a stable streamlined flow structure. Concurrently, a quantitative relationship between structural parameters and inhibition was established. Under conditions of an average sediment particle size of 5 μm and an inlet Reynolds number Re ≈ 77 000, the maximum particle separation rate can achieve to 57.8%. Subsequent experimental studies have demonstrated the inhibition effect of the device. It has been demonstrated that the device is capable of reducing the initial sediment release effectively. The utilization of a separation device has been demonstrated to reduce the sediment content (the average sediment particle size of 16.43 μm) of the discharged plume to one-third of its initial volume, under the same Reynolds number as simulation, thereby achieving a substantial plume inhibition effect.

papers.title: Aspect ratio effects on flow past a bed-mounted emergent cylinder
papers.abstract: The wake characteristics of an emergent bed-mounted circular cylinder of diameter d are investigated for intermediate aspect ratios located within a fully developed turbulent boundary layer using particle image velocimetry. The Reynolds number based on flow depth (H) and bulk velocity (Um) is 24 700, and the aspect ratio (AR), defined as the ratio of H/d, is varied from 1.7 to 6.7. The impact of AR on time-averaged flow statistics including mean velocity, Reynolds stresses, flow anisotropy, and two-point correlations was analyzed in the vertical central plane and across three spanwise planes. This study builds upon the earlier work of Heidari et al. [Phys. Fluids 29(6), 065111 (2017)], which investigated an emergent, bed-mounted cylinder with AR = 11. The results reveal that the flow topology and coherent structures in the wake are influenced by AR across all measurement planes. In the low AR cases, detached reverse flow regions were observed near the bed, as bed friction interferes with the formation of the von Kármán vortex street. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) reveals a decrease in energy content in the near-bed plane with increasing AR consistent with enhanced small-scale activity. In contrast, the trend is reversed in the mid-depth and near-free surface planes, where turbulent kinetic energy becomes concentrated in the low-order modes as AR increases. Furthermore, for AR = 1.7, the POD modes are highly correlated throughout the flow depth, whereas higher AR cases show weaker correlations, indicating complex flow structures.

papers.title: Flow characteristics prediction and sealing performance optimization of labyrinth seals in organic Rankine cycle with deep learning
papers.abstract: The low-grade energy utilization technology based on the organic Rankine cycle is an effective approach to solving global climate issues. Labyrinth seals in turbines can reduce fluid leakage and improve system efficiency. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of the performance of labyrinth seals with the thermo-fluid-structural coupling method. Employing deep learning methods, the flow characteristics prediction and sealing performance optimization of labyrinth seals are achieved. The results demonstrate that the arrangement of the disturbance groove on the stator wall can enhance energy dissipation in cavities and significantly reduce leakage, among which the circle groove performs the best. The well-trained deep learning model can reconstruct the physical distributions of cavities within 3 ms, and accurately recognize the leakage and thrust force, with prediction accuracy much higher than traditional surrogate models. The optimization framework based on a deep learning model and a gradient-based algorithm achieves great convergence and strong robustness in all optimization tasks. After optimization, the leakage of the circle groove seal is reduced by up to 19.63% compared to the straight seal structure. This research provides crucial references for further performance improvement of organic working fluid labyrinth seals, and also practical cases for the widespread application of deep learning.

papers.title: Research on gas–liquid two-phase flow characteristics of compressed air blowing water
papers.abstract: The process of compressed air being blown into a body of water generates a complex gas–liquid two-phase flow field. This paper describes numerical simulations of compressed air blowing water using the volume-of-fluid multiphase flow method. The accuracy and convergence of the numerical method are verified by comparison with experimental data and high-speed imaging results. Based on a visualized symmetric water tank blowing system, the gas–liquid two-phase flow characteristics inside the tank are analyzed. In the initial stage of the blowing process, the gas jet flow at the center is minimally affected by the gas–liquid mixing induced by the initial momentum of the compressed air. Subsequently, the gas jet mixes with the surrounding liquid water, forming an elliptical gas–liquid mixture in the middle of the tank. As the jet develops, it evolves into a turbulent mixing region influenced by the buoyancy of the surrounding environment. Under the effect of gas turbulence and buoyancy, a cavity structure forms inside the tank, causing the gas–liquid interface to separate. The liquid level rapidly drops as gas accumulates in the tank, and the water is eventually expelled. A visualized ballast tank blowing system is designed, and the gas–liquid two-phase flow patterns inside the tank are discussed. The variations in internal pressure and the free liquid surface are determined, and the air supply and drainage mechanisms of the water tank, along with their influencing factors, are clarified. The results verify the correctness of the numerical model.

papers.title: Effects of moonpools and heave plates on hydrodynamic performance of a barge-type floating offshore wind turbine platform in regular waves
papers.abstract: A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) study is conducted to evaluate the hydrodynamic performance of a barge-type floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) platform subjected to regular wave conditions. A 1:50 scale model is adopted to investigate the influence of moonpool number, dimensions, and configurations, as well as the width of the heave plate. The wave height is fixed at 0.1 m and the wave period is varied from 1.6 to 2.5 s in increments of 0.1 s. Key performance indicators, including motion response amplitude operators (RAOs), mean wave drift force, fairlead tension in mooring lines and pitch angles, are examined in detail. The platform motion response is notably affected by the length of the moonpool in the wave propagation direction. A reduction in the moonpool length slightly increases the motion responses under long-period wave conditions, while significantly decreasing the pitch RAO under short-period waves. Completely removing the moonpool results in increased wave loading, leading to the highest fairlead tension RAO and compromising both the economic viability and safety of the platform, whereas increasing the heave plate width effectively suppresses the platform motions in the heave and pitch directions. Overall, the incorporation of moonpools and heave plates substantially improves the hydrodynamic performance of the barge-type FOWT platform.

papers.title: Improving cavitating jet erosion efficiency using a multi-orifice nozzle: Experimental and numerical study
papers.abstract: Conventional cavitating water jet nozzles exhibit local material removal efficiency and energy utilization limitations, making them insufficient for low-power applications. To address this issue, this study proposed a novel multi-orifice cavitating water jet nozzle. Multiple inclined micro-orifices were uniformly distributed around a central main orifice to enhance the generation and collapse of cavitation bubbles. This structure promoted cavitation collapse and turbulence intensification, improving local impact intensity and material removal efficiency. Computational fluid dynamics simulations were conducted using the mixture multiphase model combined with the re normalization group k–ε turbulence model. The cavitating jet behaviors of both the novel and conventional nozzles were simulated. Key flow features such as pressure distribution, vapor volume fraction, and turbulence kinetic energy were analyzed. Meanwhile, a fluid–structure interaction simulation was introduced to calculate the distributions of static pressure and wall shear stress on the target surface, further evaluating the impact capability of the jet on the material surface. In the experimental section, 7075 aluminum alloy was selected as the target material. Surface morphology evolution and damage mechanisms under different erosion durations were systematically investigated using scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive spectroscopy, and surface roughness measurements. The results showed that, under the 90-min condition, the novel nozzle produced irregular deep pits, plastic deformation, and tearing features with a concentrated distribution. The study confirmed the ability of nozzle geometry to regulate jet behavior. Experimental basis and a technical approach were provided to support the application of water jet technology in high-efficiency and low-power scenarios.

papers.title: On-demand electrohydrodynamic inkjet printing utilizing water hammer effect and direct current electric fields
papers.abstract: In this study, we propose a drop-on-demand (DOD) electrohydrodynamic (EHD) jetting method based on the water hammer effect. This approach utilizes a single-pulse excitation applied to a piezoelectric actuator to induce abrupt axial displacement of a capillary, resulting a pulsatile pressure near the nozzle. This pressure pulse initiates pronounced oscillations of the liquid meniscus. The subsequent application of an direct current (DC) electric field to the oscillating meniscus can trigger EHD jetting synchronized with the excitation signal. We demonstrate that the pulsatile flow field at the orifice, in conjunction with the electric stress, can sharpen the liquid interface into a conical shape with a singularity within tens of microseconds. This extremely short tip-formation timescale enables the realization of high-frequency DOD jetting at rates up to 1 kHz. In addition, a series of parametric experiments were conducted to elucidate the EHD jetting characteristics based on which an DOD printing control strategy was developed. The proposed method achieves robust and accurate droplet deposition across a broad ink viscosity range (2.5–1410 mPa·s) without relying on complex pulsed electric field modulation. These findings provides both theoretical insight and technical guidance for the advancement of drop-on-demand EHD jet printing under DC electric fields.

papers.title: Viscosity ratio as a governing factor in microdroplet generation and size modulation
papers.abstract: This study utilizes numerical methods to systematically investigate the effect of viscosity ratio on the formation dynamics and size modulation of microdroplets within cross-shaped microchannels with a contraction structure. It demonstrates that varying the viscosity ratio between the dispersed and continuous phases gives rise to three droplet formation modes: dripping, transition, and jetting. In contrast to standard cross-junction microchannels, the contraction geometry significantly enhances local shear stress and pressure differentials, resulting in a non-monotonic dependence of droplet size on viscosity ratio—exhibiting an initial decrease followed by a subsequent increase. Specifically, in the dripping mode, a higher dispersed phase viscosity reduces internal vorticity and deformation resistance, increases pressure-driven forces beyond the interfacial tension, and thereby accelerates droplet breakup to yield smaller droplets. Conversely, in the jetting mode, the high viscosity of the dispersed phase impedes deformation, elongates the breakup cycle, and ultimately increases droplet size. The flow field analysis reveals the underlying force competition mechanism that dynamically governs the droplet breakup process across regimes. Additionally, theoretical scaling relations are proposed for predicting droplet size, which is derived from the capillary number and viscosity ratio, and validated against simulation data.

papers.title: Behavior of coupled translational bubbles in a focused ultrasonic field
papers.abstract: Cavitation structures generated in deionized by high-intensity focused ultrasound with 500 kHz and 1 MHz center frequencies were recorded using a high-speed camera and characterized by image-processing techniques, including the maximum intensity projection method. Bubble streams were observed along the axis of the pre-focal and post-focal regions of the acoustic field, and the translational trajectories fluctuated due to the primary Bjerknes force. In addition, the central bubble streams were surrounded by bubble chains, which exhibited spatial structures, including semicircular, spiral, straight-line, and string structures. Bubble pairs were also observed moving in the 1 MHz focused field, with three trajectories: attraction, self-propulsion, and ejection. Meanwhile, the radiation field of a concentrated transducer was simulated to investigate the mechanism of bubble interaction in the tank. The numerical results show that acoustic streaming accelerates bubble streams and affects the cavitation structure's spatial arrangement. A coupled migration model was also developed to trace the trajectories of bubble pairs in a standing acoustic field. Bubble ejection and self-propulsion occur at speeds comparable to the streaming velocities, potentially serving as driving forces of these bubbles. The impulsive repulsion of the secondary Bjerknes force between the bubbles leads to bubble ejection. A classification method was developed using AlexNet to analyze the relationship between parameters and the migration types, and it was found that the trajectories are nonlinearly related to the parameters. The resonance radius plays an important role in the parameter correlation.

papers.title: Soret effect on interfacial instability of droplet driven by surface acoustic waves
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) atomization enables rapid generation of aerosol droplets with micrometer- and sub micrometer-scale diameters. For the first time, a theoretical analysis is conducted to explore the impact of the Soret effect on interfacial instability in droplets subjected to SAW actuation. An evolution equation of a droplet is derived, with its behavior governed by dimensionless parameters, including the Soret number Sr, acoustic capillary number E, thermal Marangoni number MaT, and solutal Marangoni number Mac. The lines method is used to numerically simulate the droplet evolution process. The droplet height h(x, t) decreases and the characteristic length L increases with increasing Mac and Sr, and decreasing MaT. Additionally, an increase in wave peaks brought on by rising Mac and Sr, and falling MaT may lead to droplet atomization. The droplet aspect ratio ε drops sharply at the beginning, but its rate of decline progressively slows down as time t goes on. When the rate of change of ε for time approaches zero, the corresponding interval is defined as the quasi-stable stage. At the same time, the preceding period is identified as the unstable stage. An earlier commencement of the quasi-stable stage is caused by the acceleration of the rate at which ε declines and the shortening of the transition time as Mac, Sr, and E rise. Moreover, increases in Mac and Sr, result in a reduction in the final ε.

papers.title: Reducing pressure fluctuations in a giant Francis turbine using biomimetic draft tubes
papers.abstract: Hydropower plays a pivotal role in water–wind–solar complementary systems, providing dispatchable energy to compensate for the intermittency of wind and solar resources. However, challenges such as hydraulic vibrations, flow instabilities, and pressure pulsations pose significant threats to its reliability. This study proposes a biomimetic draft tube inspired by fin tubercles of humpback whales to alleviate swirling vortex structures and mitigate pressure pulsation. The eight tubercles are designed following a wavy generatrix and with a height of 0.3 times the inlet diameter of the draft tube. Three-dimensional detached Eddy simulations are employed to explore pressure pulsation, fluctuating energy, and turbulent structures for both the biomimetic and prototype draft tubes. The results show that, compared with the prototype Francis turbine, the biomimetic draft tube, with the middle protuberance height, effectively diminishes the amplitude of hydraulic force pulsations and the peak value shows a 28% decrease. The amplitudes of primary pressure pulsations show reductions of 47% in the conical section and 30% at the elbow of the draft tube, which is advantageous for avoiding fatigue failure. Moreover, the biomimetic draft tube effectively suppresses the formation and separation of swirling flow vortices, while wall-bounded annular vortices in the straight cone are disrupted and disintegrated by the biomimetic tubercles. However, the biomimetic draft tubes with low and high protuberance heights partially increase pressure pulsations and fail to control unsteady flow dynamics.

papers.title: Comparison of characteristics of unstable laminar and turbulent lean hydrogen–air flames
