The effects of parameters such as fiber orientation angle, damping coefficient, liquid volume coefficient, liquid velocity, and external excitation amplitude on the frequency responses of the FRC three-dimensional pipe were explored. To ensure the correctness of this analytical method, the present results were contrasted with the response curve obtained by the Runge–Kutta technique. Additionally, the nonlinear dynamic evolution of the pipelines, including the bifurcation and chaos, was further predicted using global bifurcation diagrams incorporated with phase diagrams and Poincaré diagrams, which provided a significant reference for the design of the pipes conveying the two-phase flow. Additionally, this study designed two additional NES attached on the pipeline structure to conduct the three-dimensional vibration control, analyzed their vibration reduction effect, and optimized the control parameters through genetic algorithm to improve their vibration control effect.

papers.title: Multi-objective optimization and analysis of rotor blades in Mars atmospheric environment based on surrogate model and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm
papers.abstract: The successful flight demonstration of Ingenuity in the Martian atmosphere offers novel insights for Mars exploration, where the rotor, as a core component of Mars drones, critically determines mission success. This study presents a surrogate model-based optimization method for rotor design, employing the clf5605 airfoil as a baseline for parametric modeling. To achieve efficient optimization, a sensitivity analysis was first conducted to identify high-impact design variables. A radial basis function neural network surrogate model was then constructed, coupled with a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm to derive optimal airfoil configurations. Results indicate that five key parameter categories—twist angle distribution, chord length distribution, thickness distribution, maximum curvature position, and maximum curvature (totaling 14 control parameters)—dominate rotor performance, with sensitivity coefficients of 0.914 (Earth) and 0.947 (Mars). The optimized airfoils outperformed the clf5605 baseline across all objectives: a 16.4% increase in the A1 figure of merit, a 10.03% boost in the A2 lift coefficient, a 10.00% reduction in A3 rotor mass, and an 8.62% decrease in A4 energy consumption. Aerodynamic tests of an A1 prototype under Earth conditions further validated the method's efficacy. This work systematically analyzes the influence of rotor parameters on aerodynamic performance and provides a practical framework for future rotor optimization in extraterrestrial environments.

papers.title: Impact of compositional gradient on gas–oil contact determination in nano-confined shale gas-condensate reservoirs
papers.abstract: Nano-confinement effects significantly alter fluid properties and influence gas–oil contact (GOC) prediction and multi-phase flow behavior in shale reservoirs. This study, for the first time, integrates nano-confinement effects into a compositional gradient model to determine the GOC. Results show that incorporating critical property shifts of fluid components in nanopores increases the GOC depth. The nano-confinement effect partially offsets compositional gradient changes caused by gravitational differentiation. Production above the GOC leads to a sharp decline in oil production and an increase in gas output due to gravitational differentiation. Conversely, production below the GOC enhances oil recovery while reducing gas production. The nano-confinement effect moderates the rate of compositional gradient variations, thereby mitigating these shifts. Additionally, it elevates the produced gas–oil ratio by reducing the dew point pressure, prolonging single-phase gas production. Validation using a real reservoir model confirms that accounting for both nano-confinement and compositional gradients improves predictive accuracy.

papers.title: Study on the bivariate distribution characteristics of extreme wave height and wave direction under different weather systems
papers.abstract: Significant wave height and wave direction are key parameters in ocean dynamics. Investigating their bivariate distribution characteristics under extreme conditions caused by different weather systems is of great significance for practical applications in ocean engineering. The present study analyzes these characteristics in the southern Yellow Sea and the northern East China Sea. Due to the clear trajectory records, extreme waves driven by tropical cyclones are identified through trajectory tracking and time matching. Due to the significant characteristics of the atmospheric circulation pattern, extreme waves driven by other weather systems are identified by the K-means clustering method. The results show that two types of extreme waves are derived, and the weather pattern characteristics indicate that their driving weather systems are cold surges and extratropical cyclones. By analyzing the temporal and directional characteristics of these waves, significant distribution differences are detected, confirming the rationality and necessity of the classification. For instance, the bivariate distribution characteristics of extreme wave height and wave direction under different weather systems may vary significantly. The main direction sector of extreme waves driven by the same weather system in the study region [e.g., the sector (240°–330°) of extreme waves driven by cold surges] can be derived, providing powerful support for the directional protection of ocean engineering.

papers.title: Theoretical solution of conical detonation waves with chemical equilibrium and variable specific heat
papers.abstract: To advance the design of conical oblique detonation engines, this study develops a rapid and accurate method for predicting wave angles and post-wave parameters. Existing theoretical models for conical oblique detonation waves are limited by simplified heat release assumptions, restricted accuracy, or high computational costs. This work addresses these limitations by solving the Taylor–Maccoll equations integrated with chemical equilibrium calculations, incorporating variable specific heat effects induced by hypersonic inflow. The proposed method achieves enhanced accuracy under both cold and heated conditions (wave angle errors of 0.001% and 0.3%, respectively) while maintaining computational efficiency. Validation against numerical simulations and experimental data confirms the method's reliability. Analysis of detonation polar curves reveals that the stationary range of conical detonation waves is narrower and weaker than that of planar counterparts at identical geometric angles. The minimum detonation Mach number for conical configurations exhibits an inverted J-shaped distribution, with the inflow Mach number dominating stationary ranges. At fixed cone angles, the detonation wave angle decreases with rising inflow temperature or decreasing pressure and peaks near equivalence ratios slightly over 1. Furthermore, conical structures in oblique detonation engines simplify wall interaction dynamics and generate higher post-wave total pressure compared to planar configurations.

papers.title: Effect of hydrostatic pressure on air layer morphology in axisymmetric underwater vehicles
papers.abstract: Air layer drag reduction is a promising drag reduction technique, whereas the ventilation process demonstrates dependence on hydrostatic pressure. In this study, using a combination of experimental and numerical simulations, a numerical model was developed for air layer drag reduction on axisymmetric underwater vehicles. A systematic investigation was conducted on air layer evolution and flow field characteristics under hydrostatic pressure ranging from 0.1 to 3 MPa. The results indicate that when the volumetric flow rate is used to characterize ventilation rate, hydrostatic pressure exerts a weak influence on the air layer shape, while a distinct linear relationship is observed between the mass flow rate and the absolute pressure at the jet nozzle. It is noteworthy that an increase in hydrostatic pressure alters air density, thereby affecting momentum exchange between the air layer and the external flow. This causes the re-entrant flow that severs the continuous gas layer to shift upstream, resulting in a reduction in the coverage area of the gas layer. This research contributes to the design of air layer drag reduction systems for axisymmetric underwater vehicles operating at varying submersion depths.

papers.title: Header microstructure effects on hotspot cooling in microchannel heat sinks
papers.abstract: Among the microstructural parameters influencing hotspot cooling in microchannel heat sinks, the header design plays a particularly significant role in thermal management. This study conducted numerical simulations to investigate hotspot heat dissipation in pin-fin microchannel heat sinks with inlet and outlet header structures. A detailed analysis was performed on the temperature distribution, flow characteristic, and field synergy in pin-fin microchannel heat sinks with different header microstructures. Furthermore, the mechanisms by which these microstructures influence heat transfer in the hotspot region were investigated. The results indicate that, under varying header parameters, changes in the field synergy angle within the microchannels are consistent with variations in the convective heat transfer coefficient. Moreover, the header configuration with Mhead = 2 mm and Hhead = 0.55 mm yielded the lowest maximum temperature on the hotspot surface, reducing it by 6 K compared to the peak temperature observed among all cases. This study offers a new approach to mitigating the heat dissipation challenges associated with local hotspot.

papers.title: Unsteady shock wave behaviors in supersonic nozzle exit under varying over-expanded conditions
papers.abstract: To elucidate the unsteady shock-containing flow features in an over-expanded supersonic jet issuing from an axisymmetric nozzle, a comprehensive study combining schlieren visualization, pressure, and force/moment measurements was conducted at varying nozzle pressure ratios (NPRs). The resulting grayscale images were subsequently analyzed utilizing a multi-modal decomposition framework, including the randomized singular value decomposition-based proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and its quadruple reconstruction (QPOD), as well as dynamic mode decomposition. Under over-expanded conditions, two dominant unsteady mechanisms were identified: (1) large-scale, low-frequency (approximately Strouhal number (St) of 0.007) shock system migration and reciprocating oscillation; and (2) relatively high-frequency (St of around 0.023) shear layer mixing, corresponding to the Kelvin–Helmholtz instability. POD analysis revealed descending energy ratios distinguishing these behaviors, where the shock migration exhibits a linear variation without a characteristic frequency, while its oscillation manifests as a distinct periodic feature. The QPOD results indicate that the shear layer instability significantly contributes to unsteady energy, influencing the fluctuation of nozzle forces. Despite symmetric exit flow in schlieren images, unsteady circumferential non-uniformities induce off-axis forces. Statistical and modal analysis shows that the flow unsteadiness grossly enhanced with decreasing of NPR, while the characteristic frequencies remain essentially consistent. Specifically, near NPRs transitioning from oblique shocks to Mach disk, the nonlinear coupling results in the “frequency locking” phenomena.

papers.title: Heat transfer enhancement in a square cavity using ternary nanofluid
papers.abstract: This study considers natural convection heat transfer in a permeable cavity using ternary nanoparticles. The primary objective of adopting ternary nanoparticles is to enhance the thermal conductivity of a regular base fluid. It is also examined how thermal radiation and heat generation affect the thermal performance of a fluid in a cavity. The proposed model is solved using the finite difference method, and simulations are conducted using MATLAB software. It is observed that the heat transfer in a cavity can be enhanced by replacing the conventional fluid with ternary nanofluid. Furthermore, the amount of heat transferred is relatively low when the right wall is maintained at a constant temperature (ϵ=0); however, it increases when ϵ>0.

papers.title: The asymptotic evolution of nanoparticles due to Brownian coagulation in the temporal mixing layer with average kernel method and iterative direct numerical simulation
papers.abstract: This study investigates the long-term evolution of nanoparticles in a two-dimensional temporal mixing layer using direct numerical simulation and the average kernel method. Focusing on two-vortex interactions, we analyze the transient non-equilibrium effects of vortex breakdown and turbulence intermittency on particle distribution. The results indicate that nanoparticle coagulation process closely follows the flow field due to low Stokes numbers, with coagulation significantly altering the amplitude of particle moments. As the flow transitions to Couette flow, nanoparticles exhibit asymptotic behavior consistent with zero-dimensional models. The average kernel method demonstrates computational efficiency comparable to Taylor-series expansion method of moments while maintaining accuracy.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network based on the finite volume method for solving forward and inverse problems
papers.abstract: The physics-informed neural network (PINN) is a promising approach in scientific computing. However, PINNs still face significant challenges, including high training costs, weak physical constraints, and difficulties in handling multi-scale problems. To address these challenges, this paper presents a PINN based on the finite volume method (FVM), referred to as FVM-PINN. FVM-PINN replaces the partial differential equations in the loss function with discretized equations derived using the FVM. Since the discretized equations exclude derivative terms and enforce conservation principles at more collocation points, FVM-PINN avoids the computationally intensive automatic differentiation operations in the complex computational graph and also imposes more rigorous physical constraints in the loss function. To demonstrate the performance of FVM-PINN, the forward and inverse problems of lid-driven square cavity flow are studied. The results show that FVM-PINN achieves a higher accuracy than PINN while requiring only one-tenth of the training time. Notably, it can predict the subtle, multi-scale behavior of lid-driven square cavity flow at higher Reynolds numbers, which outperforms PINN. This study also investigates the influence of different discretization schemes on the performance of FVM-PINN. It is shown that the schemes based on more physically rational profile assumptions and involving more surrounding points enhance the model's compliance with physical constraints, thereby improving the model's convergence performance and prediction accuracy. Additionally, the accuracy of the discretization schemes is also important for the accuracy of the model. These findings provide the guidelines for selecting appropriate discretization schemes when constructing the loss function of FVM-PINN for different flow problems.

papers.title: Modeling heat loss correction effects in large eddy simulation of swirl-stabilized flame with simplified reaction mechanisms
papers.abstract: We propose a non-adiabatic correction model for large eddy simulation (LES) of turbulent premixed and partially premixed combustion with simplified chemical mechanisms. The heat loss correction is incorporated by scaling the source term in the filtered species mass fraction and energy transport equations, ensuring that the correct flame propagation speed is recovered under non-adiabatic conditions. The correction factor is tabulated as a function of the equivalence ratio and the normalized enthalpy defect, based on simulations of freely propagating premixed flames. Under non-adiabatic conditions, the simplified mechanisms mispredict the flame speed if no heat loss correction is applied. For a two-step mechanism, the correction factor increases with the extent of heat loss and deviation from stoichiometry. We have evaluated the proposed non-adiabatic correction model a posteriori in LES of a swirl-stabilized premixed CH4-air flame under different mass flow rates and equivalence ratios using experimentally measured thermal boundary conditions. The correction model was observed to improve the predicted flame angle and/or height across all test conditions. This improvement is more significant under conditions of higher mass flow rates and greater deviations from stoichiometry, where neglecting the heat loss correction also mispredicts the flame shape. Additionally, we have found that neglecting the heat loss correction causes the flame root to stabilize further upstream and reduces the oscillations in the flame surface area in LES. These results demonstrate the importance of the heat loss correction when using simplified chemistry for LES of practical swirl-stabilized combustors.

papers.title: Turbulent mixing dynamics of under-expanded hydrogen jets in propulsion systems
papers.abstract: Underexpanded jets are present in various engineering applications; in recent years, they have gained special attention because of the development of gas-fueled propulsion systems. In these apparatuses, the direct injection of fuels such as hydrogen in innovative low-emission engines' chambers induces turbulent under-expanded jets. In this study, we performed high-fidelity large eddy simulations of under-expanded hydrogen jets to investigate mixing characteristics and provide valuable insights for developing injectors suitable for hydrogen and, more generally, gaseous-fueled propulsion systems. We initially assessed the method's accuracy, evaluating the convergence and uncertainty of the numerical results and validating them against experimental particle image velocimetry and Schlieren data. The simulated jets, the Mach disk dimensions, and the resulting velocity field align closely with the experimental observations. Then, we analyzed the jet structure for pressure ratios of 4 to 25 and examined the effects of the geometrical configuration of the nozzle on the characteristics of the air-fuel mixture obtained. We compared the jets resulting from a round-hole nozzle with annular ones resembling outward-opening injectors.

papers.title: Interfacial entanglement-induced time-dependent solidification of polymeric fluids
papers.abstract: The structure of polymers at solid interfaces evolves over time, but the corresponding changes in their rheological properties remain poorly understood. Here, using a home-built quartz tuning fork atomic force microscope-based nano-rheometer, we directly measure the time-dependent viscoelasticity of the interfacial fluid. The bottommost layer, closest to the substrate, undergoes solidification over 10 h, exhibiting an approximately fivefold increase in storage modulus and a twofold increase in loss modulus. This arises from interfacial entanglement due to the strong binding of polymers to the solid surface, driven by solid-wall attractive interactions. In contrast, within the second and third layers, the storage modulus remains nearly constant over time, while the loss modulus shows approximately twofold increase. In this region, unlike the strongly bound first layer, entropic repulsion dominates, allowing the material to behave fluid-like while becoming increasingly viscous. Notably, as the first layer, where interfacial entanglement occurs, undergoes solidification, the flow boundary for interfacial fluid flow shifts upward away from the substrate, resulting in a negative slip length. This highlights the critical role of nanoscale interfacial structure and properties in governing macroscopic flow behavior.

papers.title: Numerical investigations of chamber floor ports system
papers.abstract: The dynamically balanced systems are widely used in high-head locks. However, due to numerous branch culverts and diversion points, the structure of the system is highly complex. To address this problem, this paper, inspired by the German pressure chamber system, proposes a new leveling system—the Chamber Floor Ports system. The new system is investigated numerically using a “hybrid model” approach that combines a full-scale Computational Fluid Dynamics model with a local generalization model. The study shows that vortices induce transverse asymmetric (Q_dev < 1) outflow of ports near the chamber center in the sections e and b, creating uneven jet distributions and strong transverse forces. In contrast, the terminal ports of sections e and b and all of sections a and f experience minimal vortex influence, maintaining symmetric outflow (Q_dev ≈ 1) with correspondingly smaller transverse forces. The outflow in section e is symmetric (Q_dev ≈ 1) to section b in the longitudinal direction, resulting in a small longitudinal force in the middle of the chamber where the ship is moored. The pressure distribution demonstrates vortex-induced pressure reduction in the center of the pressure chamber, causing poor outflow uniformity in sections e and b (Flow Nonuniformity Coefficient ∈ [0.8, 1] in sections e and b). The analysis shows that the longitudinal diffusion range of vortices increases quadratically with the increase in the velocity of the impinging jet due to the strong wall-effect. An empirical equation describing the longitudinal diffusion range of bounded vortices is then proposed based on this relationship.

papers.title: Synthesis of linear alkyl benzene sulfonic acid by gas–liquid sulfonation under annular flow pattern in the cross-shaped microreactor: Mass transfer model and reaction kinetics
papers.abstract: The synthesis of linear alkyl benzene sulfonic acid (LABSA) by gaseous SO3-sulfonated linear alkyl benzene (LAB) under annular flow in microreactors is limited by the lack of sufficient mass transfer model and reaction kinetics support, which hinders the understanding of gas–liquid micro-sulfonation process and the enhancement of LABSA yield. Therefore, the mass transfer model with chemical reaction is established to overcome this difficulty. First, the gas–liquid physical mass transfer mechanism is proposed in the cross-shaped microreactor based on the stretching deformation of liquid elements at the phase interface and small-scale eddies, and the gas–liquid physical mass transfer model is obtained by computational fluid dynamics. Then, the macroscopic reaction kinetics model of gas–liquid micro-sulfonation process is established, and the kinetic parameters are obtained combined with the experimental results. Finally, the chemical mass transfer model is constructed by integrating the physical mass transfer model with the reaction kinetic parameters. Studies show that SO3 absorption rate can reach 97% at 602.4–1168.5 mm of the microreactor. This study can guide SO3 concentration distribution in the microreactor and provide a theoretical basis for the length design of microreactors and the optimization of gas–liquid velocity conditions.

papers.title: Unveiling the frequency-dependent dynamics of acoustic radiation force on lipid-coated ultrasound bubbles
papers.abstract: Ultrasonic contrast agent bubbles are a good medium for particle manipulation due to their high acoustic contrast factor. As a kind of widely used acoustic contrast agent, the surface tension of lipid bubbles is complicated, so the solution of its oscillation is normally obtained numerically rather than analytically. Another issue is that the Gorkov's formula for acoustic radiation force (ARF) used for the manipulation of small particles do not apply to bubbles in some frequency ranges. In this paper, the analytical solution of the oscillation of lipid-coated bubbles excited by ultrasound of different frequencies is given, and the frequency dependent ARF of lipid bubbles is obtained theoretically and verified by experiments. The theory complements the widely used Gorkov force, addressing the limitation that Gorkov force is only applicable when the particle density and compressibility are similar to the medium. The results have theoretical significance for the biomedical application of lipid bubbles and may provide theoretical basis for particle manipulation, particularly for the emerging field of manipulating biological particles containing gas bubbles.

papers.title: Turbulence-driven shock wave enhancement in detonation engines through obstacle design across hydrogen, acetylene, and kerosene
papers.abstract: Pre-detonators serve as preferred shock initiators in aerospace applications, particularly when prioritizing power and weight over direct initiation with substantial energy demands. Strategically positioned obstacles within pulse detonation engines play a crucial role in shortening shock generation time while ensuring unimpeded blast passage. Enhanced turbulence within the duct contributes significantly to achieving elevated temperature, pressure, and velocity levels, resulting in more robust shock waves, particularly at heightened equivalence ratios. Accordingly, this study delves into the numerical investigation of hydrogen-oxygen, acetylene-oxygen, and kerosene-oxygen couples in two-dimensional configurations. The investigation encompasses obstacle heights ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 mm within tubes, evaluated at equivalence ratios of 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 under identical initial conditions. The numerical analysis discerns variations in pressure, temperature, and velocity parameters induced by diverse fuels and obstacle ratios from shock wave inception to tube exit. Within our designed Ø10 × 210 mm pre-detonator, acetylene and hydrogen were observed to generate shock waves approximately 20 mm from the tube inlet. Specifically, hydrogen demonstrated the highest velocity among all fuel-oxygen mixtures, registering 1672.64 m/s at a 0.5 mm barrier height and 0.5 equivalence ratio. Acetylene at a 1.5 mm obstacle height and 1.0 equivalence ratio exhibited a peak average flame temperature of 8940 K. For kerosene, escalating obstacle heights at 0.5 and 1.0 equivalence ratios led to amplified temperature, pressure, and velocity values. These findings underscore the importance of tailoring blockage ratio and equivalence ratio levels, especially for highly reactive fuels like hydrogen, to optimize shock wave performance in pre-detonator applications.

papers.title: Comparison of two-dimensional wavelets techniques for variable-order time fractional Regularized Long Wave Burgers equation representing propagation of surface water wave in a channel
papers.abstract: This paper presents novel computational approaches for the numerical solution of the variable-order time fractional Regularized Long Wave Burgers (RLW-Burgers) equation based on two-dimensional wavelets. By employing the shifted Legendre, Euler, and Gegenbauer wavelets basis for the function approximation, alongside the operational matrices together with collocation points, the variable-order time fractional RLW-Burgers equation is transformed into a system of algebraic equations. In order to verify and validate our results obtained by the two-dimensional wavelets method, we also present the spectral collocation method (SCM) for solving this equation. The SCM is based on the shifted Legendre Gauss–Lobatto collocation (SL-GL-C) and shifted Chebyshev Gauss–Radau collocation (SC-GR-C) methods. The results obtained by the two-dimensional wavelets method using various wavelets have been compared with the results obtained by SCM. To comprehensively evaluate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed two-dimensional wavelet-based approach, we employ the well-known spectral collocation method (SCM) as a benchmark for comparison. This benchmarking allows for a systematic assessment of the relative performance of both methodologies. A thorough comparison of the proposed wavelet approach and SCM is carried out over a wide range of test cases, notably those requiring complicated variable-order fractional dynamics. The findings of this research clearly demonstrate that the proposed wavelet-based strategy consistently outperforms other methods in terms of numerical accuracy, effectiveness, and moderate computational cost. These results showcase the robustness and practical effectiveness of our strategy, especially when dealing with challenging problems that may pose difficulties for existing spectral methods. Furthermore, several useful theorems are explored rigorously to assess the convergence and error estimation of the two-dimensional wavelets method. Finally, several numerical examples are provided to validate the computational efficiency and demonstrate the practical applicability of this proposed numerical approach.

papers.title: Effects of autoignition mode induced by periodic thermal stratification on deflagration-to-detonation transition
papers.abstract: In this study, the partially stirred reactor model is utilized to simulate the turbulent–chemical interactions involved in deflagration-to-detonation transition (DDT). Jet-A/air is used as the reactant to simulate flame propagation within an inhomogeneous temperature field with periodic thermal stratification. The results reveal that autoignition induced by periodic thermal stratification plays a crucial role in the DDT. Two autoignition modes are identified: diffusion autoignition, driven by molecular thermal diffusion, and critical autoignition, triggered by shock waves inducing new hot kernels. The occurrence of autoignition considerably increases the flame surface area, expediting the propagation of deflagration flame and shortening the time until DDT onset. By varying the amplitude and wavelength, the characteristics of periodic thermal stratification are adjusted. At appropriate amplitudes, periodic thermal stratification notably promotes DDT, but excessive amplitude leads to multiple autoignition kernels forming simultaneously, hindering the DDT onset. A reduction in wavelength increases the number of diffusion autoignition kernels, delaying DDT onset compared to cases with larger wavelengths. Additionally, detonation wave decoupling is caused by the detonation wave being diffraction by obstacles and the effects of thermal stratification. An analysis of the decoupled detonation and its subsequent re-initiation confirm a shock–detonation re-initiation mode.

papers.title: Experimental investigation on flow-induced vibration suppression by drag-reducing polymers
papers.abstract: The polymer drag reduction in turbulent flow has been extensively studied for decades, with both commercial applications and fundamental implications. It is widely acknowledged within the scientific community that polymers primarily act by suppressing turbulent fluctuations, thereby significantly reducing flow resistance. Thus, the present work explored the potential of drag-reducing polymers to suppress flow-induced vibration by measuring the acceleration level of the fixed outer cylinder in a concentric rotor device. Maximum vibration suppression (Δ) of 7.54 dB and maximum drag reduction of 41.88% were achieved. The effects of Reynolds number (Re), polymer concentration, and molecular weight on the vibration suppression level and the time-dependent decay were all investigated. A distinct peak in vibration suppression level when Re = 75 990 was observed across all tested cases, attributed to the intrinsic properties of the flow-induced vibration in the rotor device. The vibration suppression, together with the drag reduction, decayed over time due to mechanical scission, with the Kohlrausch–Williams–Watt function quantitatively modeling the temporal behavior effectively. Notably, the vibration suppression diminished more slowly than the corresponding drag reduction. Moreover, solutions with the highest concentration or the largest molecular weight exhibited the best vibration suppression and drag reduction efficiency under both the successively increasing Re testing and the degradation testing. This dual suppression effect highlights the potential of drag-reducing polymers in simultaneously mitigating flow-induced vibration and energy loss.

papers.title: Singular solution of the Navier–Stokes equation for plane Poiseuille flow
papers.abstract: In previous studies, experiments and numerical simulations have shown that the transition to turbulence depends on both the Reynolds number and the magnitude of disturbances. However, the underlying physical mechanisms driving this phenomenon are still poorly understood. In this study, we analyzed the solution of the Navier–Stokes equation for plane Poiseuille flow, with a particular focus on the behavior of instantaneous velocity under disturbance effects. For the first time, we demonstrate how the interaction between the base flow and disturbance evolves to produce a point in instantaneous velocity where the Laplace term (viscous term) equals zero. Subsequently, a rigorous analysis is conducted on the solution of the Navier–Stokes equation at the critical condition of zero Laplace term, revealing that it constitutes a physical singularity of the equation. The instability of flow at singularity leads to the formation of negative velocity spikes in the instantaneous velocity. The theoretical results are compared against experimental data, yielding qualitative agreement that aligns with the simulation results reported in existing literature. The appearance of singularities and the generation of turbulence lie on the streamwise extension and compression of fluid elements. The research results indicate that although the Navier–Stokes equation may have a unique solution in theory for transitional and turbulent flows, this solution lacks global smoothness due to the non-differentiability at singularities. In addition, based on the vorticity transport equation, we have demonstrated that singularity is necessary within the flow field when turbulence is generated. Finally, it is elucidated that the conserved soliton-like coherent structure observed in transitional flows arises from the negative velocity spike.

papers.title: The effect of induced flow on the water wave skewness
papers.abstract: Nonlinear wave-induced perturbations are discussed within the framework of the second-order theory. Due to the slow attenuation of the long perturbations with depth, they modulate motions beneath surface waves down to the bottom and can strongly affect the wave statistics. The disturbance which corresponds to the second harmonic, at a sufficient depth, inverses the phase, thereby qualitatively changing the shape of individual waves. The skewness coefficients of the surface displacement and the bottom pressure fluctuations are considered. It is shown that the bottom pressure skewness may have different signs and magnitudes depending on the water depth and the configuration of nonlinear wave groups that compose the wave field. The effect on the surface displacement skewness is much weaker. Mechanisms leading to strong deviation of the skewness coefficient from the nonlinear Stokes wave theory are discussed.

papers.title: On the aeroacoustic characteristics of a plunging airfoil
papers.abstract: The aeroacoustic characteristics of a two-dimensional (2D) plunging SD7003 airfoil at a Reynolds number of 10 000 are investigated using direct numerical simulations (DNS) based on an in-house 2D high-fidelity compressible Navier–Stokes solver. The plunging frequency is fixed as 1.25, while the Mach number is varied between 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3, denoted as M1, M2, and M3, respectively. The mean and root mean square values of the surface pressure coefficients at M3 are substantially different from those at M1 and M2, which is connected with the leading edge (LE) shear layer evolutions. Surface pressure fluctuations are found to be the dominant noise sources for all three Mach numbers. For the second harmonic (2fo), the airfoil is no longer acoustically compact for these three cases. This results in a sound pressure magnitude scaling different from M2.5. In particular, the power spectral magnitude and phase angle of the surface pressure jump (Δp) between the suction and pressure sides of M3 show a large magnitude near the trailing edge and a less destructive phase distribution near the LE, respectively. To enable rapid acoustic predictions, a compact linear model is developed by combining the Theodorsen model and Ffowcs Williams–Hawkings acoustic analogy, showing good agreement with DNS results.

papers.title: Aqueous humor outflow and intraocular drug transport through trabecular and uveoscleral pathways
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting the temporal and spatial distribution of intraocular drugs to enhance anti-glaucoma treatment efficacy remains a significant challenge in clinical ophthalmology. Developing more precise numerical models of intraocular drug transport holds substantial clinical value. This study establishes a model of intraocular drug transport, which includes the trabecular meshwork (TM), collector channels (CC), and uveoscleral outflow pathway, and analyzes the parameters affecting aqueous humor (AH) outflow and the impact of the uveoscleral pathway on drug transport. Results indicate that the uveoscleral pathway influences AH outflow, with its porous media significantly impeding drug clearance, leading to drug accumulation in the anterior chamber and higher concentrations in the TM. A reduction in TM porosity or the number of CC hinders drug transport to varying extents, increasing peak drug concentration at TM targets by 11.27% and 12.8%, respectively. Furthermore, neglecting the uveoscleral pathway may result in an 10.93% underestimation of TM drug concentration. This study provides insight into the pathways involved in anti-glaucoma drug transport, contributing to the optimization of drug design for improved therapeutic outcomes.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification and parameter assimilation of the shear stress transport model for supersonic nozzle separated flow
papers.abstract: To address the severe limitation of turbulence model uncertainty on the accuracy of numerical reconstruction of supersonic nozzle separation flow fields, this study conducts uncertainty quantification and parameter assimilation of the shear stress transport (SST) model. A high precision flow field surrogate model based on principal component analysis and deep neural networks (PCA-DNN) is used. Compared with direct DNN and second-order polynomial chaos expansion, the constructed PCA-DNN surrogate reduces root mean square error by 33.87% and 58.53%, respectively, and significantly improves DNN modeling efficiency, providing a solid foundation for uncertainty quantification and parameter assimilation. Uncertainty quantification is performed using 677 Latin hypercube sampled SST model parameters cases, revealing that parameters σω2 and β2 dominate uncertainty contributions. Shock location prediction deviation is the dominant mechanism driving downstream uncertainty propagation, causing maximum impulse deviations of up to 88.8% for free shock separation (FSS) and 15.3% for restricted shock separation (RSS). Furthermore, an engineering optimization approach is explored to improve the SST model's prediction of the pressure ratio for the FSS-to-RSS transition based on β*. Finally, a high-accuracy numerical flow field reconstruction framework based on parameter assimilation is established. Parameter assimilation driven by wall pressure data achieves a reduction of wall pressure error sum of squares by 94.14% (FSS) and 76.85% (RSS) within only 2 to 6 particle swarm optimization incremental iterations, along with global correction of the shock system, effectively suppressing the origin of flow field uncertainty.

papers.title: Colliding gravity currents in a stratified environment
papers.abstract: This study examines the collision of two counterflowing gravity currents (GCs) in a stratified environment using large-eddy simulation. A half-depth lock-exchange configuration with linearly stratified ambient fluid is used to study symmetric collision (i.e., GCs with the same densities and heights). Numerical experiments on collision of both subcritical and supercritical GCs are performed for weak and strong stratification. The focus is on the investigation of both collision and post-collision phases, with emphasis on the height and the vertical velocity of the collided fluid, the bore velocity during the post-collision phase, and the mixing and its efficiency. The results indicate that stronger stratification causes the GCs to become subcritical and decelerate before collision. In contrast, for weaker stratification, GCs become supercritical and the collision resembles that in a non-stratified environment. Subcritical collision is characterized by oscillatory vertical motion of the collided fluid, which can suppress bore formation. Supercritical collision is distinguished by clearly defined phases and bore development during the post-collision phase, similar to that in a non-stratified environment. The qualitative difference between the collision of subcritical and supercritical GCs is due to the occurrence of internal waves, which emerge during GC propagation before collision and interfere in the middle of the tank, determining collision dynamics. Mixing during collision is also affected by stratification strength. While stronger stratification suppresses turbulence and mixing, weaker stratification enhances turbulence and broadens the mixing region, leading to higher mixing with reduced mixing efficiency.

papers.title: Long-lasting ultra-high-temperature salt-resistant filtration control agents based on nano-hydrophobic composites
papers.abstract: With advancements in drilling technology, oil and gas drilling is increasingly extending into ultra-deep and extra-deep wells. Consequently, the drilling environment is becoming more complex. High-temperature and high-salinity formations pose severe challenges, often causing excessive filtration loss in drilling fluids. These filtration losses can lead to critical safety hazards, including severe leakage and borehole instability. Therefore, elucidating the failure mechanisms of drilling fluids under extreme conditions and developing targeted additives are essential for ensuring operational success. To address these technical challenges, a novel nano-composite filtration control agent was synthesized via emulsion polymerization by incorporating hydrophobically modified titanium dioxide nanoparticles into a polymer system comprising 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropane sulfonic acid, dimethyl diallyl ammonium chloride, N-vinyl-2-pyrrolidinone, and N, N-dimethylacrylamide, namely, ANDT-70 (2-acrylamido-2-methylpropane sulfonic acid, N-vinyl-2-pyrrolidinone, N,N-dimethylacrylamide, dimethyl diallyl ammonium chloride, and titanium dioxide nanoparticles). The performance and filtration control mechanism of ANDT-70 were evaluated through filtration loss tests, temperature and salt resistance tests, and microscopic analysis using scanning electron microscopy and transmission electron microscopy. The results demonstrated that the incorporation of hydrophobically modified titanium dioxide significantly enhanced the thermal stability of ANDT-70 and improved the dispersion of bentonite. Consequently, ANDT-70 was confirmed to exhibit superior resistance to high-temperature and high-salinity environments. Bentonite slurry containing 2.0% ANDT-70 was aged at 260 °C for 16 h, resulting in an American Petroleum Institute (Abbreviation: API) filtration loss of only 10.2 ml with negligible viscosity change. Furthermore, even after 72 h of aging at 260 °C, the bentonite slurry with ANDT-70 effectively withstood the effects of saturated sodium salt and 5% calcium salt. Thus, this study provides valuable insights for the future development of nano-composite drilling fluid filtration control agents designed for high-temperature and high-salinity environments.

papers.title: A novel fractal Langmuir and machine learning framework for precise prediction of CH4/CO2 adsorption in heterogeneous shale: Implications for CO2 sequestration
papers.abstract: Capturing the adsorption behavior of gases in heterogeneous shale is crucial for CH4 enhanced recovery and CO2 geological sequestration. This study derives a fractal Langmuir adsorption model that incorporates energy heterogeneity across pore sizes to characterize CH4 and CO2 adsorption in real shale. The results show that the fractal Langmuir model provides accurate fitting and high stability, effectively calculating gas adsorption amounts within various shale pore size ranges. It reveals that CH4 and CO2 are primarily adsorbed in micropores, with adsorption amounts influenced by the interplay of pore quantity and adsorption energy. In mesopores and macropores, gas predominantly exists in a free state, and the volume of free gas is dependent on pore volume. Additionally, a variance-based sensitivity analysis was applied to quantitatively assess the impact of shale pore structure (minimum pore diameter, λmin; maximum pore diameter, λmax; and porosity) on gas adsorption. The analysis demonstrates that λmin has the greatest effect on adsorption, followed by porosity, while λmax exerts a lesser influence. Increased porosity significantly enhances the adsorption capacity of shale for both CH4 and CO2. Finally, to overcome the physical assumptions of the fractal Langmuir model, a Convolutional Neural Networks-Gaussian Process Regression machine learning framework was developed that directly uses the N2 adsorption–desorption curve at 77 K as input to predict CH4/CO2 adsorption in shale, achieving comparable accuracy.

papers.title: Liquid accumulation in a horizontal–vertical pipe system based on the interface tracking method
papers.abstract: During valve opening in gas–liquid two-phase pipeline systems, fluid accumulation at local low points may trigger upstream cavitation, leading to complex air–water interface dynamics and pressure oscillations. To explore the underlying mechanisms, Computational Fluid Dynamics simulations based on an interface-tracking method were conducted under varying inlet flow rates, gas volume fractions, and liquid accumulation conditions, and their effects on pipeline pressure characteristics were systematically analyzed. This study investigates the gas–liquid two-phase flow behavior in a downstream pipeline–riser system under assumed operating conditions representative of a helical axial-flow gas–liquid transport unit, aiming to provide theoretical support and boundary condition references for future experimental research on such spiral transport devices. To validate the numerical model, a rapid water-filling process involving a retained air pocket in a horizontal pipeline was simulated, confirming the suitability of the two-dimensional Volume of Fluid model. The investigation addressed cavitation formation, pressure distribution, and interface evolution, with emphasis on pressure and differential pressure variations at key locations under different operating conditions. Results show that liquid blockage induces substantial flow instability. At high flow rates and low gas fractions, large pressure fluctuations and peak pressures occur near the inlet. In contrast, at low flow rates, repeated rupture and reformation of the interface boundary of the liquid plug induce sustained pressure pulsations. Transient pressure fluctuations associated with liquid film breakage and interface evolution are also captured, and the overall trend of mean pipeline pressure is analyzed. These findings enhance the understanding of two-phase flow transients and offer theoretical guidance for the design and stable operation of gas–liquid transport systems.

papers.title: Thermo-Elasto-Hydro-Dynamic model on variable preload tilting-pad journal bearing
papers.abstract: To rapidly adjust the real-time performance of tilting-pad journal bearings (TPJBs), a novel variable preload TPJB is proposed, and its Thermo-Elasto-Hydro-Dynamic (TEHD) lubrication model with consideration of the variable preload factor is developed. Taking the six-pad TPJBs for the high-pressure rotor in a 1000 MW steam turbine as the object, a comparative study is conducted on the performance of TPJBs with and without considering the TEHD lubrication effect, which indicates that the influence of TEHD lubrication needs to be fully considered in the case of preload variation, and the maximum calculation errors with the non-considering TEHD lubrication effect can be up to 88.5%. When the preload factor increases from 0.1 to 0.3, the load capacity of TPJBs is increased by approximately 50%. As the preload factor of the upper pads (both pad-2 and pad-6) changes, it can effectively improve the dynamic characteristic coefficients of TPJBs. By increasing the preload factor of secondary load-bearing pads (both pad-3 and pad-5) from 0.1 to 0.3, the oil film pressure, temperature, and deformation of the main load-bearing pad have increased about 90%, 10%, and 45%, respectively. The research results are aimed at the flexible and rapid adjustment of preload TPJBs.

papers.title: Why do solid particles form quadric hypersurfaces in thermovibrational fluid flow?
papers.abstract: Recent experiments conducted in space have confirmed the discovery of a new category of inertial particle attractors in fluid flow, originally predicted (a decade ago) on the basis of numerical simulations. Although the underlying physical mechanism have been clarified over the years through a modeling hierarchy based on a wide range of model types, spanning from basic to intricate, where different processes were activated or deactivated, characterization of these phenomena under a precise “geometrical” perspective is still missing due to the inherent difficulties related to any attempt to unveil the underlying (hidden) “mathematical order.” This study represents the first attempt to fill this gap. In particular, in our endeavor to meet this objective, the discussion is articulated along two different threads, that is, (1) creating the right connections between the emerging particle formations and the geometry of quadratic surfaces, which are generally represented as level sets of second-degree polynomial expressions, and (2) defining the affine and/or projective transformations that can be used to turn one surface into another as the physical conditions that can produce them are varied; thereby, a general mathematical framework is defined that can encapsulate in a single treatment the outcomes of Computational Fluid Dynamics simulations based on a hybrid Eulerian–Lagrangian approach and the idealized mathematical shapes mimicking the particle formations obtained accordingly. The resulting framework not only represents a more fundamental description of this subject than what preceded it but also provides a rich context for a more rational and thorough characterization of these phenomena, thereby giving this discovery a firm mathematical grounding.

papers.title: A train of burst vortices and a coexisting large cumulative vortex induced by a single-dielectric-barrier-discharge plasma actuator in burst mode
papers.abstract: The generation and evolution of heated vortex structures induced by a single-dielectric-barrier-discharge plasma actuator under burst-mode actuation are investigated in initially quiescent air using a fourth-order flux reconstruction scheme. In each burst cycle, a burst vortex forms by the rolling up of the head of the hot wall jet generated by the actuator. The burst vortex travels faster in the streamwise direction than in the wall-normal direction because it receives streamwise-dominant momentum injected by the actuator and gains additional acceleration from the induced velocity field of its adjacent downstream burst vortex. Burst vortices generated from different burst cycles ultimately merge downstream to form a large cumulative vortex, a phenomenon not previously documented. This cumulative vortex carries significantly more momentum, heat, and vorticity than the burst vortices and is believed to play a critical role in flow control. Since the cumulative vortex does not directly receive the streamwise-dominant momentum injected by the actuator, its motion shows no directional preference and its speeds in the streamwise and wall-normal directions are comparable. The burst frequency controls the spacing between adjacent burst vortices and, thereby, influences their interaction, resulting in faster streamwise motion as the burst frequency increases. However, it does not affect the size or motion of the cumulative vortex because the actuator's effective actuation duration remains unchanged. In comparison, increasing the duty-cycle ratio prolongs the actuation duration per burst cycle, generating larger vortices that carry more momentum, heat, and vorticity and move faster in both directions. These findings highlight the multi-scale vortex system generated by burst-mode actuation, which is significant for achieving more effective plasma-based flow control.

papers.title: Effects of hinge properties on the hydroelastic response of an interconnected very large floating structure under wave–current interactions
papers.abstract: Based on the discrete-module-beam (DMB) method and stiffness approximation method (SAM), this paper establishes a hydroelastic model for interconnected very large floating structures (VLFS). The core of the DMB method involves discretizing VLFSs into multiple rigid modules, which are subsequently interconnected by multiple beam elements. To accurately model hinge connections between modules, the SAM is employed. Thus, the present study performs a hydroelastic analysis of the interconnected VLFS by coupling multi-body hydrodynamics, Euler–Bernoulli beam assumption, and hinge stiffness matrix. To ensure the accuracy of the proposed method, the validation is conducted based on existing data. Afterward, this paper analyzes the effects of hinge properties on the hydroelastic behavior of VLFSs under wave–current interactions, including the position, number, and stiffness. The results indicate that the hinge properties significantly influence the hydroelastic response of the VLFS. On the whole, the analytical methods and findings presented in the present study provide valuable insights into the practical engineering applications of VLFS.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic simulation and investigation on the pumping reliability of a mixed pumped-storage power station
papers.abstract: Mixed Pumped-Storage Power Stations (MPSPSs), transformed from cascade hydropower systems, are critical to improving grid flexibility amid increasing renewable energy penetration. However, during pumping operations, a hydrodynamic issue known as the pumping funnel, characterized by a rapid water level drop near the inlet or outlet, can severely impact system reliability. This study establishes dual hydrodynamic models (MIKE 21 and HEC-RAS) to analyze this phenomenon in the Lianghekou MPSPS (1200 MW total capacity), currently the largest MPSPS under construction in China. This study has developed a dual-index framework combining flow deviation and funnel hydrodynamics to evaluate pumping reliability. A pumping limit point based on a 5% flow deviation threshold, with baseline continuous pumping duration limited to 6.8 h, has been identified; and multi-scenario simulations have been applied to quantify the effects of inlet/outlet layout, conveyance capacity, and operational flow conditions. Notably, optimized layout and conveyance capacity improve pumping duration by 0.64 and 2.24 h, respectively. Qualitative analysis reveals that pumping reliability is sensitive to hydraulic design and boundary flow conditions and that proper engineering interventions can mitigate funnel formation. This work provides simulation-based evaluation methods and actionable guidance for the design and operation of large-scale MPSPSs in complex river basins.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of shock train characteristics in an annular isolator under incident shock waves and rotating backpropagation pressure wave
papers.abstract: To study the characteristics of shock train in the isolator of a rotating detonation ramjet engine, three-dimensional unsteady RANS simulations were conducted on annular isolators under the influence of uniform incoming flow and incident shock waves, respectively, with the effect of rotating detonation waves simulated by a rotating unsteady pressure exhibiting high-frequency and non-uniform features. Compared to uniform incoming flow, the shock train exhibits significant asymmetry under the influence of incident shock waves. The wall toward which the shock train is biased is directly affected by the wave system within the shock train. The mechanism analysis indicates that the shock train is biased toward the wall with higher pressure at the shock train's leading edge. The shock train's bias varies circumferentially, causing the backpropagation pressure wave propagating spirally upstream to exhibit circumferential fluctuations. During the backpropagation pressure wave propagating upstream, the propagation speed gradually decreases, and the shape evolves from shock wave to shock train. The shock train's leading edge oscillates periodically under the backpropagation pressure wave. Under uniform incoming flow, the oscillation range on the inner and outer walls is basically consistent. Compared to uniform incoming flow, under the influence of incident shock wave, the oscillation amplitude of the shock train's leading edge is smaller, with the most upstream position on the inner wall being further upstream, while on the outer wall, it is slightly further downstream. The dominant frequency of the wall pressure oscillation is consistent with the rotating frequency of the rotating backpressure.

papers.title: The effect of particle mass concentration on the motion characteristics of particles in a helical-bladed multiphase pump
papers.abstract: The helical-bladed multiphase pump demonstrates significant advantages in transporting complex media. However, the presence of solid particles complicates the fluid–structure interaction mechanism, posing challenges to studying solid–liquid two-phase flow within the pump. This research focuses on a self-developed three-stage helical-bladed multiphase pump, employing numerical simulation with experimental validation, to systematically investigate the effect of particle mass concentration (Cm = 1‰, 5‰, and 1%) on particle motion characteristics. The results indicate particle velocity distribution follows similar trends under different Cm conditions. In the impeller flow passage, the circumferential velocity of particles increases significantly while axial velocity changes marginally. Upon entering the guide vanes, circumferential velocity decreases, whereas axial velocity increases. The absolute velocity rises axially along each impeller stage but declines axially in each guide vane stage. As Cm increases, particle backflow intensifies, leading to aggravated flow blockage in the reflux zone at the first-stage impeller inlet. Under high-concentration conditions, particles aggregate into clusters within the flow passage, elevating collision probability. Particle distribution shifts from low-speed to medium-speed regions: dispersed at low Cm but concentrated toward medium-speed zones at medium-to-high Cm. Particle collision frequency rises with Cm, with increased proportions of collisions against the shroud and hub but decreased proportions against blades. The total particle–wall contact force escalates with higher Cm, with impeller-wall forces exceeding guide-vane-wall forces. In the guide vane region, contact forces distribute as blades > shroud > hub. These findings elucidate the kinetic characteristics of solid particles, providing a basis for the optimal design of multiphase pumps.

papers.title: Investigation on the dynamic characteristics of a droplet subjected to a divergent shock wave
papers.abstract: The present study numerically investigates the dynamic characteristics of a cylindrical droplet impinged by a divergent shock wave, focusing on deformation morphology, the onset of Kelvin–Helmholtz (K-H) instability, and global dynamics. Key features of droplet deformation, including general flattening, interface instabilities, and the formation and spanwise elongation of liquid ligaments, are captured and analyzed. Comparisons with the planar shock case indicate the significant role of shock wave curvature in droplet deformation. Ligaments form closer to the front stagnation point and experience further spanwise extension in the divergent shock case. Moreover, the inception location of the windward K-H instability is found to almost coincide with the windward fixed-point, which forms and migrates as a result of the combined effects of external and internal flows before resting. A theoretical analysis reveals that the initial location of the fixed-point coincides with the critical contact point of the transmitted shock. This location will move downstream with the increase in the shock curvature radius. This study is expected to provide new insights into the shock–droplet interaction problem, contributing to a better understanding of fuel atomization in supersonic propulsion systems.

papers.title: Advantages exploration and flowfields of waveriders with variable Mach numbers in hypersonic regime
papers.abstract: Variable-Mach-number waveriders (VMWs) were believed to perform well over a wide range of hypersonic velocities. However, comparisons with traditional fixed-Mach-number waveriders (FMWs) have not considered identical planforms and equal volumes. Accordingly, the alleged advantages of VMWs over a wide-speed range are not persuasive. In this study, the VMW configurations given leading-edge profiles were generated using the planform-customized waverider design method. Meanwhile, the FMW configurations featuring identical leading edges and equal volumes as the VMWs were also built to be compared. Computational fluid dynamics techniques are used to analyze the flowfields and calculate the aerodynamic forces of the equivalent configurations to explore whether wide-speed advantages truly exist for VMWs in the hypersonic regime. The results show that, compared with FMWs with identical planforms and equal volumes, VMWs offer no advantages in terms of the lift-to-drag ratio at hypersonic velocities. Moreover, the basis variable-Mach-number flowfields and therefore the caused change in waveriding surface merely influenced the longitudinal stability when the planform was fixed. Two preliminary explanations for this phenomenon are provided, and we hypothesize that traditional waveriders designed using a fixed-Mach-number flowfield achieve satisfactory wide-speed performance in the hypersonic regime. Consequently, improving the wide-speed performance for a waverider ought to focus on the sub-, trans-, and supersonic states, which dramatically deviate from the on-design state, instead of the hypersonic regime.

papers.title: Confined and focused electric fields induce array jet crosstalk suppression for multi-nozzle electrohydrodynamic printing
papers.abstract: Multi-nozzle electrohydrodynamic (EHD) printing is an efficient direct-writing technology that has significant advantages in the large-scale preparation of micrometer- and nanometer-scale arranged patterns. However, the non-uniform electric field between different nozzles causes obvious jet crosstalk or inconsistent injection during the printing process, which significantly affects the printing effect. In this paper, a new active control method is proposed to suppress array jet crosstalk by coupling the effect of electric field confinement and focusing, where the confinement electric field is generated by a ring-shaped electrode, and a focusing electric field is generated by a needle-shaped electrode. According to the simulation analysis and the experiments, the coupling effect of electric field confinement and focusing has obvious suppression on array jet crosstalk, and multi-nozzle electrospinning achieved less than 2% spacing deviation, compared to approximately 20% in the traditional electrospinning process. By rotating the print head by 36°, the line spacing was reduced to 80% of the nozzle spacing, and excellent printing quality could still be maintained using the method proposed in this paper. This novel method offers a promising solution for achieving high-precision, large-scale, and multi-nozzle EHD printing.

papers.title: Research on non-thermal flow field characteristics of a three-phase rotary arc plasma exciter in aero-engine combustor
papers.abstract: This paper describes the design of a three-phase rotary arc exciter based on the principle of plasma-assisted combustion and presents analysis on the operation characteristics of it. A dual-stage swirler and a three-phase arc exciter is integrated by mounting three needle electrodes on the internal surface of Venturi tube of the swirler uniformly. In this work, the arc development process was studied and the influence of discharge on main flow field was obtained. Moreover, the species and intensity of active particles generated by discharge were analyzed. It is found that the three-phase rotary arc exciter transits between two discharge mode due to variations of air flow rates. The application of three-phase rotating gliding arc discharge reduces the turbulent intensity. Plasma discharge of the exciter could generate excited-state nitrogen molecules N2(C3Π), oxygen molecules O2(a1Δg), and other reactive particles, which has been verified to be beneficial to combustion chemical reactions.

papers.title: Particle flow simulation on shear mechanical behaviors, energy evolution, and fracture responses of rough layered rock mass
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the mechanical properties and failure mechanisms of layered rock masses in direct shear tests. PFC2D (Particle Flow Code) model with dimensions of 100 × 100 mm was first established, and the fine-scale parameters were calibrated by the results of laboratory uniaxial tests on standard samples of rock-like materials of matrix and then conducted direct shear simulations in terms of various bedding inclinations (α = 15°–75°), joint roughness coefficients (JRC = 2–20), and initial normal stresses (σn = 1–4 MPa). The results show that the bedding inclination, the joint roughness coefficients (JRC), and the initial normal stress significantly impact the evolution mechanism of the cracks and instability-slip. With the increase in bedding inclination, JRC, and initial normal stress, the shear slipping shifts from interlayer-controlled to matrix-controlled. The inhibitory effect of the initial normal stress on shear slipping gradually shifts to a slow enhancement with increasing initial normal stress. Notably, the layered rock samples with high normal stress and JRC exhibit a significant pre-failure phase before shear slipping. The increasing bedding inclination inhibits the development and expansion of cracks along the layers, resulting in the morphology of shear failure surfaces to experience the evolution of “along layers shape – V-shape – arc-shape – linear shape.” As bedding inclination increases from 15° to 75°, the proportion of shear cracks initiating from joint surfaces decreases by 25%, 2%, 0%, and 1%, respectively; however, the proportion of tensile cracks initiating from matrix increases by 23%, 3%, 2%, and 3%. The interfacial transition zone can be observed in the displacement fields of the layered rock samples, and the direction of interfacial transition zone is consistent with the layers and deviates gradually with the increasing bedding inclination. With the increasing bedding inclination and JRC, numerous secondary cracks originate from the matrix, eventually connecting with the joint surfaces. Consequently, numerous discontinuous rock blocks are generated between the upper and lower plates, leading to a significantly increase in the area of the force chain missing zone. Furthermore, the stress-inducing effect of joint surfaces bulges is further enhanced. The findings will contribute to a better understanding of the mechanical responses and failure mechanisms of the rock mass with multiple parallel rough joint surfaces.

papers.title: Unsteady flow structures and noise characterization under stator skew in pump-jet propulsors
papers.abstract: This study explores how stator skew affects pump-jet propulsor (PJP) performance. A hybrid Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes/large eddy simulation strategy is utilized to analyze the flow, and the Ffowcs Williams–Hawkings equation is applied for noise calculation. First, the original PJP is examined and found that the stator's trailing edge vortex strongly affects the flow field's fluctuation. Next, different stator skews are examined, and it is observed that skew increases the flow speed around the blades, particularly the circumferential speed. This results in a larger rotor incidence angle and stronger fluctuations. It is also found that high skew generates strong vortices at the stator corner, which disrupt the rotor blade tip vortex and amplify flow field fluctuations. Finally, the impact of skew on noise is studied. Low skew is shown to reduce noise levels while discrete frequency features are maintained. High skew is associated with increased overall noise levels, especially broadband noise. In general, noise levels are found to rise as skew increases. This research provides a new method for reducing noise in PJPs.

papers.title: A subvoxel-level peak location method based on a simultaneous multiplicative algebraic reconstruction technique for tomography particle image velocimetry
papers.abstract: Tomographic particle image velocimetry reconstructs three-dimensional particle distributions in flow fields from multi-view two-dimensional images, but its accuracy is limited by discretization errors, particle elongation, and ghost particles. This paper proposes a subvoxel-level peak localization simultaneous multiplicative algebraic reconstruction technique (SPL-SMART) to optimize discretization errors and particle elongation. The method employs subvoxel resolution as the minimum unit for spatial discretization. By analyzing subvoxel regions around grid points to determine the peak positions of reconstructed Gaussian blobs, the reconstructed particles more closely resemble actual particles rather than Gaussian blobs with a particle size of 1–2 voxels. The reconstruction quality factor Q was employed to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm in terms of discretization errors, camera viewing angles, and particle concentration. Compared with other algorithms, the SPL-SMART algorithm has higher particle positioning accuracy. Discretization error was simulated by constraining the particle generation range. Under the conditions of a constraint range side length of 48 μm (accounting for 96% of the voxel edge length), a camera angle of 30° relative to the Z-axis, and a particle concentration of 0.05 particles per pixel (ppp), the SPL-SMART algorithm achieved 99.56% alignment accuracy of reconstructed intensity peaks with actual particle centers within the same voxel. Under the same conditions, the Inte-SMART algorithm achieved only 85.29% alignment accuracy. Under the condition of a particle concentration of 0.125 ppp, 83% of ghost particles were filtered out by removing particles with intensities below the maximum reconstruction intensity threshold.

papers.title: Modeling sinusoidal exhalation: An unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes-based approach for predicting breathing flow dynamics
papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of exhalation dynamics is essential in estimating infection rates. In this study, we analyzed the predictive capabilities of three Unsteady Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (URANS)-based turbulence models: Realizable k–ε, renormalization group (RNG) k–ε, and shear-stress transport (SST) k–ω for sinusoidal exhalation. The exhaled jet flow extends over a distance from the exhalation source, normalized by the exhalation source diameter, and was analyzed across the jet region. Furthermore, this region was divided into three sub-regions: near-field, transitional, and fully developed field for turbulence evaluation. These models were validated against time-resolved particle image velocimetry data and empirical measurements under quiescent ventilation conditions. Results from the centerline velocity decay profiles demonstrated that each model exhibited performance across the sub-regions of the exhaled jet. Using three performance metrics for quantitative validation, the RNG k–ε model demonstrated superior performance overall across the jet flow region. When sectioned into sub-regions, its performance is better in transitional and fully developed regions due to its enhanced strain-term formulation. Meanwhile, the SST k–ω model provides superior accuracy in near-wall shear and boundary–layer interactions. The Realizable k–ε model performs well in the transitional region but underperforms in the near-field and fully developed regions. These results advance the characterization of breath-generated flows, providing insights into airborne transmission dynamics that can inform the optimization of ventilation strategies and mitigation measures in indoor environments. Semi-empirical equations, derived using the best-performing region-specific URANS models, estimate centerline velocities during exhalation (0 < t < 2 s) in developed field regions.

papers.title: Numerical study of the motion of a microfiber near a floating microbubble
papers.abstract: Due to their high aspect ratios and neutral buoyancy characteristics, microfibers exhibit complex dynamic behavior during migration in water. This complex behavior significantly limits the efficiency with which they can be removed by air-flotation methods. During this study, a numerical model based on the lattice Boltzmann method was established to study the motion of a microfiber near a floating microbubble with the goal of discovering the mechanism that governs bubble-wake entrainment. The effects of four key factors—the bubble size, the microfiber length, the lateral distance between the microfiber and the microbubble, and the initial microfiber orientation—on the microfiber motion were analyzed. When there was a large difference between the sizes of the microfiber and the microbubble, a higher relative velocity caused the microfiber to rapidly slide along the bubble surface, while capillary pressure pushed it away. However, when the microfiber was slightly longer than the microbubble diameter, the microfiber was more likely to enter the bubble-wake region; thus, a stronger drafting force would act on the trailing microfiber. A smaller initial distance between the microfiber and the bubble's central axis leads to a more drastic change in the angular orientation of the microfiber. When the initial orientation angle ranges from 45° to 60°, the microfiber is strongly affected by the bubble wake. Specifically, a “strong wake entrainment” phenomenon was observed at 30°; in this phenomenon, the microfiber becomes trapped within the wake of the microbubble.

papers.title: Integrated aerodynamic optimization of diverterless supersonic inlet using full turbulence adjoint method
papers.abstract: Diverterless supersonic inlets (DSI) is the predominant system for supersonic aircraft below Mach 2, offering superior boundary layer displacement and stability margins. However, conventional discrete adjoint optimization frameworks relying on the constant eddy viscosity (CEV) assumption introduce significant gradient errors in turbulent flow sensitivity analysis, limiting performance refinement of DSI configurations characterized by shock-boundary layer interactions and separation phenomena. This study addresses this challenge through a novel discrete adjoint framework integrating upwind schemes and full turbulence adjoint modeling, enabling accurate gradient computation while maintaining numerical stability for high-speed flows. The method is applied to optimize an integrated DSI system encompassing compression bump, diffuser duct, and cowl lip geometries. Gradient validation against finite-difference results demonstrates improved convergence efficiency and sensitivity accuracy compared to CEV-based approaches. At Mach 1.8, the optimized DSI achieves shock-on-lip (SOL) conditions with 4.0% total pressure recovery improvement (0.914) and 64.2% reduction in distortion index (0.273). Off-design performance at Mach 0.6–0.9 maintains exceptional recovery coefficients (0.982/0.973), demonstrating multi-point operational robustness. The design simultaneously minimizes internal flow separation, enhances boundary layer control, and balances supersonic pressure recovery with sub/transonic efficiency. This work advances adjoint-based aerodynamic optimization by resolving CEV limitations in capturing viscous-inviscid interactions, establishing a pathway for next-generation DSI development.

papers.title: Coupled effects between shielding and gap resonance phenomena for vessel entering floating dock
papers.abstract: This study numerically investigates the coupled hydrodynamic phenomena that arise when a surface vessel enters a floating dock. A modified potential flow model is used to capture both the shielding effect and gap resonance between the vessel and dock side-walls. The concepts of primary and secondary responses are defined based on different wave angles. The whole process for a vessel entering dock is divided into pre-entry, entry, and post-entry. Numerical results reveal that during the pre-entry and entry phases, the shielding effect plays distinct roles depending on the incident wave angle, and in the post-entry phase, the shielding effect leads to a noticeable reduction in primary responses but results in an increase in the secondary responses. Dual-mode piston resonance is observed for the first time in a large-scale engineering structure due to the formulation of a “pseudo-three-body” system. With increasing channel width, numerical simulation found that a simultaneous reduction in both the shielding effect and the intensity of dual-mode gap resonance. From the industry engineering perspective, the pre-piston resonance occurs in a lower frequency range overlapped with a high-energy range in the middle and high sea states, and therefore generates more damage than the well-known piston resonance.

papers.title: Enhanced oil recovery of tight oil reservoirs by active carbonated water imbibition: Underlying mechanisms and influential factors
papers.abstract: Active carbonated water (ACW) imbibition has emerged as a promising enhanced oil recovery method. Nevertheless, the mechanism is insufficiently understood, particularly as pore-scale oil displacement characterization remains unexplored. Furthermore, the influence of key factors on ACW imbibition performance requires systematic investigation.
