A self-developed triaxial seepage test system was utilized to carry out seepage tests during loading and unloading on broken coal-rock masses under conditions of different particle sizes, coal-rock mixing ratios, coal-rock mixing modes, and loading and unloading times. Research results show that the permeability of broken coal-rock masses increases with increasing particle size, decreases with growing proportion of coal in the broken coal-rock samples, and decreases with increasing loading and unloading times, while it is not dependent on the two mixing modes. The absolute stress sensitivity coefficients of permeability of broken coal-rock samples in various stages during loading are always greater than those during unloading. The stress sensitivity of permeability of broken coal-rock masses in the loading and unloading processes increases with increasing particle size, grows with increasing proportion of coal in the broken coal-rock samples, and decreases with increasing loading and unloading times, while it is not dependent on the two mixing modes. The research results provide guidance for the layout of gas drainage boreholes in the goaf of pressure-relief mining of coal seam groups with high gas content and low permeability, contributing to the prevention and control of coal and gas outburst disasters.

papers.title: The effects of oscillation on the mobility of wind-driven sessile droplets
papers.abstract: The oscillation of sessile droplets induced by shear flow is believed to enhance droplet mobility, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. An experimental investigation was conducted to explore the impact of oscillation on droplet mobility before the incipient motion. While instantaneous droplet profiles were measured by a high-resolution high-speed imaging system, time-resolved velocity profiles in the droplet wake were measured by a time-resolved particle image velocimetry system. As for the oscillation characteristics, the results demonstrate that the primary eigenfrequency of wind-driven droplets closely matches their dominant oscillation frequency. The frequency of velocity fluctuations in the droplet wake exhibits a strong correlation with the primary oscillation frequency of the droplet height. These oscillation characteristics represent critical parameters for developing an accurate quantitative model of droplet dynamics. The centroid displacement along the flow direction was found to be proportional to the adhesion force, indicating that a dynamic model of centroid displacement could serve as an effective tool for studying droplet mobility dominated by the adhesion force. A dynamic model was developed based on the classical oscillation theory and the oscillation characteristics to address the research gap regarding the dynamic analysis of wind-driven droplets. The model reveals that the eigenfrequency approaches the frequency of the periodic aerodynamic drag, resulting in resonance that induces significant oscillation in low-viscosity droplets. This droplet oscillation significantly increases centroid displacement, thereby enhancing droplet mobility, which was validated by experiments.

papers.title: Experimental study on hypersonic conical boundary layer flow under microstructure-seepage
papers.abstract: Seepage through microstructure on the surface, as a novel approach for boundary layer flow control, holds considerable promise for drag and thermal reduction in hypersonic vehicles. This paper presents an experimental study conducted in a Mach 6 hypersonic high-temperature wind tunnel, utilizing a cone with seepage through microstructure on the surface. The study employs schlieren, high-frequency fluctuating pressure measurement techniques, and infrared thermometry. It focuses on the influence of the amplitude-frequency characteristics of the second-mode waves within the hypersonic boundary layer on aerodynamic heating on the wall. According to the research, the following findings were observed: For smooth surfaces, the characteristic frequency of the second-mode wave decreases from 109 to 87 kHz along the flow direction. However, microstructures cause an average increase in the characteristic frequency by approximately 20 kHz, while seepage causes the characteristic frequency along the flow direction to change little. Under the same seepage flow rate, the amplitude of the second-mode waves within the boundary layer exhibits two peaks along the flow direction. When the second-mode wave reaches the first peak, the wall temperature rise also peaks at the same location, indicating a synchronous increase and decrease between the second-mode waves and wall temperature rise during this stage. Under different seepage flow rates, the downstream wall with microstructure-seepage experiences the lowest temperature rise when F = 0.019 19% which may be attributed to the formation of small vortices within the microstructures by the seepage.

papers.title: Propulsive performance analysis of a full-active rotating flapping foil
papers.abstract: The conventional heaving flapping-foil propulsion system, which couples heaving and pitching motions, shows considerable application potential in the field of underwater propulsion owing to its performance advantages. To further advance underwater propulsion technology, this study proposes a fully active rotating flapping foil propulsion device with compound rotating–pitching motion. A three-dimensional flapping foil of a National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) section 0012, subjected to coupled rotating and pitching motions, is simulated using the finite volume method, the sliding mesh technique, and user-defined functions. The research analyzes the effects of maximum angular displacement, pitching amplitude, and nominal rotational speed on its propulsive performance. Results indicate that increasing the maximum angular displacement can effectively enhance the thrust generated by the rotating flapping foil. However, with the increase in pitching amplitude, the mean thrust coefficient of the rotating flapping foil first increases and then decreases, suggesting that an optimal pitching amplitude exists for the rotating flapping foil propulsion system. Further analysis was conducted on the effect of nominal rotational speed on the propulsive performance of the rotating flapping foil. It was found that the nominal rotational speed exhibits a positive correlation with the generated thrust: the higher the nominal rotational speed, the greater the thrust output of the rotating flapping foil. Furthermore, compared with conventional heaving flapping foils, the rotating flapping foil achieves a 22.5% increase in thrust under identical operational conditions. The full-active rotating flapping foil proposed in this study exhibits excellent hydrodynamic performance, paving a new way to develop underwater propulsion technology.

papers.title: Development and validation of a multi-timescale reduced-order model for high-speed simulations of solid–fluid systems
papers.abstract: The discrete element method coupled with computational fluid dynamics (DEM-CFD) method has been extensively employed as the standard numerical approach to scientifically elucidate complex solid–fluid systems. However, the excessive computational cost of DEM-CFD simulations is one of the essential problems to clarify the dominant phenomena efficiently. Recently, the data-driven reduced-order models (ROMs) have been developed to accelerate computational efficiency. Nevertheless, ROMs have critical problems such as the decision of time step for each physical variables since the dynamics of distinct physical variables feature different timescales. Indeed, this fact is true without exception of the ROM-based DEM-CFD method. To resolve this inherent problem of ROM, a novel multi-timescale ROM (MT-ROM) is proposed for the DEM-CFD simulation, employing an error-estimation-based algorithm to optimize the timescale for each variable individually, enabling high-speed and high-accuracy simulations with the optimally required snapshots. Validated in two typical solid–liquid and gas–solid flow systems, namely a bead mill and a fluidized bed, MT-ROM achieves extremely high acceleration over the traditional DEM-CFD method while preserving adequate fidelity for a wide range of physical variables. The criterion for reliable MT-ROM simulations is also established for physical variables in DEM-CFD simulations. The proposed MT-ROM effectively leverages the advantages of data-driven modeling through a common error estimation approach. Ultimately, our proposed MT-ROM makes it feasible to clarify the complex phenomena for solid–fluid mixture systems efficiently and scientifically.

papers.title: Characterization of rarefied gas flows within narrow-confined spaces in grating interferometers
papers.abstract: High-speed motion of the reading head in grating interferometers induces rarefied gas flow perturbations in narrow-confined microstructure spaces with micro- and nano-periodic structures, leading to the fluctuations of air-refractive index and nanometer-scale interferometric measurement errors. To address this, an integrated fluid–solid-optical framework combining the Information Preservation Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (IP-DSMC) method, a modified Edlén refractive index model, and a ray-tracing method is developed. The IP-DSMC method is implemented within the OpenFOAM framework and validated against benchmark Couette flow cases. This study systematically characterizes the effects of Knudsen numbers and geometric parameters on flow perturbations and interferometric measurement errors. Results reveal that interferometric measurement errors are highly sensitive to refractive index non-uniformities induced by flow perturbations, jointly governed by rarefaction effects and microstructure geometries. A dynamic fluctuation model of air-refractive index incorporating Kn- and geometry-dependent corrections achieves high accuracy, showing that pressure-driven fluctuations of air-refractive index dominate interferometric measurement errors, reaching 13.2 nm at Kn is 0.25. The ray-tracing result confirms the reduction of the optical path difference with rising Kn, while geometric effects are secondary. This study provides a foundation for the error compensation in the high-precision grating interferometer under rarefied flow conditions.

papers.title: Role of inclined magnetic field on Couette slip flow and heat transfer with viscous dissipation in a rotating porous channel: Application in pumping systems
papers.abstract: The flow of electrically conducting fluids in rotating porous channels is of significant importance in various engineering and industrial applications, including the cooling of rotating electrical machines, magnetohydrodynamic generators, biomedical devices involving rotational blood flow, and filtration systems in chemical reactors. Motivated by these applications, this paper investigates the flow through a rotating porous channel bounded by two impermeable horizontal plates, where the lower plate is stationary and the upper plate moves at a constant velocity. The system is subjected to a uniform inclined magnetic field, incorporates wall slip effects, and accounts for viscous dissipation. The channel rotates with a constant angular velocity, inducing a secondary flow due to Coriolis effects. Analytical expressions for the velocity profiles and flow rates in both directions are derived, while the temperature distribution is computed numerically using the Runge–Kutta method via MATLAB's built-in solver. A parametric study is conducted to analyze the influence of the Hartmann number, Taylor number, slip parameter, inclination angle of the magnetic field, and Eckert number. A contour plot between the Hartmann number and Taylor number is also analyzed. Furthermore, asymptotic analysis is performed to understand the limiting behavior of the solution with respect to key parameters. Future studies may extend this work to non-Newtonian fluids, transient flow, or geometrically more complex domains.

papers.title: Propulsion prediction of morphing flapping wings using reduced order model from deep-learning
papers.abstract: Morphing the wing shape properly could improve the flapping performance of micro air vehicles (MAVs) incredibly. To design the proper morphing wings, the unsteady flapping performance needs to be estimated and predicted accurately. Compared with traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation, reduced order model (ROM) from machine learning presents a more rapid and accurate way for flapping performance prediction, which is the key to real-time prediction in flight. In this study, a morphing flapping wing is studied at low Reynolds number (Re = 1000). The ROM of propulsive performance in forward flight is established from deep learning. The source datasets are generated from CFD simulation, with input about flapping/morphing motion and output about propulsion performances. The relationship between flapping/morphing motions and propulsion is extracted based on bidirectional long short-term memory networks (Bi-LSTM). The results from ROM are compared with CFD simulation, which indicate that the ROM predicts the flapping propulsion performance accurately in a wide range of flapping and morphing parameters. The overall errors of the ROM prediction from CFD data for thrust coefficient CT and consumed the power coefficient CP are 6.14% and 2.72%, respectively. The ROM has strong generalization performance too, which can be applied to rigid wings or morphing wings, either in the time domain or in the frequency domain. At the same time, the computational time of the ROM prediction is only 8.65% of CFD simulation time, which enormously improves computational efficiency. The ROM can be applied for optimization design and real-time control of high-performance flapping wings with morphing capabilities.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of impacts of discrete droplets versus continuous streams on discharge characteristics at various electrode distances
papers.abstract: Accumulated rainwater may form discrete droplets or continuous streams, both of which degrade the electrical insulation performance of outdoor equipment. The distinct effects of discrete droplets and continuous streams on the gap discharge characteristics remain unreported. Using a customized rod–plane short air gap (25–70 mm) alternating current discharge experimental platform, this study systematically investigates the modulation mechanisms of droplets and streams, along with their distinct electrohydrodynamic and morphodynamic behaviors, at various electrode distances. Increasing the initial velocity of the rainwater induces a droplet-stream transformation, with both droplet formation and phase transition, which accelerates the decay rates of the critical discharge voltage (Vc) and breakdown voltage (Vb). For gaps smaller than 47.5 mm, rainwater droplets/streams attain their maximum length (Lmax) under the critical discharge conditions, before contraction precedes complete breakdown. The Lmax values of water streams substantially exceed the droplet dimensions, corresponding to reductions of 51.8% and 38.5% in Vc and Vb, respectively. Droplets transition from spherical to pear-shaped before elongating into bar-like structures under maximum stretching during critical discharge, whereas streams maintain stable bar-like profiles. Conductivity variations induce nonmonotonic Lmax behavior, with an initial increase in 37.0 ± 3% before declining with rising conductivity, whereas the discharge voltage decreases proportionally before stabilizing above 3000 μS/cm. When the electrode distance exceeds 47.5 mm, stream disintegration occurs before the critical discharge. Intensifying the applied voltage reduces the stream length, diminishing the morphological distinctions between droplets and streams until the discharge voltages converge at a gap distance of 70 mm (±5% variation).

papers.title: Droplet migration in a wavy microchannel under transverse temperature gradient
papers.abstract: The migration dynamics of droplets in confined microchannels are pivotal in advancing the design and functionality of next-generation microfluidic systems, with wide-reaching implications for biological assays, chemical synthesis, drug delivery, and thermal regulation. This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of droplet behavior in a wavy microchannel subjected to a transverse temperature gradient, focusing on the complex interplay between thermocapillary forces and geometric confinement. The unique non-uniform channel topology induces spatial variations in hydrodynamic resistance and pressure distribution, which, when coupled with thermally induced Marangoni stresses, generate intricate cross-stream migration patterns. Unlike in straight channels, where migration could be explained by a simple linear superposition of flow-induced and thermocapillary effects, the oscillatory nature of the wavy walls leads to highly non-linear and coupled interactions, making the migration behavior far more complex. Our parametric analyses reveal that increasing the temperature gradient intensifies the droplet's migration toward the heated wall, while amplified oscillations are due to the periodic channel geometry. Moreover, key parameters such as wave-pitch, wave-height, initial droplet position, and the thermal conductivity ratio significantly influence both the transient migration dynamics and the final steady-state positioning of the droplet. These findings reveal a rich and nuanced control mechanism for droplet manipulation, where the geometrical modulation of the microchannel synergistically interacts with thermal gradients, facilitating precise droplet steering and positioning. The results provide key insights for designing microfluidic platforms that use temperature gradients in lab-on-chip devices, thermal droplet sorters, targeted drug delivery, and advanced diagnostics, where precise droplet control is crucial.

papers.title: Prediction of wind farm wake and output power using generative adversarial network and convolutional neural network
papers.abstract: Wake and output power prediction of wind turbine is critical for the wind farm layout optimization. Previous studies used analytical wake models and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods to fulfill this prediction. However, these methods either exhibit inadequate prediction accuracy or need excessive computational demands during prediction processes. Thus, a novel wind farm prediction system is established using the full-model CFD simulation and a surrogate modeling method based on convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial networks to ensure the fidelity and efficiency of the prediction. By containing an incoming speed distribution generator module (Gin), a wake distribution generator model (Gw), a rotational speed prediction module (R), and a power prediction module (P), this system can predict high-dimensional incoming data, the rotational speed, power output, and three-dimensional wake fields. The system uses the incoming wind speed (Vin) and turbulence intensity to determine the optimal placement of turbines in the wind field. The Gin, R, Gw, and P module are validated through high-resolution experimental and computational data. The system is applied to a tandem wind farm and the Horns Rev 1 wind farm. The predicted data show satisfactory agreement with high-resolution experimental and computational data, fully validating the robustness and generalization capability of the system. The proposed prediction system is of great engineering significance for optimizing wind farm layout.

papers.title: Flexible gas-sealing optimization and leakage prevention mechanism in gob-side entry retaining: An innovative gas control method
papers.abstract: In Y-type ventilation systems, sealing walls are prone to crack development under mining pressure, allowing gas to migrate from the goaf into the gob-side entry retaining, creating serious gas accidents. This study proposes a novel flexible gas-sealing technology for gob-side entry retaining applications. Based on this, the interactive effects of three factors—air distribution ratio, airbag width, and airbag thickness—on gas concentration in the gob-side entry retaining were analyzed using a combination of design of experiments, response surface methodology, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation. The technique parameters were then optimized, and the mechanism by which the flexible airbag influences gas leakage has been elucidated. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method was validated through a field test. The results showed that airbag width and thickness had a more significant impact on the gas concentration compared with the air distribution ratio, and strong nonlinear interactions were observed among the three factors. The optimal parameters derived from the response surface optimization were an air distribution ratio of 5:1, an airbag width of 3.414 m, and a thickness of 0.587 m. The airbag alleviated the pressure gradient in the goaf, reduced leakage from the coal face, and increased wind pressure in the gob-side entry retaining, thereby weakening methane leakage intensity. Field tests demonstrated good performance, reducing gas concentration to 0.1%–0.15%, increasing airflow velocity to 2.46, m/s, and decreasing the resistance per 100 m and friction resistance coefficient to 0.009 and 0.012 N·s2/m4, respectively.

papers.title: Advanced machine learning analysis of bioconvection in nanofluid with oxytactic microorganisms in a porous wavy enclosure under inclined periodic magnetic effects
papers.abstract: This study investigates the bioconvection behavior of a nanofluid containing oxytactic microorganisms within a permeable wavy cavity under an external magnetic field. The analysis includes the effects of Brownian motion and thermophoresis. The dimensionless governing equations are solved using the finite-element method (FEM). A comprehensive parametric study is conducted for various dimensionless numbers: Brownian motion, Hartmann number (Ha), Rayleigh number (Ra), thermophoresis parameter, Lewis number (Le), Péclet number (Pe), nanoparticle volume fraction, bioconvection Rayleigh number (Rb), Darcy number (Da), and wall undulation. The impacts on streamlines, isotherms, and isoconcentration contours of oxygen and microorganisms are illustrated and discussed. The results indicate that cavity undulation has significant influence on the bioconvection flow and thermal transport. Increasing Ra enhances both flow circulation and bioconvective effects. Stronger thermal gradients and higher isoconcentrations of oxygen and microorganisms occur at higher Da. Furthermore, increasing Rb from 0.1 to 10 results in a 37.6% decrease in the average Nusselt number (Nuav) and a 12.1% increase in the average Sherwood number, demonstrating their influence on heat and mass transport. Both Brownian motion and thermophoresis enhance heat transfer rates. A higher Le distinctly reduces micro-organism concentration. To improve the accuracy of predictions for average Nu under fixed values of Ra, Rb, Ha, Da, Le, and Pe, an artificial neural network (ANN) combined with FEM is utilized. Optimal training is achieved at epoch 9, resulting in a mean squared error of 4.5%. The ANN demonstrates strong prediction capability with a correlation coefficient (R-value) of 0.98, confirming its excellent performance.

papers.title: A universal model for surge frequency prediction based on the equivalent hydraulic spring: From theoretical derivation to experimental verification
papers.abstract: This study proposes an innovative surge frequency prediction model based on an equivalent hydraulic spring analogy to address the critical limitation of conventional stability analysis methods (e.g., the B-parameter method) in predicting surge frequency, where they can only qualitatively assess stability but fail to accurately determine compressor surge frequency. The model establishes fundamental analogies between surge oscillations and mechanical mass-spring-damper systems by incorporating three key fluid dynamic characteristics: fluid inertia as equivalent mass, compressibility as equivalent stiffness, and viscous dissipation as equivalent damping. Through systematic axisymmetric simplification and linearization of the Navier–Stokes equations, we derive an analytical solution that reveals the nonlinear coupling between surge frequency and cavity geometric/fluid properties. Experimental validation was performed on a single-stage axial compressor test rig, where pressure fluctuations were measured under varying rear cavity volumes. Advanced signal processing techniques, including fast Fourier transform analysis and nonlinear regression, were employed for frequency extraction and model calibration. The results demonstrate exceptional prediction accuracy exceeding 95%, significantly outperforming traditional methods. The model's breakthrough lies in its first-time incorporation of post-surge airflow elasticity effects into the analytical framework, providing new insights into cavity–flow coupling mechanisms while offering practical design tools for turbomachinery stability optimization.

papers.title: Influence of pier-grid energy dissipator on energy dissipation and diversion characteristics of stilling basin in turning section
papers.abstract: To investigate how the pier-grid energy dissipator (P-GED) mitigates adverse hydraulic effects caused by centrifugal force and flow inertia in bend sections, this study takes the turning-section stilling basin as the research object. A total of 27 P-GED schemes were designed using the controlled variable method. Based on the coefficient of variation of water surface superelevation and energy dissipation rate, three evaluation methods—Simple Weighted Method, Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution, and Entropy Weight Method—were applied for scheme selection. Subsequently, six indicators, including the water-depth adjustment coefficient of the concave and convex banks, flow velocity reduction ratio, turbulence intensity, and turbulence kinetic energy, were used to compare flow characteristics under conditions with and without P-GED. The results indicate that for energy dissipation, the influencing factors are ranked as pier height > pier length > grid height, whereas for flow guidance, pier length > grid height > pier height. The P-GED significantly increases water depth along the stilling basin, suppresses end wall overflow and fold flow, and enhances water surface uniformity by raising the water-depth adjustment coefficient of the concave and convex banks beyond 90% in the downstream region. The velocity reduction ratio in the P-GED arranged zone reaches 87.92%, an increase of 34.23% compared to the case without P-GED. Meanwhile, turbulence is significantly intensified, with longitudinal and lateral turbulence intensity increased by 358.82% and 280.00%, respectively, accelerating kinetic energy dissipation. These results provide reference for the design and safe operation of turning-section stilling basins.

papers.title: Rheological properties of deep-sea sediment flows with different sediment grain sizes and concentrations
papers.abstract: Submarine sediment flows, as the primary transport mechanism for deep-sea sediments, are a crucial component of the marine sediment “source-sink” system. The type and movement velocity of sediment flows are governed by their rheological properties, which fundamentally depend on the variations in sediment grain size composition and concentration. To accurately describe the processes and velocities of sediment flows, as well as to predict its potential disaster effects and impacts, it is essential to obtain precise rheological characteristics of sediment flows with differing sediment grain sizes and concentrations. This study employs a rheometer to measure the rheological properties of sediment flows with varying sediment grain sizes and concentrations. It presents the threshold values of sediment content at which the fluid properties of sediment flows change for different grain sizes. The results indicate that the rheological behavior of sediment flows transitions from Newtonian to Bingham fluid and ultimately to pseudoplastic fluid types with increasing concentration. Additionally, variations in grain size govern the critical concentrations at which these fluid-type transitions occur. The foundational data on the rheological property transitions of sediment flows, as revealed by the research findings, exhibit broad applicability. These data can support the simulation of sediment flow movement and evolution processes and contribute to the prediction of sediment flow velocity.

papers.title: A sparse dynamic mode decomposition for time-dependent parameterized partial differential equations based on generalized empirical interpolation
papers.abstract: Reduced-order modeling of parameterized partial differential equations has emerged as a prominent research focus in computational mathematics. As an efficient data-driven approach, dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) has demonstrated remarkable advantages. However, existing improved DMD methods still exhibit systematic limitations when addressing complex problems where spatial dimensions significantly exceed temporal dimensions. To mitigate this problem, we innovatively propose a GEIM (generalized empirical interpolation method)-DMD reduced order modeling framework that synergistically integrates GEIM with DMD. By employing GEIM to construct a deterministic spatial collocation point selection strategy for dimensionality reduction, the GEIM-DMD maintains accuracy comparable to standard DMD while significantly reducing computational costs. To further extend parametric applications, a K-nearest neighbors (KNN)-based algorithm, termed KNN-GEIM-DMD, which constructs an efficient mapping from the parameter space to the solution space, is proposed. Numerical results demonstrate the high efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method, which matches that of the standard DMD and exceeds that of the compressed DMD.

papers.title: Investigation of cavitation jet erosion based on the Eulerian-Lagrangian approach coupled with dynamic mesh
papers.abstract: Cavitation jet nozzles are widely used for cutting, crushing, cleaning, etc., but the erosion behavior of cavitation jets remains highly unpredictable owing to the multiscale complexity of cavitation. The present work integrates an energy balance approach with a hybrid Eulerian–Lagrangian cavitation model, and incorporates the dynamic mesh approach to represent the erosion morphology explicitly. The large eddy simulation approach is used to calculate the turbulent flow dynamics, while a random nucleation method is applied to consider cavitation nuclei. A two-way transformation algorithm is employed for bridging between the continuous phase (modeled in the Eulerian framework) and the discrete bubbles (tracked through the Lagrangian approach). An erosion prediction indicator using the material derivative of multiscale vapor volumes is used to assess the cavitation erosion distribution and compare with the previous experiment [Liu and Ma, “Erosion behavior of aluminum by an inclined cavitating jet,” Wear 474–475, 203751 (2021)]. A hybrid model coupling cavitation erosion risk with the dynamic mesh technique is proposed to enable high-fidelity prediction of erosion hotspots. The proposed model demonstrates enhanced accuracy in cavitation features through multiscale coupled simulation of large cavities and tiny bubbles, as well as in cavitation erosion distributions by dynamically adjusting mesh nodes according to the erosion risk distribution and achieving specimen surface morphology reconstruction. The results indicate that the multiscale model considering tiny bubbles well reveals the secondary erosion area, and the dynamic mesh coupled method better captures the erosion area compared with the method with a static mesh.

papers.title: Upstream flow separation is not a triggering factor in wake bi-stability of the square-back Ahmed body
papers.abstract: Wake bi-stability is a common flow instability phenomenon observed in the square-back Ahmed body, which has a significant impact on aerodynamic performance and vehicle drag. Recent studies have indicated that upstream boundary layer separation is a key factor triggering wake bi-stability, and suppressing leading-edge separation using suction control methods can eliminate wake bi-stability [D. Ahmed and A. S. Morgans, “Wake bi-modality: The effect of upstream boundary layer dynamics” J. Fluid Mech. 975, A7 (2023)]. However, we found that the simulation time in that study was relatively short, which may not have fully captured the switching process of the bi-modal characteristics. Therefore, in this study, we conducted a large eddy simulation for the square-back Ahmed body over a longer timescale and employed an improved data analysis method to further explore the generation mechanism of wake bi-stability. The results show that even when there is no significant boundary layer separation at the leading edge of the body, the bi-modal flow characteristics in the wake region still persist, suggesting that the triggering mechanism may not solely depend on leading-edge separation. The findings of this study provide new insights into the optimization of wake control strategies and offer important guidance for vehicle aerodynamic design.

papers.title: Construction and thickening mechanism of polymer nanospheres' inclusion synergistic enhancement system based on supramolecular interactions
papers.abstract: CO2 flooding effectively enhances oil recovery in low-permeability reservoirs while enabling CO2 geological storage. However, natural fractures and high-permeability channels in such reservoirs are prone to cause CO2 channeling, significantly reducing displacement efficiency. To address this challenge, this study innovatively developed a nanospheres inclusion synergistic enhancement system (ISES) based on cyclodextrin polymer (β-CDAM, host) and acid-resistant hydrophobic polymer nanospheres (PARC, guest). This system achieves shear-responsive intelligent viscosity modulation via a supramolecular self-assembly mechanism. The optimal preparation method for ISES was determined using apparent viscosity as the evaluation criterion. Furthermore, the correlation mechanism between the microstructure and rheological properties of ISES was elucidated using pyrene fluorescence probing, atomic force microscopy (AFM), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), and rheological analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that under conditions of 85 °C and 1000 mg/l NaCl salinity, the viscosity of ISES reached 24.6 mPa s, representing a 92.24% increase compared to the viscosity of β-CDAM. The cavities of cyclodextrin present on the β-CDAM chain enable inclusion complexation with the surface hydrophobic chains of PARC. This interaction constructs a denser three-dimensional network structure, resulting in a significant increase in system viscosity. The system exhibits low viscosity under high-shear injection rates to improve injectivity. Upon entering the reservoir under low-shear conditions, it achieves in situ viscosity recovery through supramolecular self-assembly, thus effectively plugging gas channeling pathways and enabling deep conformance control. This study provides novel insights for preventing and controlling CO2 channeling, holding significant implications for the successful implementation of CO2 flooding.

papers.title: Analysis of pressure variation within multiple water columns induced by shock wave
papers.abstract: This paper numerically investigates the law of pressure variation inside the shocked water columns at varying gap distances using a quasi-conservative five-equation model. The morphology and pressure value when the water column was affected by the wave converging and showed peak negative pressure were analyzed qualitatively and quantitatively. It is found that the peak negative pressure all occurred when the reflected waves formed a “horse-shoe” structure. The variation law of the peak negative pressure is the same when the water columns are placed at the same dimensionless spacing. When the water columns are placed in tandem, the peak negative pressure in the downstream column exhibits a linear relationship with the relative distance. When the columns are arranged diagonally, the peak negative pressure in the downstream column shows varied regular changes at different relative distances. Optimizing the placement of the water columns can either enhance or weaken the focused negative pressure in the downstream column, with potential increases of up to 33% or decreases of up to 80%.

papers.title: Attenuation of weak spherical shock waves in an accelerating flow
papers.abstract: This study reports experimental investigations of a weak spherical shock wave propagating into an accelerating flow induced by a fan. Pressure measurements are conducted for shock waves propagating in both a static fluid and an accelerating flow, and comparisons reveal the influence of the accelerating flow on shock wave properties. The pressure jump of the shock wave is reduced after propagation in the accelerating flow, indicating attenuation of the shock wave. Greater attenuation is observed with increasing longitudinal velocity gradient in the shock propagation direction, corresponding to higher acceleration. When the velocity gradient becomes sufficiently large, the pressure jump is no longer identifiable, implying the disappearance of the shock wave. This attenuation is consistent with the one-dimensional model of a shock wave crossing a surface with an infinitely large velocity gradient, as the experimental conditions approach those of the model with increasing gradient. The attenuation does not affect the fluctuating behavior of the pressure jump. Additionally, the histogram of pressure jumps suggests that attenuation occurs for all shock waves propagating in the accelerating flow. The present experimental results support the shock wave attenuation predicted by the one-dimensional model, offering new insights into shock wave propagation in non-uniform flows.

papers.title: Effects of ignition time differences and array parameters on acoustic characteristics of multi-detonation-tube arrays
papers.abstract: This paper explores the acoustic characteristics of detonation sound waves (DSWs) generated by multiple detonation tubes through experiments considering various ignition time differences (ITDs), numbers of tubes, and tube spacings. The experiments use methane as the fuel and oxygen as the oxidant and measure the peak sound pressure, effective sound pressure level, and frequency spectrum. The experimental data show that the pressure level of DSWs can be effectively improved by increasing the number of detonation tubes. However, in the case of simultaneous ignition or small ITDs, increasing the number of tubes does not significantly change the wave structure of the DSW. In the case of multiple detonation tubes, there is a marked decline in the peak pressure and effective sound pressure level as the ITD increases. These energy attenuations are mainly concentrated in the low-frequency region below 1000 Hz and gradually shift to lower frequencies with increasing ITD. Moreover, changes in the ITD modify the structure of the DSWs, with increases in the ITD extending the duration of the positive-pressure region, but paradoxically reducing the energy proportion. Under asynchronous ignition conditions, the peak pressure and effective sound pressure level can be enhanced by increasing the tube spacing so as to reduce the interference of the central jet. These changes indicate that the ITD has a relatively significant negative impact on the pressure characteristics of DSWs and regulates the associated energy distribution.

papers.title: A comprehensive study of interpolation methods in electrohydrodynamic cone-jet across diverse liquid conductivities
papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of electrohydrodynamic atomization (EHDA) in the cone-jet regime requires reliable interpolation of fluid properties—such as permittivity, conductivity, and viscosity—across the liquid–gas interface. While the weighted arithmetic mean (WAM) is widely used in two-phase simulations due to its simplicity and stability, it may introduce significant inaccuracies in electrohydrodynamic (EHD) applications by over-smoothing critical property gradients. This study presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of five mean interpolation methods—weighted arithmetic mean (WAM), weighted harmonic mean (WHM), geometric mean (GM), modified geometric mean (mGM), and power-law mean (PLM)—for modeling electrohydrodynamic atomization (EHDA) processes under varying conductivity regimes. By evaluating their performance on key EHD metrics such as surface charge distribution, cone-jet dynamics, droplet size, jet breakup, and beam current, we reveal the strengths and limitations of each method. Numerical results were validated against experimental data and established scaling laws. For low-conductivity fluids, WAM demonstrated superior accuracy in predicting droplet sizes and beam currents due to its balanced interpolation and numerical robustness, while WHM offered stronger charge retention at the expense of stability. GM, mGM, and PLM provided improved physical accuracy under conditions of assured numerical stability. In the medium-conductivity regime, WHM emerged as the most effective method for capturing interfacial charge dynamics and droplet formation, although WAM excelled in predicting geometric features such as jet length and Taylor-cone height. For high-conductivity fluids, all five interpolation schemes yielded comparable results, accurately estimating droplet sizes and beam currents within a 5% margin of experimental values. The findings underscore the importance of selecting appropriate interpolation methods based on fluid conductivity, with WAM favored for low-conductivity fluids, WHM for medium-conductivity systems, and flexibility among all schemes for high-conductivity scenarios. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting or tuning interpolation methods in two-phase EHD simulations and establish a robust framework for improving numerical reliability in multiphase electrohydrodynamic modeling.

papers.title: Bio-inspired wing-like bluff body for wind-induced vibration energy harvesting via piezoelectric-electromagnetic hybrid mechanism
papers.abstract: Harvesting wind energy using piezoelectric and electromagnetic transduction has attracted increasing attention to implement the autonomous self-sustaining electronics over the past two decades. To offer an alternative solution for the poor robustness of typical galloping-based energy harvesters at unexpectedly high wind speed, a bio-inspired wing-like bluff body for wind-induced vibration energy harvesting via a piezoelectric-electromagnetic hybrid mechanism is proposed in this paper. The most attractive feature of the energy harvester was the adaptive shape-transforming ability of the wing-like bluff body, where the shape of wing-like bluff body could adaptively adjust with various wind speeds. Accordingly, the vibration mode of energy harvester shifted from galloping to vortex-induced vibration. Therefore, the energy harvester could yield a large electric output at low wind speed as well as possess high robustness at high wind speed and considerable power generation capability. A series of simulations and experiments have been conducted to verify the feasibility of the proposed structure and principle. The results demonstrated that width ratio and tip thickness of the wing-like bluff body brought a significant effect on the power generation capability of the energy harvester. The piezoelectric unit and electromagnetic unit achieved a maximum output power of 1.41 and 6.24 mW at a wind speed of 10 m/s with the optimal load resistances of 400 and 1.5 kΩ, respectively. Furthermore, the utilization of piezoelectric unit and electromagnetic unit enables the illumination of 86 and 250 light-emitting diodes, respectively.

papers.title: Cone-jet regime in electrospray: A comprehensive review
papers.abstract: Cone jet is a very important and promising mean in electrohydrodynamic atomization or electrospray, where a liquid cone forms at the end of a capillary tube at a rational range of potential and flow rate and a permanent, stable, and thin jet emerges from the cone tip and further disintegrates into plenty of fine drops. Owing to several advantages of uniform and microscale drop size, high-charge density, and precise trajectory control, the cone-jet electrospray effectively meets a wide range of application requirements. This work provides a critical review the recent experiments, theories, analysis, and numerical simulations concerning the formation and evolution of Taylor cone and cone jet, as well as the subsequent jet breakup and drops generation. Our aim is to offer a comprehensive understanding of the underlying physics of the process of cone jet, including the conditions for the formation and the stable operation of the cone jet, and the universal scaling laws governing minimum flow rate, drop size, and electric current, as well as the instability of cone jet. In addition, the coaxial Taylor cone jets and the recent numerical studies on cone-jet dynamics are also briefly reviewed.

papers.title: Minimum thickness of liquid film for the validity of water hammer theory
papers.abstract: Systems that clean by high-speed nanodroplet injection have recently been developed; however, elucidating the cleaning mechanism underlying nanodroplet impact is urgently required. In this study, numerical simulations of the high-speed impact phenomenon of two liquid films were performed using the Enskog–Vlasov direct simulation Monte Carlo method. We determine the minimum liquid film thickness for which the water hammer theory is applicable to the maximum pressure generated during liquid film impact. The simulation results show that the water hammer pressure was generated when the liquid film thickness exceeded the compression wavefront thickness generated by the liquid film impact, which is more than ten times the molecular diameter.

papers.title: Failure mechanisms of titanium alloy cylindrical pressure hulls under combined hydrodynamic pressure fields and implosion shock loading
papers.abstract: Pressure hulls in deep-sea environments are exposed to extreme hydrostatic pressure and implosion shocks caused by the failure of brittle structures, which may result in catastrophic failure and the underwater implosion of adjacent pressure hulls. It is, thus, essential to investigate the destructive effects of implosion shocks induced by the localized rupture of brittle structures on adjacent pressure hulls under deep-sea conditions. First, a triggered implosion and shock experiment is conducted to examine the dynamic response characteristics of titanium alloy cylindrical pressure hulls under the combined effects of the deep-sea environment and implosion shocks. Then, a high-accuracy numerical method for fluid–structure interactions based on the arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian method is developed to analyze the failure mechanisms of such hulls under implosion shocks at varying standoff distances. The results indicate that the plastic deformation induced by implosion shocks is the predominant factor contributing to the failure of cylindrical pressure hulls when the standoff distance is less than 0.33r0. As the standoff distance increases, the influence of the shock wave decreases, resulting in the predominant factor shifting toward an overall instability caused by the hydrodynamic pressure field.

papers.title: Dynamic characteristics of droplet coalescence-induced jumping on bioinspired symmetric rhombic microstructured surfaces
papers.abstract: The coalescence-induced droplet jumping phenomenon holds significant engineering potential in applications such as self-cleaning, anti-icing/frosting, and enhanced condensation heat transfer. Using a three-dimensional lattice Boltzmann method (LBM), this study numerically simulates droplet coalescence and jumping behaviors on bioinspired symmetric rhombic microstructured surfaces (BSRMS), with particular focus on the effects of droplet radius ratio and micropillar geometry on the jumping dynamics and energy conversion. The results reveal that increasing the central ridge height markedly enhances both the maximum jumping and energy conversion efficiency of jumping droplets, with the latter reaching up to 29.38% when the radius of both droplets is 20lu and the height of the middle ridge is 19lu. For two mismatched droplets, a horizontal velocity component emerges, causing the droplet to deviate from its original position, and the maximum horizontal velocity increases with the central ridge height. Importantly, jumping behavior exhibits well-defined critical conditions: no jumping occurs when the radius ratio is below 0.5 or the energy conversion efficiency is below 2%. Within a specific parameter range (radius ratio ϕ=0.75∼1, central ridge height H = 5∼15lu; ϕ=0.625, H = 7∼11lu), the energy conversion efficiency shows an approximately linear dependence on the radius ratio, and the slope of this linear relationship grows with increasing central ridge height.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic performance of a viscoelastic flexible membrane floating over a submerged rubble mound breakwater under oblique wave incidence
papers.abstract: This study investigates the scattering of oblique water waves by a viscoelastic membrane placed over a trapezoidal rubble-mound breakwater on a sloped seabed. This study considers both wave scattering and trapping when a partially reflecting seawall is positioned downstream. The boundary value problem related to the present physical setup is solved using the hybrid boundary element method-based approach by coupling the central difference scheme with the boundary element method (BEM) to handle the second-order dynamic boundary condition of the viscoelastic floating flexible membrane. The flow through the rubble mound porous breakwater is modeled using the Sollitt and Cross [“Wave transmission through permeable breakwaters,” in Coastal Engineering (ASCE, 1972), pp. 1827–1846] model, while the flow through the flexible floating viscoelastic membrane is described based on the formulation presented by Agarwal et al. [J. Fluids Struct. 129, 104167 (2024)]. According to the given model, the transmitted energy is below 30% for moderate values of the viscoelastic damping parameter of the membrane. The moderate values of the breakwater's porosity and structural size are suitable for optimal performance of the present configuration of the viscoelastic membrane–breakwater setup. Also, the wave run-up coefficient, reflected energy, and wave force acting on the partially reflecting seawall show an oscillatory pattern for numerous values of seawall coefficient and inclination angle when plotted as a function of relative spacing between the breakwater and seawall. A rubble-mound breakwater combined with a viscoelastic flexible membrane effectively reduces wave energy, creating a calmer lee side zone.

papers.title: Electroosmotic vortices-mediated active micromixer: Unveiling the performance of mixing quality
papers.abstract: This work presents a micromixer with a diamond-shaped electroosmotic mixing chamber designed to improve fluid mixing at the microscale. The micromixer employs alternating current (AC) electroosmosis, facilitated by symmetrically positioned microelectrodes, which generate vortices that disturb laminar flow and promote enhanced convective mixing. The research examines how different operational parameters, such as average inlet velocity (U0), AC frequency (f), voltage amplitude (V0), and the inclination angle (α = 0°, 20°, 40°, and 60°) of the mixing chamber, affect mixing efficiency. The investigation is carried out systematically to analyze the performance of the mixing chamber at various inclination angles to maximize the mixing quality. A comprehensive numerical investigation is conducted to evaluate the influence of key parameters, including average inlet velocity (U0), AC frequency (f), voltage amplitude (V0), and the inclination angle of the mixing chamber (α). The governing equations for laminar flow, electric currents, and species transport are solved using the finite element-based solver. The results indicate that the diamond-shaped chamber geometry is critical in creating stable, symmetric vortices, which enhance the interaction between the two fluid streams. The optimal mixing performance is achieved at α = 20° with U0 = 0.05 mm/s, V0 = 0.5 V, and f = 8 Hz, reaching a maximum mixing quality of 98.47%, while maintaining a relatively low mixing cost of 0.001 485, under these conditions. Moreover, the study evaluates the relationship between mixing cost, mixing quality, and pressure drop, emphasizing how different inclination angles affect both. Pressure variation along the microchannel is also analyzed for different inclination angles, showing a trade-off between mixing quality and pressure drop. The findings highlight the potential of electrode-driven micromixers in achieving efficient mixing for low-Reynolds-number microfluidic systems, with potential applications in lab-on-a-chip devices and biochemical processes.

papers.title: A deep learning-based hybrid-coupled multiscale modeling framework for real-time flow field prediction in porous media
papers.abstract: Porous media flows are ubiquitous in natural and engineered systems, where pore-scale dynamics fundamentally govern macro-scale transport behavior. Accurate flow field prediction is essential for evaluating, optimizing, and controlling such systems. However, realistic porous structures feature multiscale heterogeneity spanning several orders of magnitude, rendering high-fidelity pore-scale simulations computationally intractable for system-scale applications. Moreover, conventional upscaling approaches struggle in heterogeneous media where representative elementary volumes are ill-defined. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid-coupled multiscale framework that explicitly models the dynamic coupling between pore-scale and Darcy-scale processes. Within this framework, a lightweight deep neural network is used to rapidly predict pore-scale flow fields under evolving boundary conditions. The results show that the proposed deep learning model effectively learns high-fidelity, physically consistent mappings from geometry and boundary conditions to multi-physics flow fields, enabling robust generalization across a wide range of flow scenarios. The multiscale method supports fast, reliable upscaling of pore-scale information in heterogeneous structures and accurately predicts complex flow patterns within 1 s, achieving over 640 times speedup and 97% memory savings compared to conventional pore-scale methods. This work bridges the gap between pore-scale insights and macro-scale applicability, establishing a powerful and efficient paradigm for porous media analysis.

papers.title: Experimental investigation on liquid–gas interfacial dynamics and phase transition effects under non-isothermal sloshing conditions
papers.abstract: Non-isothermal sloshing frequently occurs in cryogenic fuel tanks (e.g., liquefied natural gas and liquefied hydrogen) during marine transportation. The resulting liquid–gas phase transition is strongly influenced by sloshing flows, inducing instantaneous pressure and temperature variations that compromise operational safety and reliability of liquid cargo systems. This paper experimentally investigates the liquid–gas interfacial dynamics and phase transition effects on tank thermodynamics under non-isothermal sloshing conditions. Visual experiments were conducted across four sloshing frequencies and three amplitudes, revealing four distinct sloshing regimes based on interfacial behaviors. The two-phase interfacial region emerges in sloshing regime III due to disturbances from liquid jets and phase transition, and expands significantly in regime IV, which replaces the clear free surface. Non-isothermal sloshing triggers brief surface evaporation and pressurization, followed by sustained vapor condensation and depressurization. Thermal stratification persists in regimes I and II, while de-stratification initiates in the liquid phase (regime III) and extends to both phases (regime IV). The measured results indicate that the peak and average condensation rates scale cubically with those of evaporation rates, and the logarithmic average evaporation rate varies linearly with frequency and follows a power-law dependence on amplitude. We finally propose empirical correlations linking sloshing parameters to evaporation rates and condensation rates to evaporation rates, showing good agreement with experimental data.

papers.title: A general theoretical framework for equilibrium scour due to inclined jets based on the Phenomenological Theory of Turbulence
papers.abstract: We present the derivation and validation of a novel, complete theoretical framework for jet-induced scour, illuminated by the Phenomenological Theory of Turbulence. The framework is designed to account for all flow conditions and a wide range of bed-particle sizes, with the potential to extend it to the entire range. The theory naturally subsumes previous results obtained by the first author for coarser materials under the assumption of the Reynolds number tending to infinity. By invoking the different stages of the power spectrum of the turbulent energy and the incipient conditions for sediment motion, the developed framework allows for a unique, physically based description of the changing habits of jet scour, as a function of the particle size and power of the jet at the equilibrium state. After specifying the details of the general theory, we focus on finer materials and uncover a novel expression as a special case. We test the model using experimental data involving an extremely wide range of particle sizes. The model appears to very well predict the experiments for non-cohesive sediment. The comparison with cohesive sediment provides noteworthy insights, highlighting the need for further research to incorporate cohesive-sediment parameters into the developed framework. We determine important constants from previous developments and re-interpret the flow resistance phenomenon at the bottom of the scour hole. Finally, we discuss a bi-modal perspective for the analysis of the problem of scour.

papers.title: Electric field-controlled bubble nucleation and heat transfer enhancement on nanoparticle surfaces: A multiphysics simulation based on lattice Boltzmann method
papers.abstract: Nanoparticles and nanobubbles play critical roles in various fields, including thermal management, enhanced heat transfer, and interfacial reaction. Investigating the microscale mechanisms by which electric fields regulate bubble nucleation on nanoparticle surfaces and enhance heat transfer is essential for further advancing application performance. In this work, the lattice Boltzmann method is employed to study the dynamic effects of electric fields on bubble nucleation, growth, and departure on nanoparticle surfaces under the synergistic action of multiple physical fields, coupling the two-phase flow model, gas–liquid phase change model, and electric field model. The results demonstrate that the electric field significantly optimizes bubble behavior and heat transfer efficiency. Specifically, as the electric capillary number (CaE) increases from 0 to 1.6, the bubble departure diameter decreases by up to 66.08%, while the departure frequency increases by up to 75.86%. Moreover, the spatiotemporally averaged heat flux increases by up to 130.03% as CaE rises from 0 to 1.6. Under the combined action of electrophoretic and dielectrophoretic forces, bubbles detach more efficiently from the nanoparticle surface, thereby enhancing liquid agitation and thermal exchange, which ultimately leads to a substantial improvement in heat transfer performance. This study provides a theoretical foundation for the electric-field-regulated nanoparticle/nanobubble systems.

papers.title: Intelligent identification method for oil–gas two-phase flow patterns in aviation engine scavenge pipes based on multidimensional image features
papers.abstract: In response to the limitations regarding applicable pipe diameters and media in the study of two-phase flow in aviation engine scavenge pipe, a flow pattern identification method that integrates image features with neural networks has been proposed, offering an innovative solution for the analysis of intricate oil–gas flow states. A small-diameter oil–gas two-phase flow experimental system was developed, utilizing high-speed imaging technology to capture 1104 sets of images representing four distinct flow patterns. Following the feature selection criteria delineated in this study, 12 multidimensional feature parameters encompassing color, texture, and shape were extracted through various image processing techniques. Comparative validation revealed that the Elman neural network significantly outperforms the back propagation neural network in flow pattern identification, achieving an impressive accuracy of 97.06%. This research elucidates the mechanisms by which oil–gas media influence flow morphology through image analysis, effectively addressing the adaptability limitations of conventional water–gas models. The intelligent flow pattern identification framework constructed herein provides substantial data support for the structural optimization of aviation engine scavenge pipes, and its non-intrusive analytical characteristics hold considerable practical value in monitoring the flow states of lubrication systems.

papers.title: A universal blade modeling method based on the virtual constraint boundaries for a controllable channel and loading form
papers.abstract: Rethinking the design method for high-performance two-dimensional blade profiles is crucial for the development of advanced aero engines. This study reexamines the blade design process from the channel perspective and proposes a universal blade modeling method for turbomachinery based on virtual constrained boundaries. This method can control the expansion and contraction process and quantify the cascade channel's loading form. Then, a parameterized comparative analysis was performed on the channel of a high subsonic compressor cascade. Our modeling method effectively reproduced the geometric and aerodynamic characteristics of the initial cascade. By optimizing the cascade channel's diffusion angle distribution, our method greatly improved the cascade's deviation angle characteristics. Under the proposed model, the cascade's deviation angle was reduced by 8.30%, but the impact of changes in the distribution of channel diffusion angle on the total pressure loss coefficient was relatively small. Additionally, the blade loading distribution's impact on its aerodynamic performance was explored by changing the loading form coefficient, and it was found that a front-loaded blade distribution greatly improved the cascade performance under a high attack angle. For example, at an attack angle of +6°, the deviation angle and total pressure loss coefficient of front-loaded cascades were reduced by 21.78% and 24.16%, respectively, compared with aft-loaded cascades. This meant that the attack angle region with low cascade loss was greatly enlarged, thus proving the effectiveness of our modeling method and demonstrating its broad industrial application potential.

papers.title: Migration and plugging for temporary plugging balls in a multi-cluster fractured horizontal well
papers.abstract: Ball-throwing temporary plugging technology addresses non-uniform fracture propagation in multi-cluster fracturing, though controlling ball movement for effective sealing remains challenging. This study investigates the migration of temporary plugging balls in horizontal wells using experimental and numerical simulation approaches. The two-phase flow dynamics of the fracturing fluid and the ball are simulated using a coupled computational fluid dynamics-discrete element method, and the accuracy of this method is validated through experimental testing. The results demonstrate that a reduction in the ball velocity before entering the perforation cluster, combined with an increase in the radial displacement of the ball, is conducive to achieving effective temporary sealing of the perforation. Furthermore, the influence of ball and fracturing fluid parameters on the migration is systematically examined. The results indicate that the critical value for effective perforation plugging falls within a ball-to-perforation diameter ratio range of 1.08–1.15. The injection rate of the fracturing fluid primarily affects the ball's velocity, while the fluid viscosity predominantly influences the ball's radial displacement. Optimal conditions for migrating the ball to the perforation and achieving successful sealing are observed at an injection rate of 4 m3/min and a viscosity of 18 mPa s. By analyzing the two-phase flow dynamics of the fracturing fluid and the plugging ball, this study provides optimized parameters for ball size and fracturing fluid injection, offering valuable insights for enhancing the development efficiency of unconventional oil and gas resources.

papers.title: Effect of filter kernel on scale energetics of near-wall turbulent structures
papers.abstract: Inter-scale energy fluxes, Πλ, are widely used as a diagnostic tool to analyze energy transfer across length scales, λ, in turbulence data. Here, we investigate how the choice of filter kernel (sharp spectral, Gaussian, and box) affects the computed energy fluxes at constant filter width. We apply spatial filtering to a turbulent pipe flow simulation dataset and assess the effect on the local structure of Π. While the mean energy flux profile at each wall-normal distance is qualitatively robust across kernels, we observe significant differences in the intensity and spatial distribution of localized Π events. Correlations between typical flow structures in the buffer layer (streaks, vortices, and Q events) and regions of forward/backward transfer in the instantaneous Π field differ markedly between kernel types. Cross-correlations appear strongly upstream–downstream symmetric when using the sharp spectral kernel but asymmetric for the Gaussian and box kernels. For the Gaussian and box kernels Π events tend to localize along the inclined meander of streaks, while they are centered on top of the streaks for the sharp spectral kernel. Moreover, using the sharp spectral kernel, we observe a coincidence of backward scatter and fluid transport away from the wall (Q1), which does not appear with the Gaussian and box kernels. All kernels, however, predict backward scatter directly downstream of Q1 events. The results suggest that interpretations of inter-scale energy flux based on sharp spectral scale separation should be treated with caution, since such kernels act non-local in physical space, whereas Π events are inherently localized. Our Python post-processing tool eFlux for scale separation and energy flux analysis in pipe flows is freely available and readily adaptable to other flow configurations and filter widths.

papers.title: Influence of tip clearance on the flow field of variable inlet guide vane cascade in air storage centrifugal compressor
papers.abstract: This study investigated the impact of tip clearance on the aerodynamic performance of variable inlet guide vane (VIGV) cascade within a centrifugal compressor for compressed air energy storage. The exploration was carried out by combining numerical simulation and wind tunnel test validation. The study revealed that at 0.19Ma, tip clearance variations significantly affected the total pressure loss coefficient (Cpt), leakage flow, and deviation angle. Under small incidence angles (5°–20°), Cpt initially increased then decreased with larger clearances, peaking at 2.5% tip clearance (10% higher than original) and dropping by 30% at 10% tip clearance. Under large incidence angles (25°–30°), Cpt showed continuous reduction, achieving 30% decrease at 10% tip clearance. When tip clearance exceeded 7.5%, its impact on leakage flow diminished noticeably, while the effect on deviation angle remained limited (maximum 3° increase). This work filled a research gap regarding VIGV tip clearance effects and laid groundwork for future 3D guide vane clearance studies.

papers.title: Attenuating wake features of an underwater vehicle using deep reinforcement learning in an experimental environment
papers.abstract: The wake features of underwater vehicles play a crucial role in many underwater detection technologies. Effectively attenuating these features holds significant value in naval engineering applications. In this study, we propose a closed-loop control strategy aimed at attenuating wake features using deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-guided active flow control. An underwater vehicle model is towed in an automatic water tank at a Reynolds number of 105, based on the model length and towing velocity. Jet actuators positioned at the tail regulate wake flow dynamics, while velocities at 25 monitoring locations provide real-time feedback via a particle image velocimetry system and a graphics processing unit-accelerated optical flow algorithm. The DRL framework determines the control strategy through stochastic training in the towing tank. The trained DRL agent learns to suppress the variation rate of wake velocity to nearly zero and reduces turbulent kinetic energy by over 16% at 2.5 diameters downstream of the stern. Transfer learning applied to a higher Reynolds number case (Re=2×105) demonstrates superior performance compared to direct learning and realizes similar wake feature attenuation performance. This study validates the concept of hydrodynamic stealth in experimental and turbulent flow environments and confirms the effectiveness of DRL in developing robust flow control strategies for complex hydrodynamic scenarios.

papers.title: Effects of the anode vapor on the anode erosion with deformation in vacuum arc
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the anode deformation under the effects of the anode vapor in the vacuum arc. A self-consistent model is established to simulate the arc parameters, the anode temperature and the anode deformation. The simulations predict that the anode can be melted under sufficient high current, forming a melting pool on the anode surface. When the anode temperature is high enough, the anode vapor has great effects on the fluidity of the melting pool on the anode surface. In addition, the movement of the melting pool can affect the anode temperature and thus affect the anode vapor characteristics. The melting pool can exist even after the current zero, which may be harmful to the post-arc period. Simulation results indicate that a self-consistent model is necessary for analyzing the anode deformation.

papers.title: Near-wall turbulent fluctuations and coherent structures in wall-modeled large-eddy simulation
papers.abstract: Wall-modeled large-eddy simulation (WMLES) of turbulent channel flow is performed to evaluate its predictive capability for near-wall turbulent fluctuations, coherent structures, and turbulence kinetic energy (TKE) budget—aspects that have received relatively little attention in previous studies. Our investigation begins with a low Reynolds number case (Reτ ≈ 1000) to establish the baseline performance of WMLES, followed by an assessment of its generalizability under moderately higher Reynolds number conditions (Reτ ≈ 5200). The results show that WMLES tends to overestimate the low-wavenumber (frequency) component of wall pressure fluctuations. Two convection ridges are observed in its wavenumber-frequency spectra. Further analyses reveal that the additional low-speed convection ridge is primarily attributed to the low-speed wall-attached eddies. When the first-layer grid height is large, these wall-attached eddies are nonphysically elongated in the wall-normal direction. Under-resolving buffer layer degrades streak coherence, suppresses ejection (Q2), and sweep (Q4) events. The probability density function of streamwise velocity fluctuations at y+=15 tends to a Gaussian distribution, indicating a loss of turbulence anisotropy and intermittency. Additionally, a term-by-term comparison of TKE budget equation indicates a shift in the turbulent core region near the wall—from a fully resolved balance between turbulence production (Pk) and viscous dissipation (ε) to a balance dominated by Pk and turbulent transport (Tk). To improve the predictive accuracy of WMLES for near-wall turbulence fluctuations and coherent structures, appropriately resolving the buffer layer (Δyw+=10) is essential. The conclusions of this study are consistent across the range of Reynolds numbers considered.

papers.title: Global stability prediction of compression ramp flow based on deep neural networks
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks incorporating an AutoEncoder architecture are applied to compression ramp flow with shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction. This study aims to demonstrate how the fusion of aerodynamic data distributed over the compression ramp surface enables global stability predictions of compression ramp flow using high-fidelity data from small datasets, thereby significantly reducing data acquisition costs. The deep learning model is trained on direct numerical simulations of supersonic to hypersonic compression ramp flows, with global stability assessed using global stability analysis. The predictions agree well with experimental data and numerical simulations across a wide range of freestream Mach numbers, Reynolds number, far-field flow temperature, ramp angle of the geometry, and wall temperature ratio. Furthermore, by leveraging feature extraction techniques to train the model on a limited set of critical data points, the results remain highly accurate. This highlights an effective approach for optimizing sensor quantity and placement to evaluate the global stability of flows.

papers.title: Robust enhanced sound insulation of advanced nanoparticle-reinforced carbon fiber double-walled panel under external mean flow
papers.abstract: This study established a theoretical model of vibro-acoustic coupling for the double-walled panel composed of nanoparticle-reinforced carbon fiber laminates with external mean flow. The effects of external mean flow and the mass of the nanoparticle on the sound transmission loss (STL) characteristics of nanoparticle-reinforced carbon fiber double-walled panel were investigated. Theoretical calculations indicate that the mass of inclusion particles and external mean flow have a significant impact on the STL of the structure. Under the combined effects of inclusion particle mass, external flow, and boundary conditions, the structure shows a remarkable improvement in STL at low frequencies. Based on the designability of nanoparticle-reinforced carbon fiber laminates, a configuration of double-walled panel was proposed that exhibits exceptional sound insulation performance at high Mach numbers. These results demonstrate the potential of this study in the improvement of sound insulation applications of carbon fiber double-walled panels.

papers.title: Predicting surface pressure fields and lift coefficients of subsonic airfoils by machine-learning-enhanced compressive sensing framework
papers.abstract: Aerodynamic performance assessment is pivotal in aircraft design optimization, yet traditional airfoil optimization methods remain computationally expensive and inefficient. To address this challenge, we introduce a machine-learning-enhanced compressive sensing (ML-CS) framework that synergizes data-driven learning with compressive sensing to accurately predict surface pressure fields and lift coefficients of subsonic airfoils. A geometry-informed sparse sampling strategy is developed using airfoil camber-thickness curve parameterization, enabling efficient feature extraction from limited training data. The development of the ML-CS framework employs a three-stage process: first, the ML-CS reconstruction efficiency is optimized, achieving more than 92% accuracy in pressure coefficient prediction using only ten sparse sensors; second, a Kriging-surrogate-assisted sensor value prediction method that robustly preserves prediction accuracy despite missing sensor data is proposed; third, a lift coefficient prediction module that reduces errors by 35.5% compared to conventional surrogate models while simultaneously reconstructing surface pressure distributions is proposed. The framework demonstrates superior efficiency and generalizability, offering a paradigm shift in aerodynamic surrogate modeling.

papers.title: Nonlinear Rayleigh-Taylor instability of pendent finite-thickness film subjected to vibration
papers.abstract: In this study, the realization of nonlinear saturation states in Rayleigh-Taylor instability subjected to vertical vibration is extended beyond the constraints of the thin film regime through comprehensive linear stability analysis and direct numerical simulations. The linear analysis reveals that increasing fluid layer thickness significantly reduces critical amplitudes for the onset of Faraday instability (FI) at low frequencies, while this effect diminishes at high frequencies due to the associated increase in critical wavenumber. The nonlinear evolution of perturbation amplitude proceeds through three distinct stages: growth, decay, and quasi-steady evolution. The excitation and eventual stabilization of FI are clarified using the local average thickness model, which demonstrates the coupling mechanism between FI mode amplitude and local thickness variations. It is found that the saturated amplitude of the interface decreases with increasing vibration amplitudes. Furthermore, the presence of stable RT modes is shown to effectively suppress FI, ultimately leading the interface to harmonic saturated states.

papers.title: Three-dimensional disturbances in a conducting liquid film flowing down an inclined plane in the presence of constant electromagnetic field
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional stability features of an electrically conducting viscous liquid film flowing down an inclined plane are investigated under the action of gravitational force, surface tension as well as magnetic and coupling influence of electric and magnetic (electromagnetic) field of forces. Our (linear and nonlinear stability) analysis, based on the three-dimensional wave equation which is nonlinear in nature and obtained by using the classical momentum-integral method, indicates the reality of four different (explosive, supercritical, unconditional and subcritical) flow zones of this flow problem depending upon the sign of the curves ωi+ (temporal growth rate) and J2 (second Landau constant) which contain electric parameter E, magnetic parameter M, Reynolds number Re, Weber number We, angle of inclination θ, and angle of propagation φ.
