This design achieves notable force mitigation and trajectory stabilization, suggesting a promising strategy for high-speed water-entry vehicles.

papers.title: Pore-scale insight into the impact of heterogeneity in porous media on CO2–oil immiscible displacement
papers.abstract: CCUS (carbon dioxide capture, utilization, and storage) technology constitutes a pivotal solution for achieving net-zero carbon emissions. As an important implementation pathway of CCUS, CO2–Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) can not only enable CO2 storage but also substantially improve the hydrocarbons production. The pore structure of reservoir porous media greatly impacts microscopic CO2 displacement, which is crucial for CO2–EOR. Pore-structure heterogeneity, a dominant factor in CO2 flooding, exerts pivotal control over displacement dynamics, which remains unclear. To bridge gaps, this study employs pore-scale numerical simulations coupling the Navier–Stokes (N-S) equations with phase-field method to elucidate heterogeneity effects on immiscible CO2–oil displacement. The recovery in porous media, the types of residual oil, and the morphology of the CO2–oil displacement front are systematically investigated across varying capillary numbers (Ca) and wettability conditions. The results demonstrate that enhanced heterogeneity induces preferential flow channel development in porous media, which accelerates CO2 breakthrough time and impairs oil recovery efficiency. In highly heterogeneous models, Ca effects are diminished with displacement front shape and residual oil distribution dominated by heterogeneity, and oil recovery even decreases anomalously with increasing Ca. Contact angle (θ) impact on heterogeneity depends on wettability: under oil-wet conditions (θ < π/2), higher θ mitigates CO2 channeling from heterogeneity, while under CO2-wet conditions (θ > π/2), higher θ exacerbates such channeling. This study reveals the critical role of pore-scale heterogeneity in CO2–oil displacement, which is significant for optimizing CO2–EOR efficiency.

papers.title: Drag correlations and flow evolution of non-spherical biomass particles in fluidized beds via experimental and numerical perspectives
papers.abstract: Biomass energy has attracted considerable attention as a renewable and clean energy source that can be stored and transported effectively. A critical component in this context is the fluidized bed, which plays a vital role in biomass energy utilization. An in-depth understanding of the flow characteristics of non-spherical biomass particles within the fluidized bed is essential for improving energy efficiency. This study utilizes a combination of numerical simulations and experimental analysis to explore the flow patterns of biomass particles under eight distinct drag correlations. The investigation covers various flow regimes in the fluidized bed, concentrating on critical parameters such as flow evolution, gas-phase pressure distribution, particle phase velocity vectors, bed pressure drop, particle mixing characteristics, bed expansion height, and the energy-dynamic behavior of the particles. The results indicate that the Ergun resistance model closely matches the experimental data, particularly regarding the flow evolution of the particles. This model shows a more uniform mixing of the particles and greater stability in the magnitude and frequency of pressure fluctuations at the bed surface. This stability is reflected in the average pressure drop, highlighting the enhanced performance of the fluidized bed. Overall, this research sheds light on the intricate dynamics of non-spherical biomass particles in fluidized beds and provides valuable insights for optimizing particle design. By focusing on design enhancements, it is possible to achieve higher combustion efficiency, supporting the broader objective of sustainable energy utilization. In summary, this study emphasizes the significance of precise modeling and understanding of flow characteristics in the fluidized bed, which is crucial for advancing biomass energy technologies.

papers.title: A high-order flux reconstruction solver of the linearized Euler equation for acoustic wave propagation
papers.abstract: This paper presents a high-order flux reconstruction solver for the linearized Euler equations, developed to accurately simulate acoustic wave propagation in complex media. The solver utilizes polynomial-based approximations to construct the local solution and employs correction functions for flux-derivative reconstruction. Temporal integration is performed using a five-stage, fourth-order Runge–Kutta scheme. The solver also incorporates automatic derivative computation for the mean flow fields using the polynomial approximation. Numerical tests confirm that the solver achieves the expected (p+1)-th order convergence rate, where p is the polynomial order. A series of benchmark problems illustrates the framework's efficiency in handling unstructured meshes, complex boundary conditions, acoustic scattering in non-uniform flows, flow-induced noise, and large-scale parallel computations. Further analyses of shear-flow cases demonstrate the solver's ability in mitigating numerical instabilities and underscore the importance of choosing suitable equation formulations based on flow characteristics.

papers.title: Analysis of three-dimensional flow characteristics around a finite-length square cylinder based on proper orthogonal decomposition and high-order dynamic mode decomposition approaches
papers.abstract: This study integrates Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and High-Order Dynamic Mode Decomposition (HODMD) reduced-order model (POD-HODMD), combining POD's energy-ranking capability with HODMD's frequency uniqueness, which establishes systematic correlations, energy, and frequency. Using POD-HODMD as a tool, the study analyzes the flow characteristics of a three-dimensional square prism through integrated wind tunnel tests and computational fluid dynamics simulations. The results reveal three dominant frequency bands: the vortex shedding band, the low-frequency band, and the high-frequency band. The vortex shedding band governs the crosswind force, driven by flow separation and reattachment at the structure's edges, forming a C-shaped pressure gradient and periodic vortex shedding in the wake. The low-frequency band dominates the along-wind force, manifested through a significant pressure difference between the windward and leeward sides, accounting for large-amplitude low-frequency vibrations. The high-frequency band induces instantaneous vortex generation and dissipation, leading to turbulent fluctuations. The reduced-order model effectively identifies dominant modes in both the pressure and velocity fields and facilitates quantitative characterization of the dynamic interactions between wind and structure. This research offers a robust tool for improving structural safety and wind load predictions in wind engineering.

papers.title: Two-way coupled large eddy simulation for non-equilibrium suspended sediment transport
papers.abstract: Non-equilibrium suspended sediment transport in coastal engineering is characterized by complex interactions among turbulent flows, seabed topography, and structures. This study developed a two-way coupled large eddy simulation suspended sediment transport model sedTransFoam based on the open-source OpenFOAM framework. The solver comprehensively accounts for turbulence modulation caused by high-concentration sediment and interactions between sediment. Additionally, it incorporates a flux boundary condition based on turbulent burst theory to accurately simulate instantaneous sediment transport characteristics under strong turbulence effects. The sloped terrain and pile group structure generate complex turbulence-sediment interactions, making them a classic setting for studying non-equilibrium suspended sediment transport. The solver is employed to investigate sediment dynamics, where sloped terrain and pile groups generate complex turbulence and sediment transport patterns. The simulations demonstrate that the sloped terrain induces large-scale Kelvin–Helmholtz vortices, which drive erosion through enhanced shear stress. Pile groups shift vortices toward interfaces, where shear stress and turbulent kinetic energy primarily govern sediment transport. Transverse momentum exchange is predominantly driven by turbulent mixing (accounting for approximately 75%), while high-density pile configurations increase siltation due to reduced turbulence scales.

papers.title: Framework and computational model of bubble dynamics under water
papers.abstract: Bubble dynamics under water is significant for both life and engineering applications since 71% of the Earth is covered by water. In this paper, the classical models of bubble dynamics are reviewed and analyzed, and we propose an advanced model, named the Adeba–Fan model; meanwhile, the framework and computational methods are illustrated. The Adeba–Fan model systematically incorporates the key physical mechanisms—shock wave propagation, thermal conduction, evaporation and condensation, viscosity, surface tension, compressibility, and gravitation—within a unified framework, ensuring applicability across all scenarios. A central feature of the model is the use of retarded time corrections, which refine the velocity potential and pressure formulations to consistently capture finite wave propagation effects. The theoretical formulation, based on the fundamental conservation laws of mass, momentum, and energy, ensures a consistent representation of the underlying physics, while detailed mathematical derivations and computational methods are presented. The model is capable of simulating spherical bubble behavior in an incompressible–compressible fluid across diverse input energy scales and fluid depths. Validation via experimental data and theoretical benchmarks, including laser-induced cavitation and underwater explosions at various water depths, demonstrates its superior accuracy in capturing bubble growth, collapse, rebound, shockwave interactions, and thermal effects. A Comparative analysis with existing models highlights its advantages in prediction accuracy, application range, and computational efficiency. Therefore, the Adeba–Fan model advances the study of bubble dynamics under water and provides a robust tool for applications in marine engineering, industrial cavitation, and underwater explosion analysis.

papers.title: Experimental and numerical investigation of heat transfer deterioration in upward vertical flow of supercritical hydrocarbon fuel
papers.abstract: Regenerative cooling technology holds significant promise for high-Mach-number propulsion systems. In such systems, hydrocarbon fuels enter supercritical states, exhibiting highly nonlinear thermophysical property variations and anomalous heat transfer behavior. This study conducts a systematic experimental investigation of the heat transfer characteristics of supercritical hydrocarbon fuel under varying heat flux and mass flow rate conditions. The wall-temperature-based criterion is employed to classify heat transfer regimes along the flow path, revealing that heat transfer deterioration (HTD) occurs under conditions of high heat flux and low mass flow. Building on these observations, a coupled numerical model is utilized to explore the underlying mechanisms of HTD and its influence on thermal stress. It is found that the velocity profile evolves from a “U” shape to an “M” shape due to thermal acceleration. The thermal acceleration effect leads to stratification of velocity and density. This results in the formation of a laminarized boundary layer and a consequent reduction in turbulent kinetic energy. The flow and thermal stratification severely hinder the efficient transport of heat from the near-wall region to the core flow. The temperature rise causes the near-wall thermal conductivity to decrease by nearly 50%, thereby increasing the thermal-conduction resistance. The resulting increase in local temperature gradients leads to a 6.6% rise in thermal stress. These findings offer valuable insights for the design of cooling channels and the safe operation of regenerative cooling systems.

papers.title: Unsteady flow field analysis of suction surface adjustable vane
papers.abstract: The variable area guide vane is a core component of variable cycle engine. At present, the main type of variable area vane works by varying the installation angle. However, leakage flow and varied installation angle introduce pressure losses and offset the gains of the variable cycle. This paper investigated the suction surface adjustable guide vane as an alternative type to the variable installation angle guide vane. The delayed detached-eddy simulation method was adopted to analyze the pressure waves, shock waves, wake vortices, and the interference between shock waves and wake vortices for the suction surface adjustable guide vane. The mass flow rate, pressure loss characteristics, and outlet flow angle of suction surface adjustable guide vane and variable installation angle guide vane were compared. The results indicated that in the suction surface adjustable guide vane, when the suction surface rotated by 5°, two shock waves appeared, and the shock waves accelerated the dissipation speed of wake vortices. For suction surface adjustable guide vane, when the mass flow rate decreased by 17%, total pressure loss coefficient increased by 0.04, and the outflow angle decreased by 2.2°. For variable installation angle guide vane, under the same mass flow adjustment, the total pressure loss coefficient increased by 0.06–0.09, and the outlet flow angle changed by 5°–7°. The suction surface adjustable guide vane demonstrated effective control of flow capacity, with lower pressure losses and smaller changes in outlet flow angle compared with the variable installation angle guide vane.

papers.title: Prediction and verification of virgin rock temperature in deep-buried tunnels in complex mountainous areas
papers.abstract: Active faults are prominent in the Gaoligong Mountain deep-buried tunnel, presenting significant geological challenges such as high geothermal heat, high-pressure and high-temperature water, and high ground stress. Accurate prediction of the virgin rock temperature is crucial for ventilation and cooling design during tunnel construction and operation. To better solve the problem of predicting the temperature field and virgin rock temperature of deep-buried tunnels in complex mountainous areas, this paper integrates key technical data from such regions, including complex undulating terrain, geological structures, high-temperature water, surface temperature variations, borehole temperature measurements, and rock thermal properties. This study examines the coupled heat transfer mechanism between groundwater and underground rocks in mountainous areas. It also investigates the analysis principles and calculation methods for predicting the temperature field and virgin rock temperature of deep-buried tunnels under nonlinear hydrothermal coupling, scale effects, and complex boundary and initial conditions. Building on this, a digital-twin geothermal analysis and inversion system for complex mountainous areas were developed and validated against measurements from the Gaoligong Mountain tunnel. The system demonstrated excellent agreement, with absolute errors of −0.91 to +0.71 °C and relative errors of −2.4% to +1.88%. This validates the predictive theory, calculation methods, and formulation of boundary and initial conditions for deep-buried geothermal fields and virgin rock temperatures in mountainous areas. The research provides accurate predictions of the temperature field and virgin rock temperature in deep-buried tunnels within complex mountainous regions, offering crucial technical support for railway route selection and for designing effective ventilation and heat-damage prevention strategies during tunnel construction and operation.

papers.title: A novel residual multilayer perceptron-based graph convolutional network for modeling heat transfer and fluid flow
papers.abstract: Conventional computational fluid dynamics methods are computationally intensive for tasks such as design optimization and real-time control, and while convolutional neural network-based surrogates potentially offer faster alternatives, their reliance on structured grids, static neighborhood definitions, and limited extrapolation capabilities highlights the need for more flexible and generalizable frameworks. Graph convolutional networks (GCNs), with their ability to operate on unstructured meshes and dynamically encode spatial relationships, offer a compelling alternative. In this work, a novel residual multilayer perceptron-based GCN (ResMLP-GCN) architecture is proposed, and its utility is demonstrated by applying it to three benchmark problems: (i) transient non-linear diffusion–advection problem, (ii) double lid-driven cavity flow, and (iii) backward-facing step flow. The developed models are trained on data from numerical simulations, using nodal coordinates and physical field variables as node features, employing a finite element-inspired hypergraph ϕ topology. The heat transfer model, trained on data from t=0 to 1000 s, accurately predicts the spatiotemporal evolution of temperature fields up to t=2000 s, maintaining relative errors below 8%. In the double lid-driven cavity problem, the model trained on Reynolds numbers ranging from 100 to 2000 achieves mean percentage errors under 14% when evaluated on extrapolated Reynolds numbers up to 3000. Similarly, for the backward-facing step, the model predicts the reattachment lengths for extrapolated Re with relative errors below 3%. These results highlight the potential of ResMLP-GCNs to capture complex spatiotemporal dynamics and generalize across temporal and parametric domains, offering a robust surrogate modeling strategy for heat and fluid flow problems.

papers.title: An improved forcing scheme for high-density-ratio multiphase flows based on the three-dimensional cumulant lattice Boltzmann method
papers.abstract: This study presents an improved forcing scheme for high-density-ratio multiphase flow simulations within the three-dimensional cumulant lattice Boltzmann method. By modifying the structurally compatible forcing scheme and conducting rigorous asymptotic analysis of second-order correction terms, we successfully integrate the pseudopotential model with the three-dimensional twenty-seven velocities (D3Q27) cumulant lattice Boltzmann method for high-density-ratio simulations, which is performed for the first time and achieves remarkable density ratios. The proposed scheme concurrently satisfies the macroscopic Navier–Stokes equations and thermodynamic consistency while preserving the core architecture of the original forcing scheme. Enhanced thermodynamic consistency is achieved through optimized correction terms derived from asymptotic analysis. Numerical validation reveals significant stability improvements, attaining minimal reduced temperatures of 0.135 and 0.387 for planar and curved interfaces, respectively, under the pseudopotential model. The scheme achieves a maximum density ratio enhancement exceeding two orders of magnitude compared with existing cumulant-based forcing schemes, demonstrating enhanced numerical stability. The practical utility of the scheme is confirmed through simulations of wettability-driven droplet dynamics and ternary droplet coalescence phenomena. The quantitative agreement between numerically predicted capillary phenomena in square channels and prior experimental correlations further validates the applicability to practical multiphase flow systems. This work establishes a framework for implementing the pseudopotential model within the D3Q27 cumulant lattice Boltzmann method, offering a reference for high-density-ratio flow simulations.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of flow and heat transfer in turbine blade tip clearances across actual and approximate cascade configurations
papers.abstract: Simplified linear and annular cascades have frequently been used by researchers to conduct extensive experimental and numerical studies on flow and heat transfer in tip clearances of turbine rotor blades. However, these studies often ignore the differences in flow and heat transfer characteristics between actual cascade configurations (the fully representative annular cascades with rotating, three-dimensional twisted blades and realistic geometric scaling) and approximate cascade configurations (simplified models including both static blade and static shroud setups, as well as static blades with moving shroud simulating relative motion). This study employs three-dimensional steady Reynolds averaged Navier–Stokes simulations with the standard k–ω turbulence model to systematically analyze different relative motion mechanisms, including actual blade rotation (within the actual cascade), shroud rotation/translation (as part of approximate cascades), static conditions (also part of approximate cascades), and various operating conditions covering typical engineering values of tip clearance ranges (0.5%–8% span), based on a gas turbine rotor blade. Key flow phenomena identified include the presence of corner vortex structures dominating flat tip flows, while squealer tips exhibit complex vortex systems comprising pressure side cavity vortexes, suction side cavity vortexes, and scraping vortexes (SV) under relative motion conditions. Under static conditions, the SV is absent. The flat tip with shroud translation effectively simulates the impact of clearance variations under the actual blade rotation condition. This study provides a theoretical basis for selecting experimental cascade configurations and offers critical support and data references for evaluating gas turbine performance and optimizing blade designs.

papers.title: Gravity wave interaction of fibrillar adhesive floating breakwater proximity to rigid and porous structures positioned at a finite distance from a monotonically decreasing seabed
papers.abstract: The influence of proximity rigid and porous structure for mitigating the wave force and excessive motion on the fibrillar adhesive floating breakwater positioned at a finite distance from the monotonically decreasing seabed is investigated under the presumption of linear water wave theory. The objective of the study is to examine various hydrodynamic characteristics associated with wave scattering and radiation, including the added mass and radiation damping coefficients, which pertain to the heave, surge, and pitch motions of the fibrillar adhesive floating breakwater, as well as the vertical force, horizontal force, and moment acting on the fibrillar adhesive floating breakwater across a range of wave and structural parameters. The physical setup is solved semi-analytically by employing the Eigenfunction expansion method and multi-domain boundary element method, and its findings are validated against prior studies. The study reveals that the decrease in the friction coefficient of the porous structure enhances resonant peaks in wave force, moment, added mass, and damping coefficient corresponding to all motions of the fibrillar adhesive floating breakwater. Further, the larger ripple amplitude of the monotonically decreasing seabed alters the pressure distribution and wave kinematics on the fibrillar adhesive floating breakwater. Moreover, the surface elevation is most prominent around structural gaps and the recesses and edges of the step-like front face of the fibrillar adhesive floating breakwater, where constructive interference and partial wave entrapment occur. Thus, by focusing on wave-structure interaction modeling and system-level performance evaluation of fibrillar adhesive floating breakwater, this paper lays a strong foundation for subsequent research that will include parametric studies, material optimization, and large-scale prototype development in diverse coastal applications.

papers.title: Development of a chemistry model for vibronically excited species in direct simulation Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: This article presents the derivation of a five-species air mixture chemistry model that accounts for the electronic excitation of all species. The chemistry model consists of a vibronic extension of the quantum-kinetic (QK) chemistry models for the direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method. Grounded on first-principle calculations and benefiting from the development of the vibronic model in DSMC, the vibronic QK model provides an electronic state-specific description of kinetic processes. The vibronic QK model is validated against the most representative experimental measurements and quasi-classical trajectory calculations for the 19 chemical reactions constitutive of the five-species air model in both thermal equilibrium and non-equilibrium. The vibronic QK model demonstrates excellent reproduction of the reference database in both thermal equilibrium and non-equilibrium. The vibronic QK model presents slower reaction rates than the former QK model, especially for the dissociation of nitric oxide. Additionally, the model is verified for the decomposition of an air mixture in typical post-shock flow conditions. It is shown that the vibronic QK model accurately recovers the detailed balance principle and achieves appropriate thermochemical equilibrium. Finally, the model is applied to canonical hypersonic flows past a cylinder body, demonstrating the inaccuracy of the traditional assumption of the electronically excited states being distributed according to the Boltzmann statistics. It is also shown that the population of the electronically excited states and their vibrational quantum levels strongly deviate between the two approaches, suggesting a significant impact on the line intensity of the molecular species' absorption spectrum.

papers.title: A generalized correlation for predicting microdroplet sizes in a squeezer T-junction microfluidic device with various squeezer types
papers.abstract: This paper describes an extensive study on the dynamic behaviors of droplet formation in a Squeezer T-junction Microfluidic Device (STMFD) with various squeezers. The effects of squeezer size (Ws), squeezer location (Ls), water fraction (wf), and capillary number (Ca) on the droplet formation in this device were explored. The two-phase fluid flow in the microchannel is captured using the two-dimensional finite volume method and the volume of fluid model. This study aims to determine the squeezer shape, size, and position to expand the stable droplet formation region and generate uniform-sized droplets efficiently. Consequently, the droplet formation regime, droplet size, and droplet generation frequency are affected significantly by the presence of the squeezers. A rectangle-shaped squeezer design shows the most effective generation in the squeezing mode among the shapes considered. Then, phase diagrams of the droplet formation are constructed elaborately for this squeezer-shaped design. Particularly, a generalized correlation as a function of four important parameters (Ws, Ls, wf, and Ca) is first proposed to quickly and effectively predict the droplet size in the STMFD for various squeezer types. These results enhance the understanding of microdroplet dynamics in T-junction devices, offering potential applications in biomedical and drug delivery systems.

papers.title: Magnetohydrodynamic natural convection of a ternary nanofluid with variable properties in a wavy trapezoidal enclosure
papers.abstract: This study deals with the natural convective ternary hybrid nanofluid flow in a trapezoidal enclosure bounded by a wavy sidewall. The effects of the magnetic field and variable thermophysical properties are also included. Here, the ternary nanofluid is a water-based suspension of copper (Cu), silicon dioxide (SiO2), and multi-walled carbon nanotube nanoparticles. The governing equations with considered physics were first converted into dimensionless equations, which were then transformed into a system suitable for the computational domain. The system is then solved utilizing the efficient compact finite difference method. Flow and heat transfer behaviors are illustrated with volume fraction φ (=0%–2%), inclined wall angle with Y-axis θs (=−15°–20°), Rayleigh number Ra (=103–106), and Hartmann number Ha (=0–70). Interestingly, flow intensity and heat transfer show different behaviors for variable and constant thermophysical properties. As φ increases from 0% to 1.5% the flow intensity decreases, while a small increase is found for the increment from 1.5% to 2%. The converse pattern in the flow field occurs for increasing θs. However, the magnitude of the stream function significantly increases with higher Ra and decreases for increasing Ha. A significant increase in the heat transfer occurs with the increment of Ra and θs and a decrease happens for larger Ha.

papers.title: Influence of trailing-edge flaps on the flow field and noise generation characteristics of airfoils
papers.abstract: High-lift flow control devices are widely used in the aerospace field. Currently, most research on high-lift devices focuses on the impact of flaps on the aerodynamic characteristics of modified wing profiles, while studies on the mechanisms and characteristics of noise generation caused by the addition of high-lift flow control devices are relatively scarce. This study employs delayed detachment edy simulation and the Ffowcs Williams–Hawkings acoustic analogy method to numerically simulate the flow field around the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) 0021 airfoil at an angle of attack of 15°, systematically investigating the effects of trailing edge flaps (TEFs)—a high-lift device—on energy distribution, flow field structure, and noise generation and characteristics. The results indicate that compared to the original airfoil, the flow field around the airfoil with a TEF exhibits a reduction in noise at medium and low frequencies, with a maximum reduction of 21.51 dB. However, broadband noise increases in the medium and high-frequency ranges, with a maximum increase of 19.12 dB, and the average total sound pressure level increases by 3.83 dB. By integrating the analysis of time-averaged pressure pulsation distribution and boundary enstrophy flux (BEF)analysis for different airfoils, it was revealed that the periodic trailing edge separation vortices and their interactions, along with the increased vorticity generated by the wall, leading to an increase in vortex structures, are the primary causes of the increased noise in the TEF airfoil. The results of this study not only provide new insights into the noise mechanisms of high-lift wing profiles but also offer important references for noise reduction designs based on flow control.

papers.title: Effects of wake-added turbulence on extreme loads and fatigue damage of floating offshore wind turbines
papers.abstract: Wake-added turbulence (WAT) is a critical component of wake effects in floating wind farms. Although previous studies have shown that wakes reduce the inflow wind speed and increase turbulence intensity for wake-affected floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), the specific impacts of wake effects and WAT on FOWTs under identical mean inflow wind speed conditions remain insufficiently quantified. To address this gap, an unwaked FOWT with the same average inflow wind speed as the wake-affected FOWT is established to enable comparative analysis of the dynamic responses, thereby investigating the influence of wake effects on FOWTs. WAT is further incorporated to assess its impact on the dynamic responses of wake-affected FOWTs. The average conditional exceedance rate method is employed to estimate short-term extreme loads, and short-term damage equivalent loads are calculated at critical structural locations. Results show that, compared to the unwaked FOWT, the surge motion and structural load amplitudes of the wake-affected FOWT exhibits up to 42% and 28%, respectively. Neglecting wake effects can lead to an underestimation of short-term extreme loads by approximately 10%. Under below-rated wind speed, WAT intensifies wake effects, increasing structural load amplitudes by about 7%, and causing fatigue loads to be underestimated by up to 8% if WAT is not considered. This study quantitatively analyzes wake effects and WAT on FOWT responses, offering insights for structural design verification and fatigue life prediction of FOWTs, and contributing to the refinement of wake modeling in international design standards.

papers.title: Experimental investigation on the vibration response of an inclined near-wall flexible pipe span conveying different internal flows
papers.abstract: This paper reports the experimental results of the vortex-induced vibration (VIV) and pipe-wall impact of an inclined near-wall flexible pipe transporting three representative internal flows with oblique angle (θ) ranging from 0° to 45°. The flexible pipe with an aspect ratio of 57 was fixed at both ends. The tests were performed in a recirculation water flume in the reduced velocity range of Ur = 7.92–23.92 using the non-intrusive optical measurement. The experimental results indicate that the existence of internal flow causes the tilt of the peaks of root-mean-squared (RMS) amplitude toward the downstream of internal flow. Nevertheless, with increasing θ, the peaks of RMS amplitude tilt to the upstream of internal flow. The mode competition of the pipe conveying gas flow is the weakest, but it is the most sensitive to θ. In contrast, the most intense mode competitions are observed in the pipe conveying gas–liquid flow and the pipe conveying liquid flow for the in-line and cross-flow directions, respectively. Five pipe-wall impact patterns are identified based on the impact position and frequency, and the partition of wall-impact pattern is provided in the s/L–Urn diagram. The impact position undergoes spatial transfer with the change of θ, especially for the pipe conveying gas flow. By comprehensive consideration of the spatial-temporal evolution of VIV response and impacting segments, the independence principle is invalid in predicting the VIV of near-wall flexible pipe span conveying internal flow.

papers.title: Taylor cone film-jet electrospray
papers.abstract: We present an electrospray configuration in which a thin, low-viscosity charged liquid film flows over a rigid dielectric cone set to the Taylor angle and converges toward the apex, where it is expelled as a steady micro- or nanojet. The method relies on the existence of an inertial region near the cone tip, where inertial forces overwhelm viscous diffusion. Beyond a critical axial distance, viscous effects dominate, but the system's fundamental properties—emitted current and jet diameter—are fixed within the inviscid zone. Analytical solutions describe both the inner (inviscid) and outer (viscous) film regimes, showing that—unlike the classical Taylor cone–jet—the electric current is decoupled from bulk conductivity and flow rate, and depends only on the applied field. This enables stable electrosprays of ultrapure water at flow rates down to 0.2 nl/min, far below the classical limit, without conductivity adjustment or auxiliary gas. The theory further predicts that jets are emitted overcharged relative to the Rayleigh limit, producing rapid convective instabilities while overall stability is preserved by the solid cone. This opens access to regimes unreachable by conventional electrosprays, including steady low-current jets and high-specific impulse operation relevant to electrospray ionization mass spectrometry, single-cell proteomics, and space microthrusters. Initial experiments with polymeric high-resolution printed cones demonstrate their operational robustness and confirm the predicted current–voltage scaling and ultra-low-flow operation, validating the model and consolidating this electrospray mode as both a fundamental electrohydrodynamic regime and a practical platform for ultra-low-flow applications.

papers.title: Investigation on the influence of vertical baffles on the internal surface sloshing in a rectangular tank with two immiscible liquids
papers.abstract: An experimental investigation is conducted on the effects of vertical baffles on resonant sloshing at the internal surface in a two-dimensional (2D) rectangular tank filled with two immiscible liquids. This work established three experimental devices with different oil–water height ratios to explore the inhibitory effect of baffles and the number of baffles on internal surface resonant sloshing. Special attention is given to the internal surface wave amplitudes at the first mode, third mode, and fifth mode resonant conditions of the internal surface. Experimental findings reveal that at the first mode resonant condition of the internal surface, the presence of vertical baffles significantly suppress internal surface sloshing amplitudes, where the suppression effect exhibits a linear relationship with baffle quantity. At the resonant condition of the third mode, the influence of baffles on the internal surface motion has no certain regularity. Under the fifth mode resonant condition, the introduction of vertical baffles conversely enhances internal surface wave amplitude. In addition, the influence of the number of baffles on the internal surface sloshing is independent of changes in the oil-water height ratio.

papers.title: Lattice Boltzmann study on sedimentation behavior of two porous particles with different Darcy numbers in a narrow channel
papers.abstract: This study investigates the sedimentation behavior of two porous particles under gravity in a two-dimensional (2D) infinite channel using the multiple-relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann method. Three cases of initial configurations are considered for the Darcy number (Da) of particles, i.e., two particles with identical Da (case 1); the trailing particle with higher Da than the leading particle (case 2); and the leading particle with higher Da than the trailing particle (case 3). The dynamics of the drafting, kissing, and tumbling (DKT) process are examined during the particle-pair sedimentation. The results show that the increase in Da reduces the settling velocity and weakens the wake-induced hydrodynamic effects between particles, which enhances their ability to maintain the vertical alignment upon contact. When the Darcy number becomes sufficiently large, the increased fluid penetration through the particles enhances the flow velocity in their wake, which makes the two porous particles no longer come into contact while maintain a stable gap. Depending on the combination of Da for the particle pair, several sedimentation modes are identified in a phase diagram, including periodic, staggered equilibrium, aligned equilibrium, and individual settling modes during the DKT process. Especially, when the trailing particle holds a large Da, the two porous particles may span multiple transitions from periodic state to individually settling state. These findings provide new insight into porous particle interactions and may guide the control of particle settling in engineering applications, such as fluidized beds and mineral separation.

papers.title: Large-eddy simulation of bio-inspired leading-edge deformation for cavitation control on a hydrofoil
papers.abstract: Inspired by the water-entry head morphology of cetaceans, this study investigates a biomimetic leading-edge deformation strategy for a symmetric NACA (National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics) 0009 hydrofoil (with chord length C = 100 mm). A series of deformation configurations was constructed by systematically varying the leading-edge deformation region (x0) and nose-drop distance (d0), and their cavitation control performance was evaluated in detail. High-fidelity large-eddy simulations were conducted to analyze the cavity structure, boundary layer characteristics, and hydrodynamic responses of each configuration. The results reveal that moderate leading-edge deformations (d0 > 0.02C, x0 = 0.2C–0.4C) significantly reduce cavity size, suppress unsteady cloud cavitation, and induce strong favorable pressure gradients near the cavity closure. These changes accelerate the boundary layer and enhance near-wall momentum transport, leading to a reduction in the resolved Reynolds shear stress. As the reentrant jet weakens and the cavity becomes more stable, vortex structures remain attached to the suction surface, resulting in a more stable and orderly flow field. Meanwhile, the lift-to-drag ratio increases substantially from 14.46 for the original hydrofoil to 45.67 under typical deformation parameters (x0 = 0.3C, d0 = 0.03C). When the deformation region is fixed at x0 = 0.3C, increasing d0 to 0.04C leads to the complete elimination of cavitation on the suction surface. This biomimetic approach offers new physical insights and practical design strategies for low-cavitation applications in marine propulsion and hydraulic machinery.

papers.title: Influence of temperature on the load capacity of planar ferrofluid bearings
papers.abstract: A dribble of ferrofluids falls on a permanent magnet, inducing a ferrofluid buoyant force to form a liquid-soft bearing. Compared to conventional solid bearings used in the low frequency vibration shock absorbers and energy harvesters, these ferrofluid bearings exhibit a lower friction coefficient but pronounced temperature sensitivity. However, the influence of temperature on the load capacity remains insufficiently studied. Here, we investigate the load capacity variations with gap distance under different temperatures and standing times, analyzing hysteresis behavior under these conditions. Additionally, we examine the effect of alternating temperature conditions on the load capacity. We found that the temperature-induced aggregation of magnetic particles in high-gradient magnetic fields will enhance the load capacity at a small gap and weaken it at a large gap. This study clarifies the temperature range and performance of ferrofluid bearings for application.

papers.title: Thermal management of magneto-ferrofluid operated circular thermal systems with thermal radiation, peripheral distributed heating, and Y-shaped cooling channels
papers.abstract: This investigation presents a comprehensive numerical analysis of magneto-ferrofluid thermal management in circular enclosures featuring peripheral distributed heating and Y-shaped cooling channels. The study examines Fe3O4-H2O ferrofluid convection under varying geometric configurations, magnetic field conditions, and thermal radiation effects using finite element methodology. The governing equations incorporating magnetohydrodynamic effects and thermal radiation are solved across varying Rayleigh numbers (103 ≤ Ra ≤ 106), Hartmann numbers (0 ≤ Ha ≤ 70), magnetic field inclination angles (0° ≤ γ ≤ 150°), radiation parameters (0 ≤ Rd ≤ 3), and Y-shaped cooling channel heights (0.1 ≤ ht ≤ 0.35). Results demonstrate that heat transfer enhancement reaches 301% as Ra increases from 103 to 106, while magnetic field application provides systematic flow control with up to 42% suppression at Ha = 70. Thermal radiation substantially augments thermal performance, yielding 165% enhancement at Rd = 3 through synergistic radiation-convection coupling. The Y-shaped cooling channel height emerges as a critical geometric parameter, with optimal configurations (ht = 0.3–0.35) providing 23% performance improvement over baseline designs. Heatline visualization reveals complex energy transport pathways transitioning from conduction-dominated to convection-controlled mechanisms under varying operational conditions. Entropy generation analysis indicates thermal irreversibilities dominate at low Ra, while viscous and magnetic contributions intensify at higher Ra values. The investigation demonstrates that Fe3O4-H2O ferrofluid systems achieve exceptional thermal management performance through multi-modal enhancement strategies that combine geometric optimization, magnetic field control, and radiation effects. The developed correlations provide design guidelines for optimizing advanced thermal management systems in electronics cooling, renewable energy applications, and biomedical thermal devices.

papers.title: Flow around a rigid oscillating airfoil undergoing nonlinear oscillations in persistent and pulsating currents
papers.abstract: The flow over an oscillating airfoil following harmonic and nonlinear oscillations is numerically studied. Motivated by the design of energy harvesting device components, different sets of parameters are considered to vary the airfoil oscillations and flow characteristics in the Reynolds number range 200≤Re≤500. Results on the vortex shedding patterns and the resulting forces on the airfoil are included. Additionally, for the case of harmonic oscillations, the effect of a pulsating current is analyzed. The characteristics of this current are determined by a downscaling procedure based on field measurement data in the Cozumel channel, Mexico. Results show the importance of including such characteristics in the study of the hydrodynamic forces on the airfoil. Flow instability is observed in the wake behind the oscillating foil for specific parameter combinations.

papers.title: The contribution of degenerate tori: The study of strong Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser stability and barrier development
papers.abstract: We examine the degenerate tori and their stability analysis in this study. These tori are crucial to the development of robust transport barriers in Hamiltonian systems. Applications in fields including atmospheric dynamics (such as the ozone hole problem), plasma physics, and celestial mechanics—where Hamiltonian systems with degenerate tori [violating the twist requirement ω(P)≠0] are frequent—what drives this research. This work presents an original technique to investigate the identification of transport barriers and chaotic structures in periodic and quasiperiodic flows. Unlike transient recurring flows, which possess exact forward and backward time reversibility, real-world flows often lack this ideal property. By leveraging the precise characterization of transport barriers in periodic flows as material surfaces generated by trajectories from invariant sets in Poincaré maps, we explore fluid transport and chaotic structures in two-dimensional incompressible flow using Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser (KAM) theory. Furthermore, we analyze invariant tori within the flow and examine the bounded domain of the flow in finite time intervals with multi-periodic time dependence. Additionally, we illustrate strong KAM stability phenomena near degenerate tori in Hamiltonian systems. To validate our findings, we conduct an in-depth analysis of the Arnold–Beltrami–Childress (ABC) flow, a canonical example of transport and mixing phenomena.

papers.title: Validation and enhancement of aerodynamic heating method with computational fluid dynamics and Newtonian cooling
papers.abstract: An efficient and accurate aerodynamic heating analysis method is critical for thermal protection system (TPS) design in hypersonic vehicles. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled Newtonian cooling (NC) framework, which was proposed to predict aerothermal and drive thermal conduction efficiently, is first validated on four representative hypersonic configurations, covering flow complexities from axisymmetric bow shocks to shock/shock interactions. Compared with high-fidelity CFD coupled computational thermal dynamics, the CFD/NC approach maintains structural temperature response prediction errors at corresponding nodes within 5% while significantly reducing computational cost, especially for the three-dimensional cases. Moreover, a segmented coupling strategy (SCS) is proposed, which periodically updates heat transfer coefficients with CFD data, thereby extending the robustness and applicability of the CFD/NC approach to long-duration cases. This study advances the CFD/NC framework by providing systematic validation on diverse hypersonic configurations and by introducing SCS that extends its reliability for long-duration heating. These developments yield a balanced and scalable approach for rapid TPS design optimization and also offer potential for integration into aerothermoelastic analyses of hypersonic aircraft.

papers.title: Discrete map reduction of bursting flows in periodically driven cylindrical cavities
papers.abstract: Highly complex flow patterns arising in a viscous fluid confined within a cylindrical cavity, driven by time-periodically oscillating walls, are studied numerically. To enable predictive analysis of these dynamics, we present a reduction based on a mathematical discrete map, formulated in the vicinity of a codimension-2 bifurcation. This map, derived as a normal form using equivariant bifurcation theory and scaled according to the physical parameters of the system, captures the essential features of the burst dynamics. The reduced model accurately reflects the core dynamics observed in Direct Numerical Simulations (dns). After appropriate scaling, the map predictions show excellent agreement with dns results, successfully forecasting the range of accessible flow solutions. Furthermore, the map reveals a coherent flow pattern with non-trivial time dependence, previously overlooked, offering new insights into its emergence. These insights clarify the origin of the competition between pulsating and bursting flows, showing that it arises from heteroclinic connections between quasiperiodic flows. The scaling laws corresponding to such collision have been confirmed after a careful swipe in the parameter space, involving the computation of an extensive number of bursting regimes.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability threshold for temperature-dependent viscosity convection: Constraints from three-dimensional numerical simulations
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear stability threshold for Rayleigh–Bénard convection in infinite Prandtl number fluids with temperature-dependent viscosity by solving numerically the full system of three-dimensional (3D) convection equations below the linear critical Rayleigh number. First, for viscosity contrasts Δη from 10 to 1010, we determine the Rayleigh number at which convection ceases in a unit cell of square and hexagonal planforms. The lowest Rayleigh number at which convection exists gives the planform-specific nonlinear stability threshold. For all Δη considered, hexagons and squares yield lower thresholds than the three previously investigated cases: a unit cell of an infinite array of two-dimensional (2D) rolls, a localized 2D plume, and a localized 3D plume. The variation among thresholds for all planforms is <15%. Second, for Δη=1010 we investigate the stability of square and hexagonal planforms in a large box containing hundreds of unit cells. The square planform is stable. However, its threshold is above that found for its unit cell and is close to the threshold for localized plumes. Below the localized plume threshold, the square planform collapses to a conductive state. The hexagonal planform is unstable in a large box. At Rayleigh numbers above the threshold for localized plumes, it breaks down into several isolated localized 3D plumes, which then collapse below their threshold. An initially disordered planform evolves similarly. Thus, the nonlinear stability threshold for localized 3D plumes is a tight upper bound on the global nonlinear threshold for this system, and values much smaller than this bound are unlikely.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of control strategies for Rayleigh–Bénard convection from classical feedback methods to artificial intelligence-driven optimization for enhanced energy transport and stability
papers.abstract: Rayleigh–Bénard convection (RBC), the buoyancy-driven flow that arises when a fluid layer is heated from below and cooled from above, governs heat transport in engineering systems, geophysical and atmospheric circulation, stellar and planetary interiors, and numerous industrial processes. This review synthesizes theoretical, numerical, and experimental progress on controlling RBC, organizing methods into (i) passive strategies that modify geometry or boundary conditions and apply constant external fields, and (ii) active strategies that dynamically modulate parameters using feedback or machine learning-based controllers. Quantitatively, passive approaches can substantially delay the onset of convection: oscillatory boundary forcing increases the critical Rayleigh number Rac by up to ∼16×, and selected geometric or magnetic/rotational configurations shift stability by factors of order 1.5–3. Active approaches provide greater adaptability and depth of stabilization: Proportional feedback sustains the conductive state up to ∼4× the classical threshold, robust linear-quadratic-Gaussian designs up to ∼14.5×, while reinforcement learning reduces turbulent convective heat transport by 5.1% at Ra∼3×104, extending Rac by ∼30× over the uncontrolled case. We compare these methods on common performance metrics (extension of Rac, percentage change in Nusselt number, advantages and limitations) and discuss practical factors such as sensor placement, actuator bandwidth and saturation, and robustness to disturbances that govern deployability. The hybrid combining classical feedback with nonlinearity, augmented by multi-agent reinforcement learning, quantum-inspired optimization, and programable thermal metamaterials, provides scalable real-time solutions for precise thermal management in a wide range of scientific and industrial applications.

papers.title: Pore-scale simulation of hydrocarbon fuel flow and heat transfer in porous media
papers.abstract: Reactive coolants have gained increasing research attention in transpiration cooling, motivating further investigation into the coupled interactions of flow, heat transfer, and chemical reactions within porous media. In this paper, three three-dimensional spherical particle packing models, namely, simple cubic (SC), body-centered cubic (BCC), and face-centered cubic (FCC), are used to simulate the flow and heat transfer of hydrocarbon fuel in porous microchannels. The impact of different pore structures on the flow-heat-reaction coupling is investigated. The dependence of pyrolysis reactions on flow field is analyzed, revealing the coupling mechanism between heat and mass transfer processes in chemically reactive flow fields. Results presented herein demonstrate that under the same conditions, the SC structure microchannel exhibits excellent cooling performance. When considering cracking reactions, its maximum solid temperature decreases by 38.4% compared with the BCC structure and by 16.6% compared with the FCC structure. The value of Da in the contraction section of pore channel is considerably smaller relative to that in the expansion section, implying a higher dependence of cracking reaction on the flow field within this region. Radial distribution of Le additionally manifests that central region has a lower value than its adjacent region, suggesting a conspicuous dependence on diffusion mechanisms in the central fluid domain.

papers.title: Inflow turbulence generation for turbulent boundary layer with adverse pressure gradient using an equivalent boundary layer model
papers.abstract: For direct and large-eddy simulations of turbulent boundary layers (TBLs), the inflow turbulence conditions decisively influence the downstream flows. Recently, Wang et al. [“Inflow turbulence generation using an equivalent boundary layer model,” Phys. Fluids 35, 075110 (2023)] proposed an equivalent boundary layer (EBL) model to generate inflow turbulence fluctuations for zero-pressure gradient (ZPG) TBLs. In the present study, this model has been extended to TBLs with adverse pressure gradient (APG). Compared to the former model, the present model incorporates the mean wall-normal velocity, which is more prominent in APG TBLs than in ZPG TBLs. In addition, a filter is imposed on the streamwise velocity to suppress the amplified streamwise large-scale structures. The driving force was obtained from the databases and the prediction models of the APG TBLs. The present EBL model was applied to the generation of the inflow turbulence for two APG TBLs with (Reθ, β)=(2180,2.2) and (4100,1.4) at the inlet, where Reθ is the Reynolds number based on the momentum thickness θ and β is the Rotta–Clauser pressure-gradient parameter. The results show that the EBL model well reconstructs the turbulent fluctuations of the TBL at the corresponding Reθ and β and can ensure the natural downstream development of the flow when used as the inflow for streamwise developing TBL simulations.

papers.title: An integrated sequence-to-sequence framework for well production prediction
papers.abstract: Machine learning models, especially sequence prediction algorithms, have been widely used to predict oil production. However, most of the existing algorithms have low prediction accuracy and poor stability. Here, a new production prediction model is proposed. The model utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction of static data, a Sequence to Sequence (Seq2Seq) to capture the sequence relationship of dynamic data, and an attention mechanism (AT) to enhance the ability of Seq2Seq to learn the location and spatial relationship of sequences. Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KANs) are then introduced to integrate static and dynamic data, replacing conventional “weights” with learnable one-dimensional functions to strengthen the nonlinear fitting relationship with the target variable. Furthermore, the whale optimization algorithm (WOA) is applied to optimize hyperparameters and the network structure, ensuring the model remains in an optimal state. Finally, the WOA-CNN-Seq2Seq-AT-KAN model is established. The research results show that the WOA-CNN-Seq2Seq-AT-KAN model has high prediction accuracy and good stability. It can alleviate the problem of error accumulation in the long-term future step size, and its prediction accuracy can be improved by 31.2% compared with CNN-long short-term memory. Meanwhile, WOA-CNN-Seq2Seq-AT-KAN has good convergence, effectively captures the relationship of long-distance data, and has strong nonlinear fitting ability.

papers.title: Shape transitions of sedimenting confined droplets and capsules: From oblate to bullet-like geometries
papers.abstract: The transport and deformation of confined droplets and flexible capsules are central to diverse phenomena and applications, from biological flows in microcapillaries to industrial processes in porous media. Inspired by experiments, we perform numerical simulations to investigate their shape dynamics under varying levels of confinement and particle flexibility. A transition from an oblate to a bullet-like shape is observed at a confinement threshold, independent of flexibility, which agrees with our analytical calculations. A fluid–structure interaction analysis reveals two regimes: a pressure-dominated and a viscous-dominated regime. For highly flexible particles, the pressure-dominated regime prevails and the deformation is enhanced. These findings offer new insights into the transport of flexible particles in confined environments, with implications for biomedical applications, filtration technologies, and multiphase fluid mechanics.

papers.title: A slip boundary condition for wall-modeled large eddy simulation with synthetic turbulence generator using high-order finite difference method
papers.abstract: High-fidelity computational aeroacoustics simulations encounter significant challenges in industrial applications, especially in high Reynolds number flow regimes. These difficulties arise primarily from stringent requirements imposed by the Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy condition and the near-wall grid spacing, leading to prohibitively high computational costs. To address this limitation, this study presents a novel slip boundary condition for wall-modeled large eddy simulation that employs high-order finite-difference methods based on the dispersion-relation-preserving scheme. The slip boundary condition prescribes the tangential velocity at solid walls while enforcing zero normal penetration. The slip velocity is derived from a linearized near-wall velocity profile approximation at the sample point, significantly reducing grid resolution requirements. The slip boundary condition is first validated in turbulent channel flows at Reτ=2000 with optimized grid spacings (δ/Δx=20, δ/Δz=30, δ/Δy=20–30, δ: boundary-layer thickness), yielding mean velocity profiles and Reynolds stresses that closely match direct numerical simulation (DNS) benchmarks. Additionally, errors in the low-to-mid frequency components of the power spectral density remain within 3–6 dB. The optimized grid spacings are further validated over a range of friction Reynolds numbers (Reτ=576–5100). Besides, a synthetic turbulence inflow method is developed by superimposing divergence-free, spatially correlated steady jet structures onto the mean flow, integrated with the radiation nonreflective boundary conditions. The time-invariant source terms maintain computational efficiency while effectively suppressing spurious numerical oscillations. The synthesized velocity profiles and Reynolds stresses show excellent agreement with DNS data. While the spectra exhibit overprediction in amplitude, the characteristic shape maintain consistency with Goody's empirical model.

papers.title: Marangoni effect on compound droplet inside bifurcated micro-confinement
papers.abstract: The combination of pressure-driven flow and thermocapillary forces greatly affects droplet dynamics in microfluidic environments, which has substantial implications for droplet-based technologies. In this work, we have investigated the thermocapillary migration and deformation of a single droplet subjected to a continuous pressure-driven flow in a bifurcated Y-shaped microchannel. In this study, the combined impacts of surface wettability, viscosity ratio, surface tension fluctuation, and externally imposed temperature gradient have been the main focus. Using energy equations and numerical simulations based on Navier–Stokes, a comprehensive parametric analysis has been conducted, taking into account all appropriate interfacial boundary conditions. The outcome demonstrates that a greater temperature gradient exacerbates thermocapillary-driven motion, causing droplets to visibly migrate toward areas with less surface tension. The ratio of the droplet's viscosity to that of the surrounding fluid is discovered to significantly change the droplet's deformation and velocity. The high-viscosity droplets have been found to prevent thermocapillary-induced stretching. The study shows that surface wettability has a significant effect on the contact angle dynamics and the droplet's attachment to the channel walls. The research highlights how the variation in temperature gradient impacts the timing and position of droplet pinch-off. The effect of Marangoni flow has been studied here, and it has been found that as the Marangoni number (Ma = 0–0.4) increases, the droplet migrates toward the warmer areas with the pinch-off point moving toward the region of reduced surface tension. It alters the droplet's separation dynamics completely. Generally, at low capillary numbers (Ca = 0.01–0.15), the deformation of the droplet is minimum, but beyond a critical value, the droplet experiences an asymmetric deformation and displacement. This is due to the effect of Marangoni forces. This work examines the hydrodynamics of compound droplets in a bifurcated microchannel in a novel manner. This includes the combined impacts of capillary number, viscosity ratio, Marangoni number, and pressure-driven flow. The complex interactions between core and shell interfacial tensions are captured simultaneously. Marangoni-driven surface tension gradients and bifurcation-induced asymmetry have been studied primarily on single droplets or straight-channel configurations. By exposing previously unknown regimes where Marangoni stresses may either enhance or suppress droplet deformation and splitting, the results offer novel design insights for precise droplet manipulation in microfluidic applications. These findings may prove beneficial in targeted material delivery, biological diagnostics, and lab-on-a-chip devices.

papers.title: Toward improved offshore wind design: Variability of wind veer revealed by hybrid cluster analysis of lidar data
papers.abstract: Understanding offshore wind veer, i.e., the vertical variation of wind direction with height, is critical for improving wind turbine design, structural load assessment, and wake interaction modeling in offshore wind farms. This study aims to explore the variability of offshore wind veer and identify its primary atmospheric drivers across multiple temporal and dynamic regimes. To achieve this, a hybrid clustering framework was developed and applied to a multi-year dataset of high-resolution Doppler lidar measurements collected from an offshore platform near Hong Kong. The methodology integrates shape-oriented time series clustering with directional similarity metrics, enabling the classification of full-profile veer structures under varying conditions. The results indicate that vertical wind veer profiles vary systematically with changes in season, wind speed, and atmospheric stability. Seasonal groupings exhibited distinct profile shapes, reflecting changes in atmospheric structure likely associated with shifts in large-scale flow regimes and mesoscale conditions. Wind speed was found to influence the curvature and directional trend of veer profiles, with low and high wind speed regimes displaying markedly different vertical patterns. Similarly, variations in atmospheric stability corresponded with identifiable shifts in the shape and smoothness of veer profiles, suggesting a sensitivity to stratification and mixing conditions. While the precise physical mechanisms could not be fully resolved from the available dataset, the consistent emergence of distinct veer structures across environmental categories highlights the importance of incorporating dynamic veer characterization into offshore wind assessments.

papers.title: Numerical study of a submerged liquid metal jet in a transverse magnetic field
papers.abstract: A flow of an electrically conducting fluid in the form of a round jet entering a square duct subjected to a transverse magnetic field is studied using direct numerical simulations. The complex dynamics of the jet, determined by the effects of Joule dissipation, the flow's transformation into anisotropic states, the Kelvin–Helmholtz instability leading to the development of large-scale fluctuations, and the constraints imposed by the duct's walls, is revealed through analysis of the fields of velocity, pressure, and electric currents. The results show a good qualitative agreement with earlier experiments and provide an explanation for the experimental findings. In particular, the simulations confirm the hypothesized existence of two distinct regimes of the flow: an unstable central jet at low-to-moderate Stuart numbers N and a macrovortex shedding large-scale quasi-two-dimensional eddies at large N. The system is also used as a benchmark for the exploration of possible sources of uncertainty in experimental and numerical analysis of liquid-metal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). A detailed comparison between the results of the simulations and the experimental data, as well as a parametric study of the effects of the model assumptions, allows us to identify and quantitatively assess the main such sources: the accuracy of velocity measurement by the electric potential sensors, the uncertain electric conductivity of the walls, the velocity profile and perturbations at the inlet, and the time of averaging required for accurate evaluation of mean flow properties in the presence of large-scale eddies typical for MHD flows.

papers.title: Performance analysis of leaf-vein-inspired heat sink for enhanced nanofluid heat transfer
papers.abstract: This study investigates the heat transfer enhancement potential of leaf-vein-inspired heat sink structures using hybrid nanofluids under natural convection, which addresses a critical gap in thermal management technologies. Five distinct cases with evolving fractal geometries are analyzed through numerical simulations, evaluating the impact of the Rayleigh number (Ra) and nanoparticle volume fraction (φ) on the average Nusselt number (Nuavg). Results demonstrate that at Ra = 106, the geometric complexity progressively increases from case 1 to case 4, with Nuavg peaking at 44.3 for case 4, driven by stronger convection and improved surface area utilization. However, case 5, with four levels of branching, exhibits a decline in Nuavg, suggesting an optimal branching threshold beyond which the increased geometric complexity reduces efficiency. The addition of nanoparticles enhances thermal conductivity, although the improvement tends to diminish at higher concentrations. The numerical model developed in this study has been validated against previous studies, confirming the robustness of the proposed approach. These findings provide valuable insights for the design of efficient cooling systems for microelectronics and energy applications, thereby paving the way for more advanced thermal management solutions.

papers.title: A snapshot difference and amplitude optimization based dynamic mode decomposition method for reconstruction and prediction of flow fields
papers.abstract: Dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) is extensively used in fluid dynamics to identify dominant flow structures and facilitate flow reconstruction and prediction. Conventional DMD, however, builds temporal snapshot matrices based exclusively on state variables at individual time instants, which often inadequately captures the behavior of localized or complex flows. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes an enhanced DMD technique that incorporates time-delay embedding by using difference values between state variables at consecutive time steps as the building blocks of the snapshot matrix. This approach not only retains instantaneous flow field information but also emphasizes temporal change characteristics, thereby improving the analytical capability of DMD. Moreover, a modal amplitude optimization procedure is integrated to increase the precision of reconstruction and prediction. The proposed method is validated on three test cases with increasing complexity and diverse backgrounds. Results show that the modified method significantly enhances the robustness and reconstruction accuracy of DMD, indicating its improved reliability for practical fluid dynamics applications.

papers.title: Data-driven sparse polynomial analysis of inflow uncertainty effects on transonic compressor aerodynamics at different Reynolds numbers
papers.abstract: To meet the increasing demands for high thrust-to-weight ratios and low specific fuel consumption in modern aero engines, compressor designs are trending toward higher stage loading to reduce stage counts. However, these advancements introduce challenges related to low Reynolds number (Re) effect and elevated sensitivity to uncertainty. This study proposes a data-driven sparse arbitrary polynomial chaos expansion (DD-SAPCE) method to investigate the impact of inflow uncertainty on the aerodynamic performance of a transonic compressor rotor across different Re conditions. The DD-SAPCE framework effectively mitigates the curse of dimensionality inherent in conventional polynomial chaos approaches, reducing computational cost by nearly 60% while achieving comparable accuracy. Furthermore, the method supports modeling with discrete data, making it suitable for practical engineering applications. Statistical comparisons reveal that low Re conditions intensify the variability in mass flow while reducing the dispersion of isentropic efficiency. These effects are accompanied by enhanced nonlinear sensitivity of aerodynamic performance to inflow uncertainty. Spanwise analyses further show that changes in blade loading and shock structures are the key contributors to performance fluctuations. Furthermore, global and local sensitivity analyses based on the Shapley method identify inlet total pressure, back pressure, and flow angle as the dominant factors influencing the aerodynamic performance sensitivity to inlet flow disturbances. These findings offer critical insights for the performance influence mechanism and robust aerodynamic optimization of transonic compressor systems.

papers.title: Numerical simulation of debris-flow impact on multiple check dams using the material point method
papers.abstract: It is essential to capture the transient impact forces of debris flows on check dam barriers for accurate hazard mitigation and structural design, yet traditional depth-averaged or mesh-based numerical approaches often fail to resolve the complicated local flow–structure interaction subject to large deformation. This study employs the material point method (MPM) to simulate the impact-force evolution during a well-documented disaster—the 2010 Wenjia Gully debris flow—and investigates its interaction with a series of check dams. The MPM framework naturally handles the extreme deformation, contact between different materials, and multiphase mixing without mesh distortion. Validation against flume experiments and field measurements confirms its predictive accuracy for both the runout distance and impact loading. Results reveal a staged force attenuation mechanism—where upstream dams dissipate momentum and reduce downstream peak loads—and an intermittent load recovery phase due to flow front re-acceleration between dams. Parametric analyses highlight that the internal friction angle predominantly controls runout extent, while cohesion and density nonlinearly influence the impact magnitude. The study elucidates underlying physical mechanisms in the interaction between debris flows and barriers and demonstrates the unique suitability of the MPM in resolving localized, time-dependent impact phenomena. The findings provide insight into the optimization of the multi-dam configuration and enhance understanding of flow–structure coupling in debris-laden geophysical flows.

papers.title: Wake characteristics of a floating wind turbine in yaw under sway motions
papers.abstract: In this work, high-fidelity large eddy simulation based on the actuator line model is resorted to investigate the wake of a floating wind turbine with different yaw angles (0°, 10°, 20°, and 30°) under sway motions. The results show that floating motion can enhance wake expansion by about 30%–110% and significantly reduce instantaneous asymmetry. At small yaw angles, the wake is governed by sway motion, resulting in pronounced lateral stretching and an approximately symmetric double-peak probability density function of the instantaneous wake center. At moderate yaw angles, the wake evolution is dominated by both the sway motion and the yaw misalignment, leading to reduced wake deflection and a transition from laterally stretched wake structures to vertically elongated ones, with an obvious asymmetry of the instantaneous wake center. At large yaw angles, the sway-induced effect is suppressed by the yaw misalignment, making the wake structure and instantaneous characteristics similar to those of the fixed turbine. The wake of a yawed floating turbine is highly sensitive to the motion frequency. When the sway frequency approaches the dominant frequency of the wake meandering, lock-in occurs with an amplification factor of the wake meandering ranging from 4 to 10. Wake mixing and recovery increase with the motion amplitude. However, excessive amplitude or off resonance frequency reduces the amplification factor of the wake meandering.

papers.title: Dynamics of drops impacting on superhydrophobic concave surfaces axially decorated with a macroridge
papers.abstract: The collision behavior of water drops on a ridged concave surface (R-CVS) is analyzed through numerical simulations based on the Volume of Fluid method. Two distinct retraction modes are identified: sequential retraction mode, featuring stretched motion with potential re-coalescence, and direct retraction mode, characterized by rapid and complete separation through unidirectional retraction. A critical condition based on the Weber number (We) and the cylinder-to-drop diameter ratio (d/D) is proposed to distinguish the two modes. Compared to a typical concave surface (CVS), R-CVS promotes asymmetric momentum redistribution, which either delays or accelerates drop detachment. Theoretical models and simulations demonstrate that the residence time and detachment behavior are primarily governed by the interplay between inertial–capillary forces and geometric confinement, determined by We and d/D. These findings provide new insight into the control of drop rebound dynamics through the inner curvature of cylindrical surfaces and ridge-induced asymmetry.

papers.title: Multi-parameter evaluation for optimizing spur dike spacing in river engineering
papers.abstract: This study identifies the spacing threshold for hydraulic independence between two emerged impermeable spur dikes using validated computational fluid dynamics modeling. Numerical simulations analyzed velocity, turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), turbulence intensity (TI), and wall shear stress (WSS) across discharges (0.0336–0.2352 m3/s) and spacings (1–6 m). The results demonstrate that smaller spacings (<5 m) induce strong interactions. The downstream spur dike experiences a 25%–40% velocity reduction due to upstream shielding, while its TKE exceeds upstream values by 30%–50%. A critical threshold of 5–6 m emerges, beyond which tip velocities converge, TKE and TI disparities stabilize, and hydraulic independence is achieved. Increasing discharge amplifies turbulence magnitude but does not alter this threshold. Spacings below 5 m create merged wake zones, elevating local WSS by up to 45% compared to the widest spacing case (6 m), thereby increasing scour risk, while spacings above 5–6 m limit WSS concentrations to <10% of peak values. The novelty of this work lies in applying a multi-parameter evaluation framework (velocity, TKE, TI, and WSS) to define independence more rigorously than single-parameter studies, and in identifying the progressive transition from strong interaction to full independence. This approach provides both theoretical insight and practical design guidance for spur dike spacing optimization.

papers.title: Preferential flow in homogeneous superhydrophilic porous media
papers.abstract: Air Gap Diffusion Distillation (AGDD) is a new desalination technology that relies on superhydrophilic porous media as the primary evaporation-desalination component. In experiments, we observed preferential flow in these superhydrophilic porous media, which significantly reduces AGDD's desalination efficiency. Nevertheless, current research generally suggests that hydrophilic porous media or high initial saturations are unlikely to produce preferential flow. Therefore, point-source infiltration experiments were conducted in order to verify the phenomenon of preferential flow in porous media with high saturation/superhydrophilicity.
