Experiments showed that, similarly to conventional hydrophobic materials, increasing either saturation or infiltration flux inhibited preferential flow. The distinctive feature is that superhydrophilic porous media can maintain preferential flow across a broad initial saturation range (0%–50.7%). Compared to low-porosity wettable materials, high porosity/larger pore sizes are key factors enabling preferential flow in hydrophilic porous media. Unlike conventional hydrophobic materials, preferential flow occurs without saturation overshoot (capillary pressure overshoot). Relying on its superhydrophilic properties, stable water bridge connections form at the locations where finger flow first passes through, serving as preferential paths. In addition, the superhydrophilicity eliminates velocity differences between finger tips and preferential paths, preventing saturation overshoot. The recurrence of preferential flow in superhydrophilic porous media is caused by unsaturated hydraulic conductivity gradients along the depth direction of the infiltration front, which creates flow instability.

papers.title: Evaluation of relative permeability of two-phase flow in rough fractures considering horizontal flow structures: A viscous model and experimental validation
papers.abstract: Relative permeability (kr) is a key parameter for describing unsaturated flow properties in rock fractures. Most existing viscous kr models focus on the two-phase fluid distributions on vertical direction of fracture (along aperture direction) and ignore the impacts of flow structures in horizontal fracture plane. A novel conceptual approach that combines the sandwich model and alternating model was proposed to reflect on two-phase horizontal flow structures. According to the principle of momentum conservation and Newton's law of viscosity, a viscous model of kr curve for two-phase flow in rough fractures was established, where the wetting-phase ratio l1 was introduced to consider the effects of horizontal flow structures, in addition to fluid viscosity, residual saturation, and fracture geometry. Through the comparisons between substantial experimental data from literatures and other six classical kr models, this model has reasonable advantages with lower root mean square error in describing the two-phase flow properties in rough fractures, especially for real rough fractures with complex geometric characteristics. To further investigate the impacts of aperture variation on kr curves, a series of two-phase flow experiments (nitrogen-water) were performed. The larger value of fitting parameter l1 can effectively characterize the steeper trend of kr curves caused by greater fracture aperture. The sensitivity of model parameters to the shape of kr curves and nonlinearity of two-phase flow was analyzed in the end. This work could improve the predictive performance of viscous kr model and provide a new perspective for the multiphase flow research involved in fractured rock applications.

papers.title: Data-driven coarse-graining and reduced-order modeling of plume ejection dynamics from video observations
papers.abstract: Plume dispersion is a fundamental problem in fluid dynamics, governed by instabilities, advection, and diffusion. Monitoring atmospheric pollutant dispersion is also critical for environmental assessment. High-fidelity simulations capture plume dynamics but remain computationally expensive due to fine spatial and temporal resolution requirements. Plume evolution exhibits two regimes: (i) initial ejection driven by shear-induced Kelvin–Helmholtz instability and (ii) later diffusion and advection, often represented by Gaussian plume models. We develop a data-driven framework to model the initial regime directly from video. The method uses a two-stage algorithm: Otsu thresholding extracts contours, and a concentric circle search identifies the centerline and envelope of the plume. Tracking these features over time enables regression of polynomial and sinusoidal models, inspired by Kelvin–Helmholtz instability, to characterize trajectory, dispersion, and vorticity. This approach compresses high-resolution video into approximately eight coefficients per frame and eight per time series, enabling rapid assessment of early plume behavior and serving as a data reduction precursor to standard models. The three parameters describing the centerline extrapolate with 83% relative accuracy at distances 50% beyond the training data. The eight parameters for the upper and lower edges achieve 47–52% accuracy on withheld data. The framework is available through an open-source Python package.

papers.title: Harnessing electro-osmosis in direct contact membrane distillation: A numerical study on polarization control and flux enhancement
papers.abstract: This computational study examines the use of electro-osmosis to boost the efficiency of direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) systems. An electric field induces an electro-osmotic slip velocity at the membrane surface, calculated from the field strength, zeta potential, and fluid properties. This velocity disrupts the boundary layer, mitigating temperature polarization (TP)—a key factor limiting DCMD performance. By reducing TP, heat transfer from the bulk fluid to the membrane improves, maintaining a larger temperature gradient across the membrane, which serves as the primary driving force for vapor flux. A validated computational fluid dynamics model quantifies these effects, showing that a slip velocity of 0.0006 m/s increases permeate flux by up to 1.86% at a Reynolds number of 100. This enhancement stems from a reduced TP and an improved temperature polarization coefficient. The study further explores membrane porosity, feed temperature, and channel spacers. Higher feed temperatures amplify benefits, with flux gains reaching 3% at 70 °C due to greater vapor pressure sensitivity. Combining electro-osmosis with spacers yields synergistic effects, achieving flux increases of up to 27.2% compared to an empty channel without electro-osmosis. This work underscores electro-osmosis as a practical, effective strategy to optimize DCMD efficiency by directly addressing TP, offering valuable insight for process improvement and industrial application.

papers.title: Consistent lattice Boltzmann model for shallow water equations
papers.abstract: We present a novel discrete velocity kinetic framework to consistently recover the viscous shallow water equations. The proposed model has the following advantages: (a) A novel interpretation and general framework to introduce forces, (b) the possibility to consistently split pressure contributions between equilibrium and a force-like contribution, (c) consistent recovery of the viscous shallow water equations with no errors in the dissipation rates, (d) independent control over bulk viscosity, and (e) consistent second-order implementation of forces. As shown through a variety of different test cases, these features make for an accurate and stable solution method for the shallow water equations.

papers.title: Parameters of the shock wave generated by laser-induced discharge in argon
papers.abstract: The article presents the results of measuring the distribution of neutral particle concentration in a shock wave formed by a discharge initiated by pulsed laser radiation. The parameters of heating radiation were as follows: wavelength 10.6 μm, pulse duration 100 ns, and energy per pulse up to 1.1 J. Another laser with a wavelength of 632.8 nm was chosen as a light source for a Michelson interferometer designed for phase shift measurements caused by gas disturbance. It was found that with these parameters of the infrared laser spark in argon, an eightfold compression of the gas at the shock wave front is achieved.

papers.title: Retraction: “Numerical study on energy criterion and damage evolution of abrasive jet rock breaking under biaxial stresses” [Phys. Fluids 37 (7), 073303 (2025)]
Retraction: “Optimization and experimental validation of perforated plate acoustic liners for enhanced noise reduction in acoustic waveguides” [Phys. Fluids 37 (7), 076154 (2025)]
Magnetohydrodynamic double-diffusive convection of hybrid nanofluids in a U-grooved trapezoidal cavity
papers.abstract: A three-dimensional numerical study was developed to examine double-diffusive convection in a trapezoidal cavity with a U-shaped heated groove, filled with an Al2O3–Cu/water hybrid nanofluid. A finite element method is employed to solve the governing equations over a range of Rayleigh numbers (104–105), Hartmann numbers (0–100), buoyancy ratios (N = −2, 0, 2), and nanoparticle volume fractions (0%–4.5%). The results show that the groove acts as a focal point for the development of the Lorentz force, whose intensity increases near its lower edges under strong magnetic fields (Ha = 25, Hartmann number), suppressing convection and favoring conduction-dominated regimes. The distribution of electric potential, which is confined in the absence of nanoparticles, becomes more complex in the presence of nanofluids (φ = 4.5%), showing alternating charge zones due to induced currents and increased mixing. Heat and mass transfer are strongly influenced by the interaction between geometry, buoyancy, and magnetic damping. The U-shaped groove improves convective transport under favorable conditions while stabilizing stratified layers under unfavorable conditions. These results show that magnetohydrodynamic-nanofluid coupling in geometric cavities could be used to make compact, passive, and adjustable thermal control systems that work well in spacecraft and microgravity settings. Heat and mass transfer are strongly influenced.

papers.title: Investigation into the coupling mechanism of tailwater vortex dynamics and cavitation during pump-as-turbine operations
papers.abstract: In order to investigate the coupling mechanism between tailwater vortex and cavitation bubbles (CB) during the operation of a low-head pump-as-turbine (PAT), the method of combining experiment and numerical simulation is used to quantify the vortex dynamics characteristics in combination with the vorticity transport equation under high flow conditions for PAT mode. The results show that the decrease in Thoma number significantly regulates the symbiotic evolution of tailwater vortex and CB: prolonging the residence time of CB in the draft tube (DT) and changing its evolution mode, resulting in the extension of vortex rope (VR) generation period, length contraction, and the increase in breaking vortex in DT. The peak volume of CB is 7 times that in the rotor region, squeezing the channel vortex and the wake vortex, weakening its contribution to VR. Vortex dynamics shows that the relative vortex stretching term is the core driving force of vorticity, which causes velocity gradient distortion and VR high-frequency oscillation synchronously with vertical vorticity. The baroclinic torque term (BT) only generates pulse contribution in the early stage of CB collapse. Under critical cavitation, BT converts the cavity collapse energy into vortex energy through density-pressure gradient coupling, which expands the vortex core radius to 0.03 m, increases the circulation peak to 2.3 m2/s, and shifts outward by 27.3%, resulting in vortex energy diffusion and high-frequency oscillation of the flow field. This study provides a theoretical basis for cavitation suppression and operational optimization of low-head PAT.

papers.title: Numerical simulation study on the placement behavior of composite particle size proppants in hydraulic fractures of coal rock reservoirs
papers.abstract: Slippery water fracturing in coal reservoirs commonly employs composite proppants to improve filling efficiency; however, most studies simplify the proppant system to a single particle size, which may not accurately represent actual conditions. To address this, a CFD-DEM coupled approach with particle settings closer to field conditions was used to investigate the transport and placement of composite proppants in fractures under different engineering scenarios. Based on the simulation results, the flow capacity of different particle size combinations was evaluated. The results indicate the following: (1) Stepwise proppant injection outperforms mixed injection. For millimeter-scale coal cleavage fractures, the “70/140 + 40/70” mesh proppant size combination is recommended. (2) Adjusting the proppant size ratio can optimize sand bank distribution in branch fractures. In complex networks, increasing the 70/140 mesh proppant ratio from 1/2 to 2/3 increases the placement area in secondary cleavage fractures Frac21 and Frac22 by 2.04% and 0.8%, respectively. (3) Mixed-size proppants tend to segregate and form layered distributions, causing longitudinal variations in stacking flow capacity. Therefore, in numerical simulations, sand bank flow models assuming a single particle size may not accurately reflect fracture productivity. (4) Fracture flow capacity is positively correlated with proppant particle size. The 20/40 mesh proppant pack has higher porosity and looser packing, yielding higher post-propping fracture flow capacity, while the 70/140 mesh pack is more orderly and dense, with relatively low flow capacity. These findings provide a numerical basis for optimizing proppant placement sequences to enhance coalbed methane production.

papers.title: Droplets–liquid layer coalescence in the coupling of rotating electric and rotating flow fields
papers.abstract: The electric dehydration method offers strong controllability and high efficiency, providing a pathway to address the challenge of deep dehydration in crude oil. In this paper, the molecular dynamics method was employed to study the droplets–liquid layer (D–L) coalescence dynamics in the rotating electric and rotating flow coupled (RE&RF) fields. The effects of rotating flow (RF) field intensity, rotating electric (RE) field strength and frequency, nanoparticles (NPs), and surfactants on the D–L coalescence process were systematically analyzed. The results show that increasing the RF field intensity enhances the coalescence efficiency. However, excessively high angular velocities (ωf* ≥ 10.43) are not favorable for high water content (w ≥ 4.02 vol. %) systems. Compared with the direct current field, RE fields can destabilize water chains and promote complete coalescence by periodically altering the field direction. For low w (≤4.02 vol. %), high-frequency RE fields can be adopted to improve the coalescence efficiency; whereas, for high w (≥6.02 vol. %), low-frequency RE fields (ωE* ≤ 2.5) can effectively suppress the formation of water chains. The 45° angular interval RE fields (RE_45°) effectively promote the complete D–L coalescence at both low and high ωE*. Furthermore, the coupled RE_45°&RF fields exhibit superior performance in enhancing coalescence. The existence of Span-80 surfactants can effectively inhibit the effect of SiO2 NPs in reducing the coalescence efficiency. This study elucidates the microscopic mechanisms by which coupled RE&RF fields enhance the D–L coalescence and identifies the optimal conditions for electric dehydration. The findings provide theoretical guidance for addressing the challenges of optimizing high-efficiency and compact oil–water separators.

papers.title: Capillary-driven thinning of a dilute bidisperse polymer solution
papers.abstract: This paper examines capillary thinning of dilute monodisperse and bidisperse polymer solutions using a molecular approach and taking into account the finite extensibility (FE) of macromolecules and hydrodynamic interactions. The equations of chain stretching dynamics were used to study their time evolution at intermediate and high stretching degrees, as well as the behavior of the filament radius and the stretching rate. It is shown that in a bidisperse solution, long and short chains experience non-monotonic stretching in the elasto-capillary (EC) regime. This leads to the development of a maximum in the time-dependence of the stretching rate when the fraction of long chains is small. When the fraction of long chains exceeds some critical value, short chains relax to an equilibrium coiled state upon passing from the inertio-capillary regime to the EC regime, and then these chains stretch again. A physical explanation for this behavior is proposed.

papers.title: Aerodynamic characteristics optimization of H-type vertical-axis wind turbine based on genetic algorithm
papers.abstract: Traditional wind turbines can be classified into horizontal-axis wind turbines (HAWT) and vertical-axis wind turbines (VAWT) based on the geometric relationship between their rotor axis and the horizontal plane. VAWTs do not require automatic yawing systems and have a low center of gravity, good stability, and lower manufacturing and maintenance costs compared with HAWTs. However, it is a consensus in the wind power industry that the single-machine power generation efficiency of VAWTs is lower than that of HAWTs. Therefore, by optimizing the aerodynamic characteristics of individual VAWT, the efficiency of single machines can be improved, thereby achieving efficient operation of VAWTs in grid-connected arrays. In this paper, the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) model NACA0012 airfoil was selected for the overall design of a 10 MW H-type three-blade VAWT. Combined with the optimal Latin hypercube sampling method, the class/shape transformation method was used to mathematically express and deform the NACA0012 airfoil. Based on STAR-CCM+, computational fluid dynamics methods were used to numerically simulate a series of samples. For two important parameters characterizing aerodynamic characteristics, horizontal thrust coefficient, and energy conversion efficiency, a multi-objective optimization problem was established. Multi-objective genetic algorithm was used to optimize them to obtain the Pareto solution set. Typical optimization results from the solution set were selected for analysis. The optimization results show that when the inlet wind speed is 10 m/s and the blade tip velocity ratio is 4.5, compared with the NACA0012 prototype, the optimization result in this paper is at the cost of increasing the horizontal thrust coefficient by 5.45%; meanwhile, the actual operating power of wind turbine is increased by 1.489 MW and the energy conversion efficiency is increased by 13.78%. Additionally, the reduction in the cross-sectional area of a single blade contributed to improved economic efficiency. This paper is dedicated to the research on the optimization of fixed VAWT airfoils and provides examples of aerodynamic performance optimization. It also lays a certain research foundation for subsequent optimization research on floating VAWTs under deep-sea conditions with wind-wave flow coupling.

papers.title: On hydrodynamic loads and stability of projectile during small-angle water entry in waves
papers.abstract: This study develops a three-phase flow solver in OpenFOAM to simulate phase change between vapor and liquid for the small-angle high-speed water entry of a projectile into regular waves. Validation is performed using experimental data for high-speed entry of a projectile. The results demonstrate that the wave phase significantly influences the hydrodynamic loads on the projectile during water entry. Larger phase angles reduce the effective entry angle, defined as the sum of the initial angle and the wave-induced inclination, leading to earlier instability, cavity deformation, and trajectory deviation. By analyzing the lift force, pitching moment, and drag experienced by the projectile during water entry at different wave phases, the study reveals that instability is triggered by a “whip angular velocity” generated upon the initial impact of the projectile with the water surface. Stability is maintained if this angular velocity decays to zero before the second shoulder impact. Based on this criterion, the stable and unstable entry regions for the projectile under the specified wave conditions are delineated. Extending this classification across various wave conditions and entry angles reveals that the likelihood of stable motion increases with the effective entry angle. These findings provide insights into predicting the trajectory stability of slender projectiles entering and moving within cavities under ocean wave conditions.

papers.title: On the impact of turbulent inflow and crack-induced blunt trailing edge on the flow field and far-field noise of an airfoil
papers.abstract: An experimental investigation is carried out to characterize the physical mechanisms by which a trailing-edge crack, idealized as a rectangular cavity to represent delamination damage, affects boundary layer development, coherent vortex shedding, and far-field noise of a National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics 0018 airfoil. Both clean and turbulent inflow conditions are considered to isolate the role of inflow disturbance in modifying these mechanisms. The primary objective is to gain insight into how a geometrical discontinuity at the trailing edge alters the coupled aerodynamic and aeroacoustic behavior. Far-field acoustic measurements and near-wake velocity field data are obtained in the anechoic wind tunnel at Delft University of Technology. Acoustic data from a phased microphone array (from prior work) are combined with new velocity field measurements using particle image velocimetry. The results reveal that increasing crack size leads to enhanced near-wall velocity gradients and stronger coherent vortex shedding, resulting in higher tonal noise levels, particularly at higher frequencies. Normalized tonal frequencies agree with the empirical prediction model of Brooks, Pope, and Marcolini for blunt trailing-edge noise, affirming the relevance of this model even in the presence of geometric imperfections. Under turbulent inflow, the coherent structure scale diminishes slightly, and the tonal frequency increases in the trailing-edge noise spectrum, indicating that inflow turbulence modifies the vortex shedding dynamics and should be accounted for in predictive models. This study is a first step toward understanding and modeling trailing-edge noise in the presence of structural damage, under varying flow conditions.

papers.title: Dynamics of a single bubble collapse near a complex wall–ice boundary
papers.abstract: This study investigates the fundamental dynamics of a single pulsating bubble collapsing in the complex corner geometry formed by a rigid wall and an adjacent ice plate. Coupled experiments using spark-induced bubbles under various ice thicknesses and wall–ice angles were conducted and complemented by Arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian numerical simulations, which were validated with deviations below 10%. The results reveal a rich variety of jetting phenomena governed by the interplay between the wall–ice angle and the dynamic state of the ice boundary. We have identified and categorized four distinct and repeatable jetting modes: Fracture-redirected Jet (FRJ), bisector jet, divergent jet, and split jet (SJ). These modes are shown to be a direct consequence of the initial boundary geometry. For example, ice fracture dynamically changes the boundary from rigid to a free surface, redirecting the jet (FRJ), while a small gap at the wall–ice interface can trigger bubble fission (SJ). The resulting ice fracture patterns and structural pressure footprints serve as clear physical manifestations of these distinct fluid dynamic modes. This work establishes a direct link from initial geometric conditions to the resulting bubble jet dynamics, providing a fundamental understanding of bubble collapse in confined, complex environments.

papers.title: Heat transfer enhancement produced by an oscillatory flow of a viscoelastic fluid in a tube partially filled of porous medium
papers.abstract: This work is devoted to the detailed investigation of heat transfer enhancement caused by an oscillatory flow of a viscoelastic fluid within a tube that is partially filled with a porous medium, which results in two distinct concentric regions: a central core of free fluid and an annular layer of porous material saturated with the same fluid. Heat transfer along the tube is driven by the oscillating flow of a Maxwell fluid induced by an oscillatory pressure gradient. For the analysis, the Darcy–Brinkman and Cauchy–Euler momentum equations are employed to describe the behavior of the viscoelastic fluid flow in the porous and non-porous regions, respectively. The governing equations are presented in its dimensionless version as they are solved analytically, enabling a more precise and comprehensive analysis of key parameters, such as the Darcy, Deborah, and Womersley numbers on heat transfer, and the effective thermal diffusivity is calculated and the conditions that increase its value are analyzed, revealing that it occurs at a specific porous layer thickness. The results show that heat transfer can be enhanced compared to viscoelastic flow in a tube without a porous medium, provided that the porous insert does not reduce the permeability. For a purely viscous fluid, an increase in effective thermal diffusivity also occurs for the same dimensionless thickness of the porous medium. Overall, the combination of an oscillatory viscoelastic fluid flow through a tube that is partially filled with a porous medium improves heat transfer within the tube for a given porous layer thickness.

papers.title: Thermo- and photophoretic mobilities of an oscillating spherical aerosol particle
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analytical investigation into the thermophoretic and photophoretic dynamics of an oscillating spherical aerosol particle within a time-periodic temperature gradient. The theoretical framework is developed for the slip-flow regime (0.01<Kn<0.1) under low Péclet and Reynolds number conditions, incorporating temperature jump, frictional slip, and thermal stress slip phenomena. A central focus is placed on the Womersley number (s). Our analysis reveals that the Womersley number is not merely influential but governs the fundamental transition of the system from a quasi-steady regime at low frequencies to a thermally inertial regime at high frequencies. This transition gives rise to complex dynamic behaviors absent in steady-state models. A key unique discovery of this work is the prediction of frequency-induced phoretic force reversals and resonant phase-lag effects. Specifically, we demonstrate that under certain photophoretic conditions, increasing the oscillation frequency can reverse the direction of the in-phase force component. Expressions for the in-phase and out-of-phase components of both the phoretic force and particle velocity are derived and analyzed. While this study is purely analytical, it provides a crucial predictive benchmark and compares favorably with the steady-state limits reported in previous literature. The findings have direct implications for practical applications, including the high-frequency manipulation of particles in microfluidic devices, the dynamic modeling of black carbon aerosol lifetimes in the atmosphere, and the optimization of thermophoretic precipitators.

papers.title: Unified mixed-lubrication modeling for marine water-lubricated bearings under harsh operating conditions
papers.abstract: This paper presents an enhanced mixed lubrication (ML) model for marine water-lubricated bearings (WLBs), which are frequently subjected to harsh operating conditions. The model combines a revised average Reynolds equation, suitable for extremely low film thickness ratios, with a deterministic asperity contact model derived from numerical simulations of elastic–plastic surface interactions. Unlike conventional statistical approaches, the contact model captures local asperity deformation and mutual interactions, enabling more accurate predictions of contact pressure and film thickness in boundary-dominated regions. Overall, the framework explicitly incorporates shaft misalignment and provides a unified, computationally stable description of non-uniform lubrication states where hydrodynamic, mixed, and boundary regimes may coexist. The validity of the proposed model is confirmed through friction experiments and benchmarked against a representative ML approach. Simulation results reveal pronounced axial variations in film thickness, load-carrying capacity, and friction force. Parametric analyses further demonstrate that higher elastic modulus, yield strength, and surface roughness increase asperity contact and friction, while longitudinal surface textures weaken hydrodynamic pressure generation. The present study offers new insights into understanding and optimizing ML in WLBs, providing practical guidance for improving their tribological performance in marine applications.

papers.title: Response to “Comment on ‘An oceanic basin oscillation-driving mechanism for tides’” [Phys. Fluids 37 , 109101 (2025)]
Thermal and flow characterization of supplementary airflow and ceiling temperature in tunnels with varying fire positions
papers.abstract: To detect fire risks and ensure sufficient safety for the tunnel structure, it is essential to estimate the maximum ceiling gas temperature to which the structure is subjected. Nonetheless, research on the maximum ceiling gas temperature influenced by asymmetric supplemental airflow remains insufficient. This study conducts a series of numerical simulations to investigate the impact of longitudinal fire position on gas distribution and the maximum ceiling gas temperature in tunnels. The heat release rate increases from 3 to 10 MW, while the upstream-to-downstream length decreases from 1:1 to 1:8. Considering the velocity flow field characteristics in computational fluid dynamics simulations, the effects of the longitudinal fire position on the asymmetric airflow and the ceiling maximum temperature rise in the tunnel were studied. The results show that as the fire source gradually approaches the upstream end, the velocity difference between the upstream and downstream gradually increases, resulting in different airflow velocities on both sides of the near flame, which leads to the flame tilting to the downstream, thus affecting a series of fire thermal properties. Then, an ideal fire scenario with openings at both ends but only one end with supplementary air is proposed. In this scene, the influencing factor of fire thermal performance is only the velocity difference. It is verified in the longitudinal ventilation scenario, and the results are in good agreement to prove its effectiveness, thus making the temperature prediction formula in the longitudinal ventilation tunnel still have certain applicability in the natural ventilation tunnel.

papers.title: Investigation of in-cylinder flow and cycle-to-cycle variations in small-bore optical spark-ignition engines with different displacement volumes
papers.abstract: Small-bore engines are widely used in two- and three-wheelers due to their compactness, low cost, and favorable balance between power output and fuel economy. However, they often exhibit significant cycle-to-cycle variations (CCV) in fuel–air mixing and turbulence generation, especially under low-speed and low-throttle conditions, which can degrade combustion stability and overall performance. This variability is primarily driven by the unsteady evolution of in-cylinder flow structures. To address this, the present study utilizes particle image velocimetry to capture flow fields from two small-bore engines (with displacement volumes of 110 and 200 cm3) operating under part-open (25%) and wide-open (100%) throttle conditions. Proper orthogonal decomposition-based quadruple decomposition is employed to assess CCV with flow components—mean, coherent, transition, and turbulent—identified based on cumulative energy contributions from reconstructed modes. Additionally, the relevance index metric is used to quantify the similarity between individual cycles and ensemble-averaged flow fields. The findings of the present study indicate that during the early intake stroke, both engines exhibit nearly identical flow structures with high similarity among the collected snapshots and a dominant contribution from the mean mode. As the intake progresses, the mean energy share decreases due to the intensification of anticlockwise vortices and the onset of backflow, particularly under wide-open throttle conditions. In the compression stroke, the merging of piston-driven upward motion with residual tumble strengthens the mean flow and reduces the CCV in the flow fields. These findings provide insight into the dynamic flow behavior contributing to CCV in small-bore engines and underscore the importance of coherent structure evolution in shaping in-cylinder flow stability.

papers.title: Two-dimensional analysis of weak shock diffraction and reflection in extended Chaplygin gas
papers.abstract: The research investigates the diffraction and reflection phenomena resulting from the interaction of a weak shock wave with a wedge at an arbitrary angle utilizing a more realistic extended Chaplygin gas model. Asymptotic solutions to the two-dimensional Euler equations have been systematically derived, incorporating boundary conditions that accurately describe the diffraction of a weak shock wave encountering the wedge. The study rigorously accounts for the specific properties of the gas under consideration and evaluates their impact on the overall flow structure. A particular focus is placed on the detailed analysis of the local flow characteristics near a singular point, emphasizing the critical influence of the gas's unique behavior on the resulting flow dynamics. Moreover, a comparison is made between the polytropic gas and extended Chaplygin gas effects on the overall flow structure.

papers.title: A novel prediction model integrating physical information and data augmentation for fouling deposition in enhanced tubes
papers.abstract: In traditional data center cooling systems, fouling deposition on the inner surfaces of enhanced tubes severely affects heat exchange efficiency and operational safety, leading to significant economic losses. Due to the lack of long-term fouling test data, most of the existing fouling prediction models are constant fouling factors or semi-empirical formulas established based on accelerated particulate fouling data. These models have low computational accuracy, poor generalizability, and certain limitations in engineering application constraints. To address these challenges, this study develops and validates a high-precision prediction model for combined fouling growth based on data augmentation using long-term fouling test data. First, to overcome the challenge of insufficient data, a physics-informed Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty model is constructed in this study. The fouling thermal resistance database is expanded based on the generative adversarial network (GAN), utilizing the generated data as training sets. Simultaneously, the physical information is combined with the traditional GAN to establish a joint loss function containing physical constraints and improve the quality of the generated data. Second, a physics-informed-convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (LSTM)-Transformer model is introduced in this paper to improve prediction accuracy. To comprehensively extract the global feature information and the nonlinear relationship between each feature and the fouling thermal resistance, the Transformer is integrated with LSTM, creating a feature fusion fouling growth prediction model. Finally, SHapley Additive exPlanations were employed for interpretability analysis of the prediction model, with validation conducted using the long-term fouling test data from ASHRAE RP-1677. The results demonstrate that, compared to the baseline without data augmentation under various operating conditions, the average goodness-of-fit (R2) of the prediction model increased from −0.193 to 0.783, while the average prediction final bias decreased from 23.87% to 2.8%, confirming the superior performance of the proposed methodology.

papers.title: A new wetting boundary scheme in phase-field lattice Boltzmann model for two-phase flows with large density ratios and complex solid boundaries
papers.abstract: A new wetting boundary scheme for simulating large-density-ratio two-phase flow with complex solid boundary is developed within a modified phase-field lattice Boltzmann model. Compared to the existing schemes, the proposed method directly calculates the order-parameters gradient at boundary fluid nodes without estimating the order parameters of ghost solid nodes, and it possesses both the simplicity of geometrical formulation scheme and the accuracy of free-energy scheme. Additionally, a new method for identifying solid boundary contours is proposed, enabling the presented boundary treatment to handle arbitrary complex and irregular solid boundaries. Five benchmark cases are used to test the proposed method, including droplet spreading on a circular wall, capillary-driven flow between parallel plates, droplet impacting on a circular cylinder, capillary rise in sinusoidal wavy channels, and irregularly bounded porous media flow. The results show that the present method provides an accurate, efficient, and stable tool for simulating two-phase flows through complicated geometries at large density ratios.

papers.title: Apparent contact angle of droplet with polygonal wetting footprint on reentrant microstructure surface
papers.abstract: Reentrant microstructures characterized by excellent superhydrophobic property have demonstrated significant potential in liquid–vapor phase-change heat transfer, self-cleaning, and medical protection. Current research about droplet wetting on reentrant microstructure surfaces primarily focuses on the Cassie–Wenzel wetting transition. However, a theoretical prediction of the apparent contact angle on this heterogeneous structure for design guideline is lacking. In this work, microscale three-dimensional (3D) printing is adopted to fabricate T-shape reentrant microstructures to analyze the direction-dependent apparent contact angle of droplet with polygonal wetting footprint. We reveal the step-by-step evolution of polygonal footprint during droplet wetting on the reentrant microstructure via both experiments and lattice Boltzmann simulation. This stepwise wetting evolution is found to be caused by the de-pinning of the droplet contact line due to contacting the neighboring microstructures. We modify the classical double-radius model by considering the rotationally varied wetting radius of the polygonal wetting footprint for better fitting the droplet contour to predict the direction-dependent apparent contact angle. This wetting prediction model is validated by experimental measurement of droplet contact angle on the T-shape reentrant microstructure with varied structure spacing.

papers.title: Turbulence through the lens of a visionary: A tribute to K. R. Sreenivasan and an introduction to the special issue
papers.abstract: This special issue of Physics of Fluids celebrates the 75th birthday of Professor Katepalli Raju Sreenivasan, popularly known as Sreeni, a distinguished figure whose intellectual influence extends broadly across fluid dynamics, statistical physics, applied mathematics, and beyond. It is a privilege to introduce this collection of papers, contributed by colleagues, former students, and researchers deeply influenced by his work, reflecting the profound respect and admiration he commands within the scientific community.

papers.title: High-order compact fully discrete schemes for inviscid compressible flows simulations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an single-stage compact fully discrete scheme based on the weighted essentially non-oscillatory reconstruction and the solution formula method. The novelty of this scheme relies on three aspects. First, unlike existing single-stage compact schemes that usually require additional computation and evolution of the derivatives, the proposed scheme construct the compact stencil by utilizing the (quasi-)exact solution of the Hamilton–Jacobi equation, which is time efficient as it does not require cumbersome Lax–Wendroff method. Next, to enhance the numerical stabilities for non-smooth flows, we propose a modified entropy condition that specifically designed for the single-stage compact fully discrete scheme. In addition, we also develop a consistent evolution strategy for extending this compact fully discrete scheme to multi-dimensional situations, which can further improve the efficiency of it. A number of one-dimensional and multi-dimensional numerical examples have been tested to demonstrate its accuracy, correctness, and efficiency. For most of the cases, this single-stage compact fully discrete scheme significantly outperforms the original non-compact fully discrete scheme and semi-discrete scheme. The acceleration of this scheme compared to the s-stage semi-discrete scheme can achieve 60%–80% of the theoretical value, i.e., the stage number s, which is considerably larger than that of the existing single-stage compact fully discrete scheme.

papers.title: On the evolution of eolian ripples: An insight from wind tunnel observations and spectral analysis
papers.abstract: Eolian ripples are the most basic geomorphological structure, whose evolutionary behaviors are essential for understanding the development of landforms in arid areas, yet remain debatable. Here we address this problem via wind tunnel experiments, together with Digital Image Projection and spectral analysis. For the initially flat beds, three evolution phases are observed, including destabilization, development and saturation phases, meanwhile recovering well the linear dependence of the saturated wavelength λsatf on the wind velocity. When it comes to the initially undulated beds, the evolution process is determined by the relative magnitude of the initial wavelength λ0 and λsatf. In the cases with λ0≤λsatf, a distinct three-phase evolution process can be seen, including (1) initial modulation, where the ripple height drops sharply while the wavelength remains constant; (2) wavelength jump, where a quick rise in the wavelength is observed; (3) saturation, the wavelength reaches saturation, and the increase in height slows down. Notably, a larger saturated wavelength λsat>λsatf can be observed, indicating the existence of stable nonlinear solutions. When λ0>λsatf, the initial undulations will last for a longer time. Visually, these initial undulations can persist at low friction velocity, but meanwhile, the power spectral density indicates spectral broadening and dominance reduction. Harmonics can be generated when λ0 is sufficiently higher than λsatf. At the same time, it is found that the ripple index consistently falls within the range of 15–20 during steady-state phases, regardless of the initial morphology and wind velocity. These findings establish λ0/λsatf as a primary control parameter and demonstrate the capability of the spectral analysis in detecting the evolutionary behaviors of eolian ripples. The present findings could well inform the subsequent theoretical modeling, and serve to validate the potential fluid dynamics mechanisms.

papers.title: Numerical study on influences of water scouring on dynamic characteristics of mono-pile foundation for offshore wind turbines
papers.abstract: The structure dynamic characteristics determine the response, vibration behavior, and long-term usability of the foundation to external loads; quantitative identification of its driving factors is crucial for precise design, safety optimization, and fatigue life prediction. In harsh marine environments, local erosion around offshore foundations can significantly alter dynamic performance. Previous studies linked the depth of scour to changes in pile fundamental frequency, but largely overlooked the additional effects of scour pit morphology and hydrodynamic forces. This study established a fully coupled fluid soil pile interaction model with dynamic grids to capture real-time erosion evolution and validated it through comprehensive flume measurements. Then, the system analyzed and quantified how current velocity, water depth, and scour pit geometry collectively affect the natural frequency of the foundation. The results indicate that for maximum scour depths below 1.8 times the pile diameter, it is not sufficiently accurate to explain the frequency attenuation by considering only the maximum scour depth while ignoring scour-pit morphology. Neglecting hydrodynamic effects may result in an estimated fundamental frequency difference of up to 20% for scour pile foundations.

papers.title: The role of polymer adhesion to solid surfaces for drop rebound
papers.abstract: This work investigated the high molecular weight polymer drop rebound and deposition phenomena, particularly in the dilute regime. Enhancing drop deposition dynamics is crucial for many applications including agricultural pesticide application to minimize spray drift and drop rebound from leaves. Although high molecular weight polymer drop impact has been extensively studied and shown to improve drop retention dynamics on leaves, in this study, we show that large molecular weight (MDa) in polymers is insufficient for suppressing drop rebound. We found that when the polymer–solid interaction is favorable, it results in an anti-rebound effect; otherwise, it leads to partial or complete rebound. We utilized a drop generator and high-speed imaging to investigate the impact dynamics of various polymeric drops on a hydrophobic surface (e.g., Parafilm).

papers.title: Prediction of bubble size distribution in cloud cavitation flow based on physics-informed neural network
papers.abstract: The characterization of bubble size distribution (BSD) in the cloud cavitation region, which is critical for assessing cavitation erosion and noise, is currently inadequately captured by prevailing measurement techniques and numerical simulations. The population balanced equation (PBE) offers an effective framework for describing BSD, however, at a high computational cost. This study establishes an efficient approach to solve temporally averaged PBE using a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to determine the BSD in the cloud cavitation around a hydrofoil. By decomposing the PBE into two sub-equations for the number density n and the probability density function f, the multiscale complexity inherent in the PBE is effectively reduced. Two corresponding individual PINN networks, PINN-n and PINN-f, are created accordingly and trained to seek the solutions to the two sub-equations. Numerical simulations using large eddy simulation furnish the background flow field for the PBE, and experimental data at pointwise positions offer the boundary conditions of BSD. The reconstruction of void fraction from the solutions of number density and probability density function demonstrates that the PINN method is capable of solving the PBE with reasonable accuracy. A continuous mapping of BSD without requiring a prescribed distribution function can be acquired at any spatial location. The proposed method provides an efficient framework for predicting the BSD throughout the domain from sparse pointwise BSD information.

papers.title: Localized magnetohydrodynamic effects on natural convection in a cubic cavity at Rayleigh number up to 107
papers.abstract: Magnetic field control offers significant advantages for fluid flow and thermal regulation, including fast dynamics and contactless operation. However, magnetohydrodynamic systems at high Rayleigh number (Ra) present considerable challenges due to the intricate physics that render it into a stiff system, and the underlying mechanisms of complex thermal boundary flows in three-dimensional configurations remain poorly understood. In this study, the governing equations were non-dimensionalized using the buoyancy-driven scale and solved employing an established finite difference solver. The proposed scheme yields an error of only 0.55% compared to the reference solution. The effects of the Hartmann number (Ha), Ra, and thermal boundary conditions on natural convection within the cubic cavity were investigated. The interplay between variations in fluid velocity components and temperature distribution was elucidated. The results demonstrate that an increasing Ha induces a reversal in the direction of the horizontal velocity component along the cavity centerline, subsequently altering the temperature distribution. The magnetic field's suppression of flow and heat transfer is not uniform but exhibits localized enhancement in specific regions. At Ha=30 and Ra=106, the streamline center within the cavity evolves into four secondary centers. These findings underscore the complex influence of magnetic fields on flow and heat transfer in three-dimensional problems, with thermal boundary conditions playing a critical role.

papers.title: FluxNet: Accelerating flux calculation via coarse-to-fine neural modeling
papers.abstract: The finite volume method (FVM) has emerged as a dominant numerical framework in computational fluid dynamics for simulating complex flow phenomena, such as aerospace external aerodynamics and internal combustion engine combustion, owing to its exceptional geometric adaptability and numerical stability. Flux calculation as the core component of FVM, directly dictates the performance of large-scale simulations. However, traditional flux splitting schemes, like AUSMPW+ (advection upstream splitting method with pressure-weighted improvements, a classic upwind scheme), suffer from limited computational efficiency on high-resolution grids due to extensive conditional branching and data dependencies. To address this, we introduce FluxNet, an end-to-end flux calculation accelerator based on a lightweight neural network, designed to overcome the bottlenecks of conventional numerical methods. FluxNet employs a coarse sampling-fine prediction framework, where training data are generated on coarse grids to constrain input parameter ranges and reduce data outliers. To ensure physical consistency, this is coupled with an error-guided progressive iterative sampling method, which suppresses error accumulation through dynamic error feedback during iterative computations, ensuring physical consistency. We conduct numerical experiments on canonical test cases, including both one-dimensional and three-dimensional scenarios. The results demonstrate that FluxNet achieves a nearly fourfold acceleration compared to AUSMPW+ while maintaining an average relative error below 0.615%—and its mean absolute percentage error is less than 1%, satisfying engineering-grade accuracy requirements. This study presents a data-driven paradigm for efficient flux calculation in FVM, with potential for multi-scale modeling to expand its applicability to complex engineering scenarios.

papers.title: Investigation of solid–liquid two-phase flow dynamics and resulting wear patterns in a mixed flow pump as turbine under pumping condition
papers.abstract: Mixed-flow pump as turbine (PAT), combining pumping and power generation capabilities, is applied in low-head tidal power stations and bidirectional river water transfer projects. However, solid particles inevitably ingested during pumping condition cause wear and deformation that threatens equipment life and safety. This paper employs the Eulerian–Lagrangian multiphase model and the Tabakoff wear model to numerically simulate the pump mode, with results agreeing with experimental data. With increasing flow rate, the flow direction mismatches the impeller inlet angle, deflecting particles toward the suction surface of impeller blades. This reduces wear area on the pressure surface of impeller blades but intensifies wear at the leading edges of both the impeller and guide vane suction surfaces, extending toward the trailing edge. As particle diameter increases, greater inertia deflects trajectories toward the impeller pressure surface, increasing wear area and rate across all surfaces of the impeller and guide vanes. With rising particle volume fraction, increased collision frequency shifts trajectories toward the impeller pressure surface and elevates wear rates. Compared to pure water operation, solid–liquid flow significantly reduces efficiency and head, with particle volume fraction exerting the strongest negative effect. This research offers valuable insights for refining PAT designs to improve the wear resistance.

papers.title: Influence of the slip length on the fluid dynamics of a marine propeller
papers.abstract: Large Eddy Simulation (LES) was adopted to study the influence of the slip length of the surface of a marine propeller on its performance, the flow on its blades, and its wake in open water conditions. Computations were carried out on a cylindrical grid consisting of 6.7 × 109 points. The results of the simulations show a small reduction (within a few percent) of both thrust and torque, even with large values of the slip length, resulting in negligible effects on the overall efficiency of propulsion. The major effect was a slight delay in the transition to turbulence on the pressure side of the blades and an increase in the turbulent fluctuations in the vicinity of the trailing edge for larger slip lengths. The overall result of these phenomena was a rise in the unsteady component of the loads on the propeller. The wake flow was practically unchanged in terms of both topology and intensity of its major structures and the first and second order statistics. In conclusion, the results of the present study indicate only minor changes in the performance and wake features from the implementation of hydrophobic treatments or coatings on the surface of propellers, even when large values of the slip length are achieved at model-scale Reynolds numbers, which emphasize the effects of the hydrophobic properties of the surface. Although these results refer to a particular propeller and working condition, their root causes suggest they could be extended to different geometries and loads.

papers.title: Molecular dynamics study of bubble growth in pure water
papers.abstract: Cavitation erosion is one of the main damage styles of dynamic components of ships. In order to suppress cavitation damage, it is particularly important to elucidate the mechanism of nucleation and bubble growth. In this paper, a pure water cavitation model was established using the molecular dynamics method. Based on the constructed model, the processes of nucleation and bubble growth under varying stretching rates and temperature conditions are investigated. The results show that the bubble growth process experiences four stages: nucleation, rapid growth, stable growth, and collapse. Stable bubbles are generated in pure water only when the critical pressure falls below the saturation vapor pressure. A high stretching rate and a low system temperature can reduce the critical pressure. However, once the bubble is formed, the large stretching rate and high system temperature can expedite the bubble growth, leading to a more rapid bubble collapse. Finally, several functions that can accurately predict the nucleation and growth of bubbles under different conditions are presented.

papers.title: Time-dependent gas dissolution on kick migration during deepwater drilling
papers.abstract: Gas dissolution–desolution dynamics during drilling operations induce complex kick migration patterns, posing significant challenges to early kick detection and wellbore pressure management. In this study, a theoretical model of gas solubility in drilling fluids is proposed, incorporating the complex interactions between gas, salts, polymers, and base oil under different temperature and pressure conditions. Experimental validation demonstrates mean errors of 3.487% and 6.751% for water-based (WBDFs) and oil-based (OBDFs) drilling fluids, respectively. Considering time-dependent gas dissolution, a wellbore multiphase flow model is developed to characterize dynamic kick migration in the wellbore. Simulations indicate that gas dissolution slows the rate of change in pit gain and bottomhole pressure (BHP), resulting in concealed gas influx in deepwater drilling. A comparative analysis revealed that OBDF exhibits a slower pit gain and BHP response, with gas kick detection time 1.57 times longer than that in WBDF. During well shut-in, the gas influx predominantly remains dissolved in OBDF, causing BHP to generally stabilize at formation pressure. To mitigate gas influx desolution and expansion effects, a minimum wellhead backpressure of 5 MPa is recommended.

papers.title: Dynamic behavior of tandem perforated elastic vortex generators using two-way coupled fluid–structure interaction simulations
papers.abstract: This study presents high-fidelity, two-way coupled fluid–structure interaction (FSI) simulations to investigate the dynamic behavior of tandem perforated elastic vortex generators (EVGs) across a wide range of bending rigidity, mass ratio, and porosity, at a fixed Reynolds number and interspacing. Comparative simulations with non-perforated EVGs are also performed. Three response modes—Lodging, Vortex-Induced Vibration (VIV), and Static Reconfiguration—are observed in both configurations, while a distinct Cavity Oscillation mode emerges exclusively in non-perforated tandem EVGs. This mode is entirely suppressed with porosity due to disruption of the low-pressure cavity and increased flow transmission through pores. Frequency analyses reveal that VIV is consistently locked onto the second natural frequency, whereas the Cavity Oscillation mode is locked onto the first natural frequency and closely aligns with the first Rossiter mode, underscoring its distinct physical origin. Perforation modifies the natural frequency of the EVGs, shifting the lock-in and mode transitions toward lower bending rigidity and higher mass ratio values, and reducing oscillation amplitudes due to motion damping. Drag analysis shows consistently higher upstream drag due to wake shielding, while porosity reduces upstream drag and increases downstream drag by restoring streamwise momentum. Flow visualizations demonstrate that vortex shedding originates at the EVG tips, with perforated configurations producing smaller, more dissipative vortical structures. These results establish that porosity fundamentally alters dynamic regimes, suppresses cavity-driven instabilities, and enables passive modulation of wake dynamics in tandem EVG systems.

papers.title: Effect of different bionic structures on clearance flow and aerodynamic performance in linear cascades
papers.abstract: Three bio-inspired structures are proposed: the tip bionic chamber structure (TBC), the casing bionic chamber structure (CBC), and the pressure-side tip winglet structure (PSTW), drawing inspiration from the excellent airflow characteristics of dragonfly wing cavities and avian feather bifurcations. Numerical simulations are carried out to examine their influence on the interaction between corner flow and tip clearance leakage flow within compressor cascades. The results indicate that all three bionic cases can effectively suppress clearance leakage flow, attenuate vortex-induced losses, and diminish the total pressure loss. Overall, these bio-inspired designs optimize the clearance leakage flow characteristics. Among the three, PSTW exhibits superior performance, achieving a 16.8% reduction in tip leakage flow ratio (RQm) and a 0.64% decrease in total pressure loss coefficient (Cpt). Additionally, the mechanisms by which these structures control leakage flow behavior are systematically analyzed across various incidence angles and tip clearance heights to evaluate their potential for extending the stability margin. The findings demonstrate that all three designs effectively suppress leakage flow across a wide range of operating conditions. Notably, PSTW provides the most robust suppression of RQm across different clearance heights, despite causing a slight increase in Cpt at positive incidence angles. Generally, under various operating conditions, PSTW most significantly enhances the aerodynamic performance of the tip clearance region.

papers.title: Experimental investigation on the dynamic response and rock breaking performance of the self-controlled hydro-pick used for the cutting head
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an innovative self-controlled hydraulic cutting head (SCHCH) with adaptive hydro-picks that dynamically adjust high-pressure water supply based on cutting conditions. First, based on fracture mechanics, a model is constructed to describe the decline rate of cutting force when a water jet assists a conical pick in rock breaking. Furthermore, the flow characteristic of the self-controlled hydro-pick was carried out to explore the water-saving characteristics. Regarding the factors influencing the dynamic response characteristics of the self-controlled hydro-pick, whether for the opening or closing response time, the order of significance from high to low is cutting depth A, jet pressure C, and cutting speed B. In addition, the rock breaking performance of the cutting head with different arrangements of water jet nozzles and conical picks (WJCH) was also analyzed. The results found the cutting torque decrease percentage was 33%, 16%, 40%, and 38% for the nozzles of the cutting head positioned at the front (FWJCH), rear (RWJCH), center (CWJCH) of the pick, and SCHCH, respectively, and the standard deviation of the SCHCH was the lowest. Finally, the effect of different configuration modes on dust reduction was explored by analyzing the dust concentration during rock breaking. The dust concentrations in FWJCH, RWJCH, CWJCH, and SCHCH models were 2.34, 1.91, 1.88, and 1.97 mg/m3, respectively, and the corresponding dust reduction percentages were 32.76%, 45.11%, 45.98%, and 43.39% compared with the cutting head without water jet assistance (NWJCH).

papers.title: Biglobal linear stability analysis of a ducted premixed flame: Intrinsic thermoacoustic mode and role of exceptional point
papers.abstract: Combustion dynamics in aero-engines exhibit complex thermoacoustic behavior involving multiple interacting modes. Recent research on the so-called intrinsic thermoacoustic modes has provided new impetus for exploring the physical origins of these modes and their mutual interactions. The present study concerns the interplay between the intrinsic thermoacoustic modes and duct acoustic modes in a fundamental combustion configuration. The biglobal linear stability analysis of a ducted premixed flame is carried out by exploiting the linearized compressible reactive flow equations. The pure intrinsic thermoacoustic mode is first identified and characterized. Parameter variations are conducted to study the behaviors of eigenmode trajectories in the proximity of an exceptional point. Near the exceptional point, trajectory veering and mode switching are observed. We find that different parameter variation paths can lead to inconsistent results in mode origin identification. Hence, we propose to characterize the thermoacoustic modes based on the flow structures. Specifically, the Helmholtz decomposition is employed to extract the potential and solenoidal components of the thermoacoustic modes and we find the intrinsic thermoacoustic modes and duct acoustic modes exhibit distinct decomposed flow structures.

papers.title: Stokes flow around a paraboloid of revolution: Analytical treatment in an unbounded domain
papers.abstract: Stokes flow describes the motion of a Newtonian, incompressible fluid in regimes where inertial effects are negligible compared to viscous forces. In the case of axisymmetric flow and by employing a stream function ψ, the governing equation reduces to E4ψ=0, where E2 is a second order elliptic partial differential operator and E4=E2○E2. In this work, we derive the general solution of the equation E4ψ=0 in the parabolic coordinate system, which is given as series expansions of specific combinations of mixed-order Bessel and modified Bessel functions of first and second kinds or as a polynomial. This analytical framework is applied to study the Stokes flow around a rigid paraboloid solving a boundary value problem, accordingly. A truncated error analysis is conducted, proving that using at least eight terms of the obtained series expansion, the absolute error is less than 10−5. Sample streamlines are depicted with respect to the order of truncation. The obtained stream function expansion allows for the computation of key hydrodynamic quantities, such as the velocity and the pressure fields, offering insights into the behavior of the particular flow. It may also serve as a foundation for further investigations of problems in a wide range of areas, from chemical engineering to biomedicine.

papers.title: Investigation of coherent structures around a surface-mounted tripile cylinder array
papers.abstract: The present study examines turbulent flow around a three-dimensional tripile submerged foundation experimentally, using laser Doppler velocimetry, and numerically, using Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) and large eddy simulation (LES) techniques. The study is conducted at a Reynolds number of 104 with a tripile spacing ratio of 3. Flow measurements are compared to assess the predictive capabilities of the selected turbulence models. All RANS models succeeded in predicting primary mean flow phenomena, including flow detachment, vortex recirculation, and downstream reattachment. The LES model performed adequately well both near-wake and far-wake regions. Within the near wake region, the standard k−ϵ model exhibited the largest deviation from experimental data, although it performed appropriately well in the far-wake region. The k−ω shear stress transport model overpredicted the wake recovery. The observed discrepancies are likely due to limitations in modeling flows with large pressure gradients. Also, detailed structural analysis was conducted using the instantaneous flow data obtained from the LES simulations. Key flow features such as the horseshoe vortex, arch vortex, and a dipole structure composed of counter-rotating vortices are identified, exhibiting qualitative agreement with previous high-Reynolds number studies on an isolated cylinder. Instantaneous flow visualization revealed an antler-shaped vortex structure in the downstream wake, which resulted from the interaction of streamwise and spanwise vortices. Time-averaged surface streamlines were used to identify saddle points, attachment nodes, and swirl patterns on the tripiles. Notably, visualization at the free end of the downstream cylinder showed inward-shifted foci and a crescent-shaped recirculation region.

papers.title: Numerical study on the contribution of local flow to aerodynamic drag for high-speed trains
papers.abstract: Surface-based aerodynamic drag breakdown encounters limitations in explaining subtle drag-reduction schemes for modern high-speed trains. In this study, delayed detached eddy simulation (DDES) is employed to conduct a control volume analysis of turbulent losses around an eight-car train, quantifying the contributions of turbulence production and viscous dissipation to aerodynamic drag in specific local flow regions. While the component contributions identified by the volumetric approach largely align with surface-based breakdown results, the volumetric method offers more detailed spatial insights. For instance, the bogie region contributes the most to aerodynamic drag, accounting for 39%, with volumetric losses concentrated along the sides and underneath the bogies. This result supports the effectiveness of bogie skirt and belly fairing applications. Furthermore, the volumetric analysis reveals that viscous dissipation losses in the upper body region are primarily due to wall friction, whereas in the lower body region, turbulent viscosity from separated shear layers dominates. In the wake region, turbulence and outflow flux contribute approximately 15% of the total drag, indicating substantial potential for aerodynamic optimization. The detailed identification of local region contributions provided in this study offers a complementary perspective that can inform the design and optimization of future high-speed train.

papers.title: Influence of supraglottal tract on intraglottal pressure during vocal fold closing in human phonation
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional fluid–structure interaction (FSI) simulations were conducted to study the influence of the supraglottal tract on intraglottal pressure during vocal fold closing in human phonation. The FSI framework couples a three-mass vocal fold model, an incompressible Navier–Stokes flow solver, and a linear perturbed compressible acoustic solver. Four configurations were simulated under varying subglottal pressures, combining divergent and nearly straight vocal fold closing patterns with and without a supraglottal tract. Comparison of straight closing configurations with and without a supraglottal tract revealed the isolated effect of supraglottal inertance, while the analysis of divergent closing configurations showed the combined effects of supraglottal inertance and intraglottal flow separation. Parameters, including the glottal opening, glottal angle, medial surface wall pressure, which directly reflects how intraglottal pressure is converted to the driving force of the vocal fold motion, and intraglottal flow dynamics, were analyzed. The results show that the supraglottal tract influences intraglottal pressure, as well as the medial surface wall pressure, through two primary mechanisms. First, it reduces medial surface wall pressure through inertance effects during flow deceleration. Second, in the divergent closing configurations, it further decreases medial surface wall pressure by intensifying the flow separation effect. This enhanced flow separation effect is because the supraglottal tract increases peak jet velocity during glottis closing, which strengthens the shear layer and enhances flow circulation after flow separation. Consequently, it leads to more negative glottal pressure, particularly under high subglottal pressures.

papers.title: Hydrodynamics of an unconstrained self-propelled flexible fin with pure pitching motion
papers.abstract: The hydrodynamic performance of an unconstrained self-propelled flexible fin undergoing pure pitching motion, free to move in both the horizontal and lateral directions, is investigated using two-dimensional numerical simulations. A systematic parametric analysis is conducted to examine the effects of pitching frequency, amplitude, and bending stiffness on propulsion characteristics. For a uniformly flexible fin, three distinct propulsion regimes are identified: steady swimming, deflected swimming, and backward swimming, each associated with variations in flapping symmetry and wake structure. In contrast, a rigid fin exhibits only steady swimming across all tested conditions, maintaining symmetric kinematics and coherent wake patterns. Although the flapping amplitudes of the rigid fin's leading and trailing edges are smaller than those of the uniformly flexible fin, the rigid fin consistently achieves higher cruising speed and propulsive efficiency. This superior performance is attributed to a small phase lag between the lateral motions of the leading and trailing edges, which promotes more synchronized deformation and thereby enhances momentum transfer. When a spatially non-uniform bending stiffness is introduced into the flexible fin, performance enhancement is achieved through increased flapping amplitudes and improved phase coordination. The resulting deformation facilitates the constructive merging of vortices shed from the leading and trailing edges, producing stronger and more coherent wake structures. Consequently, the non-uniformly flexible fin outperforms not only the uniformly flexible fin but also the rigid fin in overall propulsive performance. Although this superiority is consistently observed in the low-Re regime, the efficiency advantage shifts in favor of the rigid fin at higher Re.

papers.title: Parameter identification for gradient porous media flow using sparse data
papers.abstract: Parameter identification for flow and heat transfer in gradient porous media plays a critical role in engineering design and anomaly detection in applications such as transpiration cooling. In this work, our recently developed TB (trunk-branch)-net physics-informed neural network (PINN) is combined with sparse pressure sensor data to enable the identification of porosity and permeability in dual-domain and multi-domain gradient porous flow, achieving satisfactory results. Meanwhile, the forward inversion results of pressure and velocity fields also exhibit accurate flow trends. Compared with traditional regularization techniques, the use of TB-net PINN eliminates the need of multiple forward solution iterations, enabling complex parameter identification in multi-domain scenarios.

papers.title: Flow dynamics and velocity decay in vegetated leaky barrier wakes
papers.abstract: Leaky barriers serve as a soft-engineering approach for river management and have become indispensable for river restoration and bank stabilization. In this study, we idealized multiple full-span leaky barriers as horizontally arranged cylindrical arrays with uniform diameters (d) and equal spacing (0.5d). Flow field visualization was conducted using tracer techniques, and particle image velocimetry was employed to quantify the effects of blockage ratio on wake structures behind these barriers. Results demonstrate that flow deflection induced by barrier obstruction generates a primary jet through basal gaps. The maximum velocity of the primary jet (u¯max) increases with the blockage ratio (ψ), reaching 2.82–4.43 times the average velocity of the incoming flow (U0). The primary jet retains initial velocity at x/d≤0.5, decaying linearly within 0.5<x/d<2.4. Within 2.4<x/d<8, the decay rate diminishes due to jet merging and weakened adverse pressure gradient. Multiple secondary jets emerge within inter-cylinder gaps and are deflected by the low-pressure zones downstream of cylinders. These jets coalesce before merging with the primary jet. Coherent vortex bands with elevated vorticity develop near wake shear layers, significantly enhancing turbulent kinetic energy in these regions. Jet interactions modulate velocity decay patterns in both primary and secondary jets. This work reveals fluid-barrier interaction mechanisms, advances hydrodynamic understanding of leaky barriers, and evaluates their ecohydraulic implications for riverine ecosystems.

papers.title: Influence of periodic pulsations on separation induced by shock wave–boundary layer interaction
papers.abstract: Shock wave–boundary layer interaction in a duct is investigated via large eddy simulation to understand the effects of strong pulsations induced by blade row interaction in highly loaded turbomachinery. Periodic inlet total pressure pulsations with varying frequencies are imposed at the inlet. Numerical results show that the separation bubble, induced by the interaction between the shock wave and the boundary layer, is suppressed under the influence of the imposed pulsations. The suppression effect varies with frequency, with a maximum reduction in the time-averaged separation bubble length reaching approximately 10%. Spectral analyses reveal that vortex shedding and breakdown behavior in the shear layer are modulated by the imposed pulsations. At specific forcing frequencies, large-scale unsteady motions become fully synchronized with the pulsations. Further analysis of turbulence statistics shows that peak turbulent kinetic energy in the shear layer increases under pulsations, indicating enhanced turbulence intensity. This leads to stronger momentum exchange between the core flow and the separation bubble, thereby promoting separation suppression. These findings provide new insights into how periodic pulsations can control shock–boundary layer interactions. This study could inspire the development of unsteady flow control technologies, such as plasma-based or pulsed jet techniques, for separation control in high-load compressors by targeting the unsteady characteristics of the near-wall shear layer.

papers.title: Entropy generation in time-fractional magnetohydrodynamic nanofluid Couette flow between permeable walls
papers.abstract: This study investigates entropy generation in magnetohydrodynamic radiative nanofluid Couette flow through a permeable channel using the Caputo time-fractional derivative framework. The model incorporates thermal radiation, magnetic field effects, viscous and Joule heating, nanoparticle volume fraction, and wall suction/injection, with the upper permeable wall moving and subject to convective heat exchange with its surroundings. The fractional derivative captures memory-dependent transport processes, extending classical models of transient nanofluid flow and heat transfer. The governing fractional partial differential equations for velocity and temperature are solved numerically via a hybrid Euler wavelet collocation method for spatial discretization and a fractional finite difference scheme for temporal discretization, with Newton's method employed for nonlinear resolution. Key thermophysical quantities such as Bejan number, entropy generation rate, skin friction and Nusselt number are analyzed to assess irreversibilities and transport mechanisms. The parametric results reveal that increasing the fractional-order parameter and nanoparticles volume fraction enhances thermal performance but also augment entropy generation , while stronger magnetic fields and wall permeability significantly alter momentum transport and entropy distribution. These findings provide valuable guidelines for entropy management in nanofluid-based thermal–fluid systems with applications in energy conversion, microfluidics, and advanced cooling technologies.

papers.title: Efficient scaling line-based scaled boundary finite element method for transient seepage problems in semi-infinite discontinuous foundations
papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of transient seepage in semi-infinite discontinuous foundations remains a significant challenge in geotechnical engineering due to geometric and material discontinuities and the presence of unbounded domains. To address this, a scaling line-based scaled boundary finite element method (SBFEM) is developed and extended to simulate transient seepage behavior. The governing equation of hydraulic head is first derived using the weighted residual method and then transformed into a transient seepage matrix form, which is subsequently solved through continued-fraction expansion. The solution to the transient seepage problem is first obtained by solving the eigenvalue problem to obtain the steady-state solution, and then the determined mass matrix is used to solve the time-domain water head solution using the modified precise time step integration method (MPTSIM). The accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method are validated through numerical examples, followed by its application to more complex seepage scenarios involving discontinuous foundations.
